في أكتوبر 2020، أعربت امرأة تبلغ من العمر 90 عامًا تُدعى نانسي راسل، وكانت تقيم في دار لرعاية المسنين في تورونتو، كندا، عن رغبتها في أن يساعدها طبيب على قتل نفسها. فقد شعرت أن العزلة التي عاشتها خلال الأشهر القليلة السابقة تفوق قدرتها على الاحتمال، ولم ترَ لها نهاية.

لم تكن نانسي راسل مصابة بالخرف، ولم تكن تعاني من أي حالة تُعد عادةً مرضًا عضالًا. لكن في كندا، ليس من الضروري أن يكون المرء مصابًا بمرض عضال كي يطلب المساعدة على الانتحار بمساعدة طبيب. وتُطلق كندا على هذا الإجراء اسم «المساعدة الطبية على الموت» (MAID). يوحي الاسم بأن الأمر يتعلق بالرعاية التلطيفية، لكن الواقع أنه لا يمت إليها بصلة.

استمع طبيب مختص بطب الشيخوخة إلى قصتها ووافق على مساعدتها. وخرجت من دار الرعاية لتقضي الأسبوع التالي مع أسرتها. وفي نهاية ذلك الوقت، أُعطيت حقنة قاتلة بحضور أفراد أسرتها. وهذه ليست حالة معزولة؛ ففي عام 2020، انتحر 7,595 شخصًا بمساعدة طبيب.

حين أتأمل هذه الإحصاءات المفجعة، أشعر بحزن عميق. فهناك معنى تتخلى فيه أسر كثيرة عن أفرادها المسنين أو المرضى. ويبدو أن جائحة كوفيد لم تفعل سوى تفاقم هذه المشكلة. وثمة مشكلة أكبر، وهي أن مجتمعنا لم يعد يقدّر حياة كبار السن.

إن المجتمع الذي لم يعد يقدّر كل حياة بشرية باعتبارها مهمة، يبدأ في السماح بأمور مثل الانتحار بمساعدة طبيب، بل وحتى القتل الرحيم. فالقتل الرحيم هو أن يعطي شخصٌ دواءً لشخص آخر بقصد قتله، أما الانتحار بمساعدة الغير فهو أن يزوّد شخصٌ آخرَ بدواء يتولى ذلك الآخر «بنفسه» تناوله، فيقتل نفسه بذلك.

من المفيد أن نراجع كيف نتعامل نحن، بوصفنا مسيحيين، مع حالات نهاية الحياة، وأن نحاول أن نفهم أين انحرف العالم من حولنا انحرافًا فادحًا.

مخلوقون على صورة الله

فخلق الله الإنسان على صورته، على صورة الله خلقه؛ ذكرًا وأنثى خلقهم –تكوين 1:27. وجبل الرب الإله آدم ترابًا من الأرض، ونفخ في أنفه نسمة حياة، فصار آدم نفسًا حية –تكوين 2:7.

وهب الله آدم وحواء الحياة أثناء الخلق. صاغ آدم من تراب الأرض، وصنع حواء من ضلع آدم. والله نفسه هو الذي نفخ فيهما نسمة الحياة. وفوق ذلك، طبع عليهما صورته هو.

لا يستمد البشر قيمتهم من الخدمات التي يقدمونها للآخرين، ولا تكون لهم قيمة بسبب ذكائهم أو مواهبهم. بل إن قيمة البشر تكمن في أن الله خلقهم لغرض؛ فهو يقدّر كل واحد منهم.

لأنه هكذا أحب الله العالم حتى بذل ابنه الوحيد، لكي لا يهلك كل من يؤمن به، بل تكون له الحياة الأبدية –يوحنا 3:16. يرى بعضهم أن هذه الآية أشهر مقطع في الكتاب المقدس، وهي توضح أن كل واحد منا له قيمة عند الله ومستحق لفدائه. فعبارة «كل من» تعني «كل واحد منا».

وثمة آيات كثيرة أخرى، مثل إرميا 1:4-5 ومزمور 139:13-15، تتحدث عن معرفة الله المسبقة بخلقنا. لم يخطط الله ببساطة لإدخال آدم وحواء إلى هذا العالم ثم ترك الأمور تسير من تلقاء نفسها. بل إنه يرشد تكوّن كل مولود ونموه. قد لا نفهم جميع مقاصد الله، لكن يمكننا أن نقول بيقين إن الله لا يخطئ.

نوعية الحياة

يتعلق جانب كبير من الأخلاقيات المرتبطة بقضايا نهاية الحياة بمفاهيم مثل «نوعية الحياة» و«الكرامة». وتشير نوعية الحياة إلى مدى قدرة الشخص على الاستمتاع بأنشطته اليومية المعتادة. أما الكرامة فتشير إلى شعور الناس بأنهم يحظون بقدر كافٍ من الاحترام.

يشعر كثيرون بأن هذين الأمرين — نوعية الحياة والكرامة — يتراجعان عندما يصاب المرء بمرض شديد ومُنهك. وقد يشعر المصابون بأمراض كهذه، ممن لا تربطهم علاقة شخصية بيسوع، بأنهم بلغوا مرحلة لم يعودوا فيها راغبين في مواصلة الحياة.

إن الاعتقاد بأن الحياة لا تستحق أن تُعاش إلا عندما تكون الأمور سهلة وتكون نوعية الحياة مرتفعة موقف خطير.

نحن، أتباع المسيح، ندرك أن المعاناة ستصيبنا جميعًا. ونحن نمجّد الله حين نعاني بروح وديعة وهادئة. وإضافة إلى ذلك، تعلّم معاناتنا الآخرين قوة الحياة التي غيّرها الله. لا نستطيع احتمال هذه المحن وحدنا، ولا نحتاج إلى ذلك، لأن روح الله معنا ويمنحنا القوة لنحتمل بأمانة إلى النهاية.

تسليم حياتنا إلى يدي الله

ينبغي ألا يكون المسيحيون قدريين. فنحن لا نؤمن بأننا، مهما فعلنا، سنموت حتمًا في يوم محدد سلفًا.

يبدو من المرجح أن لكل واحد منا عمرًا أقصى، لكننا نستطيع تقصيره كثيرًا باتخاذ قرارات سيئة.

قد لا يعيش طويلًا من يقود السيارة وهو ثمل، أو يتعاطى المخدرات غير المشروعة، ما لم يُصلح سلوكه. وبدرجة أقل، قد يقصّر أيضًا من يتبع نظامًا غذائيًا سيئًا ويرفض ممارسة الرياضة عمره، وقد تكون صحته أسوأ بكثير من صحة من يختار أسلوب حياة صحيًا.

إذ قدّرت أيامه، وعدد شهوره عندك، وجعلت له أجلًا لا يتجاوزه –أيوب 14:5. أيامنا في يدي الله، وليس من شأننا أن نفعل شيئًا يقصّرها عمدًا.

إحدى الوصايا العشر هي: لا تقتل – خروج 20:13. ومن المؤكد أن هذه الوصية تمنع الأطباء من تعمّد إنهاء حياة مرضاهم. كما أنها تنهى المرء عن إنهاء حياته بنفسه.

من الأفضل بكثير أن نترك أيامنا وساعاتنا بين يدي الله. وليس علينا إلا أن نخدمه بأفضل ما نستطيع في الوقت المتاح لنا. فنحن لا نختار مقدار الوقت الممنوح لنا.

نهاية الحياة

يصعب إطلاق أحكام عامة على ما يمكن أو ينبغي أن يختبره المرء في نهاية حياته. فبعض الأمراض العضال، مثل السرطان ذي النقائل العظمية، قد تسبب ألمًا شديدًا. وفي المقابل، تسبب بعض الأمراض، مثل الفشل الكلوي أو الخرف، ألمًا ضئيلًا جدًا، إن سببت ألمًا أصلًا.

يفضل بعض الناس عدم اللجوء إلى علاجات مكثفة. فالعلاج الكيميائي وغسيل الكلى وكثير من العلاجات الحديثة الأخرى لها آثار جانبية، وبعضها قد يكون سلبيًا للغاية. واختيار عدم تلقي علاج لمرض ما يختلف عن اختيار إنهاء حياتنا عمدًا.

ومن المهم أيضًا أن يكون القرار قرار الشخص نفسه، لا قرارًا يُفرض عليه. ففي السويد أثناء جائحة كوفيد، قررت الحكومة عدم علاج المقيمين المسنين في مرافق الرعاية من كوفيد. ولم يُعطَ كثيرون حتى الأكسجين، بل بدأوا ببساطة بتلقي المورفين والمهدئات «لإراحتهم» ريثما ينتظرون النهاية.

لا تتصرف بدافع الخوف

تُتخذ قرارات كثيرة عند مواجهة تشخيص بمرض عضال بدافع الخوف. فقد يخشى الناس الآثار الجانبية للأدوية أو الموت، أو يخشون ببساطة أن يكونوا عبئًا على أسرهم.

ينبغي ألا يتصرف المسيحيون بدافع كهذا. لأن الله لم يعطنا روح الفشل، بل روح القوة والمحبة والنصح –تيموثاوس الثانية 1:7.

نحن، أبناء الله، لا نخاف الموت. ثم لا أريد أن تجهلوا أيها الإخوة من جهة الراقدين، لكي لا تحزنوا كالباقين الذين لا رجاء لهم. لأنه إن كنا نؤمن أن يسوع مات وقام، فكذلك الراقدون بيسوع سيحضرهم الله أيضًا معه –تسالونيكي الأولى 4:13-14.

ندرك أن مخلّصنا قد انتصر على الموت ونزع شوكته. انتصر يسوع على الموت والقبر، لكي نعيش نحن أيضًا بلا خوف.

قد نختار الخضوع لعلاجات مكثفة، لكن دافعنا لن يكون محاولة يائسة لتأجيل الموت.

الاتكال على قوة الله

أستطيع كل شيء في المسيح الذي يقوّيني –فيلبي 4:13. تأتي هذه الآية بعد أن يتحدث الرسول بولس عن قدرته على الاكتفاء في كل حال، في أوقات الوفرة وفي أوقات العوز.

ونرى بوضوح في حياته أنه طبّق هذا الأمر. فقد تعرض للرجم والضرب وعانى من حوادث تحطم السفن. ولا بد أن جسده كان يشكو كل مساء حين يستلقي لينام، مذكرًا إياه بكل ما عاناه من مشقة وحرمان.

لم يكن الإيبوبروفين أو التايلينول ما أعانه على اجتياز تلك الأوقات (فهذه الأدوية لم تُخترع إلا بعد قرون كثيرة). بل كانت القوة التي منحته إياها علاقته بالله. وهذه القوة نفسها متاحة لنا اليوم، مهما كان ما نواجهه، حتى لو كان مرضًا عضالًا.

أدرك أن الألم مرجح

من الخيارات المتاحة للناس في نهاية الحياة قبول الرعاية التلطيفية. وهي نوع من الرعاية صُمم خصيصًا لمعالجة الألم والأعراض الأخرى، وعادةً ما يُقدّم للمريض المصاب بمرض عضال (لإراحته، لا لمحاولة شفائه). وهذا هو نوع الرعاية الذي تقدمه برامج الهوسبيس، أي برامج الرعاية التلطيفية في دور رعاية المحتضرين.

يركز الأطباء والممرضون في برامج رعاية المحتضرين أساسًا على إزالة الألم بدلًا من السعي إلى علاج المريض. ولذلك يعتمدون كثيرًا على صراحة المرضى بشأن مستويات الألم لديهم، حتى يتمكنوا من إعطائهم الجرعات التي يرون أنهم يحتاجون إليها للسيطرة على ألمهم.

وبالطبع، هذا أمر صعب. فكثيرًا ما تكون الطريقة الوحيدة لإزالة الألم تمامًا هي إعطاء الشخص جرعات كبيرة جدًا من مسكنات الألم، بحيث لا يعود قادرًا على التواصل مع من حوله. وكما هو الحال دائمًا، لا بد من تحقيق توازن بين السيطرة على الألم وبين تجنب إعطاء قدر كبير من الدواء يجعل الشخص مترنحًا ونعسانًا.

يُمجَّد الله في معاناتنا

لأن خفة ضيقتنا الوقتية تنشئ لنا أكثر فأكثر ثقل مجد أبديًا، ونحن غير ناظرين إلى الأشياء التي تُرى، بل إلى التي لا تُرى؛ لأن التي تُرى وقتية، وأما التي لا تُرى فأبدية –كورنثوس الثانية 4:17-18.

لا يستمتع أحد منا بالمعاناة، وبالتأكيد لا نسعى إليها. وعندما نعاني، يرى العالم من حولنا كيف نتعامل معها، ويمكنهم أن يلاحظوا إن كان فينا ما يميزنا.

نعلم أن يسوع عانى كثيرًا أثناء محاكمته وصلبه. وأي معاناة نمر بها ضئيلة جدًا بالمقارنة بذلك.

والأهم أن نثبت أنظارنا على مخلّصنا. فهو الذي يمنحنا القوة لنصبر إلى النهاية، وهو أمين دائمًا.

الخاتمة

العالم مكان مظلم في هذه الأيام. ويبدو أن قيمة الحياة قد تضاءلت مع مرور الوقت. فالمزيد من البلدان يسمح للأطباء بوصف أدوية تتيح للمرضى إنهاء حياتهم بأنفسهم، فيما يذهب آخرون إلى حد السماح للأطباء بإعطاء المرضى أدوية تقتلهم.

من المهم أن نواصل تقدير حياة الإنسان وأن نمجّد الله في كل ما نواجهه، حتى إن كنا نعاني مرضًا عضالًا.

إذا كنا مسؤولين عن رعاية شخص في مثل هذه الحالة، فمن المهم جدًا أن نؤكد له قيمته ونتأكد من أنه يفهم أنه ليس عبئًا. فالله يقدّر حياته، وينبغي لنا نحن أيضًا أن نقدّرها. وسيساعده هذا الدعم وهو يكافح القيود التي فرضتها حالته الصحية عليه.

لن يعيش أحد منا إلى الأبد، لكن ما نفعله هنا تترتب عليه عواقب أبدية لنا ولمن نؤثر فيهم.

The storm was dark and threatening,
Dark clouds billowed o’er head.
Lightning flashed around me,
Fears gripped and filled me with dread.

Thunder rolled out its forebodings.
My heart felt heavy and numb.
All around the storm was raging,
The turmoil inside struck me dumb.

Not only was the danger around me,
But just as real was the peril within.
I trembled as I looked at the future,
Not knowing how next to begin.

What lay behind the fog?
The wind whistled in my ears.
Suggesting questions, tripping my feet,
And ladening me down with fears.

This storm had removed all signs of the path,
That one time I had thought I could see.
Now, all the familiar was gone to my eyes,
Each step taken hesitatingly.

At the end of myself, I cried out in fear...
"Lord, come unto me! Tarry not, oh my King!"
Silence reigned heavy, I felt all alone,
Only to hope did I cling.

Then a still, but strong voice spoke in my ear,
"My precious child, look up."
Why such a request? When engulfed as I was,
In the fog that refused to break up.

Still in hope, I lifted my eyes,
Trembling at the dark clouds around.
Yet as I looked, I saw something more,
A treasure in the sky there was found.

Amidst all the dark and threatening clouds,
There it was! A cleft of light!
A rainbow shone through, of loveliest hue,
A beacon amidst this dark night.

"My child, fear not, you were never alone.
Not for a second could I leave your side.
Though the path is obscure, and there is much to endure,
Do not doubt that in Me you can hide."

"Yes, for now, you walk amidst trials,
Fears threaten both inside and out.
You wonder and question what is next to be done,
Dangers seem to laugh and flout."

"But here I have placed My rainbow,
That amidst all the darkness and fear,
You can see that My promise is certain.
I will never forsake, but always be near."

"If you keep your eyes on this promise,
My light will guide your way.
The fears and dangers surrounding,
Will then be held at bay."

"This promise can also open to you,
The secrets that are hid 'midst the storm.
For My strength and power are manifest,
When these to My will conform."

"So, My child, gaze long at the rainbow.
Ponder the message it brings.
Though all around you is angry and wild,
Remember the promise that it sings."

~by Adrianna Fanton

La tormenta era oscura y amenazante,
Nubes negras se arremolinaban sobre mí.
Los relámpagos brillaban a mi alrededor,
El temor me atrapó y me llenó de espanto.

Los truenos anunciaban malos presagios.
Sentía el corazón pesado y entumecido.
A mi alrededor, la tormenta arreciaba,
La agitación interior me dejó sin palabras.

No solo me rodeaba el peligro,
También era real el que llevaba dentro.
Temblé al mirar hacia el futuro,
Sin saber cómo seguir.

¿Qué había más allá de la niebla?
El viento silbaba en mis oídos,
Sugiriendo preguntas, haciéndome tropezar,
Y cargándome de temores.

Esta tormenta había borrado todas las señales del camino,
Que una vez pensé que podía ver.
Ahora, todo lo familiar había desaparecido de mi vista,
Y daba cada paso con vacilación.

Al llegar al límite de mis fuerzas, grité con miedo...
«¡Señor, ven a mí! ¡No tardes, oh Rey mío!»
Reinó un silencio abrumador; me sentí sin compañía,
Y solo a la esperanza me aferré.

Entonces una voz suave, pero firme, me habló al oído:
«Criatura preciosa, mira hacia arriba».
¿Por qué pedir eso, si yo estaba tan inmerso
En la niebla que se negaba a disiparse?

Aún con esperanza, alcé la mirada,
Temblando ante las nubes oscuras que me rodeaban.
Pero al mirar, vi algo más:
Allí en el cielo encontré un tesoro.

En medio de todas aquellas nubes oscuras y amenazantes,
¡Allí estaba! ¡Una abertura de luz!
Un arcoíris brillaba con los colores más hermosos,
Un faro en medio de aquella noche oscura.

«Criatura mía, no temas; nunca estuviste sin compañía.
Ni por un segundo me aparté de tu lado.
Aunque el camino sea incierto y haya mucho que soportar,
No dudes de que puedes refugiarte en Mí».

«Sí, por ahora caminas entre pruebas,
Los temores te amenazan por dentro y por fuera.
Te preguntas y dudas sobre lo que debes hacer,
Los peligros parecen reírse y desafiarte».

«Pero aquí he puesto Mi arcoíris,
Para que, en medio de toda la oscuridad y el temor,
puedas ver que Mi promesa es segura.
Nunca te abandonaré; siempre estaré cerca».

«Si mantienes la mirada fija en esta promesa,
Mi luz guiará tu camino.
Los temores y peligros que te rodean
quedarán entonces a raya».

«Esta promesa también puede revelarte
los secretos ocultos en medio de la tormenta.
Pues Mi fuerza y Mi poder se manifiestan
cuando estas cosas se someten a Mi voluntad».

«Así que, criatura mía, contempla largamente el arcoíris.
Medita en el mensaje que trae.
Aunque todo a tu alrededor sea furioso y violento,
recuerda la promesa que anuncia».

~por Adrianna Fanton

And David said, What have I now done? Is there not a cause? –1 Samuel 17:29.

The story of David and Goliath took place over three millenniums ago and has been a perennial favorite of the young and old ever since. There is something about the plight of the underdog that we all relate to. Perhaps we subconsciously view ourselves in such odds and secretly hope that there will come a day when our own “ship will come in” in a similar fashion. Unfortunately, that sort of random success seems more akin to a Hollywood production than to real life. We see only the conflict between the young and the old, the shepherd and the warrior, and the heavy military weapons and the sling. Yet there were some preliminary principles that David embraced in his youth that made him a prime candidate for success. But these often go unheralded in our love for a climactic romantic victory.

If the only vision we have of ourselves comes from the social mirror about us, we will carry a warped inner perception similar to what we see as we glance into a trick mirror at a carnival. The social opinions and perceptions of our environment often cast an awkward and skewed description of our person before our eyes and ears. Sometimes it is unrealistically positive, building the person up in the eyes of the media when there is very little heroic character displayed.

The sports arena is probably the biggest offender in this. The individuals are praised who can run, throw, or shoot better than everyone else. But sporting talent adds little to their honest pure worth as a human. The other side of the coin produces an immense amount of negative and degrading input that seeks to thwart any effort to try. These comments are produced in copious showers by stressed parents, insecure siblings, frustrated bosses, and a host of other acquaintances struggling for identity in a “survival of the fittest” society. The input from these two camps is both disjointed, and out of proportion. To be told you are great will never produce greatness any more than a barrage of derogatory remarks will produce humility. Unfortunately, too often many of us allow these disproportionate projections to affect our thinking and chart our course.

The greatest and superior endowment given to mankind over the rest of creation is not found in his physical abilities, but in his mind. The most intelligent of animals can be trained to be responsible, but they cannot choose or direct that training. But as humans, we can write new programs for ourselves totally independent of our instincts or environmental training. Those of us who live in natural accordance with our instincts and conditioning, will scarcely rise above the animal kingdom. But those who will exercise and develop those endowments shall uniquely fill the role God has designed for them in their encounter with the giants. While David’s time and position were unique, the principles he embraced were universal. If I could teach my dog to yodel, it would prove that yodeling is achievable for dogs and open the possibility for others to do it too. Likewise, if David defeated Goliath by miracle alone, then there is no hope for us but to sit and wait for God to do the same for us. However, if principles were at the core of the victory, then there is an example for us to follow and a virtue to secure for use on our own battlefield.

As David arose early that morning and shouldered his pack of corn, bread, and cheese to take to his brothers, he had no idea what the day would bring forth. The Lord was his Shepherd, and he had no lack, but as he came upon the scene he was shocked at the sight. Both armies were positioned on opposite mountains and locked in a stalemate. To take your entire army down into the valley and fight the opposition uphill would leave you at a tremendous disadvantage. One that neither side was willing to risk. So, the Philistines evoked a common dimension of warfare proposing that two warriors would fight in the valley giving no advantage to either side. But the Philistines had a giant among their numbers that terrified the army of Israel. As David inquired into the situation as to why no one would confront the reproachful blasphemies of the infidel, he was met with a stiff rebuke from his oldest brother: …and Eliab’s anger was kindled against David, and he said, Why camest thou down hither? and with whom hast thou left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart; for thou art come down that thou mightest see the battle. And David said, What have I now done? Is there not a cause? –1 Samuel 17:28-29.

Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God –Hebrews 12:2. When a man has a cause set before him, he can endure almost anything. Some endure for a corruptible crown. King Saul had offered tax exempt wealth and son-in-law status, but the earthly dowry elicited no volunteers. While the thought of earthly prominence meant nothing to the tender heart of David, there was a jealous fire kindled by the blasphemous taunts of Goliath and he stepped forward by faith. But faith is not just a whim that may be inflated by an emotional tire pump. For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works [action] is dead also –James 2:26. Thus, with the cause clearly before him, and his God beside him, David offers to fight Goliath.

So David moved forward acting according to godly, uncorrupted principles…

A Caring Conscience is seated in the soul of man and determines what we care about. Many think that a conscience is only useful as a limiting guide. But the human conscience was also created to function in the reverse. When we are convicted that something is good and right, we pursue it with a passion. Thomas Edison said that genius is 1% inspiration and 99% perspiration. While this may be true enough, it is without question that the inspiration must arrive first. Jacob’s aspirations for Rachael made him forget the seven years of labor. Edison’s pursuit of a successful light bulb caused him to forget the thousands of elements that had failed.

Careless apathy is the opposite and is the result of a seared conscience. David was amazed that the blasphemous taunts of Goliath produced no cause for action on the part of God’s army. Give a man a reason to live and he will supply the how –Nietzke. As a holocaust prisoner in a Nazi concentration camp, Victor Frankl was commissioned to labor in the ward of the camp where prisoners were dying of typhus. He observed that when a person gave up hope, death was soon to follow. Likewise, for many of our day, when the hope of personal gain evaporates in the fray, so does the passion to overcome. Most workers today are more concerned about their paycheck than of doing a good and worthy job. Often when a man loses his feelings for his wife, he believes that he is incapable of loving her, but a man with a healthy conscience toward godly principles will act in loving fashion toward her regardless of his feelings or her response. The cause is aroused and fueled by the conscience and lays the foundation for passionate action.

An Honest Imagination belongs to the realm of the spirit and is driven by our conscience. Necessity is the mother of invention –Unknown. Some are waiting for life to be discovered while others are inventing it as they go. This is not a license to claim false ideals. David’s pursuit is honest for he was not warped by the media about him. He has met with success over the beasts (a lion and a bear) in the hills of Bethlehem and with God’s help, incurs no fear of contending with one (a man of war from his youth) in the valley of Elah.

As Saul reluctantly consents to David’s proposal, he proceeds to arm the lad in typical worldly fashion. While it may have been an honor to wear the armor of the king, David would have none of it: …I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them. And David put them off him –1 Samuel 17:39, choosing five stones instead. Knowing what others do and knowing what to do are not necessarily the same thing.

The cowering beliefs of the Israelite army were rooted in a pagan value system. Goliath was not the problem, but rather, faithless fear and the assumption that they needed to engage in the warfare on the terms of the world. Those that embrace a true and worthy cause will surely find the imagination to pursue it.

Goliath had automatically assumed that he would be in combat under his own terms. Insulted and angered he cries out: …Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field –1 Samuel 17:44. As a giant, speed and agility are not his forte and so he orders David to come to him. But Goliath has grossly overestimated his personal ability and underestimated his foe. According to some estimates, at six or seven revolutions per second, David’s sling had the stopping power of a 45 mm handgun, and the hand of a skillful slinger …could sling stones at an hair breadth, and not miss –Judges 20:16. It was not unusual for them to be able to hit birds in flight. Ancient ruins have uncovered tongs that were believed to be used by the military to remove embedded stones from wounded soldiers. If Goliath had a spear and David a pistol, we would not be so quick to believe that the larger man held the major advantage.

Faithful Action is inevitable when our bodies are subject to our soul and spirit, and they are under the direction of God’s Spirit. We are then free to act independently of our nature and other influences. When the lustful passions of the mortal body hold sway over our inner heart and mind, we are defeated before we take one step toward the enemy. As vessels of God’s design, with a moral free will, we have the divine ability to choose our course of action. Some believe that being proactive is merely taking the initiative. But initiative alone will not fit us for victory any more than it did for the sons of Sceva. The desire to dominate is no more noble than Goliath’s unbridled rage to destroy this young upstart. His adrenaline flowed as he scorned David’s youth, jumped to conclusions, was easily insulted, and marveled at the ignorance of others.

But David carried no such reactive mission. His endeavor was that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel. And all this assembly shall know that the LORD saveth not with sword and spear… –1 Samuel 17:47. Faithful action must be focused on yielding what you have, rather than obtaining what you don’t. If life erects concerns outside of our ability to change, it is fruitless to give them our attention. Joseph could not change his brothers’ reception, his master’s wife’s deception, the jail’s seclusion, or the butler’s delusion. The faith of the shepherd boy teaches us to stop lamenting over what we wanna-be and start being what we oughta-be. We need to stop looking for a miracle and start looking for an opportunity. It is not about overcoming extreme odds, but rather it is how we respond to a traffic jam, a disobedient child, an irate customer, or a demanding spouse. It is about owning a cause big enough to defuse selfish reaction and incite charitable pro-action.

Why would Japanese Kamikaze pilots die for a losing cause during World War Two? Why would Muslim terrorists blow themselves up? Why do Catholic Priests and Nuns take vows of celibacy and poverty? Is there no cause for the Christian that extends broader and deeper than the giants of this world? Is there not a cause that stirs our imagination and sanctifies our action? Or isn’t there even one that transforms our mundane work into a channel of grace for the service of the King of the Universe? How would history be different if Jesse would have spent his retirement like the elders of our day? God slays giants by the instruments we yield to him, from the needle of Dorcas… to the nail of Jael, from Zebedee’s boats of the business… to the boys of his bosom.

Shamgar had an oxgoad;
David had a sling;
Dorcus had a needle;
Rahab had a string;
Samson had a jawbone;
Moses had a rod;
Mary had some ointment;
And all were used for God!

Και είπε ο Δαβίδ: «Τι έκανα τώρα; Δεν υπάρχει λόγος;» –Α΄ Σαμουήλ 17:29.

Η ιστορία του Δαβίδ και του Γολιάθ διαδραματίστηκε πριν από περισσότερες από τρεις χιλιετίες και έκτοτε παραμένει αγαπημένη ιστορία μικρών και μεγάλων. Κάτι υπάρχει στη δύσκολη θέση του αουτσάιντερ με το οποίο όλοι ταυτιζόμαστε. Ίσως ασυνείδητα βλέπουμε τον εαυτό μας σε τέτοιες πιθανότητες και κρυφά ελπίζουμε πως κάποια μέρα θα μας «έρθει η μεγάλη ευκαιρία» με παρόμοιο τρόπο. Δυστυχώς, αυτού του είδους η τυχαία επιτυχία μοιάζει περισσότερο με παραγωγή του Χόλιγουντ παρά με την πραγματική ζωή. Βλέπουμε μόνο τη σύγκρουση ανάμεσα στον νέο και τον ηλικιωμένο, τον βοσκό και τον πολεμιστή, τα βαριά πολεμικά όπλα και τη σφεντόνα. Ωστόσο, υπήρχαν ορισμένες προκαταρκτικές αρχές που ενστερνίστηκε ο Δαβίδ στα νιάτα του, οι οποίες τον κατέστησαν ιδανικό υποψήφιο για επιτυχία. Όμως αυτές συχνά μένουν στην αφάνεια, καθώς αγαπάμε τη ρομαντική νίκη της κορύφωσης.

Αν η μόνη εικόνα που έχουμε για τον εαυτό μας προέρχεται από τον κοινωνικό καθρέφτη γύρω μας, θα αποκτήσουμε μια παραμορφωμένη εσωτερική αντίληψη, παρόμοια με εκείνη που βλέπουμε όταν κοιτάζουμε σε έναν παραμορφωτικό καθρέφτη σε πανηγύρι. Οι κοινωνικές γνώμες και αντιλήψεις του περιβάλλοντός μας συχνά παρουσιάζουν μπροστά στα μάτια και στα αυτιά μας μια αδέξια και στρεβλή περιγραφή του προσώπου μας. Μερικές φορές η εικόνα είναι εξωπραγματικά θετική, εξυψώνοντας το άτομο στα μάτια των μέσων ενημέρωσης, ενώ επιδεικνύει ελάχιστο ηρωικό χαρακτήρα.

Ο αθλητικός στίβος είναι μάλλον ο μεγαλύτερος παραβάτης σε αυτό. Επαινούνται όσοι μπορούν να τρέχουν, να ρίχνουν ή να σουτάρουν καλύτερα από όλους τους άλλους. Όμως το αθλητικό ταλέντο προσθέτει ελάχιστα στην αληθινή, καθαρή αξία τους ως ανθρώπων. Η άλλη όψη του νομίσματος παράγει τεράστιο όγκο αρνητικών και εξευτελιστικών σχολίων που αποσκοπούν στο να ματαιώσουν κάθε προσπάθεια. Τέτοια σχόλια πέφτουν βροχή από αγχωμένους γονείς, ανασφαλή αδέλφια, απογοητευμένους προϊσταμένους και πλήθος άλλων γνωστών που πασχίζουν να βρουν την ταυτότητά τους σε μια κοινωνία «επιβίωσης του ισχυρότερου». Τα μηνύματα αυτών των δύο στρατοπέδων είναι ασύνδετα και δυσανάλογα. Το να σου λένε ότι είσαι σπουδαίος δεν θα σε κάνει ποτέ σπουδαίο, όπως ακριβώς και ένας καταιγισμός υποτιμητικών σχολίων δεν θα σε κάνει ταπεινό. Δυστυχώς, πολύ συχνά πολλοί από εμάς αφήνουμε αυτές τις δυσανάλογες προβολές να επηρεάζουν τη σκέψη μας και να χαράζουν την πορεία μας.

Το μεγαλύτερο και ανώτερο χάρισμα που δόθηκε στο ανθρώπινο γένος σε σχέση με την υπόλοιπη δημιουργία δεν βρίσκεται στις σωματικές του ικανότητες, αλλά στον νου του. Τα πιο έξυπνα ζώα μπορούν να εκπαιδευτούν ώστε να είναι υπεύθυνα, αλλά δεν μπορούν να επιλέξουν ή να κατευθύνουν αυτή την εκπαίδευση. Εμείς όμως, ως άνθρωποι, μπορούμε να γράψουμε νέα προγράμματα για τον εαυτό μας, εντελώς ανεξάρτητα από τα ένστικτά μας ή την εκπαίδευση που μας διαμόρφωσε το περιβάλλον. Όσοι ζούμε σε φυσική συμφωνία με τα ένστικτα και την εξαρτημένη συμπεριφορά μας, δύσκολα θα ξεπεράσουμε το ζωικό βασίλειο. Όσοι όμως ασκήσουν και αναπτύξουν αυτά τα χαρίσματα, θα εκπληρώσουν μοναδικά τον ρόλο που τους έχει σχεδιάσει ο Θεός όταν βρεθούν αντιμέτωποι με τους γίγαντες. Ο χρόνος και η θέση του Δαβίδ ήταν μοναδικά, αλλά οι αρχές που ενστερνίστηκε ήταν καθολικές. Αν μπορούσα να μάθω στον σκύλο μου να γιουκαλίζει, αυτό θα αποδείκνυε πως οι σκύλοι μπορούν να μάθουν να γιουκαλίζουν και θα άνοιγε τον δρόμο και για άλλους. Παρόμοια, αν ο Δαβίδ νίκησε τον Γολιάθ μόνο με θαύμα, τότε δεν υπάρχει ελπίδα για εμάς παρά να καθίσουμε και να περιμένουμε να κάνει ο Θεός το ίδιο για εμάς. Αν όμως στον πυρήνα της νίκης βρίσκονταν αρχές, τότε έχουμε ένα παράδειγμα προς μίμηση και μια αρετή που μπορούμε να αποκτήσουμε για να τη χρησιμοποιήσουμε στο δικό μας πεδίο μάχης.

Όταν ο Δαβίδ σηκώθηκε νωρίς εκείνο το πρωί και φόρτωσε στους ώμους του το σακί με σιτηρά, ψωμί και τυρί για να τα πάει στους αδελφούς του, δεν είχε ιδέα τι θα έφερνε η μέρα. Ο Κύριος ήταν ο Ποιμένας του και δεν του έλειπε τίποτα, αλλά όταν έφτασε στο σημείο, έμεινε έκπληκτος με αυτό που αντίκρισε. Και οι δύο στρατοί είχαν παραταχθεί σε απέναντι βουνά και βρίσκονταν σε αδιέξοδο. Αν κατέβαζες ολόκληρο τον στρατό σου στην κοιλάδα και πολεμούσες τον αντίπαλο από χαμηλότερη θέση, θα βρισκόσουν σε τεράστιο μειονέκτημα. Κανένα από τα δύο μέρη δεν ήταν διατεθειμένο να διακινδυνεύσει κάτι τέτοιο. Έτσι, οι Φιλισταίοι πρότειναν μια συνηθισμένη τακτική πολέμου: δύο πολεμιστές να αναμετρηθούν στην κοιλάδα, χωρίς να έχει πλεονέκτημα καμία πλευρά. Όμως ανάμεσα στους Φιλισταίους υπήρχε ένας γίγαντας που τρομοκρατούσε τον στρατό του Ισραήλ. Όταν ο Δαβίδ ρώτησε γιατί κανείς δεν αντιμετώπιζε τους υβριστικούς βλασφημισμούς του απίστου, δέχτηκε την αυστηρή επίπληξη του μεγαλύτερου αδελφού του: …και άναψε ο θυμός του Ελιάβ εναντίον του Δαβίδ, και είπε: Γιατί κατέβηκες εδώ; Και σε ποιον άφησες εκείνα τα λίγα πρόβατα στην έρημο; Ξέρω την υπερηφάνειά σου και την κακία της καρδιάς σου· κατέβηκες για να δεις τη μάχη. Και είπε ο Δαβίδ: Τι έκανα τώρα; Δεν υπάρχει λόγος; –Α΄ Σαμουήλ 17:28-29.

Ατενίζοντας στον Ιησού, τον αρχηγό και τελειωτή της πίστης μας· ο οποίος, για τη χαρά που είχε μπροστά του, υπέμεινε σταυρό, καταφρονώντας την ντροπή, και κάθισε στα δεξιά του θρόνου του Θεού –Εβραίους 12:2. Όταν ο άνθρωπος έχει μπροστά του έναν σκοπό, μπορεί να υπομείνει σχεδόν τα πάντα. Κάποιοι υπομένουν για ένα φθαρτό στεφάνι. Ο βασιλιάς Σαούλ είχε προσφέρει αφορολόγητο πλούτο και την ιδιότητα του γαμπρού του, όμως η επίγεια προίκα δεν προσέλκυσε κανέναν εθελοντή. Ενώ η σκέψη της επίγειας προβολής δεν σήμαινε τίποτα για την ευαίσθητη καρδιά του Δαβίδ, οι βλάσφημες προκλήσεις του Γολιάθ άναψαν μέσα του τη φωτιά του ζήλου κι εκείνος προχώρησε με πίστη. Η πίστη όμως δεν είναι απλώς μια παρόρμηση που μπορεί να φουσκώσει με μια συναισθηματική τρόμπα. Επειδή, όπως το σώμα χωρίς το πνεύμα είναι νεκρό, έτσι και η πίστη χωρίς έργα [δράση] είναι νεκρή –Ιακώβου 2:26. Έτσι, με τον σκοπό ξεκάθαρο μπροστά του και τον Θεό στο πλευρό του, ο Δαβίδ προσφέρεται να πολεμήσει τον Γολιάθ.

Έτσι, ο Δαβίδ προχώρησε ενεργώντας σύμφωνα με θεοσεβείς, αδιάφθορους κανόνες…

Συνείδηση που νοιάζεται κατοικεί στην ψυχή του ανθρώπου και καθορίζει για τι νοιαζόμαστε. Πολλοί πιστεύουν ότι η συνείδηση χρησιμεύει μόνο ως περιοριστικός οδηγός. Όμως η ανθρώπινη συνείδηση δημιουργήθηκε και για να λειτουργεί αντίστροφα. Όταν έχουμε πειστεί ότι κάτι είναι καλό και σωστό, το επιδιώκουμε με πάθος. Ο Τόμας Έντισον είπε ότι η ιδιοφυΐα είναι 1% έμπνευση και 99% ιδρώτας. Αυτό μπορεί να είναι αρκετά αληθινό, αλλά είναι αναμφισβήτητο ότι πρώτα πρέπει να έρθει η έμπνευση. Οι φιλοδοξίες του Ιακώβ για τη Ραχήλ τον έκαναν να ξεχάσει τα επτά χρόνια δουλειάς. Η επιδίωξη του Έντισον να φτιάξει έναν λειτουργικό λαμπτήρα τον έκανε να ξεχάσει τα χιλιάδες υλικά που είχαν αποτύχει.

Η απρόσεκτη απάθεια είναι το αντίθετο και αποτελεί αποτέλεσμα μιας καυτηριασμένης συνείδησης. Ο Δαβίδ απορούσε που οι βλάσφημες προκλήσεις του Γολιάθ δεν αποτελούσαν λόγο για δράση από την πλευρά του στρατού του Θεού. Δώσε σε έναν άνθρωπο έναν λόγο για να ζήσει και θα βρει το πώς –Νίτσκε. Ως κρατούμενος του Ολοκαυτώματος σε ναζιστικό στρατόπεδο συγκέντρωσης, ο Βίκτορ Φρανκλ ανέλαβε να εργάζεται στον θάλαμο του στρατοπέδου όπου πέθαιναν από τύφο οι κρατούμενοι. Παρατήρησε πως όταν κάποιος έχανε την ελπίδα του, σύντομα ακολουθούσε ο θάνατος. Παρόμοια, για πολλούς ανθρώπους της εποχής μας, όταν στη μάχη εξαφανίζεται η ελπίδα προσωπικού κέρδους, εξαφανίζεται και το πάθος για υπέρβαση. Οι περισσότεροι εργαζόμενοι σήμερα νοιάζονται περισσότερο για τον μισθό τους παρά για το αν κάνουν καλή και αξιόλογη δουλειά. Συχνά, όταν ένας άντρας χάνει τα αισθήματά του για τη γυναίκα του, πιστεύει ότι δεν είναι ικανός να την αγαπήσει· όμως ο άντρας με υγιή συνείδηση προσανατολισμένη σε θεοσεβείς αρχές θα ενεργεί με αγάπη απέναντί της, ανεξάρτητα από τα αισθήματά του ή την ανταπόκρισή της. Η συνείδηση αφυπνίζει και τροφοδοτεί τον σκοπό, θέτοντας τα θεμέλια για δράση με πάθος.

Ειλικρινής φαντασία ανήκει στη σφαίρα του πνεύματος και καθοδηγείται από τη συνείδησή μας. Η ανάγκη είναι η μητέρα της εφεύρεσης –Άγνωστος. Κάποιοι περιμένουν να ανακαλυφθεί η ζωή, ενώ άλλοι τη δημιουργούν καθώς προχωρούν. Αυτό δεν αποτελεί άδεια για να διεκδικούμε ψεύτικα ιδανικά. Η επιδίωξη του Δαβίδ είναι ειλικρινής, γιατί δεν είχε διαμορφωθεί στρεβλά από τα μέσα ενημέρωσης γύρω του. Είχε επιτύχει απέναντι στα θηρία (ένα λιοντάρι και μια αρκούδα) στους λόφους της Βηθλεέμ και, με τη βοήθεια του Θεού, δεν φοβάται να αναμετρηθεί με έναν άντρα πολεμιστή από τα νιάτα του στην κοιλάδα Ηλά.

Καθώς ο Σαούλ δέχεται απρόθυμα την πρόταση του Δαβίδ, προχωρά να οπλίσει το παλικάρι με τον συνηθισμένο κοσμικό τρόπο. Μπορεί να ήταν τιμή να φορέσει την πανοπλία του βασιλιά, αλλά ο Δαβίδ δεν ήθελε να έχει καμία σχέση μ’ αυτήν: …δεν μπορώ να πάω με αυτά, επειδή δεν τα έχω δοκιμάσει. Και ο Δαβίδ τα έβγαλε από πάνω του –Α΄ Σαμουήλ 17:39, και διάλεξε αντί γι’ αυτά πέντε πέτρες. Το να γνωρίζεις τι κάνουν οι άλλοι και το να γνωρίζεις τι πρέπει να κάνεις δεν είναι κατ’ ανάγκην το ίδιο.

Οι δειλές πεποιθήσεις του στρατού του Ισραήλ είχαν τις ρίζες τους σε ένα ειδωλολατρικό σύστημα αξιών. Το πρόβλημα δεν ήταν ο Γολιάθ, αλλά ο άπιστος φόβος και η υπόθεση πως έπρεπε να πολεμήσουν με τους όρους του κόσμου. Όσοι ενστερνίζονται έναν αληθινό και αξιόλογο σκοπό ασφαλώς θα βρουν τη φαντασία να τον επιδιώξουν.

Ο Γολιάθ είχε θεωρήσει αυτονόητο ότι θα πολεμούσε με τους δικούς του όρους. Προσβεβλημένος και οργισμένος, φώναξε: …Έλα σε μένα, και θα δώσω τη σάρκα σου στα πουλιά του ουρανού και στα θηρία του αγρού –Α΄ Σαμουήλ 17:44. Ως γίγαντας, δεν διακρινόταν για την ταχύτητα και την ευκινησία του, γι’ αυτό διέταξε τον Δαβίδ να έρθει κοντά του. Όμως ο Γολιάθ είχε υπερεκτιμήσει κατά πολύ τις προσωπικές του ικανότητες και υποτιμήσει τον αντίπαλό του. Σύμφωνα με ορισμένες εκτιμήσεις, με έξι ή επτά περιστροφές το δευτερόλεπτο, η σφεντόνα του Δαβίδ είχε ανασχετική δύναμη αντίστοιχη με πιστόλι διαμετρήματος .45, ενώ το χέρι ενός επιδέξιου σφενδονιστή …μπορούσε να ρίχνει πέτρες σε απόσταση μιας τρίχας χωρίς να αστοχεί –Κριτές 20:16. Δεν ήταν ασυνήθιστο να μπορούν να πετυχαίνουν πουλιά εν πτήσει. Σε αρχαία ερείπια έχουν βρεθεί λαβίδες που πιστεύεται ότι χρησιμοποιούσε ο στρατός για να αφαιρεί σφηνωμένες πέτρες από τραυματισμένους στρατιώτες. Αν ο Γολιάθ είχε δόρυ και ο Δαβίδ πιστόλι, δεν θα βιαζόμασταν τόσο να πιστέψουμε ότι ο μεγαλόσωμος άντρας είχε το μεγαλύτερο πλεονέκτημα.

Πιστή δράση είναι αναπόφευκτη όταν το σώμα μας υποτάσσεται στην ψυχή και στο πνεύμα μας και αυτά καθοδηγούνται από το Πνεύμα του Θεού. Τότε είμαστε ελεύθεροι να ενεργούμε ανεξάρτητα από τη φύση μας και άλλες επιρροές. Όταν τα ακόλαστα πάθη του θνητού σώματος κυριαρχούν στην εσώτερη καρδιά και στον νου μας, είμαστε ηττημένοι προτού κάνουμε έστω ένα βήμα προς τον εχθρό. Ως σκεύη σχεδιασμένα από τον Θεό, με ηθική ελεύθερη βούληση, έχουμε τη θεϊκή ικανότητα να επιλέγουμε την πορεία των πράξεών μας. Μερικοί πιστεύουν ότι το να αναλαμβάνεις δράση προληπτικά σημαίνει απλώς να παίρνεις την πρωτοβουλία. Όμως η πρωτοβουλία από μόνη της δεν θα μας προετοιμάσει για τη νίκη, όπως δεν το έκανε ούτε για τους γιους του Σκευά. Η επιθυμία για κυριαρχία δεν είναι ευγενέστερη από την ασυγκράτητη οργή του Γολιάθ να καταστρέψει αυτόν τον νεαρό ανερχόμενο. Η αδρεναλίνη του Γολιάθ κυλούσε καθώς περιφρονούσε τα νιάτα του Δαβίδ, έβγαζε βιαστικά συμπεράσματα, προσβαλλόταν εύκολα και θαύμαζε την άγνοια του Δαβίδ.

Ο Δαβίδ όμως δεν είχε τέτοια αντιδραστική αποστολή. Σκοπός του ήταν να μάθει όλη η γη ότι υπάρχει Θεός στον Ισραήλ. Και όλη αυτή η σύναξη θα μάθει ότι ο ΚΥΡΙΟΣ δεν σώζει με σπαθί και δόρυ… –Α΄ Σαμουήλ 17:47. Η πιστή δράση πρέπει να επικεντρώνεται στο να προσφέρεις ό,τι έχεις, όχι στο να αποκτάς ό,τι δεν έχεις. Αν η ζωή εγείρει ζητήματα πέρα από την ικανότητά μας να τα αλλάξουμε, είναι μάταιο να τους δίνουμε την προσοχή μας. Ο Ιωσήφ δεν μπορούσε να αλλάξει την υποδοχή που του επιφύλαξαν τα αδέλφια του, την εξαπάτηση της γυναίκας του κυρίου του, τον εγκλεισμό στη φυλακή ή την αυταπάτη του οινοχόου. Η πίστη του νεαρού βοσκού μάς διδάσκει να σταματήσουμε να θρηνούμε για αυτό που θα θέλαμε να είμαστε και να αρχίσουμε να είμαστε αυτό που οφείλουμε να είμαστε. Χρειάζεται να πάψουμε να αναζητούμε ένα θαύμα και να αρχίσουμε να αναζητούμε μια ευκαιρία. Το ζήτημα δεν είναι να ξεπεράσουμε ακραίες αντιξοότητες, αλλά το πώς ανταποκρινόμαστε σε ένα μποτιλιάρισμα, ένα ανυπάκουο παιδί, έναν έξαλλο πελάτη ή έναν απαιτητικό σύζυγο. Το ζήτημα είναι να αναλάβουμε έναν σκοπό αρκετά μεγάλο ώστε να εκτονώνει τις εγωιστικές αντιδράσεις και να πυροδοτεί ανιδιοτελή, ενεργητική δράση.

Γιατί οι Ιάπωνες πιλότοι καμικάζι πέθαιναν για έναν χαμένο σκοπό κατά τον Β΄ Παγκόσμιο Πόλεμο; Γιατί οι μουσουλμάνοι τρομοκράτες ανατινάζονται; Γιατί οι καθολικοί ιερείς και οι μοναχές δίνουν όρκους αγαμίας και φτώχειας; Δεν υπάρχει για τον χριστιανό κάποιος σκοπός ευρύτερος και βαθύτερος από τους γίγαντες αυτού του κόσμου; Δεν υπάρχει κάποιος σκοπός που να διεγείρει τη φαντασία μας και να αγιάζει τη δράση μας; Ή μήπως δεν υπάρχει ούτε ένας που να μεταμορφώνει την καθημερινή εργασία μας σε αγωγό χάρης, για την υπηρεσία του Βασιλιά του Σύμπαντος; Πόσο διαφορετική θα ήταν η ιστορία αν ο Ιεσσαί περνούσε τα χρόνια της σύνταξής του όπως οι ηλικιωμένοι της εποχής μας; Ο Θεός καταβάλλει γίγαντες με τα εργαλεία που του προσφέρουμε: από τη βελόνα της Δορκάδας… ως το καρφί της Ιαήλ, από τις βάρκες της επιχείρησης του Ζεβεδαίου… ως τα αγόρια της αγκαλιάς του.

Ο Σαμγάρ είχε βουκέντρα·
Ο Δαβίδ είχε σφεντόνα·
Η Δορκάδα είχε βελόνα·
Η Ραάβ είχε ένα σκοινί·
Ο Σαμψών είχε σαγόνι γαϊδάρου·
Ο Μωυσής είχε ράβδο·
Η Μαρία είχε μύρο·
Και όλα χρησιμοποιήθηκαν για τον Θεό!

The storm was dark and threatening,
Dark clouds billowed o’er head.
Lightning flashed around me,
Fears gripped and filled me with dread.

Thunder rolled out its forebodings.
My heart felt heavy and numb.
All around the storm was raging,
The turmoil inside struck me dumb.

Not only was the danger around me,
But just as real was the peril within.
I trembled as I looked at the future,
Not knowing how next to begin.

What lay behind the fog?
The wind whistled in my ears.
Suggesting questions, tripping my feet,
And ladening me down with fears.

This storm had removed all signs of the path,
That one time I had thought I could see.
Now, all the familiar was gone to my eyes,
Each step taken hesitatingly.

At the end of myself, I cried out in fear...
"Lord, come unto me! Tarry not, oh my King!"
Silence reigned heavy, I felt all alone,
Only to hope did I cling.

Then a still, but strong voice spoke in my ear,
"My precious child, look up."
Why such a request? When engulfed as I was,
In the fog that refused to break up.

Still in hope, I lifted my eyes,
Trembling at the dark clouds around.
Yet as I looked, I saw something more,
A treasure in the sky there was found.

Amidst all the dark and threatening clouds,
There it was! A cleft of light!
A rainbow shone through, of loveliest hue,
A beacon amidst this dark night.

"My child, fear not, you were never alone.
Not for a second could I leave your side.
Though the path is obscure, and there is much to endure,
Do not doubt that in Me you can hide."

"Yes, for now, you walk amidst trials,
Fears threaten both inside and out.
You wonder and question what is next to be done,
Dangers seem to laugh and flout."

"But here I have placed My rainbow,
That amidst all the darkness and fear,
You can see that My promise is certain.
I will never forsake, but always be near."

"If you keep your eyes on this promise,
My light will guide your way.
The fears and dangers surrounding,
Will then be held at bay."

"This promise can also open to you,
The secrets that are hid 'midst the storm.
For My strength and power are manifest,
When these to My will conform."

"So, My child, gaze long at the rainbow.
Ponder the message it brings.
Though all around you is angry and wild,
Remember the promise that it sings."

~by Adrianna Fanton

तूफ़ान अँधेरा और भयावह था,
सिर पर काले बादल उमड़ते थे।
बिजली मेरे चारों ओर चमकती थी,
भय ने मुझे जकड़ लिया, आतंक से भर दिया।

गड़गड़ाहट ने अनिष्ट की आहट सुनाई।
मेरा हृदय भारी और सुन्न-सा था।
चारों ओर तूफ़ान प्रचंड था,
भीतर की उथल-पुथल ने मुझे अवाक् कर दिया।

खतरा केवल मेरे चारों ओर ही नहीं था,
भीतर का संकट भी उतना ही वास्तविक था।
भविष्य की ओर देखते हुए मैं काँप उठा,
यह जाने बिना कि अब शुरुआत कैसे करूँ।

धुंध के पीछे क्या था?
हवा मेरे कानों में सीटी बजाती थी।
सवाल सुझाती, मेरे कदम लड़खड़ाती,
और भय से मुझे बोझिल करती थी।

इस तूफ़ान ने पथ के सारे निशान मिटा दिए थे,
जिसे कभी मैंने सोचा था कि देख सकता हूँ।
अब मेरी आँखों से हर जानी-पहचानी चीज़ ओझल थी,
हर कदम हिचकिचाते हुए उठता था।

जब मैं पूरी तरह असहाय हो गया, तो भय से पुकार उठा...
"हे प्रभु, मेरे पास आ! देर न कर, हे मेरे राजा!"
भारी सन्नाटा छा गया, मैंने स्वयं को बिल्कुल अकेला पाया,
बस आशा का ही सहारा थामे रहा।

तभी एक शांत, पर दृढ़ स्वर मेरे कानों में बोला,
"मेरे अनमोल बच्चे, ऊपर देखो।"
ऐसी विनती क्यों? जब मैं इस तरह डूबा हुआ था,
उस धुंध में, जो छँटने का नाम नहीं लेती थी।

फिर भी आशा से, मैंने आँखें उठाईं,
चारों ओर के काले बादलों से काँपते हुए।
फिर भी जब मैंने देखा, तो कुछ और दिखाई दिया,
आकाश में एक ख़ज़ाना मिला।

उन तमाम अँधेरे और भयावह बादलों के बीच,
वहाँ वह था! प्रकाश की एक दरार!
मनोहर रंगों का इंद्रधनुष चमका,
इस अँधेरी रात में एक प्रकाश-स्तंभ।

"मेरे बच्चे, मत डर, तू कभी अकेला नहीं था।
एक पल के लिए भी मैं तेरा साथ नहीं छोड़ सकता था।
चाहे राह धुँधली हो और बहुत कुछ सहना पड़े,
संदेह मत कर, तू मुझमें शरण पा सकता है।"

"हाँ, अभी तू परीक्षाओं के बीच चल रहा है,
भय भीतर और बाहर, दोनों ओर से धमकाते हैं।
तू सोचता और पूछता है कि आगे क्या करना है,
ख़तरे मानो हँसते और तेरा उपहास करते हैं।"

"पर मैंने यहाँ अपना इंद्रधनुष रखा है,
ताकि सारे अँधेरे और भय के बीच,
तू देख सके कि मेरी प्रतिज्ञा अटल है।
मैं तुझे कभी नहीं त्यागूँगा, सदा पास रहूँगा।"

"यदि तू अपनी नज़र इस प्रतिज्ञा पर टिकाए रखे,
तो मेरा प्रकाश तेरी राह दिखाएगा।
चारों ओर मंडराते भय और ख़तरे,
तब दूर ही रोके रखे जाएँगे।"

"यह प्रतिज्ञा तेरे लिए खोल भी सकती है,
तूफ़ान के बीच छिपे रहस्यों को।
क्योंकि मेरी सामर्थ्य और शक्ति प्रकट होती है,
जब ये मेरी इच्छा के अनुरूप होते हैं।"

"इसलिए, मेरे बच्चे, इंद्रधनुष को देर तक निहार।
उसके लाए संदेश पर मनन कर।
चाहे तेरे चारों ओर सब कुछ उग्र और विकराल हो,
उस प्रतिज्ञा को याद रख, जिसका वह गान करता है।"

~एड्रियाना फ़ैन्टन द्वारा

In October of 2020, a 90-year-old woman named Nancy Russell, who was a resident of a nursing home in Toronto, Canada, expressed a desire to have a doctor help her kill herself. She felt that the isolation of the previous several months was more than she could endure, and she saw no end to it.

Nancy Russell did not have dementia. She did not have any condition that would normally be considered terminal. However, in Canada, it is not necessary to have a terminal condition to ask for help to go through with physician-assisted suicide. Canada calls this procedure “Medical Assistance in Dying” (MAID). The name implies that it is about comfort care, but the reality is that it is anything but comfort care.

A geriatrician heard her story and agreed to help her. She was discharged to spend the next week with her family. At the end of that time, she was given a lethal injection with her family present. This is not an isolated case. In 2020 there were 7,595 people who killed themselves with a doctor’s assistance.

As I consider these sobering statistics, I feel a great sadness. There is a sense in which many families abandon their elderly or ill family members. COVID has only seemed to worsen this problem. An even larger issue is that our society no longer values the lives of older individuals.

A society that no longer values all human lives as important, begins to allow things like physician-assisted suicide, and even euthanasia. Euthanasia is when someone administers medication to another person for the purpose of killing that other person, while assisted suicide is when one person provides medication to another person that they then “self ”-administer, thereby killing themselves.

It is helpful to review how we, as Christians, approach end-of-life situations and try to understand where the world around us has gone so terribly wrong.

Made in the Image of God

So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them –Genesis 1:27. And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul –Genesis 2:7.

God put the life into Adam and Eve during Creation. He molded Adam from the dust of the earth and made Eve from Adam’s rib. It was God Himself who breathed into them the breath of life. More than that, He stamped on them His own image.

Humans do not have value because of services they do for others. They are not worth something because of their intelligence or talents. Rather, humans have value because God created them for a purpose. He values each one of them.

For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life –John 3:16. Considered by some as the most well-known passage of Scripture, this verse makes it clear that every single one of us is valuable to God and worthy of His redemption. Whosoever means “every one of us”.

There are many other verses like Jeremiah 1:4-5 and Psalm 139:13-15 that speak of God’s foreknowledge in our creation. God didn’t simply plan to bring Adam and Eve into this world and then let things go on their own from that point. Instead, He guides the conception and development of each one who is born. We may not understand all of God’s purposes, but we can say with certainty that God does not make mistakes.

Quality of Life

Much of the ethics surrounding end-of-life issues has to do with concepts like “quality of life” and “dignity”. Quality of life is the extent to which someone can enjoy their normal, everyday activities. Dignity refers to people feeling that they are being given adequate levels of respect.

Many people feel that both of these things—quality of life and dignity—decline when someone gets a severe and debilitating illness. Those with such illnesses who do not have a personal relationship with Jesus may feel that they have reached the point where they don’t want to continue living.

It is a dangerous position when people believe that lives are only worth living when things are easy and when the quality of life is high.

We, as followers of Christ, understand that suffering will come to all of us. It brings glory to God when we suffer with a meek and quiet spirit. More than that, it teaches other people the power of a God-transformed life. We cannot bear these trials alone. And we don’t need to because God’s Spirit is with us and gives us the strength to endure faithfully until the end.

Leaving Our Lives in God’s Hands

Christians should not be fatalistic. We do not believe that regardless of what we do, we are certain to die on a pre-determined day.

It seems likely that, while there is a maximum life span for each one of us, we can shorten that considerably through poor decisions.

Someone who drives while intoxicated, or who uses street drugs, may not have a long life, unless they mend their ways. To a lesser extent, someone who eats poorly and refuses to exercise may also shorten his lifespan and have considerably worse health than someone who chooses a healthy lifestyle.

Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months are with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass –Job 14:5. Our days are in God’s hands. It is not our place to do something to deliberately shorten them.

One of the Ten Commandments is: Thou shalt not kill – Exodus 20:13. Certainly this command would forbid doctors from purposely taking the life of their patient. It would also be a command against someone ending their own life.

It is far better if we can leave our days and hours in God’s hands. We have but to serve Him the best we can with what time we have. We do not get to choose the amount of time that is allotted to us.

End of Life

It is difficult to make sweeping statements about what someone can or should experience at the end of their life. Some terminal illnesses, like cancer with bony metastases, can cause large amounts of pain. On the other hand, some diseases, like kidney failure or dementia, cause very little pain, if any.

Some people would rather not pursue aggressive treatments. Chemotherapy, dialysis, and many other modern treatments have side effects, some of which can be quite negative. Choosing not to take treatment for a disease is different from choosing to actively end our lives.

It is also important that it should be an individual person’s own decision and not one that is foisted on them. In Sweden during COVID, the government made the decision that elderly residents of nursing facilities would not be treated for COVID. Many were not even given oxygen, but simply started on Morphine and sedatives to “make them comfortable” as they waited for the end.

Do Not Act in Fear

Many of the decisions that people make as they face a terminal diagnosis are made out of fear. They may be fearful of medication side effects, fearful of death, or simply fearful of being a burden to families.

Christians should not act out of such motivations. For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind –2 Timothy 1:7.

As God’s children, we are not afraid of death. But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope. For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him –1 Thessalonians 4:13-14.

We understand that our Savior has had victory over death and that he has taken away its sting. Jesus won a victory over death and the grave, so that we too can live without fear.

We may choose to take aggressive treatments, but we won’t be motivated by a desperate attempt to stave off death.

Rely On God’s Strength

I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me –Philippians 4:13. This verse comes after the Apostle Paul spends time talking about how he is able to be content in any situation, both in times of plenty and in times of need.

We see clearly in his life that he put this very thing into practice. He experienced stonings, beatings, and shipwreck. One needs to believe that his body complained every evening when he would lie down to sleep, telling him of all the privations it had suffered.

It wasn’t ibuprofen or Tylenol that got him through these times (those wouldn’t be invented for many centuries). Rather, it was the strength which his relationship with God gave him. That same strength is available to us today, no matter what we are facing, even a terminal illness.

Understand that There Will Likely be Pain

One of the choices that people can make at the end of life is to accept palliative care. This is a type of care that is specifically designed to treat the pain and other symptoms, usually of a terminally ill patient (to keep them comfortable, not to try to cure them). This is the sort of care that is offered by hospice programs.

The doctors and nurses in hospice programs are focused primarily on eliminating pain rather than seeking a cure for the individual. Consequently, they rely very much on patients being honest about their pain levels so they can give the doses that patients feel that they need to control their pain.

Of course, this is challenging. Many times, the only way to completely eliminate pain is for a person to be so heavily medicated with pain medication that they are not able to relate to the people around them. As always, there needs to be some balance between controlling the pain and not having so much medicine that the individual is groggy and sleepy.

God is Glorified in Our Suffering

For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory; While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal –2 Corinthians 4:17-18.

None of us enjoys suffering and we certainly do not seek it out. When we go through suffering, the world around us sees how we deal with it, and they can tell if there is something different about us.

We know that Jesus suffered much during His trial and crucifixion. Whatever suffering we go through is tiny compared with that.

Most important is that we keep our eyes on our Savior. He is the one that gives us strength to endure to the end. He is always faithful.

Conclusion

The world is a dark place these days. The value of life seems to have diminished over time. More and more countries are allowing doctors to prescribe medications that allow patients to end their own lives, while others go so far as to even allow doctors to administer medications that will kill their patients.

It is important that we continue to value human life and that we glorify God in everything we face—even if we are dealing with a terminal illness.

If we are responsible for caring for someone in this situation, it is very important that we affirm their value and make certain that they understand that they are not a burden. God values their lives and so should we. This support will help them as they struggle with the limitations that their health has put upon them.

None of us will live forever, but the things we do here have eternal consequences for us and for those we influence.

In Oktober 2020 het ’n 90-jarige vrou met die naam Nancy Russell, ’n inwoner van ’n ouetehuis in Toronto, Kanada, die begeerte uitgespreek dat ’n dokter haar help om haar eie lewe te beëindig. Sy het gevoel dat die afsondering van die vorige paar maande meer was as wat sy kon verduur, en sy het geen einde daaraan in sig gesien nie.

Nancy Russell het nie demensie gehad nie. Sy het geen toestand gehad wat normaalweg as terminaal beskou sou word nie. In Kanada is dit egter nie nodig om ’n terminale toestand te hê om hulp te vra om selfdood met behulp van ’n geneesheer te pleeg nie. Kanada noem hierdie prosedure “Mediese Bystand by Sterwe” (MAID). Die naam laat dit klink asof dit oor vertroostende sorg gaan, maar in werklikheid is dit allesbehalwe vertroostende sorg.

’n Geriater het haar verhaal aangehoor en ingestem om haar te help. Sy is ontslaan om die volgende week saam met haar familie deur te bring. Aan die einde van daardie tyd is ’n dodelike inspuiting aan haar toegedien in die teenwoordigheid van haar familie. Dit is nie ’n geïsoleerde geval nie. In 2020 was daar 7 595 mense wat met die hulp van ’n dokter selfmoord gepleeg het.

Wanneer ek hierdie ontstellende statistieke oorweeg, voel ek groot hartseer. In ’n sekere sin laat vaar baie gesinne hul bejaarde of siek familielede. Dit lyk asof COVID hierdie probleem net vererger het. ’n Nog groter probleem is dat ons samelewing nie meer waarde heg aan die lewens van ouer mense nie.

’n Samelewing wat nie meer alle menselewens as belangrik beskou nie, begin dinge soos selfdood met behulp van ’n geneesheer, en selfs genadedood, toelaat. Genadedood is wanneer iemand medikasie aan ’n ander persoon toedien met die doel om daardie persoon dood te maak, terwyl selfdood met hulp plaasvind wanneer een persoon medikasie aan ’n ander persoon verskaf wat dit dan self toedien, en daardeur sy of haar eie lewe beëindig.

Dit is nuttig om na te dink oor hoe ons as Christene situasies aan die einde van die lewe benader en te probeer verstaan waar die wêreld om ons so verskriklik verkeerd geloop het.

Na die beeld van God geskape

Toe het God die mens geskape na sy beeld; na die beeld van God het Hy hom geskape; man en vrou het Hy hulle geskape –Genesis 1:27. En die HERE God het die mens geformeer uit die stof van die aarde en in sy neus die asem van die lewe geblaas. So het die mens ’n lewende siel geword –Genesis 2:7.

God het tydens die Skepping lewe in Adam en Eva geplaas. Hy het Adam uit die stof van die aarde gevorm en Eva uit Adam se rib gemaak. Dit was God self wat die asem van die lewe in hulle geblaas het. Meer nog, Hy het sy eie beeld op hulle afgedruk.

Mense het nie waarde omdat hulle dienste aan ander lewer nie. Hulle is nie iets werd vanweë hul intelligensie of talente nie. Mense het eerder waarde omdat God hulle met ’n doel geskape het. Hy heg waarde aan elkeen van hulle.

Want so lief het God die wêreld gehad, dat Hy sy eniggebore Seun gegee het, sodat elkeen wat in Hom glo, nie verlore mag gaan nie, maar die ewige lewe kan hê –Johannes 3:16. Hierdie vers, wat deur sommige as die bekendste Skrifgedeelte beskou word, maak dit duidelik dat elkeen van ons vir God waardevol is en sy verlossing waardig is. “Elkeen” beteken “elkeen van ons”.

Daar is baie ander verse, soos Jeremia 1:4-5 en Psalm 139:13-15, wat oor God se voorkennis in ons skepping praat. God het nie bloot beplan om Adam en Eva in hierdie wêreld te bring en toe alles van daar af op sy eie te laat verloop nie. Hy lei eerder die bevrugting en ontwikkeling van elkeen wat gebore word. Ons verstaan dalk nie al God se doelwitte nie, maar ons kan met sekerheid sê dat God nie foute maak nie.

Lewensgehalte

Baie van die etiek rondom kwessies aan die einde van die lewe het te doen met begrippe soos “lewensgehalte” en “waardigheid”. Lewensgehalte is die mate waarin iemand sy of haar gewone, alledaagse aktiwiteite kan geniet. Waardigheid verwys na mense se gevoel dat hulle met voldoende respek behandel word.

Baie mense voel dat albei hierdie dinge—lewensgehalte en waardigheid—afneem wanneer iemand ’n ernstige, aftakelende siekte kry. Mense met sulke siektes wat nie ’n persoonlike verhouding met Jesus het nie, voel dalk dat hulle die punt bereik het waar hulle nie meer wil aanhou lewe nie.

Dit is ’n gevaarlike standpunt wanneer mense glo dat ’n lewe slegs die moeite werd is om te leef wanneer dinge maklik is en die lewensgehalte hoog is.

Ons, as volgelinge van Christus, verstaan dat lyding oor ons almal sal kom. Dit bring heerlikheid aan God wanneer ons met ’n sagmoedige en stille gees ly. Meer nog, dit leer ander mense die krag van ’n lewe wat deur God verander is. Ons kan hierdie beproewings nie alleen dra nie. En ons hoef nie, want God se Gees is met ons en gee ons die krag om getrou tot die einde toe te volhard.

Ons lewens in God se hande laat

Christene behoort nie fatalisties te wees nie. Ons glo nie dat ons beslis op ’n voorafbepaalde dag sal sterf, ongeag wat ons doen nie.

Dit lyk waarskynlik dat daar, hoewel elkeen van ons ’n maksimum lewensduur het, ons dit aansienlik kan verkort deur swak besluite.

Iemand wat bestuur terwyl hy dronk is, of straatdwelms gebruik, sal dalk nie lank lewe nie, tensy hy sy lewe verander. In ’n mindere mate kan iemand wat swak eet en weier om te oefen ook sy lewensduur verkort en aansienlik swakker gesondheid hê as iemand wat ’n gesonde leefstyl kies.

Aangesien sy dae bepaal is, die getal van sy maande by U is, en U vir hom ’n grens gestel het wat hy nie kan oorskry nie –Job 14:5. Ons dae is in God se hande. Dit is nie ons plek om iets te doen om hulle doelbewus te verkort nie.

Een van die Tien Gebooie lui: Jy mag nie doodslaan nie – Eksodus 20:13. Hierdie gebod sou dokters beslis verbied om hul pasiënte doelbewus dood te maak. Dit sou ook ’n gebod wees teen iemand wat sy of haar eie lewe beëindig.

Dit is veel beter as ons ons dae en ure in God se hande laat. Ons hoef Hom net na die beste van ons vermoë te dien met die tyd wat ons het. Ons kan nie kies hoeveel tyd aan ons toegeken word nie.

Die einde van die lewe

Dit is moeilik om algemene stellings te maak oor wat iemand aan die einde van sy of haar lewe kan of behoort te ervaar. Sommige terminale siektes, soos kanker met beenmetastases, kan baie pyn veroorsaak. Aan die ander kant veroorsaak sommige siektes, soos nierversaking of demensie, baie min pyn, indien enige.

Sommige mense verkies om nie aggressiewe behandelings te ondergaan nie. Chemoterapie, dialise en baie ander moderne behandelings het newe-effekte, waarvan sommige baie negatief kan wees. Om te kies om nie behandeling vir ’n siekte te ontvang nie, is iets anders as om te kies om aktief ons lewens te beëindig.

Dit is ook belangrik dat dit die betrokke persoon se eie besluit moet wees en nie iets wat op hulle afgedwing word nie. In Swede het die regering tydens COVID besluit dat bejaarde inwoners van versorgingsoorde nie vir COVID behandel sou word nie. Baie het nie eens suurstof gekry nie, maar is bloot op morfien en kalmeermiddels gesit om hulle “gemaklik te laat voel” terwyl hulle op die einde gewag het.

Moenie uit vrees optree nie

Baie van die besluite wat mense neem wanneer hulle ’n terminale diagnose in die gesig staar, word uit vrees geneem. Hulle is dalk bang vir die newe-effekte van medikasie, bang vir die dood, of bloot bang om ’n las vir hul gesinne te wees.

Christene behoort nie deur sulke beweegredes gelei te word nie. Want God het ons nie ’n gees van vreesagtigheid gegee nie, maar van krag en liefde en selfbeheersing –2 Timoteus 1:7.

As God se kinders is ons nie bang vir die dood nie. Maar, broeders, ek wil nie hê dat julle onkundig moet wees met betrekking tot die ontslapenes nie, sodat julle nie treur soos die ander wat geen hoop het nie. Want as ons glo dat Jesus gesterf en opgestaan het, dan sal God ook so die ontslapenes in Jesus saam met Hom bring –1 Tessalonisense 4:13-14.

Ons verstaan dat ons Verlosser die oorwinning oor die dood behaal het en die angel daarvan weggeneem het. Jesus het die oorwinning oor die dood en die graf behaal, sodat ons ook sonder vrees kan lewe.

Ons kan kies om aggressiewe behandelings te ondergaan, maar ons sal nie deur ’n desperate poging om die dood af te weer gemotiveer word nie.

Steun op God se krag

Ek is tot alles in staat deur Christus wat my krag gee –Filippense 4:13. Hierdie vers volg nadat die apostel Paulus ’n ruk lank praat oor hoe hy in enige situasie tevrede kan wees, sowel in tye van oorvloed as in tye van gebrek.

Ons sien duidelik in sy lewe dat hy hierdie beginsel in die praktyk toegepas het. Hy het stenigings, slae en ’n skipbreuk beleef. ’n Mens moet aanneem dat sy liggaam elke aand gekla het wanneer hy gaan lê het om te slaap en hom herinner het aan al die ontberings wat dit moes verduur.

Dit was nie ibuprofen of Tylenol wat hom deur hierdie tye gehelp het nie (dit sou eers baie eeue later uitgevind word). Dit was eerder die krag wat sy verhouding met God hom gegee het. Dieselfde krag is vandag vir ons beskikbaar, ongeag waarmee ons te doen kry, selfs ’n terminale siekte.

Besef dat daar waarskynlik pyn sal wees

Een van die keuses wat mense aan die einde van die lewe kan maak, is om palliatiewe sorg te aanvaar. Dit is ’n soort sorg wat spesifiek daarop gemik is om pyn en ander simptome te behandel, gewoonlik by ’n terminaal siek pasiënt (om die pasiënt gemaklik te hou, nie om hom of haar te probeer genees nie). Dit is die soort sorg wat hospiessorgprogramme bied.

Die dokters en verpleegkundiges in hospiessorgprogramme fokus hoofsaaklik daarop om pyn uit te skakel eerder as om ’n geneesmiddel vir die individu te soek. Gevolglik maak hulle sterk staat daarop dat pasiënte eerlik oor hul pynvlakke is, sodat hulle die dosisse kan gee wat pasiënte meen hulle nodig het om hul pyn te beheer.

Dit is natuurlik ’n uitdaging. Dikwels is die enigste manier om pyn heeltemal uit te skakel dat iemand so sterk met pynmedikasie gedoseer word dat hy of sy nie meer met die mense rondom hom of haar kan kommunikeer nie. Soos altyd moet daar ’n mate van balans wees tussen die beheer van die pyn en die vermyding van soveel medisyne dat die persoon lomerig en slaperig is.

God word verheerlik in ons lyding

Want ons ligte verdrukking, wat net vir ’n oomblik is, bewerk vir ons ’n allesoortreffende, ewige gewig van heerlikheid; omdat ons nie let op die sigbare dinge nie, maar op die onsigbare; want die sigbare dinge is tydelik, maar die onsigbare ewig –2 Korintiërs 4:17-18.

Nie een van ons geniet lyding nie, en ons soek dit beslis nie op nie. Wanneer ons lyding deurmaak, sien die wêreld om ons hoe ons dit hanteer, en hulle kan agterkom of daar iets anders aan ons is.

Ons weet dat Jesus baie gely het tydens sy verhoor en kruisiging. Enige lyding waardeur ons gaan, is gering in vergelyking daarmee.

Die belangrikste is dat ons ons oë op ons Verlosser hou. Hy is die Een wat ons krag gee om tot die einde toe te volhard. Hy is altyd getrou.

Ten slotte

Die wêreld is deesdae ’n donker plek. Dit lyk asof die waarde van die lewe mettertyd afgeneem het. Al hoe meer lande laat dokters toe om medikasie voor te skryf waarmee pasiënte hul eie lewe kan beëindig, terwyl ander selfs so ver gaan om dokters toe te laat om medikasie toe te dien wat hul pasiënte sal doodmaak.

Dit is belangrik dat ons voortgaan om menselewens waardevol te ag en God te verheerlik in alles waarmee ons te doen kry—selfs al het ons met ’n terminale siekte te doen.

As ons verantwoordelik is vir die versorging van iemand in hierdie situasie, is dit baie belangrik dat ons hul waarde bevestig en seker maak dat hulle verstaan dat hulle nie ’n las is nie. God heg waarde aan hul lewens, en ons behoort dit ook te doen. Hierdie ondersteuning sal hulle help terwyl hulle worstel met die beperkings wat hul gesondheid op hulle geplaas het.

Nie een van ons sal vir ewig lewe nie, maar die dinge wat ons hier doen, het ewige gevolge vir ons en vir diegene op wie ons invloed het.

While the earth remaineth, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease –Genesis 8:22. Greetings to one and all. As I am writing this, it is the beginning of May and yet in our area it still seems as though spring has not yet quite arrived. There are glimmers of hope that summer surely will come—some of the trees are pushing their leaves and select early flowers have pushed their blossoms up to wave bravely in the cool, damp breezes. Yet, overall, the weather seems to feel much more like the month of March.

This coming week has the promise of warm, dry weather, which should make many area farmers and homeowners happy. We are anticipating a great bevy of activity as gardens and fields are tilled and seeded with this year’s crops. To those who read the Holy Scriptures and who believe the written Word of God, these normal day-to-day activities should be a reminder of God’s promises in the same way as each new sighting of a rainbow.

And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet. For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places –Matthew 24:6-7.

And there shall be … pestilences … in divers places

In February or March of 2020, COVID-19 was declared a pandemic (a disease that spreads rapidly and affects a large percentage of the population). Now, over two years later, health officials and government leaders are somewhat reticent to publicly declare that the crisis has passed.

Some parts of the world have lifted all regulations regarding COVID-19 such as Denmark and England, while others such as New Zealand are still quite rigid with their ongoing rules and guidelines. And quite recently Chinese officials again locked down certain areas of their country in their efforts to quash a recent outbreak of new infections.

Many, if not most, individuals are tired of it all, ready for it to be over, and anxious to get back to life as normal. Many have lost loved ones. Many have endured financial setbacks and economic loss. Recent data from the World Health Organization (WHO) provides the approximate deaths (both direct and indirect) from COVID-19 to be around 15 million for the first two years of the pandemic.

While recent data from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimates that the median global GDP dropped by 3.9% from 2019 to 2020, making it the worst economic downturn since the Great Depression, creating a global recession that is the deepest since the end of World War 2.

Recently, a brother mentioned to me that “the world is in a mess” and that he has heard realtors, auctioneers, and financial advisors say that the world of finance is in unprecedented waters and that no one knows where, when, or how it will all end.

However, we should not be surprised by this major worldwide struggle. The Scriptures foretell of famine and hunger, pestilence and death, plagues of all varieties, and the list goes on of things that will come upon the earth just prior to the end of time: …for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet –Matthew 24:6.

And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars

In recent years there have been numerous wars and rumors of wars. However, since February 24, 2022 when Russia launched its current full-scale invasion of Ukraine, there have been increased worries voiced by media and politicians about how this seems different. With the many sanctions enacted by the EU and the west, there have been ripple effects causing negative outcomes for many of the world’s economies, with sky-rocketing prices for many items and services being the outcome. Sure, there were high prices before this recent outbreak of war which was a result of the various supply chain problems that were caused by COVID-19 and its ripple effects. But since the sanctions were enacted against Russia the gas and oil prices have risen noticeably which in turn has caused the cost of most goods and services to follow suit.

What about all the what if ’s…? If this happens then “there will be a nuclear war.” If this happens then “it will cause World War 3 to begin.” “The Democrats are taking the U.S. to war with Russia.” These and many more comments are being made in our world today. To me it seems that when countries and individuals …trust in chariots, and some in horses: Psalm 20:7a, then their outcome will be that They are brought down and [are] fallen… –Psalm 20:8a. But if …we will remember the name of the LORD our God –Psalm 20:7b, then …we are risen, and [will] stand upright –Psalm 20:8b.

From my perspective it seems that many in the world have allowed fear to take root in their hearts during the whole COVID-19 ordeal. Now whenever some new “scary” development surfaces in this current Russia/Ukraine conflict and the many issues connected to it, again fear seems to be the prevailing motivator. This gives us a glimpse of what things will be like some day soon when: Men’s hearts [are] failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken –Luke 21:26. Because …those men which have not the seal of God in their foreheads … should be tormented five months … and shall desire to die, and death shall flee from them –Revelation 9:4-6. Also, there will come a day when …the kings of the earth, and the great men, and the rich men, and the chief captains, and the mighty men, and every bondman, and every free man, [will hide] themselves in the dens and in the rocks of the mountains; And [will say] to the mountains and rocks, Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb: For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand? –Revelation 6:15-17.

The worth of a soul

Then said Jesus unto his disciples, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me. For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it. For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul? –Matthew 16:24-26.

Recently, this verse came to my mind as I was thinking of a number of situations in our world today—both close to home and abroad.

First, that which is abroad…

I am one of those who enjoys relaxing on the porch of a house, which is located along a major highway, and watching the traffic. I also find it interesting to sit in an airport or bus terminal and observe the masses of people passing by. Many times, I have paused to consider that each one has a soul that will spend all of eternity somewhere! Alive! As I’ve pondered these thoughts, some further thoughts also come. “How many of these people have a personal awareness of eternity?” “Of life after death?” “Or of a God who is alive, sovereign, and holy who will some day require an accounting for all things done in this earthly body?”

How many of us bear a burden for the lost souls around us? I think of the testimony of a vehicle mechanic who told me how he prays and seeks the Lord’s leading about how he can speak into the lives of those who come to his shop. And of his further testimony regarding the various ways that God has led and folks have been pointed to a Living God and a life after death.

For many of us, for me in particular, it takes an effort to remember to stop and smell the roses or to pause and reflect on the beauty of a sunrise. Then it takes a further step to remember the Creator behind these earthly beauties. How much more can we become lulled into the sameness of our everyday lives and tend to forget that each soul we meet will someday stand before God? What if we were the one who God wanted to say a word for Him out of a life that was living for Him to bring His awareness to one who knows not the One, Living, and True God?

Now for that which is close…

This can take on many different situations. It can be those in our family. It can be our neighbors. It can be our more distant relatives. It can be our work associates. Finally, it can be anyone who we interact with in our daily lives.

Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me. Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee? or thirsty, and gave thee drink? When saw we thee a stranger, and took thee in? or naked, and clothed thee? Or when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came unto thee? And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me –Matthew 25:34-40.

One specific thing that I wish to focus on is this growing problem of broken relationships and emotional/mental struggles within the plain communities. I do not wish to pass judgment on anyone, nor do I wish to make anyone feel bad. In fact, one of my strongest concerns regarding these issues is that the church would do everything that it can to take away the stigma or negativity of these struggles. How did Christ relate to those who were in these types of situations? We could get hung up on the details of how Jesus responded. Let’s not allow details to hinder us from “being Christ” to these struggling individuals in our midst.

To bring perspective to how we approach and interact with someone who is struggling, we can ask ourselves several questions that will help. First a question for myself: “How would I appreciate someone responding to me if I was in that specific situation?” Second a question for the other person: “What can I do that would be a help or an encouragement to you as you are going through this difficult experience?”

Too many times, the church doesn’t have time for those who are struggling in their midst, since it is their lot in life and we are too busy to be bothered. Other times, the church doesn’t know how to respond or what to say so they decide it is better to “leave sleeping dogs lie” or that it would be best to not “open that can of worms”.

God designed us in such a way that we need our brothers and sisters. Just consider all the “one-anothering” passages in the Scriptures. Then consider how we can “be Christ” to the struggling among us. Just remember that there may come a time when “the shoe is on the other foot”, so to speak. In other words, someday we may find ourselves in a similar situation wishing that our brothers and sisters would rally around us with love and encouragement in a real way that “helps”.

Resources

It has been a while since we have reminded our readers that we have select resources on a variety of topics to assist churches and individuals as they seek a practical way forward that is pleasing to God. One resource, that is specific on the topic of how to help those in our midst, is an 8 CD set we put together titled “People Helping in the Local Church”. We have received feedback from many individuals and church leaders who have said that they found the information shared in this set to be very helpful in their efforts to understand how to “help” challenging situations in their midst.

Our resources are available free of charge to addresses located within the U.S. However, we are funded solely on the free-will offerings of God’s people, so your donation would be helpful to continue our work. If you wish to receive one or more of these CD sets, please contact our ministry using the contact information listed inside the front cover of this magazine.
