Enquanto a terra durar, não deixará de haver semeadura e colheita, frio e calor, verão e inverno, dia e noite –Gênesis 8:22. Saudações a todos. Enquanto escrevo, estamos no início de maio e, ainda assim, em nossa região parece que a primavera ainda não chegou por completo. Há alguns sinais de esperança de que o verão certamente virá — algumas árvores estão começando a brotar folhas, e certas flores precoces já abriram suas flores para balançar bravamente na brisa fria e úmida. No geral, porém, o clima parece muito mais com o mês de março.

A próxima semana promete tempo quente e seco, o que deve deixar felizes muitos agricultores e moradores da região. Esperamos uma grande movimentação, com jardins e campos sendo arados e semeados com as plantações deste ano. Para aqueles que leem as Sagradas Escrituras e creem na Palavra escrita de Deus, essas atividades cotidianas normais deveriam servir de lembrete das promessas de Deus, assim como cada novo arco-íris que avistamos.

E ouvireis falar de guerras e rumores de guerras; vede que não vos perturbeis, porque é necessário que todas essas coisas aconteçam, mas ainda não é o fim. Porquanto se levantará nação contra nação, e reino contra reino; e haverá fomes, pestes e terremotos em vários lugares –Mateus 24:6-7.

E haverá … pestes … em vários lugares

Em fevereiro ou março de 2020, a COVID-19 foi declarada uma pandemia (uma doença que se espalha rapidamente e afeta uma grande porcentagem da população). Agora, mais de dois anos depois, autoridades de saúde e líderes governamentais mostram certa relutância em declarar publicamente que a crise passou.

Algumas partes do mundo suspenderam todas as regulamentações relativas à COVID-19, como a Dinamarca e a Inglaterra, enquanto outras, como a Nova Zelândia, ainda mantêm regras e diretrizes bastante rígidas. E, muito recentemente, autoridades chinesas voltaram a impor confinamentos em certas áreas do país, na tentativa de conter um novo surto de infecções.

Muitas pessoas, se não a maioria, estão cansadas de tudo isso, prontas para que acabe e ansiosas para voltar à vida normal. Muitos perderam entes queridos. Muitos sofreram reveses financeiros e perdas econômicas. Dados recentes da Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS) estimam em cerca de 15 milhões o número de mortes (diretas e indiretas) causadas pela COVID-19 nos dois primeiros anos da pandemia.

Ao mesmo tempo, dados recentes do Fundo Monetário Internacional (FMI) estimam que o PIB global mediano caiu 3,9% entre 2019 e 2020, tornando essa a pior retração econômica desde a Grande Depressão e criando uma recessão global que é a mais profunda desde o fim da Segunda Guerra Mundial.

Recentemente, um irmão me disse que “o mundo está uma confusão” e que ouviu corretores de imóveis, leiloeiros e consultores financeiros dizerem que o mundo das finanças se encontra em águas nunca antes navegadas e que ninguém sabe onde, quando ou como tudo isso terminará.

No entanto, não deveríamos nos surpreender com essa grande luta mundial. As Escrituras predizem fome e escassez, pestilência e morte, pragas de todo tipo, e a lista de coisas que sobrevirão à terra pouco antes do fim dos tempos continua: …porque é necessário que todas essas coisas aconteçam, mas ainda não é o fim –Mateus 24:6.

E ouvireis falar de guerras e rumores de guerras

Nos últimos anos, houve inúmeras guerras e rumores de guerras. No entanto, desde 24 de fevereiro de 2022, quando a Rússia lançou sua atual invasão em grande escala da Ucrânia, a mídia e os políticos têm manifestado preocupações crescentes, dizendo que essa situação parece diferente. Com as muitas sanções impostas pela UE e pelo Ocidente, houve efeitos em cadeia que provocaram consequências negativas para muitas economias do mundo, resultando em aumentos vertiginosos nos preços de muitos produtos e serviços. É verdade que os preços já estavam altos antes desse recente início da guerra, em consequência dos diversos problemas nas cadeias de abastecimento causados pela COVID-19 e seus efeitos em cadeia. Mas, desde que as sanções contra a Rússia foram impostas, os preços do gás e do petróleo aumentaram consideravelmente, o que, por sua vez, levou ao aumento dos preços da maioria dos bens e serviços.

E todas as hipóteses…? Se isto acontecer, “haverá uma guerra nuclear”. Se aquilo acontecer, “isso dará início à Terceira Guerra Mundial”. “Os democratas estão levando os EUA a uma guerra com a Rússia.” Esses e muitos outros comentários estão sendo feitos no mundo de hoje. Parece-me que, quando países e indivíduos …confiam em carros, e alguns em cavalos: Salmo 20:7a, o resultado será que eles são derrubados e caem… –Salmo 20:8a. Mas, se …nos lembrarmos do nome do SENHOR, nosso Deus –Salmo 20:7b, então …nos levantamos e ficaremos de pé –Salmo 20:8b.

Do meu ponto de vista, parece que muitos no mundo permitiram que o medo criasse raízes em seu coração durante toda a provação da COVID-19. Agora, sempre que surge algum novo acontecimento “assustador” no atual conflito entre Rússia e Ucrânia e nas muitas questões a ele relacionadas, o medo parece voltar a ser o principal fator motivador. Isso nos dá um vislumbre de como as coisas serão algum dia, em breve, quando: os corações dos homens desfalecerão de medo, na expectativa das coisas que sobrevirão ao mundo, pois os poderes dos céus serão abalados –Lucas 21:26. Porque …aqueles homens que não têm o selo de Deus na testa … seriam atormentados durante cinco meses … e desejarão morrer, mas a morte fugirá deles –Apocalipse 9:4-6. Também chegará o dia em que …os reis da terra, os grandes, os ricos, os comandantes, os poderosos, todo escravo e todo livre [se esconderão] nas cavernas e entre as rochas das montanhas; e [dirão] às montanhas e às rochas: Caí sobre nós e escondei-nos da face daquele que está sentado no trono e da ira do Cordeiro, porque chegou o grande dia da ira dele; e quem poderá subsistir? –Apocalipse 6:15-17.

O valor de uma alma

Então Jesus disse aos seus discípulos: Se alguém quer vir após mim, negue-se a si mesmo, tome a sua cruz e siga-me. Pois quem quiser salvar a sua vida a perderá; e quem perder a sua vida por minha causa a encontrará. Pois que proveito terá alguém se ganhar o mundo inteiro e perder a própria alma? Ou o que alguém poderá dar em troca da sua alma? –Mateus 16:24-26.

Recentemente, esse versículo me veio à mente enquanto pensava em várias situações do mundo de hoje — tanto perto de casa quanto no exterior.

Primeiro, aquilo que acontece no exterior…

Sou uma daquelas pessoas que gostam de relaxar na varanda de uma casa situada junto a uma rodovia movimentada e observar o trânsito. Também acho interessante sentar em um aeroporto ou terminal rodoviário e observar as multidões passando. Muitas vezes, parei para pensar que cada uma dessas pessoas tem uma alma que passará toda a eternidade em algum lugar! Viva! Ao refletir sobre isso, também me ocorrem algumas outras perguntas: “Quantas dessas pessoas têm consciência pessoal da eternidade?” “Da vida após a morte?” “Ou de um Deus vivo, soberano e santo, que algum dia exigirá uma prestação de contas por tudo o que foi feito neste corpo terreno?”

Quantos de nós carregamos um fardo pelas almas perdidas ao nosso redor? Penso no testemunho de um mecânico de automóveis que me contou como ora e busca a orientação do Senhor sobre como pode falar à vida das pessoas que vão à sua oficina. E penso também em seu testemunho sobre as diversas maneiras pelas quais Deus o tem guiado e levado pessoas a conhecer o Deus vivo e a vida após a morte.

Para muitos de nós, e para mim em particular, é preciso esforço para lembrar de parar e sentir o perfume das rosas ou fazer uma pausa para contemplar a beleza do nascer do sol. Depois, é preciso dar mais um passo para lembrar do Criador por trás dessas belezas terrenas. Quanto mais facilmente podemos nos deixar embalar pela rotina de nossa vida cotidiana e acabar esquecendo que cada alma que encontramos um dia estará diante de Deus? E se fôssemos nós a pessoa que Deus queria usar para dizer uma palavra em seu favor, por meio de uma vida vivida para Ele, a fim de despertar a consciência daquele que não conhece o Deus único, vivo e verdadeiro?

Agora, aquilo que está perto…

Isso pode envolver muitas situações diferentes. Podem ser pessoas da nossa família. Podem ser nossos vizinhos. Podem ser parentes mais distantes. Podem ser nossos colegas de trabalho. Por fim, pode ser qualquer pessoa com quem interagimos em nosso dia a dia.

Então o Rei dirá aos que estiverem à sua direita: Vinde, benditos de meu Pai! Herdai o reino que vos está preparado desde a fundação do mundo. Pois tive fome, e me destes de comer; tive sede, e me destes de beber; era estrangeiro, e me acolhestes; estava nu, e me vestistes; adoeci, e me visitastes; estive na prisão, e fostes visitar-me. Então os justos lhe responderão: Senhor, quando te vimos com fome e te demos de comer? Ou com sede e te demos de beber? Quando te vimos estrangeiro e te acolhemos? Ou nu e te vestimos? E quando te vimos doente ou na prisão e fomos visitar-te? E o Rei lhes responderá: Em verdade vos digo que, quando o fizestes a um destes meus irmãos, ainda que dos mais pequeninos, a mim o fizestes –Mateus 25:34-40.

Uma questão específica em que desejo me concentrar é o crescente problema de relacionamentos rompidos e dificuldades emocionais e mentais nas comunidades tradicionais. Não quero julgar ninguém, nem quero fazer com que alguém se sinta mal. Na verdade, uma de minhas maiores preocupações a respeito dessas questões é que a igreja faça tudo o que puder para eliminar o estigma ou a conotação negativa associados a essas dificuldades. Como Cristo se relacionava com aqueles que passavam por situações desse tipo? Poderíamos nos prender aos detalhes de como Jesus respondeu. Não permitamos que os detalhes nos impeçam de “ser Cristo” para essas pessoas que enfrentam dificuldades entre nós.

Para termos uma perspectiva de como abordar e interagir com alguém que está passando por dificuldades, podemos fazer a nós mesmos algumas perguntas que serão úteis. Primeiro, uma pergunta para mim: “Como eu gostaria que alguém reagisse comigo se eu estivesse naquela situação específica?” Segundo, uma pergunta para a outra pessoa: “O que posso fazer para ajudar você ou encorajar você enquanto passa por essa experiência difícil?”

Muitas vezes, a igreja não tem tempo para aqueles que estão passando por dificuldades em seu meio, porque essa é a situação que lhes cabe na vida, e nós estamos ocupados demais para nos incomodar. Outras vezes, a igreja não sabe como reagir ou o que dizer e, por isso, decide que é melhor “deixar quieto” ou que seria melhor não “abrir essa caixa de Pandora”.

Deus nos criou de tal maneira que precisamos de nossos irmãos e irmãs. Basta considerar todas as passagens das Escrituras que falam sobre o que devemos fazer uns pelos outros. Depois, pensemos em como podemos “ser Cristo” para aqueles que enfrentam dificuldades entre nós. Lembremo-nos apenas de que pode chegar o momento em que “o jogo vira”, por assim dizer. Em outras palavras, algum dia poderemos nos encontrar em uma situação semelhante, desejando que nossos irmãos e irmãs se unam ao nosso redor com amor e encorajamento, de maneira concreta e que “ajude”.

Recursos

Faz algum tempo que não lembramos nossos leitores de que temos recursos selecionados sobre diversos temas para ajudar igrejas e pessoas a buscar um caminho prático que agrade a Deus. Um desses recursos, que trata especificamente de como ajudar aqueles que estão entre nós, é um conjunto de 8 CDs que preparamos, intitulado “Pessoas ajudando na igreja local”. Recebemos comentários de muitas pessoas e líderes de igrejas que disseram ter considerado muito úteis as informações compartilhadas nesse conjunto, em seus esforços para entender como “ajudar” em situações difíceis entre eles.

Nossos recursos estão disponíveis gratuitamente para endereços nos EUA. No entanto, nosso trabalho é financiado exclusivamente por ofertas voluntárias do povo de Deus, por isso sua doação seria útil para que pudéssemos continuar nosso trabalho. Se desejar receber um ou mais desses conjuntos de CDs, entre em contato com nosso ministério usando as informações de contato indicadas na parte interna da capa desta revista.

Ora, àquele que é poderoso para vos guardar de tropeçar e para vos apresentar irrepreensíveis, com grande alegria, diante da sua glória, ao único Deus sábio, nosso Salvador, sejam glória e majestade, domínio e poder, agora e para todo o sempre. Amém. – Judas 1:24-25.

Pride is something that everyone must deal with. It is something that naturally tends to come into our lives and stay. Like many other things, it is very deceitful, because it is commonly accepted by the world in which we live. People today are proud of being proud. Americans are proud of their country, their jobs, their children, their lawns, their sports teams, their vehicles, their ambitions, their goals, their looks, their friends, their homes, and the list could go on. If we think about it, the carnal man is proud of just about anything. People stand and proclaim they are proud and boast of their great accomplishments. People look at something someone has done and proclaim to the doer, “You should be proud of yourself!”

There is one problem; God hates pride! God actually despises the proud. In Psalms, it says that God will cut off …the tongue that speaketh proud things –Psalm 12:3. And in Job it says He will …behold every one that is proud, and abase [put down or make low] him –Job 40:11. Psalms 40:4 says He will not respect the proud and in Psalm 119: Thou hast rebuked the proud that are cursed, which do err from thy commandments –Psalm 119:21. In Proverbs, we read that: The LORD will destroy the house of the proud… –Proverbs 15:25, and that Every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to the LORD… –Proverbs 16:5. In Malachi, it says that …behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud… –Malachi 4:1. Finally, James states that …God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble –James 4:6.

As we can see, the Bible is very clear on pride, and the people who are proud. There is no room for pride in our hearts or lives. So, what do we do with this? Are we proud? Do we boast as the world does?

I would like to call attention to a hidden form of pride that can slip into our lives, sometimes unnoticed. We will call it false humility. If we have a false humility, would it not actually be a form of pride?

Let us look first at Law and Grace. Someone that is under the law does not desire to do what he must do, but rather, he does it because of the law. For example, the law states that we should not kill, yet (according to the law) we are allowed to be angry. Someone can hate another and even desire to kill him, but if they resist the temptation to kill, they have indeed kept the law. Many people today who claim to be Christians, are actually under the law. They do all that they do because of a law, or an order from their authority. We can see this clearly when people push the law, doing the least that is required, but still technically keeping the law.

The head covering is a good example. A woman who desires to cover her head because of what the Bible teaches, will indeed cover her head. She does not need to be reminded to do it or be admonished for doing it half-heartedly. On the other hand, there are Christians that cover their heads; however, the actual covering continues to get smaller, and less noticeable. Some even put it all the way on the back of the head and color it the same as their hair, trying to keep it from being noticed by the uncovered public. This clearly reveals the heart; they are simply complying with the law.

This type of thinking can go for many things. One more would be adornment. The bible says that the adornment should not be outward. Many Christians will not adorn themselves with flashy eye-catching things, however there are no standards about adorning homes, vehicles, and such like. So, a plain, unadorned person gets out of their adorned vehicle and walks into their very adorned home. This shows where the heart is—under the law.

Now let us look at grace. It is the power of God in the life of a human being. It causes one to actually love their enemies, to do good to those who mistreat them. It causes one to love their God with all their heart and obey God’s commands because of a passionate love for Him. The law is no longer needed because the heart is new; it desires to live for God. When someone does evil to you, you do not think about getting even. In fact, you do not even get angry. You are a new creature and because of this power—grace from God—you love him that has done you wrong. Forgiving is not a problem; helping others is natural. You are not your own and you desire to be all you can be for your Savior who died for you.

What does this have to do with pride or humility?

The Bible says that …the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ –John 1:17. It does not take God’s Spirit in our lives for us to obey the law—we can do that on our own. Therefore, we can become proud by doing things for God because WE did them. When we did not allow our anger to spew out when disagreeing with a neighbor, we think well of ourselves, and we can become proud. However, when we actually love our neighbor that has a problem with us, we cannot become proud because it was grace; it was the power of God that caused this, not ourselves. Therefore, we marvel at God and his abundant grace.

It would be foolish for someone to be proud of something that God clearly did! If Lazarus walked around boasting of himself for being raised from the dead, people would question his sanity, saying, “You did nothing! It was Jesus that did everything.”

I’m not trying to say that the Christian does nothing. No, we must humbly obey the commandments of God and walk in His ways. However, I am saying that we cannot boast in ourselves because it is God that enables us to obey His commandments.

Let us look at the popular story of David and Goliath. David went to the army to take provisions to his brothers who were fighting there. As he approached, he marveled at what he saw, a large man challenging his people! David seemed a bit shocked, and aggrieved as he asked, …who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God? –1 Samuel 17:26.

What does David’s oldest brother Eliab say to him? “I know thy pride.”

Eliab thought the attitude of David was prideful, and we can see why. A ruddy youth walks up from tending sheep and wonders why someone is not taking care of this large man. It sounds a bit off. But what was David thinking? He was only thinking about what God could, and most likely, wanted to do! He did not think for a moment that he himself could do anything in this situation.

He is then brought before King Saul: And Saul said to David, Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth –1 Samuel 17:33.

David responded, … Thy servant kept his father’s sheep, and there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock: And I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth: and when he arose against me, I caught him by his beard, and smote him, and slew him. Thy servant slew both the lion and the bear: and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, seeing he hath defied the armies of the living God –1 Samuel 17:34-36.

David here is super confident, but why?! David said moreover, The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine… –1 Samuel 17:37.

Clearly his confidence is because the Lord is fighting for him. David was not concerned that he was “but a youth” and he did not understand why people questioned him. He was only thinking about what God was going to do! However, Eliab saw David’s confidence as pride. Possibly God had not worked in Eliab’s life. Maybe he did not know of the power of God; therefore, to him it looked like foolish pride.

And Saul armed David with his armour, and he put an helmet of brass upon his head; also he armed him with a coat of mail. And David girded his sword upon his armour, and he assayed to go; for he had not proved it. And David said unto Saul, I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them. And David put them off him –1 Samuel 17:38-39.

So, David chose to not wear the armor; it would only have been a hindrance. Rather, he chose some stones then he ran out to fight the giant. Of course, the giant also did not understand. When he …saw David, he disdained him: for he was but a youth … And the Philistine said unto David, Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods. And the Philistine said to David, Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field –1 Samuel 17:42-44.

Then David said …Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied. This day will the LORD deliver thee into mine hand; and I will smite thee … that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel –1 Samuel 17:45-46.

Notice then what David did. He killed the giant, cut off his head, and took his head back to Jerusalem. What do you think Eliab thought now? Here is the younger brother marching around the streets of Jerusalem with the head of the defeated giant! King Saul calls for David and he goes to see Saul, still holding the severed head.

Why was David not proud? Because he knew it was not he himself that did it. It was God who had done a marvelous work! He was simply testifying of the grace of God.

When we do a work on our own, we cannot boast of it because we did it. It would be pride, so we remain silent and call it humility, even if we desire others to see it. However, when it is a super-natural work of God, we now must boast of what God has done! We are called to this.

Is God working in your life? Are you confused as to whether it is you or God? Ask yourself a question, “Am I doing things that people who are not relying on God can still do?” If we are not doing anything differently than the world, then God is not working in our life. It is that simple. No one enjoys getting angry. I spent most of my childhood and teenage years going to anger management classes where counselors tried to teach us how to control our anger. The unregenerate heart can learn to hide anger, but only God can change the heart. I never heard a counselor teach us how to love people instead of getting angry with them, since it is impossible! It is only a work of the living God in one’s life, and in that work, we must boast! We testify of the outpouring of the grace of God in our lives. When someone believes it is pride, just like Eliab did, it’s because they only see the working of the Law, where all is done by man’s feeble attempts.

Let us look at an example to help us understand. If you decide to build a house, every day you put on your nail bag and get to work. It takes you time and energy, but finally the house is finished. You are standing in front of the newly constructed home with a friend. “Wow,” he states, “This house is beautiful! It looks perfectly built!”

Your cheeks blush a little and you begin to point out the flaws that you know, “No, it’s not perfect, you see that over there? I messed up on that gable…. And the siding over there… it’s not exactly straight.” We do this because we want to be humble! If we would say, “Yes, it is a beautiful house; I did a great job building it!” it would be prideful, right?

Now, what if you wanted to build a house and you realize you are not able to build it; you need God’s help. You pray for help then bam, the house is built! You never even put on your nail bag; the house miraculously appeared. God built it. Now how would the conversation go with your friend? Would you still point out all the flaws? NO! You would boast of its perfection, boldly proclaiming what the Lord had done.

When God does a work in our lives, it is not pride to tell people about it. It takes humility to say that we did not do it, but that God did! However, the devil wants us to quiet down and say it is humility like Eliab wanted David to do. We need men and women today that can boldly proclaim what God is doing in their lives!

Instead, it seems we have many defeated people that actually believe it is godly to talk down about ourselves, to act as if we are a defeated sinner trying to struggle through this earthly existence. “Rise up, Oh man of God! Be done with lesser things!”

I realize one could ask, “So, we should go around boasting about how righteous we are?” To this question, I will paint another picture. A poor criminal who has only known the city streets as home, steals and robs just to get by. He knows he is a bad person, yet he knows nothing else. One day God reveals himself to this man. In a dark alley he repents of his sin and gives his life to the Lord. God saves him, transforms him, converts him. He leaves that alley a new person! He has joy in his heart and peace in his soul!

What do you expect him to tell his friends? Um, the siding over there is not straight, the windows are too small….

NO, certainly not! Rather, he would say I’m perfect! God has done a great work, look at me! I’ve been saved by the power of God! By the blood of Jesus! All this as he skips down the road in the beauty of holiness.

Trots is iets waar iedereen mee te maken krijgt. Het is iets dat van nature de neiging heeft ons leven binnen te komen en te blijven. Net als veel andere dingen is het zeer misleidend, omdat het algemeen aanvaard wordt in de wereld waarin we leven. Mensen zijn tegenwoordig trots op hun trots. Amerikanen zijn trots op hun land, hun werk, hun kinderen, hun gazons, hun sportteams, hun voertuigen, hun ambities, hun doelen, hun uiterlijk, hun vrienden, hun huizen, en zo kan de lijst nog wel even doorgaan. Als we erover nadenken, is de vleselijke mens op zowat alles trots. Mensen staan op en verkondigen dat ze trots zijn, en scheppen op over hun grote prestaties. Mensen kijken naar iets wat iemand heeft gedaan en zeggen tegen degene die het deed: ‘Je mag trots zijn op jezelf!’

Er is één probleem: God haat trots! God verafschuwt de trotsen werkelijk. In Psalmen staat dat God …de tong zal afsnijden die grote woorden spreekt –Psalm 12:3. En in Job staat dat Hij …ieder die trots is zal aanschouwen en hem zal vernederen [neerhalen of laag maken] –Job 40:11. Psalm 40:4 zegt dat Hij de trotsen niet zal aanzien, en in Psalm 119 staat: U hebt de trotsen bestraft, die vervloekt zijn en van uw geboden afdwalen –Psalm 119:21. In Spreuken lezen we: De HEER zal het huis van de trotsen verwoesten… –Spreuken 15:25, en dat Iedereen die trots is van hart, is een gruwel voor de HEER… –Spreuken 16:5. In Maleachi staat dat …zie, de dag komt die zal branden als een oven; en alle trotsen… –Maleachi 4:1. Ten slotte zegt Jakobus: …God keert Zich tegen de trotsen, maar geeft genade aan de nederigen –Jakobus 4:6.

Zoals we zien, is de Bijbel heel duidelijk over trots en over mensen die trots zijn. Er is geen plaats voor trots in ons hart of in ons leven. Wat doen we hier dan mee? Zijn we trots? Scheppen we op zoals de wereld dat doet?

Ik wil de aandacht vestigen op een verborgen vorm van trots die ons leven kan binnensluipen, soms zonder dat we het merken. We zullen dit valse nederigheid noemen. Als we valse nederigheid hebben, is dat dan niet in werkelijkheid een vorm van trots?

Laten we eerst kijken naar de wet en de genade. Iemand die onder de wet staat, verlangt er niet naar te doen wat hij moet doen, maar doet het omdat de wet het voorschrijft. De wet zegt bijvoorbeeld dat we niet mogen doden, maar (volgens de wet) mogen we wel boos zijn. Iemand kan een ander haten en zelfs verlangen hem te doden, maar als hij de verleiding weerstaat om hem te doden, heeft hij zich inderdaad aan de wet gehouden. Veel mensen die tegenwoordig beweren christen te zijn, staan in werkelijkheid onder de wet. Ze doen alles wat ze doen vanwege een wet of een bevel van iemand met gezag. Dat zien we duidelijk wanneer mensen de wet oprekken en zo weinig mogelijk doen als vereist is, terwijl ze zich toch technisch gezien aan de wet houden.

Het hoofdbedeksel is hiervan een goed voorbeeld. Een vrouw die haar hoofd wil bedekken vanwege wat de Bijbel leert, zal haar hoofd ook daadwerkelijk bedekken. Ze hoeft er niet aan herinnerd te worden dat te doen, en hoeft niet berispt te worden omdat ze het halfslachtig doet. Aan de andere kant zijn er christenen die hun hoofd bedekken, maar het bedeksel wordt steeds kleiner en valt steeds minder op. Sommigen dragen het zelfs helemaal achter op hun hoofd en kiezen een kleur die overeenkomt met hun haar, in een poging te voorkomen dat het opvalt bij het onbedekte publiek. Dit maakt duidelijk wat er in hun hart leeft: ze voldoen eenvoudigweg aan de wet.

Deze manier van denken kan op veel dingen van toepassing zijn. Nog een voorbeeld is versiering. De Bijbel zegt dat de versiering niet uiterlijk moet zijn. Veel christenen zullen zichzelf niet versieren met opvallende, in het oog springende dingen, maar er zijn geen normen voor het versieren van huizen, voertuigen en dergelijke. Zo stapt iemand die eenvoudig en onopgesmukt is uit zijn opgesmukte voertuig en loopt een zeer opgesmukt huis binnen. Dit laat zien waar het hart staat: onder de wet.

Laten we nu naar genade kijken. Het is de kracht van God in het leven van een mens. Ze brengt iemand ertoe zijn vijanden werkelijk lief te hebben en goed te doen aan degenen die hem slecht behandelen. Ze brengt iemand ertoe God lief te hebben met heel zijn hart en Gods geboden te gehoorzamen vanuit een vurige liefde voor Hem. De wet is niet langer nodig, want het hart is nieuw; het verlangt ernaar voor God te leven. Wanneer iemand je kwaad doet, denk je er niet aan om het hem betaald te zetten. Sterker nog, je wordt niet eens boos. Je bent een nieuw schepsel en dankzij deze kracht—genade van God—heb je degene lief die jou onrecht heeft aangedaan. Vergeven is geen probleem; anderen helpen gaat vanzelf. Je bent niet van jezelf en je verlangt ernaar alles te zijn wat je kunt zijn voor je Heiland, die voor jou gestorven is.

Wat heeft dit te maken met trots of nederigheid?

De Bijbel zegt: …de wet is door Mozes gegeven, maar de genade en de waarheid zijn door Jezus Christus gekomen –Johannes 1:17. We hebben Gods Geest niet nodig om de wet in ons leven te gehoorzamen—we kunnen dat op eigen kracht. Daarom kunnen we trots worden wanneer we dingen voor God doen, omdat WIJ ze hebben gedaan. Wanneer we onze boosheid niet de vrije loop lieten toen we het oneens waren met een buurman, denken we goed over onszelf en kunnen we trots worden. Maar wanneer we onze buurman die een probleem met ons heeft werkelijk liefhebben, kunnen we niet trots worden, want het was genade; het was Gods kracht die dit teweegbracht, niet wijzelf. Daarom staan we verwonderd over God en zijn overvloedige genade.

Het zou dwaas zijn als iemand trots was op iets waarvan God duidelijk de bewerker is! Als Lazarus had rondgelopen om op te scheppen dat hij uit de dood was opgewekt, zouden mensen aan zijn verstand hebben getwijfeld en hebben gezegd: ‘Jij hebt niets gedaan! Jezus heeft alles gedaan.’

Ik wil niet zeggen dat de christen niets doet. Nee, we moeten Gods geboden nederig gehoorzamen en in zijn wegen wandelen. Wat ik wel zeg, is dat we niet op onszelf kunnen pochen, omdat God ons in staat stelt zijn geboden te gehoorzamen.

Laten we eens kijken naar het bekende verhaal van David en Goliat. David ging naar het leger om proviand te brengen voor zijn broers, die daar vochten. Toen hij dichterbij kwam, verbaasde hij zich over wat hij zag: een grote man die zijn volk uitdaagde! David leek enigszins geschokt en verontwaardigd toen hij vroeg: …wie is deze onbesneden Filistijn, dat hij de legers van de levende God tart? –1 Samuël 17:26.

Wat zegt Eliab, Davids oudste broer, tegen hem? ‘Ik ken je trots.’

Eliab dacht dat Davids houding trots was, en we kunnen begrijpen waarom. Een rossige jongeman komt aanlopen van het hoeden van schapen en vraagt zich af waarom iemand niet met die grote man afrekent. Dat klinkt een beetje vreemd. Maar wat dacht David? Hij dacht alleen aan wat God kon doen en waarschijnlijk wilde doen! Hij dacht geen moment dat hij zelf iets aan deze situatie kon doen.

Daarna wordt hij voor koning Saul gebracht: En Saul zei tegen David: U kunt niet tegen deze Filistijn ten strijde trekken: want u bent nog maar een jongen, en hij is al van jongs af aan een krijgsman –1 Samuël 17:33.

David antwoordde: … Uw dienaar hoedde de schapen van zijn vader, en er kwam een leeuw en een beer die een lam uit de kudde meenamen. Ik ging achter hem aan, sloeg hem en bevrijdde het lam uit zijn muil. Toen hij zich tegen mij keerde, greep ik hem bij zijn baard, sloeg hem en doodde hem. Uw dienaar heeft zowel de leeuw als de beer gedood; en met deze onbesneden Filistijn zal het net zo gaan, omdat hij de legers van de levende God heeft getart –1 Samuël 17:34-36.

David is hier buitengewoon zelfverzekerd, maar waarom?! David zei bovendien: De HEER, die mij uit de klauwen van de leeuw en uit de klauwen van de beer heeft gered, zal mij ook redden uit de hand van deze Filistijn… –1 Samuël 17:37.

Het is duidelijk dat zijn vertrouwen voortkomt uit het feit dat de Heer voor hem strijdt. David maakte zich er geen zorgen over dat hij ‘nog maar een jongen’ was en begreep niet waarom mensen hem in twijfel trokken. Hij dacht alleen aan wat God zou gaan doen! Eliab zag Davids zelfvertrouwen echter als trots. Misschien had God niet in Eliabs leven gewerkt. Misschien kende hij de kracht van God niet; daarom leek het hem dwaze trots.

Saul rustte David uit met zijn wapenrusting, zette een koperen helm op zijn hoofd en trok hem een maliënkolder aan. David gordde zijn zwaard over zijn wapenrusting en probeerde op weg te gaan, want hij had het niet uitgeprobeerd. David zei tegen Saul: Ik kan hiermee niet gaan, want ik heb het niet uitgeprobeerd. En David deed de wapenrusting weer uit –1 Samuël 17:38-39.

David koos er dus voor de wapenrusting niet te dragen; die zou hem alleen maar hinderen. In plaats daarvan koos hij een paar stenen en rende toen naar voren om de reus te bevechten. Natuurlijk begreep de reus het ook niet. Toen hij …David zag, verachtte hij hem, want hij was nog maar een jongen … En de Filistijn zei tegen David: Ben ik een hond, dat je met stokken naar me toe komt? En de Filistijn vervloekte David bij zijn goden. De Filistijn zei tegen David: Kom maar naar me toe, dan geef ik je vlees aan de vogels in de lucht en aan de dieren van het veld –1 Samuël 17:42-44.

Toen zei David: …U komt naar mij toe met een zwaard, een speer en een schild, maar ik kom naar u toe in de naam van de HEER van de legermachten, de God van de legers van Israël, die u hebt getart. Vandaag zal de HEER u in mijn hand overleveren; ik zal u neerslaan … zodat de hele aarde zal weten dat er een God is in Israël –1 Samuël 17:45-46.

Let vervolgens op wat David deed. Hij doodde de reus, hakte zijn hoofd af en nam het mee terug naar Jeruzalem. Wat denken jullie dat Eliab nu dacht? Daar loopt de jongere broer door de straten van Jeruzalem met het hoofd van de verslagen reus! Koning Saul laat David roepen en David gaat naar Saul, nog steeds met het afgehakte hoofd in zijn hand.

Waarom was David niet trots? Omdat hij wist dat hij het niet zelf had gedaan. God had een wonderbaarlijk werk verricht! David getuigde eenvoudigweg van Gods genade.

Wanneer we zelf iets tot stand brengen, kunnen we er niet over pochen, want wij hebben het zelf gedaan. Dat zou trots zijn, dus blijven we stil en noemen we het nederigheid, zelfs als we graag willen dat anderen het zien. Maar wanneer het een bovennatuurlijk werk van God is, moeten we juist pochen over wat God heeft gedaan! Daartoe zijn we geroepen.

Werkt God in jouw leven? Weet je niet zeker of jij het bent of God? Stel jezelf dan de vraag: ‘Doe ik dingen die mensen die niet op God vertrouwen ook kunnen doen?’ Als we niets anders doen dan de wereld, werkt God niet in ons leven. Zo eenvoudig is het. Niemand vindt het prettig om boos te worden. Een groot deel van mijn jeugd en tienerjaren bracht ik door in cursussen woedebeheersing, waar begeleiders ons probeerden te leren onze boosheid te beheersen. Het onwedergeboren hart kan leren boosheid te verbergen, maar alleen God kan het hart veranderen. Ik heb nooit een begeleider ons horen leren hoe we mensen moeten liefhebben in plaats van boos op hen te worden, omdat dat onmogelijk is! Het is alleen een werk van de levende God in iemands leven, en over dat werk moeten we pochen! We getuigen van de uitstorting van Gods genade in ons leven. Wanneer iemand denkt dat dat trots is, net als Eliab, komt dat doordat hij alleen het werk van de wet ziet, waarbij alles door de zwakke pogingen van de mens wordt gedaan.

Laten we een voorbeeld bekijken om dit beter te begrijpen. Stel dat je besluit een huis te bouwen. Elke dag doe je je spijkerschort om en ga je aan het werk. Het kost tijd en energie, maar uiteindelijk is het huis af. Je staat met een vriend voor het pas gebouwde huis. ‘Wauw,’ zegt hij, ‘wat een prachtig huis! Het lijkt perfect gebouwd!’

Je bloost een beetje en begint de gebreken aan te wijzen die je kent: ‘Nee, het is niet perfect, zie je dat daar? Die topgevel heb ik verkeerd gedaan… En de gevelbekleding daar… die is niet helemaal recht.’ We doen dit omdat we nederig willen zijn! Als we zouden zeggen: ‘Ja, het is een prachtig huis; ik heb het geweldig gebouwd!’ zou dat trots zijn, toch?

Maar wat als je een huis wilde bouwen en je beseft dat je dat niet kunt; je hebt Gods hulp nodig. Je bidt om hulp en bam, het huis staat er! Je hebt niet eens je spijkerschort omgedaan; het huis is op wonderbaarlijke wijze verschenen. God heeft het gebouwd. Hoe zou het gesprek met je vriend dan gaan? Zou je nog steeds alle gebreken aanwijzen? NEE! Je zou pochen over de volmaaktheid ervan en vrijmoedig verkondigen wat de Heer heeft gedaan.

Wanneer God in ons leven een werk verricht, is het geen trots om mensen erover te vertellen. Er is nederigheid voor nodig om te zeggen dat wij het niet hebben gedaan, maar dat God het heeft gedaan! De duivel wil echter dat we onze mond houden en zeggen dat het nederigheid is, zoals Eliab wilde dat David deed. We hebben vandaag mannen en vrouwen nodig die vrijmoedig kunnen verkondigen wat God in hun leven doet!

In plaats daarvan lijkt het erop dat we veel verslagen mensen hebben die werkelijk geloven dat het godvrezend is om zichzelf naar beneden te halen, om te doen alsof we verslagen zondaars zijn die zich moeizaam door dit aardse bestaan worstelen. ‘Sta op, o man Gods! Laat die mindere dingen achter je!’

Ik besef dat iemand zou kunnen vragen: ‘Dus moeten we overal rondlopen en opscheppen over hoe rechtvaardig we zijn?’ Als antwoord op die vraag schets ik een ander beeld. Een arme misdadiger die alleen de straten van de stad als thuis kent, steelt en berooft om rond te komen. Hij weet dat hij een slecht mens is, maar kent niets anders. Op een dag openbaart God Zich aan deze man. In een donker steegje krijgt hij berouw van zijn zonde en geeft hij zijn leven aan de Heer. God redt hem, verandert hem en bekeert hem. Hij verlaat dat steegje als een nieuw mens! Hij heeft vreugde in zijn hart en vrede in zijn ziel!

Wat verwacht je dat hij tegen zijn vrienden zegt? Eh, de gevelbekleding daar is niet recht, de ramen zijn te klein…

NEE, natuurlijk niet! Hij zou juist zeggen: Ik ben volmaakt! God heeft een groot werk gedaan, kijk maar naar mij! Ik ben gered door de kracht van God! Door het bloed van Jezus! En dat alles terwijl hij huppelend over de weg gaat in de schoonheid van heiligheid.

And David said, What have I now done? Is there not a cause? –1 Samuel 17:29.

The story of David and Goliath took place over three millenniums ago and has been a perennial favorite of the young and old ever since. There is something about the plight of the underdog that we all relate to. Perhaps we subconsciously view ourselves in such odds and secretly hope that there will come a day when our own “ship will come in” in a similar fashion. Unfortunately, that sort of random success seems more akin to a Hollywood production than to real life. We see only the conflict between the young and the old, the shepherd and the warrior, and the heavy military weapons and the sling. Yet there were some preliminary principles that David embraced in his youth that made him a prime candidate for success. But these often go unheralded in our love for a climactic romantic victory.

If the only vision we have of ourselves comes from the social mirror about us, we will carry a warped inner perception similar to what we see as we glance into a trick mirror at a carnival. The social opinions and perceptions of our environment often cast an awkward and skewed description of our person before our eyes and ears. Sometimes it is unrealistically positive, building the person up in the eyes of the media when there is very little heroic character displayed.

The sports arena is probably the biggest offender in this. The individuals are praised who can run, throw, or shoot better than everyone else. But sporting talent adds little to their honest pure worth as a human. The other side of the coin produces an immense amount of negative and degrading input that seeks to thwart any effort to try. These comments are produced in copious showers by stressed parents, insecure siblings, frustrated bosses, and a host of other acquaintances struggling for identity in a “survival of the fittest” society. The input from these two camps is both disjointed, and out of proportion. To be told you are great will never produce greatness any more than a barrage of derogatory remarks will produce humility. Unfortunately, too often many of us allow these disproportionate projections to affect our thinking and chart our course.

The greatest and superior endowment given to mankind over the rest of creation is not found in his physical abilities, but in his mind. The most intelligent of animals can be trained to be responsible, but they cannot choose or direct that training. But as humans, we can write new programs for ourselves totally independent of our instincts or environmental training. Those of us who live in natural accordance with our instincts and conditioning, will scarcely rise above the animal kingdom. But those who will exercise and develop those endowments shall uniquely fill the role God has designed for them in their encounter with the giants. While David’s time and position were unique, the principles he embraced were universal. If I could teach my dog to yodel, it would prove that yodeling is achievable for dogs and open the possibility for others to do it too. Likewise, if David defeated Goliath by miracle alone, then there is no hope for us but to sit and wait for God to do the same for us. However, if principles were at the core of the victory, then there is an example for us to follow and a virtue to secure for use on our own battlefield.

As David arose early that morning and shouldered his pack of corn, bread, and cheese to take to his brothers, he had no idea what the day would bring forth. The Lord was his Shepherd, and he had no lack, but as he came upon the scene he was shocked at the sight. Both armies were positioned on opposite mountains and locked in a stalemate. To take your entire army down into the valley and fight the opposition uphill would leave you at a tremendous disadvantage. One that neither side was willing to risk. So, the Philistines evoked a common dimension of warfare proposing that two warriors would fight in the valley giving no advantage to either side. But the Philistines had a giant among their numbers that terrified the army of Israel. As David inquired into the situation as to why no one would confront the reproachful blasphemies of the infidel, he was met with a stiff rebuke from his oldest brother: …and Eliab’s anger was kindled against David, and he said, Why camest thou down hither? and with whom hast thou left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart; for thou art come down that thou mightest see the battle. And David said, What have I now done? Is there not a cause? –1 Samuel 17:28-29.

Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God –Hebrews 12:2. When a man has a cause set before him, he can endure almost anything. Some endure for a corruptible crown. King Saul had offered tax exempt wealth and son-in-law status, but the earthly dowry elicited no volunteers. While the thought of earthly prominence meant nothing to the tender heart of David, there was a jealous fire kindled by the blasphemous taunts of Goliath and he stepped forward by faith. But faith is not just a whim that may be inflated by an emotional tire pump. For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works [action] is dead also –James 2:26. Thus, with the cause clearly before him, and his God beside him, David offers to fight Goliath.

So David moved forward acting according to godly, uncorrupted principles…

A Caring Conscience is seated in the soul of man and determines what we care about. Many think that a conscience is only useful as a limiting guide. But the human conscience was also created to function in the reverse. When we are convicted that something is good and right, we pursue it with a passion. Thomas Edison said that genius is 1% inspiration and 99% perspiration. While this may be true enough, it is without question that the inspiration must arrive first. Jacob’s aspirations for Rachael made him forget the seven years of labor. Edison’s pursuit of a successful light bulb caused him to forget the thousands of elements that had failed.

Careless apathy is the opposite and is the result of a seared conscience. David was amazed that the blasphemous taunts of Goliath produced no cause for action on the part of God’s army. Give a man a reason to live and he will supply the how –Nietzke. As a holocaust prisoner in a Nazi concentration camp, Victor Frankl was commissioned to labor in the ward of the camp where prisoners were dying of typhus. He observed that when a person gave up hope, death was soon to follow. Likewise, for many of our day, when the hope of personal gain evaporates in the fray, so does the passion to overcome. Most workers today are more concerned about their paycheck than of doing a good and worthy job. Often when a man loses his feelings for his wife, he believes that he is incapable of loving her, but a man with a healthy conscience toward godly principles will act in loving fashion toward her regardless of his feelings or her response. The cause is aroused and fueled by the conscience and lays the foundation for passionate action.

An Honest Imagination belongs to the realm of the spirit and is driven by our conscience. Necessity is the mother of invention –Unknown. Some are waiting for life to be discovered while others are inventing it as they go. This is not a license to claim false ideals. David’s pursuit is honest for he was not warped by the media about him. He has met with success over the beasts (a lion and a bear) in the hills of Bethlehem and with God’s help, incurs no fear of contending with one (a man of war from his youth) in the valley of Elah.

As Saul reluctantly consents to David’s proposal, he proceeds to arm the lad in typical worldly fashion. While it may have been an honor to wear the armor of the king, David would have none of it: …I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them. And David put them off him –1 Samuel 17:39, choosing five stones instead. Knowing what others do and knowing what to do are not necessarily the same thing.

The cowering beliefs of the Israelite army were rooted in a pagan value system. Goliath was not the problem, but rather, faithless fear and the assumption that they needed to engage in the warfare on the terms of the world. Those that embrace a true and worthy cause will surely find the imagination to pursue it.

Goliath had automatically assumed that he would be in combat under his own terms. Insulted and angered he cries out: …Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field –1 Samuel 17:44. As a giant, speed and agility are not his forte and so he orders David to come to him. But Goliath has grossly overestimated his personal ability and underestimated his foe. According to some estimates, at six or seven revolutions per second, David’s sling had the stopping power of a 45 mm handgun, and the hand of a skillful slinger …could sling stones at an hair breadth, and not miss –Judges 20:16. It was not unusual for them to be able to hit birds in flight. Ancient ruins have uncovered tongs that were believed to be used by the military to remove embedded stones from wounded soldiers. If Goliath had a spear and David a pistol, we would not be so quick to believe that the larger man held the major advantage.

Faithful Action is inevitable when our bodies are subject to our soul and spirit, and they are under the direction of God’s Spirit. We are then free to act independently of our nature and other influences. When the lustful passions of the mortal body hold sway over our inner heart and mind, we are defeated before we take one step toward the enemy. As vessels of God’s design, with a moral free will, we have the divine ability to choose our course of action. Some believe that being proactive is merely taking the initiative. But initiative alone will not fit us for victory any more than it did for the sons of Sceva. The desire to dominate is no more noble than Goliath’s unbridled rage to destroy this young upstart. His adrenaline flowed as he scorned David’s youth, jumped to conclusions, was easily insulted, and marveled at the ignorance of others.

But David carried no such reactive mission. His endeavor was that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel. And all this assembly shall know that the LORD saveth not with sword and spear… –1 Samuel 17:47. Faithful action must be focused on yielding what you have, rather than obtaining what you don’t. If life erects concerns outside of our ability to change, it is fruitless to give them our attention. Joseph could not change his brothers’ reception, his master’s wife’s deception, the jail’s seclusion, or the butler’s delusion. The faith of the shepherd boy teaches us to stop lamenting over what we wanna-be and start being what we oughta-be. We need to stop looking for a miracle and start looking for an opportunity. It is not about overcoming extreme odds, but rather it is how we respond to a traffic jam, a disobedient child, an irate customer, or a demanding spouse. It is about owning a cause big enough to defuse selfish reaction and incite charitable pro-action.

Why would Japanese Kamikaze pilots die for a losing cause during World War Two? Why would Muslim terrorists blow themselves up? Why do Catholic Priests and Nuns take vows of celibacy and poverty? Is there no cause for the Christian that extends broader and deeper than the giants of this world? Is there not a cause that stirs our imagination and sanctifies our action? Or isn’t there even one that transforms our mundane work into a channel of grace for the service of the King of the Universe? How would history be different if Jesse would have spent his retirement like the elders of our day? God slays giants by the instruments we yield to him, from the needle of Dorcas… to the nail of Jael, from Zebedee’s boats of the business… to the boys of his bosom.

Shamgar had an oxgoad;
David had a sling;
Dorcus had a needle;
Rahab had a string;
Samson had a jawbone;
Moses had a rod;
Mary had some ointment;
And all were used for God!

E Davi disse: Que fiz eu agora? Não há uma causa? –1 Samuel 17:29.

A história de Davi e Golias aconteceu há mais de três milênios e, desde então, tem sido uma favorita perene entre jovens e idosos. Há algo na situação do azarão com que todos nos identificamos. Talvez, inconscientemente, nos vejamos diante de probabilidades semelhantes e esperemos secretamente que um dia a nossa própria “sorte mude” de maneira parecida. Infelizmente, esse tipo de sucesso aleatório parece mais próprio de uma produção de Hollywood do que da vida real. Vemos apenas o conflito entre o jovem e o velho, o pastor e o guerreiro, e as pesadas armas militares e a funda. No entanto, havia alguns princípios preliminares que Davi abraçou na juventude e que o tornaram um candidato ideal ao sucesso. Mas eles muitas vezes passam despercebidos em nosso amor por uma vitória romântica e culminante.

Se a única visão que temos de nós mesmos vem do espelho social à nossa volta, carregaremos uma percepção interior distorcida, semelhante à que vemos ao olhar para um espelho deformador numa feira. As opiniões e percepções sociais do nosso meio frequentemente apresentam diante dos nossos olhos e ouvidos uma descrição estranha e distorcida de quem somos. Às vezes, ela é irrealisticamente positiva, elevando a pessoa aos olhos da mídia quando quase nenhum caráter heroico se manifesta.

O mundo dos esportes é provavelmente o maior responsável por isso. São elogiados os indivíduos que conseguem correr, arremessar ou chutar melhor do que todos os outros. Mas o talento esportivo pouco acrescenta ao seu valor humano genuíno e honesto. O outro lado da moeda produz uma enorme quantidade de mensagens negativas e degradantes que procuram frustrar qualquer tentativa de esforço. Esses comentários vêm em profusão de pais estressados, irmãos inseguros, chefes frustrados e muitos outros conhecidos que lutam por uma identidade numa sociedade de “sobrevivência do mais apto”. As mensagens desses dois grupos são desconexas e desproporcionais. Dizer a alguém que é excelente nunca produzirá excelência, assim como uma saraivada de comentários depreciativos não produzirá humildade. Infelizmente, com frequência muitos de nós permitimos que essas projeções desproporcionais afetem nosso pensamento e determinem nosso rumo.

O maior e mais elevado dom concedido à humanidade acima do restante da criação não se encontra em suas capacidades físicas, mas em sua mente. O mais inteligente dos animais pode ser treinado para ser responsável, mas não pode escolher nem dirigir esse treinamento. Nós, porém, como seres humanos, podemos criar novos programas para nós mesmos, totalmente independentes dos nossos instintos ou do condicionamento ambiental. Aqueles de nós que vivem em conformidade natural com seus instintos e condicionamento dificilmente se elevarão acima do reino animal. Mas aqueles que exercitarem e desenvolverem esses dons ocuparão de modo singular o papel que Deus planejou para eles ao se depararem com os gigantes. Embora o tempo e a posição de Davi fossem únicos, os princípios que ele abraçou eram universais. Se eu pudesse ensinar meu cão a cantar tirolês, isso provaria que cães são capazes de fazê-lo e abriria a possibilidade para que outros também o fizessem. Do mesmo modo, se Davi derrotou Golias apenas por milagre, então não há esperança para nós, a não ser sentar e esperar que Deus faça o mesmo por nós. Contudo, se os princípios estavam no cerne da vitória, então temos um exemplo a seguir e uma virtude a cultivar para usar no nosso próprio campo de batalha.

Quando Davi se levantou cedo naquela manhã e pôs aos ombros sua sacola com milho, pão e queijo para levar aos irmãos, não tinha ideia do que o dia traria. O Senhor era seu Pastor, e nada lhe faltava, mas, ao chegar ao local, ficou chocado com o que viu. Os dois exércitos estavam posicionados em montanhas opostas e presos num impasse. Levar todo o exército para o vale e combater o adversário encosta acima deixaria você numa tremenda desvantagem. Nenhum dos lados estava disposto a correr esse risco. Então os filisteus recorreram a uma prática comum de guerra e propuseram que dois guerreiros lutassem no vale, sem dar vantagem a nenhum dos lados. Mas entre os filisteus havia um gigante que aterrorizava o exército de Israel. Quando Davi perguntou por que ninguém enfrentava as blasfêmias ultrajantes do infiel, recebeu uma severa repreensão do irmão mais velho: …e a ira de Eliabe se acendeu contra Davi, e ele disse: Por que desceste aqui? E com quem deixaste aquelas poucas ovelhas no deserto? Conheço a tua soberba e a maldade do teu coração; pois desceste para ver a batalha. E Davi disse: Que fiz eu agora? Não há uma causa? –1 Samuel 17:28-29.

Olhando para Jesus, autor e consumador da nossa fé; o qual, pela alegria que lhe estava proposta, suportou a cruz, desprezando a vergonha, e está assentado à direita do trono de Deus –Hebreus 12:2. Quando um homem tem diante de si uma causa, consegue suportar quase tudo. Alguns perseveram por uma coroa corruptível. O rei Saul oferecera riquezas isentas de impostos e a condição de genro, mas o dote terreno não atraiu voluntários. Embora a perspectiva de proeminência terrena não significasse nada para o coração sensível de Davi, as provocações blasfemas de Golias acenderam nele um fogo de zelo, e ele avançou pela fé. Mas a fé não é apenas um capricho que se pode inflar com uma bomba emocional. Porque, assim como o corpo sem o espírito está morto, assim também a fé sem obras [ação] está morta –Tiago 2:26. Assim, com a causa claramente diante de si e seu Deus ao seu lado, Davi se oferece para lutar contra Golias.

Então Davi avançou, agindo de acordo com princípios piedosos e não corrompidos…

Uma consciência atenciosa está alojada na alma do homem e determina aquilo com que nos importamos. Muitos pensam que a consciência só serve como um guia que impõe limites. Mas a consciência humana também foi criada para funcionar no sentido inverso. Quando estamos convictos de que algo é bom e certo, buscamos isso com paixão. Thomas Edison disse que o gênio é 1% inspiração e 99% transpiração. Embora isso possa ser suficientemente verdadeiro, não há dúvida de que a inspiração precisa vir primeiro. As aspirações de Jacó por Raquel fizeram-no esquecer os sete anos de trabalho. A busca de Edison por uma lâmpada bem-sucedida fez com que esquecesse os milhares de elementos que haviam fracassado.

A apatia descuidada é o oposto e resulta de uma consciência cauterizada. Davi ficou espantado que as provocações blasfemas de Golias não levassem o exército de Deus a agir. Dê a um homem uma razão para viver, e ele encontrará o como –Nietzke. Como prisioneiro do Holocausto num campo de concentração nazista, Victor Frankl foi designado para trabalhar na enfermaria do campo, onde os prisioneiros morriam de tifo. Ele observou que, quando uma pessoa perdia a esperança, a morte logo vinha em seguida. Da mesma forma, para muitos em nossos dias, quando a esperança de ganho pessoal se dissipa na luta, também desaparece a paixão por vencer. Hoje, a maioria dos trabalhadores se preocupa mais com o salário do que em fazer um trabalho bom e digno. Muitas vezes, quando um homem perde o que sente pela esposa, acredita que é incapaz de amá-la; mas um homem cuja consciência está bem formada em relação aos princípios piedosos agirá com amor para com ela, independentemente do que sente ou da resposta dela. A consciência desperta e alimenta a causa, lançando as bases para uma ação apaixonada.

Uma imaginação honesta pertence ao domínio do espírito e é impulsionada pela nossa consciência. A necessidade é a mãe da invenção –Desconhecido. Alguns esperam que a vida seja descoberta, enquanto outros a inventam à medida que avançam. Isso não é uma licença para reivindicar ideais falsos. A busca de Davi é honesta, pois ele não foi distorcido pela mídia ao seu redor. Ele já vencera as feras (um leão e um urso) nas colinas de Belém e, com a ajuda de Deus, não teme enfrentar uma (um homem de guerra desde a juventude) no vale de Elá.

Quando Saul, relutantemente, consente com a proposta de Davi, procede a equipar o rapaz à maneira típica do mundo. Embora pudesse ser uma honra vestir a armadura do rei, Davi não quis usá-la: …Não posso ir com estas, pois nunca as experimentei. E Davi tirou-as de si –1 Samuel 17:39, escolhendo cinco pedras em vez disso. Saber o que os outros fazem e saber o que fazer não são necessariamente a mesma coisa.

As crenças temerosas do exército israelita estavam enraizadas num sistema de valores pagão. Golias não era o problema, mas sim o medo sem fé e a suposição de que precisavam travar a guerra nos termos do mundo. Aqueles que abraçam uma causa verdadeira e digna certamente encontrarão a imaginação necessária para persegui-la.

Golias presumira automaticamente que o combate ocorreria nos termos dele. Ofendido e enfurecido, gritou: …Vem a mim, e darei a tua carne às aves do céu e aos animais do campo –1 Samuel 17:44. Como era um gigante, velocidade e agilidade não eram seu forte; por isso, mandou Davi ir até ele. Mas Golias superestimou grosseiramente a própria capacidade e subestimou o adversário. Segundo algumas estimativas, a seis ou sete rotações por segundo, a funda de Davi tinha o poder de parada de uma pistola de 45 mm, e a mão de um fundeiro habilidoso …podia arremessar pedras à largura de um fio de cabelo, sem errar –Juízes 20:16. Não era incomum que conseguissem atingir aves em voo. Ruínas antigas revelaram pinças que, segundo se acreditava, eram usadas pelos militares para remover pedras alojadas nos soldados feridos. Se Golias tivesse uma lança e Davi uma pistola, não acreditaríamos tão prontamente que o homem maior tinha a grande vantagem.

Ação fiel é inevitável quando nosso corpo está sujeito à nossa alma e ao nosso espírito, e ambos estão sob a direção do Espírito de Deus. Então somos livres para agir independentemente da nossa natureza e de outras influências. Quando as paixões lascivas do corpo mortal dominam nosso coração e nossa mente interiores, somos derrotados antes mesmo de dar um passo em direção ao inimigo. Como vasos concebidos por Deus, com livre-arbítrio moral, temos a capacidade divina de escolher nosso curso de ação. Alguns acreditam que ser proativo é apenas tomar a iniciativa. Mas a iniciativa, por si só, não nos preparará para a vitória, assim como não preparou os filhos de Ceva. O desejo de dominar não é mais nobre do que a fúria desenfreada de Golias para destruir aquele jovem arrivista. Sua adrenalina aumentava enquanto desprezava a juventude de Davi, tirava conclusões precipitadas, se ofendia facilmente e se espantava com a ignorância dos outros.

Mas Davi não tinha uma missão tão reativa. Seu propósito era que toda a terra soubesse que há um Deus em Israel. E toda esta assembleia saberá que o SENHOR não salva com espada nem com lança… –1 Samuel 17:47. A ação fiel precisa se concentrar em oferecer aquilo que você tem, em vez de obter aquilo que não tem. Se a vida suscita preocupações que estão além da nossa capacidade de mudar, é inútil dar atenção a elas. José não podia mudar a maneira como seus irmãos o receberam, o engano da mulher de seu senhor, o isolamento da prisão ou a ilusão do copeiro. A fé do jovem pastor nos ensina a parar de lamentar o que queríamos ser e começar a ser o que deveríamos ser. Precisamos parar de procurar um milagre e começar a procurar uma oportunidade. Não se trata de vencer probabilidades extremas, mas de como reagimos a um engarrafamento, a um filho desobediente, a um cliente irritado ou a um cônjuge exigente. Trata-se de assumir uma causa suficientemente grande para desarmar a reação egoísta e incitar uma ação proativa e caridosa.

Por que pilotos japoneses kamikazes morreriam por uma causa perdida durante a Segunda Guerra Mundial? Por que terroristas muçulmanos se explodiriam? Por que padres e freiras católicos fazem votos de celibato e pobreza? Será que o cristão não tem uma causa mais ampla e profunda do que os gigantes deste mundo? Não há uma causa que desperte nossa imaginação e santifique nossa ação? Ou será que não há nem mesmo uma que transforme nosso trabalho cotidiano num canal de graça para o serviço do Rei do Universo? Como a história teria sido diferente se Jessé tivesse passado a aposentadoria como os idosos de nossos dias? Deus abate gigantes por meio dos instrumentos que lhe entregamos, desde a agulha de Dorcas… até o prego de Jael, desde os barcos comerciais de Zebedeu… até os meninos que ele ama.

Sangará tinha uma aguilhada de bois;
Davi tinha uma funda;
Dorcas tinha uma agulha;
Raabe tinha um cordão;
Sansão tinha uma queixada;
Moisés tinha uma vara;
Maria tinha um pouco de unguento;
E tudo foi usado por Deus!

One day you may be walking along a seashore. You glance back to watch your footprints disappear with the next surge of foaming water. You love to hear the soothing swish of the breakers. You gaze at the graceful sweep of shoreline and glittering ocean way out to the horizon. Life is good.

Suddenly a huge wave sweeps in and lifts you off your feet. You struggle and flail to regain your footing. Or the wave may even carry you farther and slam you against a rock wall, leaving you stunned and gasping in pain.

This wave may be called grief, as expressed in the following stanza from the song by Mary A. Baker.

Master, with anguish of spirit
I bow in my grief today;
The depths of my sad heart are troubled;
Oh, waken and save, I pray!
Torrents of sin and of anguish
Sweep o’er my sinking soul!
And I perish! I perish, dear Master;
Oh hasten, and take control.

In the past year, many of us have lost loved ones. Perhaps it was a childhood friend, or someone from our church family, or even from our immediate family. Depending on how close we were, we felt drops, splashes, or even tidal waves of grief.

Our grief stems from the relationship we shared. We have invested in each other’s lives to some degree. We have loved, but now that love has nowhere to go. We could say that grief is the price of love.

Here is how one widow described grief: “At the sudden and untimely death of my husband, the feeling was one of overwhelming shock, disbelief, and even panic, as I faced an uncertain future without him at the age of 51. Looking back, I realize how merciful God is to allow us to be in a certain state of numbness and shock at a time like this, allowing the reality to sink in more slowly.”

How did she cope? She says, “I am also awed at how He provides the grace and strength to go through hard things in life that we never thought we would have to face. He walks with us as we go through the valley of grief, so we are never walking alone. The journey of grief is not the same for everyone. It is not over in a few months. For me, I still cried a year later. It took a long time for the pain to fade and for life to become meaningful again. But praise God, that time does come! It is best not to look too far into the future. We walk one day at a time with Jesus, knowing that the best is yet to come.”

Here are more experiences from those who have been there:

  • “I am still learning that when we say, ‘It’s all right, Lord,’ we need to leave it there, at Jesus’ feet.”
  • “Grieving people are very lonely, but there’s also an aloneness that comes from not having a place to belong. You may be in a room of people, and still feel utterly alone, because you’ve lost your sense of belonging, or your category of belonging has changed.”
  • “The presence of a grieving person can be painful for others. It’s a reminder that “bad” things can happen. So, at times they are not invited, which is painful. A grieving person wants to be invited, but at times when included they feel their lack of belonging anew and think they should have stayed at home. Most times, casual conversation can be difficult for them when their world has been violently shaken. Their hearts are heavy while the mood of others is lighthearted, making them feel even more despondent. Understandably, many people don’t know what to do when they see others grieving, so they default to doing nothing and walk away. Many friendships are lost after a loss, which is even more painful.”
  • “God was so close. He was always there. ‘Underneath are the everlasting arms’, and I felt them.”

God can use sorrow and grief to teach us what we might not learn in happier times. We learn to depend on Him. We think of the seriousness of life. We learn to embrace eternal values and anticipate heaven. We are motivated to cherish the loved ones we still have when we hear expressions such as this: “Looking back, I wish we would not have taken the time we had together for granted. I wish I would have recognized his personality traits as strengths rather than things that annoyed.”

Those who lose loved ones often find themselves in the limelight for a time. Many people want to know how they are responding, especially when the death is an unusual situation. Consider the experience of Elizabeth Elliot and the four others who were made widows in 1956 by jungle killers in Ecuador. Or think of Marie Troyer whose husband John was murdered by guerrillas in Guatemala in 1981, or the mothers of the girls killed in Nickel Mines, Pennsylvania in 2006.

These women found themselves in the glare of an almost worldwide spotlight. Their greatest opportunity to display God’s enabling grace likely came at a time when they wanted it least. But their responses of forgiveness, unselfishness, and trust in God amazed the world, at least considering the amount of media attention. Truly, A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid –Matthew 5:14.

While we and those we know will hardly face that level of exposure, we too have a unique platform to display God’s grace. We may never have a better opportunity to touch hardened or seeking hearts than in our own hour of grief.

When we hear that people have indeed been drawn to God through the death of our loved one, it can be a source of comfort and meaning. This death was not a senseless tragedy; it was meant to bring glory to God. In other words, God does not waste our sorrows.

It reminds us of Jesus’ words about Lazarus when he said, …This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God might be glorified thereby –John 11:4. Jesus is our perfect example for relating to those in sorrow. He came to Mary and Martha and listened. He cried with them even though He knew He could and then did transform the whole situation by raising Lazarus.

How do we help?

What is our part in helping a grieving sister glorify God in the midst of her situation? Consider the thoughts shared by the following widows:

  • “What helped was when a dear sister sat with me and told me she cared. And in her quietness, I could feel that her love was real.”
  • “Grief is surprising and unexpected. The person may be having a good day when they hear a song, smell a certain scent, or see a familiar article of clothing which triggers a memory followed by a flood of tears. If this happens when you’re with them, it’s okay. Tears are okay. Tears are healing. Stay present and help them through it. Press in; grieve with them. It’s better to err in doing something than in doing nothing. You may not understand. That’s okay. You don’t need to experience loss to show that you care.”
  • “Grief is exhausting and mentally debilitating. So don’t just ask what you can do; look for a need they may have and try to fill it. For example, ‘I’d like to come over Tuesday evening and fix your faucet’ or ‘We’d like to come and bring a meal if you’re up to it?’”
  • “One thing that meant a lot to me was when people shared pleasant memories of our loved one, or things they appreciated about him. Even today, almost nineteen years later, it still warms my heart when people do that.”
  • “It was all the cards that came every day for the first two months after my husband died. I looked forward to them every day, and the first day without a card was hard.”
  • “What really helped me was when someone told me to focus on my blessings; that they are praying for me, and they care. Or they invited me to go along even if the number was then lopsided. Another thing was when they stopped by for coffee breaks or when they sent a text.”
  • “Widows need encouragement on their anniversary date and on the date their husband died. It means a lot if someone ‘actually’ remembers! A widow’s supper is nice. So is having a secret sister. It helped when someone gave a listening ear and was there to help with the work and the young children. Most of all, I knew people were praying for us.”

What do we say?

We may struggle with what to say to a bereaved friend. After all, we do not want to be like Job’s wife or his friends whose words only increased Job’s suffering. Here are some perspectives:

  • “They need not tell us we are alone now. We know that already.”
  • “Grief may really shake someone’s faith in God, momentarily paralyzing them, especially if they haven’t experienced much trauma before. As much as they long to trust God and accept this new reality in their lives, sometimes it takes time to simply get through the shock and be able to talk to God again. This is okay. They will most likely find healing and deepen their faith, but give them space to struggle, wrestle, and grieve deeply. Listen and try to refrain from “fixing” their faith with words such as “All things work together for good…”, or “At least you…”
  • “Asking a grieving person how they are doing could put them in a difficult position. Asking in a crowd of people may not be the best time. It may be best not to ask unless you really want to know and are willing to take the time to listen.”
  • “It is hard to think rationally in those first hard months. I did not appreciate being asked those first months what I would do for a living. I first needed to process my grief. I was also trying to help my young daughters who were devastated at the loss of their beloved daddy. That decision could wait.”

The following excerpts reveal other struggles with grief:

  • “Everyone grieves differently; there is no right or wrong way. And it never goes away even though all my friends’ lives go on as normal, which is very painful to watch. Holidays are very hard. Attending weddings is almost not doable. This is a couple’s world and only by the grace of God is it possible. Actually, the weeks before the annual anniversary dates are harder than the actual days.”
  • “One thing I realized very quickly was that we live in a very couple-orientated world. At the loss of a spouse, one is left trying to figure out where they fit in. I deeply appreciate, when I’m in a group setting that includes widows and singles, that there are those who try to make me feel included and not the odd one out.”
  • “You can’t put a time limit on grief. It’s different for everyone. There’s no ‘getting over it’ so that it doesn’t hurt anymore. If grieved properly, the wound is not as raw, and it becomes a scar. It’s like getting used to living without an arm or a leg. You adjust to it not being there, but you never stop missing it.”
  • “Death in the family or losing a spouse is harder than one can imagine until they are going through the same thing. I wish we would have had more church support. Our boys need a father figure to follow, one to teach them what a dad would.”
  • “Our children make mistakes as other children do; they need encouragement, not criticism. Also, they could use a helping hand with their work. I wish I would not have needed to leave my youngest child alone so much when I went to work. I broke out in a sweat more than once wondering where the money was coming from to pay the bills, but I thank the Lord that it was always there.”

How can we remember to support the grieving beyond those first days and weeks? We could mark our calendars with the dates of their birthdays, anniversaries, and their loved one’s death date. Then we could designate a certain day of the week to do something for them. If we make a plan, we are more likely to carry out our good intentions.

Finally, we should also remember the “widows who aren’t”. Sometimes there are those among us whose life is racked by a grief worse than that of an actual death. Perhaps there was betrayal, abandonment, incarceration, or suicide in their life’s journey. They may almost envy the clean wound of the “normal” widow. Or they may struggle with guilt on top of their grief.

These situations are often located far outside our comfort zones. There are no easy answers of how to deal with them. But let us not stay aloof from such a sister if we have the opportunity. God will help us find a way to show we care if we ask Him.

As we, and those we love, keep walking with God, may we portray the scene in the final verse of the song mentioned earlier:

“Master, the terror is over, the elements sweetly rest;
Earth’s sun in the calm lake is mirrored,
And heaven’s within my breast.
Linger, O blessed Redeemer,
Leave me alone no more;
And with joy I shall make the blest harbor,
And rest on the blissful shore.”

Let’s conclude with a quote from a widow:

“Walk with them until they can come out of the cave and feel the sunshine again. It may require hard work and getting messy at times, but to them you will be Jesus ‘with skin on’. You are not responsible for their healing; only Jesus can do that. But you can bring them to Him.

Remember the friends that brought the paralyzed man to Jesus, lowering him through the roof. And, behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy; Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee … And Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts? For whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and walk? But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, (then saith he to the sick of the palsy,) Arise, take up thy bed, and go unto thine house. And he arose, and departed to his house. But when the multitudes saw it, they marvelled, and glorified God, which had given such power unto men –Matthew 9:2-8.

What a beautiful picture! In like manner, you can carry your grief-‘paralyzed’ friend to Jesus. Watch them be healed, shoulder their burden of grief, and then move on toward their heavenly home. As we see God doing a work in their heart, we can all praise God together!”

~In this article, the sections in quotation marks were shared with the author by a number of anonymous widows.
