Og David sa: «Hva har jeg nå gjort? Er det ikke en sak?» –1. Samuelsbok 17:29.

Fortellingen om David og Goliat fant sted for over tre årtusener siden og har vært en evig favoritt blant både unge og gamle helt siden da. Det er noe ved den underlegnes kår som vi alle kan kjenne oss igjen i. Kanskje ser vi ubevisst oss selv i en slik situasjon og håper i hemmelighet at vår egen «lykkedag skal komme» på lignende vis. Dessverre virker slik tilfeldig suksess mer som noe fra en Hollywood-produksjon enn fra virkeligheten. Vi ser bare konflikten mellom den unge og den gamle, gjeteren og krigeren, de tunge militære våpnene og slyngen. Men det var noen grunnleggende prinsipper David tok til seg i ungdommen, som gjorde ham til en svært god kandidat for å lykkes. Disse blir imidlertid ofte oversett i vår begeistring for en romantisk seier i siste øyeblikk.

Hvis det eneste bildet vi har av oss selv, kommer fra det sosiale speilet rundt oss, vil vi få en forvrengt indre oppfatning, omtrent som når vi ser oss i et forvrengende speil på et tivoli. De sosiale meningene og oppfatningene i omgivelsene våre gir ofte et klønete og skjevt bilde av oss, både for øynene og ørene våre. Noen ganger er bildet urealistisk positivt og løfter en person fram i medienes øyne, selv om vedkommende viser svært lite heroisk karakter.

Idrettsarenaen er sannsynligvis den største synderen her. De som kan løpe, kaste eller skyte bedre enn alle andre, blir hyllet. Men idrettstalent bidrar lite til deres ekte, grunnleggende verdi som mennesker. Den andre siden av saken byr på en enorm mengde negativ og nedverdigende påvirkning som forsøker å hindre ethvert forsøk på å prøve. Slike kommentarer kommer i strie strømmer fra stressede foreldre, usikre søsken, frustrerte sjefer og en mengde andre bekjente som kjemper for å finne sin identitet i et samfunn der «den sterkeste overlever». Påvirkningen fra disse to leirene er både usammenhengende og ute av proporsjon. Å bli fortalt at man er stor, vil aldri gjøre en stor, like lite som en skur av nedsettende bemerkninger vil skape ydmykhet. Dessverre lar altfor mange av oss disse uforholdsmessige forestillingene påvirke tankegangen vår og stake ut kursen vår.

Den største og mest opphøyde utrustningen mennesket har fått framfor resten av skaperverket, finnes ikke i de fysiske evnene, men i sinnet. De mest intelligente dyrene kan trenes til å være ansvarsfulle, men de kan ikke selv velge eller styre treningen. Men som mennesker kan vi skrive nye programmer for oss selv, helt uavhengig av instinktene våre eller den miljømessige treningen. De av oss som lever i naturlig samsvar med instinktene våre og den påvirkningen vi er blitt formet av, vil knapt heve oss over dyreriket. Men de som vil øve opp og utvikle disse utrustningene, vil på en særskilt måte fylle den rollen Gud har utformet for dem når de møter kjempene. Davids tid og stilling var unik, men prinsippene han tok til seg, var universelle. Hvis jeg kunne lære hunden min å jodle, ville det bevise at hunder kan lære å jodle, og åpne muligheten for at andre også kan gjøre det. På samme måte: Hvis David beseiret Goliat utelukkende ved et mirakel, finnes det ikke noe håp for oss annet enn å sitte og vente på at Gud skal gjøre det samme for oss. Men hvis prinsipper lå til grunn for seieren, har vi et eksempel å følge og en dyd å sikre oss til bruk på vår egen slagmark.

Da David sto opp tidlig den morgenen og tok sekken med korn, brød og ost på skulderen for å bringe den til brødrene sine, ante han ikke hva dagen ville bringe. Herren var hans hyrde, og han led ingen nød, men da han kom fram til stedet, ble han sjokkert over synet. Begge hærene sto på hver sin fjellside og var låst fast i en stillingskrig. Hvis man skulle føre hele hæren ned i dalen og kjempe mot fienden oppoverbakke, ville man være svært ugunstig stilt. Ingen av sidene var villige til å ta den risikoen. Derfor tok filisterne i bruk en vanlig form for krigføring og foreslo at to krigere skulle kjempe i dalen, slik at ingen av sidene fikk noen fordel. Men blant filisterne var det en kjempe som skremte Israels hær. Da David spurte hvorfor ingen ville konfrontere den vanærende gudsbespottelsen fra den vantro, fikk han en skarp irettesettelse av sin eldste bror: … Da flammet Eliabs vrede opp mot David, og han sa: «Hvorfor er du kommet hit ned? Og hvem har du latt de få sauene være igjen hos i ødemarken? Jeg kjenner din stolthet og ditt onde hjerte; du er kommet hit ned for å se på kampen.» David sa: «Hva har jeg nå gjort? Er det ikke en sak?» –1. Samuelsbok 17:28-29.

Med blikket festet på Jesus, troens opphavsmann og fullender, han som for den gleden som ventet ham, utholdt korset og aktet ikke skammen, og som nå sitter ved høyre side av Guds trone –Hebreerne 12:2. Når et menneske har en sak foran seg, kan det holde ut nesten hva som helst. Noen holder ut for en forgjengelig krans. Kong Saul hadde tilbudt skattefri rikdom og status som kongens svigersønn, men den jordiske medgiften lokket ingen frivillige. Mens tanken på jordisk anseelse ikke betydde noe for Davids milde hjerte, ble det tent en brennende nidkjærhet av Goliats gudsbespottelige hån, og David trådte fram i tro. Men tro er ikke bare et innfall som kan blåses opp med en følelsesmessig luftpumpe. For slik kroppen er død uten ånd, slik er også troen død uten gjerninger [handling] –Jakobs brev 2:26. Med saken klart for seg og Gud ved sin side tilbød David seg derfor å kjempe mot Goliat.

David gikk altså fram og handlet etter gudfryktige, ufordervede prinsipper …

Et omsorgsfullt samvittighetsliv har sitt sete i menneskets sjel og avgjør hva vi bryr oss om. Mange mener at samvittigheten bare er nyttig som en begrensende veileder. Men menneskets samvittighet ble også skapt til å virke motsatt. Når vi blir overbevist om at noe er godt og rett, følger vi det med lidenskap. Thomas Edison sa at genialitet er én prosent inspirasjon og 99 prosent svette. Selv om dette kan være sant nok, er det ingen tvil om at inspirasjonen må komme først. Jakobs lengsel etter Rakel fikk ham til å glemme de sju årene med arbeid. Edisons jakt på en fungerende lyspære fikk ham til å glemme de tusenvis av materialene som hadde slått feil.

Tankeløs likegyldighet er det motsatte og er et resultat av en avstumpet samvittighet. David undret seg over at Goliats gudsbespottelige hån ikke fikk Guds hær til å handle. Gi et menneske en grunn til å leve, så vil det finne ut hvordan –Nietzke. Som fange i en nazistisk konsentrasjonsleir under holocaust fikk Victor Frankl i oppdrag å arbeide på sykestuen i leiren, der fangene døde av tyfus. Han la merke til at når et menneske ga opp håpet, fulgte døden snart etter. På samme måte mister mange i vår tid lidenskapen for å overvinne når håpet om personlig vinning svinner i kampen. De fleste arbeidstakere i dag er mer opptatt av lønnsslippen enn av å gjøre en god og verdifull jobb. Når en mann mister følelsene for kona si, tror han ofte at han ikke er i stand til å elske henne. Men en mann med en sunn samvittighet som retter seg etter gudfryktige prinsipper, vil handle kjærlig mot henne uansett hva han føler, eller hvordan hun svarer. Saken vekkes til live og får næring av samvittigheten og legger grunnlaget for handling med lidenskap.

En ærlig forestillingsevne hører til åndens område og drives av samvittigheten vår. Nødvendigheten er oppfinnelsenes mor –Ukjent. Noen venter på at livet skal bli oppdaget, mens andre skaper det mens de går. Dette gir ikke rett til å hevde falske idealer. Davids mål var ærlig, for han var ikke blitt forvrengt av mediene omkring seg. Han hadde hatt framgang mot villdyrene (en løve og en bjørn) i åsene ved Betlehem, og med Guds hjelp var han ikke redd for å kjempe mot en (en krigsmann fra ungdommen av) i Ela-dalen.

Da Saul motvillig samtykker til Davids forslag, går han i gang med å ruste gutten på typisk verdslig vis. Selv om det kan ha vært en ære å bære kongens rustning, ville David ikke ha noe av det: … Jeg kan ikke gå med dette, for jeg har ikke prøvd det. Så tok David det av seg –1. Samuelsbok 17:39, og valgte i stedet fem steiner. Å vite hva andre gjør, og å vite hva man selv bør gjøre, er ikke nødvendigvis det samme.

De skjelvende forestillingene til Israels hær var rotfestet i et hedensk verdisystem. Goliat var ikke problemet; problemet var snarere den troløse frykten og antakelsen om at de måtte føre krigen på verdens premisser. De som omfavner en sann og verdifull sak, vil visselig finne forestillingsevnen til å følge den.

Goliat hadde tatt for gitt at han skulle kjempe på sine egne premisser. Fornærmet og sint roper han: … Kom hit til meg, så skal jeg gi kjøttet ditt til himmelens fugler og markens dyr –1. Samuelsbok 17:44. Som kjempe har han ikke hurtighet og smidighet som sine sterkeste sider, og derfor befaler han David å komme til ham. Men Goliat har grovt overvurdert sine egne evner og undervurdert motstanderen. Ifølge enkelte anslag hadde Davids slynge, med seks eller sju omdreininger i sekundet, en stopeffekt som et 45 mm håndvåpen, og en dyktig slyngers hånd … kunne slynge stein på et hårs bredde og ikke bomme –Dommerne 20:16. Det var ikke uvanlig at de traff fugler i flukt. I ruiner fra oldtiden har man funnet tenger som man tror ble brukt av militæret til å fjerne steiner som hadde satt seg fast i sårede soldater. Hvis Goliat hadde hatt et spyd og David en pistol, ville vi ikke vært så raske til å tro at den største mannen hadde det største overtaket.

Trofast handling er uunngåelig når kroppen vår er underordnet sjelen og ånden, og disse ledes av Guds Ånd. Da står vi fritt til å handle uavhengig av vår natur og andre påvirkninger. Når den dødelige kroppens begjærlige lidenskaper får makt over hjertet og sinnet vårt, er vi beseiret før vi har tatt ett skritt mot fienden. Som kar utformet av Gud, med en fri moralsk vilje, har vi en gudgitt evne til å velge hvordan vi vil handle. Noen tror at det å være proaktiv bare betyr å ta initiativ. Men initiativ alene gjør oss ikke bedre skikket til seier enn det gjorde for sønnene til Skeva. Ønsket om å dominere er ikke edlere enn Goliats hemningsløse raseri etter å ødelegge denne unge oppkomlingen. Adrenalinet strømmet mens han hånte Davids ungdom, trakk forhastede slutninger, lett lot seg fornærme og undret seg over andres uvitenhet.

Men David hadde ikke et slikt reaktivt oppdrag. Hans mål var at hele jorden skulle vite at det finnes en Gud i Israel. Og hele denne forsamlingen skal vite at Herren ikke frelser med sverd og spyd … –1. Samuelsbok 17:47. Trofast handling må være rettet mot å gi det du har, snarere enn å skaffe deg det du ikke har. Hvis livet fører med seg bekymringer utenfor vår evne til å forandre dem, er det nytteløst å vie dem oppmerksomhet. Josef kunne ikke forandre brødrenes mottakelse, bedraget fra sin herres kone, isolasjonen i fengselet eller munnskjenkens vrangforestillinger. Gjeterguttens tro lærer oss å slutte å sørge over det vi gjerne ville vært, og begynne å være det vi burde være. Vi må slutte å lete etter et mirakel og begynne å se etter en mulighet. Det handler ikke om å overvinne usannsynlige odds, men om hvordan vi reagerer på en trafikkork, et ulydig barn, en rasende kunde eller en krevende ektefelle. Det handler om å ta eierskap til en sak som er stor nok til å dempe egoistiske reaksjoner og vekke barmhjertig handling.

Hvorfor døde japanske kamikazepiloter for en tapt sak under andre verdenskrig? Hvorfor sprenger muslimske terrorister seg selv i luften? Hvorfor avlegger katolske prester og nonner løfter om sølibat og fattigdom? Finnes det ikke en sak for den kristne som strekker seg bredere og dypere enn denne verdens kjemper? Finnes det ikke en sak som vekker forestillingsevnen vår og helliger handlingene våre? Eller finnes det ikke engang én som forvandler det dagligdagse arbeidet vårt til en kanal for nåde i tjenesten for universets konge? Hvordan ville historien ha vært annerledes hvis Isai hadde tilbrakt pensjonisttilværelsen sin slik de eldre i vår tid gjør? Gud feller kjemper gjennom de redskapene vi stiller til rådighet for ham, fra Dorkas’ nål … til Jaels teltplugg, fra Sebedeus’ båter brukt i virksomheten … til sønnene som lå ham nær.

Shamgar hadde en oksedrivers stav;
David hadde en slynge;
Dorkas hadde en nål;
Rahab hadde en snor;
Samson hadde et kjevebein;
Moses hadde en stav;
Maria hadde salve;
Og alt ble brukt for Gud!

One day you may be walking along a seashore. You glance back to watch your footprints disappear with the next surge of foaming water. You love to hear the soothing swish of the breakers. You gaze at the graceful sweep of shoreline and glittering ocean way out to the horizon. Life is good.

Suddenly a huge wave sweeps in and lifts you off your feet. You struggle and flail to regain your footing. Or the wave may even carry you farther and slam you against a rock wall, leaving you stunned and gasping in pain.

This wave may be called grief, as expressed in the following stanza from the song by Mary A. Baker.

Master, with anguish of spirit
I bow in my grief today;
The depths of my sad heart are troubled;
Oh, waken and save, I pray!
Torrents of sin and of anguish
Sweep o’er my sinking soul!
And I perish! I perish, dear Master;
Oh hasten, and take control.

In the past year, many of us have lost loved ones. Perhaps it was a childhood friend, or someone from our church family, or even from our immediate family. Depending on how close we were, we felt drops, splashes, or even tidal waves of grief.

Our grief stems from the relationship we shared. We have invested in each other’s lives to some degree. We have loved, but now that love has nowhere to go. We could say that grief is the price of love.

Here is how one widow described grief: “At the sudden and untimely death of my husband, the feeling was one of overwhelming shock, disbelief, and even panic, as I faced an uncertain future without him at the age of 51. Looking back, I realize how merciful God is to allow us to be in a certain state of numbness and shock at a time like this, allowing the reality to sink in more slowly.”

How did she cope? She says, “I am also awed at how He provides the grace and strength to go through hard things in life that we never thought we would have to face. He walks with us as we go through the valley of grief, so we are never walking alone. The journey of grief is not the same for everyone. It is not over in a few months. For me, I still cried a year later. It took a long time for the pain to fade and for life to become meaningful again. But praise God, that time does come! It is best not to look too far into the future. We walk one day at a time with Jesus, knowing that the best is yet to come.”

Here are more experiences from those who have been there:

  • “I am still learning that when we say, ‘It’s all right, Lord,’ we need to leave it there, at Jesus’ feet.”
  • “Grieving people are very lonely, but there’s also an aloneness that comes from not having a place to belong. You may be in a room of people, and still feel utterly alone, because you’ve lost your sense of belonging, or your category of belonging has changed.”
  • “The presence of a grieving person can be painful for others. It’s a reminder that “bad” things can happen. So, at times they are not invited, which is painful. A grieving person wants to be invited, but at times when included they feel their lack of belonging anew and think they should have stayed at home. Most times, casual conversation can be difficult for them when their world has been violently shaken. Their hearts are heavy while the mood of others is lighthearted, making them feel even more despondent. Understandably, many people don’t know what to do when they see others grieving, so they default to doing nothing and walk away. Many friendships are lost after a loss, which is even more painful.”
  • “God was so close. He was always there. ‘Underneath are the everlasting arms’, and I felt them.”

God can use sorrow and grief to teach us what we might not learn in happier times. We learn to depend on Him. We think of the seriousness of life. We learn to embrace eternal values and anticipate heaven. We are motivated to cherish the loved ones we still have when we hear expressions such as this: “Looking back, I wish we would not have taken the time we had together for granted. I wish I would have recognized his personality traits as strengths rather than things that annoyed.”

Those who lose loved ones often find themselves in the limelight for a time. Many people want to know how they are responding, especially when the death is an unusual situation. Consider the experience of Elizabeth Elliot and the four others who were made widows in 1956 by jungle killers in Ecuador. Or think of Marie Troyer whose husband John was murdered by guerrillas in Guatemala in 1981, or the mothers of the girls killed in Nickel Mines, Pennsylvania in 2006.

These women found themselves in the glare of an almost worldwide spotlight. Their greatest opportunity to display God’s enabling grace likely came at a time when they wanted it least. But their responses of forgiveness, unselfishness, and trust in God amazed the world, at least considering the amount of media attention. Truly, A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid –Matthew 5:14.

While we and those we know will hardly face that level of exposure, we too have a unique platform to display God’s grace. We may never have a better opportunity to touch hardened or seeking hearts than in our own hour of grief.

When we hear that people have indeed been drawn to God through the death of our loved one, it can be a source of comfort and meaning. This death was not a senseless tragedy; it was meant to bring glory to God. In other words, God does not waste our sorrows.

It reminds us of Jesus’ words about Lazarus when he said, …This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God might be glorified thereby –John 11:4. Jesus is our perfect example for relating to those in sorrow. He came to Mary and Martha and listened. He cried with them even though He knew He could and then did transform the whole situation by raising Lazarus.

How do we help?

What is our part in helping a grieving sister glorify God in the midst of her situation? Consider the thoughts shared by the following widows:

  • “What helped was when a dear sister sat with me and told me she cared. And in her quietness, I could feel that her love was real.”
  • “Grief is surprising and unexpected. The person may be having a good day when they hear a song, smell a certain scent, or see a familiar article of clothing which triggers a memory followed by a flood of tears. If this happens when you’re with them, it’s okay. Tears are okay. Tears are healing. Stay present and help them through it. Press in; grieve with them. It’s better to err in doing something than in doing nothing. You may not understand. That’s okay. You don’t need to experience loss to show that you care.”
  • “Grief is exhausting and mentally debilitating. So don’t just ask what you can do; look for a need they may have and try to fill it. For example, ‘I’d like to come over Tuesday evening and fix your faucet’ or ‘We’d like to come and bring a meal if you’re up to it?’”
  • “One thing that meant a lot to me was when people shared pleasant memories of our loved one, or things they appreciated about him. Even today, almost nineteen years later, it still warms my heart when people do that.”
  • “It was all the cards that came every day for the first two months after my husband died. I looked forward to them every day, and the first day without a card was hard.”
  • “What really helped me was when someone told me to focus on my blessings; that they are praying for me, and they care. Or they invited me to go along even if the number was then lopsided. Another thing was when they stopped by for coffee breaks or when they sent a text.”
  • “Widows need encouragement on their anniversary date and on the date their husband died. It means a lot if someone ‘actually’ remembers! A widow’s supper is nice. So is having a secret sister. It helped when someone gave a listening ear and was there to help with the work and the young children. Most of all, I knew people were praying for us.”

What do we say?

We may struggle with what to say to a bereaved friend. After all, we do not want to be like Job’s wife or his friends whose words only increased Job’s suffering. Here are some perspectives:

  • “They need not tell us we are alone now. We know that already.”
  • “Grief may really shake someone’s faith in God, momentarily paralyzing them, especially if they haven’t experienced much trauma before. As much as they long to trust God and accept this new reality in their lives, sometimes it takes time to simply get through the shock and be able to talk to God again. This is okay. They will most likely find healing and deepen their faith, but give them space to struggle, wrestle, and grieve deeply. Listen and try to refrain from “fixing” their faith with words such as “All things work together for good…”, or “At least you…”
  • “Asking a grieving person how they are doing could put them in a difficult position. Asking in a crowd of people may not be the best time. It may be best not to ask unless you really want to know and are willing to take the time to listen.”
  • “It is hard to think rationally in those first hard months. I did not appreciate being asked those first months what I would do for a living. I first needed to process my grief. I was also trying to help my young daughters who were devastated at the loss of their beloved daddy. That decision could wait.”

The following excerpts reveal other struggles with grief:

  • “Everyone grieves differently; there is no right or wrong way. And it never goes away even though all my friends’ lives go on as normal, which is very painful to watch. Holidays are very hard. Attending weddings is almost not doable. This is a couple’s world and only by the grace of God is it possible. Actually, the weeks before the annual anniversary dates are harder than the actual days.”
  • “One thing I realized very quickly was that we live in a very couple-orientated world. At the loss of a spouse, one is left trying to figure out where they fit in. I deeply appreciate, when I’m in a group setting that includes widows and singles, that there are those who try to make me feel included and not the odd one out.”
  • “You can’t put a time limit on grief. It’s different for everyone. There’s no ‘getting over it’ so that it doesn’t hurt anymore. If grieved properly, the wound is not as raw, and it becomes a scar. It’s like getting used to living without an arm or a leg. You adjust to it not being there, but you never stop missing it.”
  • “Death in the family or losing a spouse is harder than one can imagine until they are going through the same thing. I wish we would have had more church support. Our boys need a father figure to follow, one to teach them what a dad would.”
  • “Our children make mistakes as other children do; they need encouragement, not criticism. Also, they could use a helping hand with their work. I wish I would not have needed to leave my youngest child alone so much when I went to work. I broke out in a sweat more than once wondering where the money was coming from to pay the bills, but I thank the Lord that it was always there.”

How can we remember to support the grieving beyond those first days and weeks? We could mark our calendars with the dates of their birthdays, anniversaries, and their loved one’s death date. Then we could designate a certain day of the week to do something for them. If we make a plan, we are more likely to carry out our good intentions.

Finally, we should also remember the “widows who aren’t”. Sometimes there are those among us whose life is racked by a grief worse than that of an actual death. Perhaps there was betrayal, abandonment, incarceration, or suicide in their life’s journey. They may almost envy the clean wound of the “normal” widow. Or they may struggle with guilt on top of their grief.

These situations are often located far outside our comfort zones. There are no easy answers of how to deal with them. But let us not stay aloof from such a sister if we have the opportunity. God will help us find a way to show we care if we ask Him.

As we, and those we love, keep walking with God, may we portray the scene in the final verse of the song mentioned earlier:

“Master, the terror is over, the elements sweetly rest;
Earth’s sun in the calm lake is mirrored,
And heaven’s within my breast.
Linger, O blessed Redeemer,
Leave me alone no more;
And with joy I shall make the blest harbor,
And rest on the blissful shore.”

Let’s conclude with a quote from a widow:

“Walk with them until they can come out of the cave and feel the sunshine again. It may require hard work and getting messy at times, but to them you will be Jesus ‘with skin on’. You are not responsible for their healing; only Jesus can do that. But you can bring them to Him.

Remember the friends that brought the paralyzed man to Jesus, lowering him through the roof. And, behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy; Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee … And Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts? For whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and walk? But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, (then saith he to the sick of the palsy,) Arise, take up thy bed, and go unto thine house. And he arose, and departed to his house. But when the multitudes saw it, they marvelled, and glorified God, which had given such power unto men –Matthew 9:2-8.

What a beautiful picture! In like manner, you can carry your grief-‘paralyzed’ friend to Jesus. Watch them be healed, shoulder their burden of grief, and then move on toward their heavenly home. As we see God doing a work in their heart, we can all praise God together!”

~In this article, the sections in quotation marks were shared with the author by a number of anonymous widows.

एक दिन शायद आप समुद्र-तट पर टहल रहे हों। आप पीछे मुड़कर देखते हैं कि झागदार पानी की अगली लहर के साथ आपके पैरों के निशान मिट जाते हैं। लहरों की शांतिदायक सरसराहट सुनना आपको अच्छा लगता है। आप तटरेखा के सुंदर घुमाव और दूर क्षितिज तक चमकते समुद्र को निहारते हैं। जीवन अच्छा है।

अचानक एक विशाल लहर आकर आपको पैरों से उखाड़ देती है। आप संभलकर खड़े होने के लिए संघर्ष करते और हाथ-पैर मारते हैं। या फिर लहर आपको और दूर ले जाकर चट्टान की दीवार से पटक सकती है, जिससे आप स्तब्ध रह जाते हैं और दर्द से हाँफने लगते हैं।

इस लहर को शोक कहा जा सकता है, जैसा कि मैरी ए. बेकर के गीत के निम्नलिखित पद में व्यक्त किया गया है।

स्वामी, मन की व्याकुलता लिए
आज शोक में झुकती हूँ मैं;
मेरे दुखी हृदय की गहराइयाँ व्याकुल हैं;
ओह, जागिए और बचाइए, यही विनती है!
पाप और पीड़ा की धाराएँ
मेरी डूबती आत्मा को बहा ले जाती हैं!
और मैं नष्ट हो रही हूँ! मैं नष्ट हो रही हूँ, प्रिय स्वामी;
ओह, शीघ्र आइए और नियंत्रण संभालिए।

पिछले वर्ष, हममें से बहुतों ने अपने प्रियजनों को खोया है। शायद वह बचपन का कोई मित्र था, या हमारे कलीसिया-परिवार का कोई सदस्य, या यहाँ तक कि हमारे निकटतम परिवार का कोई सदस्य। हम उनके कितने करीब थे, इसके अनुसार हमने शोक की बूँदें, छींटे या यहाँ तक कि ज्वारीय लहरें महसूस कीं।

हमारा शोक उस रिश्ते से उपजता है जो हमारे बीच था। हमने किसी न किसी रूप में एक-दूसरे के जीवन में अपना निवेश किया है। हमने प्रेम किया है, लेकिन अब उस प्रेम को व्यक्त करने का कोई ठिकाना नहीं रहा। हम कह सकते हैं कि शोक प्रेम की कीमत है।

एक विधवा ने शोक का वर्णन इस तरह किया: “मेरे पति की अचानक और असमय मृत्यु पर, मुझे भारी सदमे, अविश्वास और यहाँ तक कि घबराहट का अनुभव हुआ, क्योंकि 51 वर्ष की आयु में मुझे उनके बिना अनिश्चित भविष्य का सामना करना पड़ा। पीछे मुड़कर देखती हूँ, तो समझती हूँ कि परमेश्वर कितना दयालु है कि ऐसे समय में वह हमें सुन्नता और सदमे की एक अवस्था में रहने देता है, जिससे वास्तविकता धीरे-धीरे मन में उतर सके।”

उसने इस स्थिति का सामना कैसे किया? वह कहती है, “मैं इस बात से भी विस्मित हूँ कि वह जीवन की कठिन बातों से गुज़रने के लिए अनुग्रह और सामर्थ्य कैसे प्रदान करता है—ऐसी बातों से जिनका सामना करने की हमने कभी कल्पना भी नहीं की थी। जब हम शोक की घाटी से गुज़रते हैं, तो वह हमारे साथ चलता है, इसलिए हम कभी अकेले नहीं चलते। शोक की यात्रा हर किसी के लिए एक जैसी नहीं होती। यह कुछ महीनों में समाप्त नहीं होती। मेरे लिए, एक साल बाद भी आँसू बहते थे। दर्द के कम होने और जीवन के फिर से अर्थपूर्ण होने में बहुत समय लगा। लेकिन परमेश्वर की स्तुति हो, वह समय सचमुच आता है! भविष्य में बहुत दूर तक देखने की कोशिश न करना ही अच्छा है। हम यीशु के साथ एक-एक दिन करके चलते हैं और जानते हैं कि सबसे अच्छा अभी आना बाकी है।”

यहाँ उन लोगों के कुछ और अनुभव दिए गए हैं जो इस दौर से गुज़रे हैं:

  • “मैं अब भी यह सीख रही हूँ कि जब हम कहते हैं, ‘प्रभु, सब ठीक है,’ तो हमें बात वहीं छोड़ देनी चाहिए—यीशु के चरणों में।”
  • “शोक से गुज़र रहे लोग बहुत अकेले होते हैं, लेकिन अपनापन महसूस करने की जगह न होने से भी एक तरह का अकेलापन पैदा होता है। आप लोगों से भरे कमरे में हो सकते हैं, फिर भी पूरी तरह अकेला महसूस कर सकते हैं, क्योंकि अपनापन होने का एहसास खो गया है, या अपनापन पाने का आपका दायरा बदल गया है।”
  • “शोक में डूबे व्यक्ति की मौजूदगी दूसरों के लिए पीड़ादायक हो सकती है। यह याद दिलाती है कि ‘बुरी’ बातें हो सकती हैं। इसलिए कभी-कभी उन्हें बुलाया नहीं जाता, जो पीड़ादायक है। शोक में डूबा व्यक्ति बुलाया जाना चाहता है, लेकिन कभी-कभी शामिल किए जाने पर भी उसे फिर से अपनापन न होने का एहसास होता है और वह सोचता है कि उसे घर पर ही रहना चाहिए था। अक्सर, जब उसकी दुनिया हिंसक रूप से हिल गई हो, तो उसके लिए सामान्य बातचीत करना कठिन हो सकता है। दूसरे लोगों का मन हल्का-फुल्का होता है, जबकि उसका हृदय बोझिल होता है, जिससे वह और भी निराश महसूस करता है। यह समझ में आता है कि दूसरों को शोक में देखकर बहुत-से लोग नहीं जानते कि क्या करें, इसलिए वे कुछ न करने का रास्ता चुनते हैं और चले जाते हैं। किसी प्रियजन को खोने के बाद कई मित्रताएँ टूट जाती हैं, जो और भी अधिक पीड़ादायक है।”
  • “परमेश्वर बहुत निकट था। वह हमेशा वहाँ मौजूद था। ‘नीचे अनन्त भुजाएँ हैं,’ और मैंने उन्हें महसूस किया।”

परमेश्वर दुःख और शोक का उपयोग हमें वे बातें सिखाने के लिए कर सकता है जिन्हें हम अधिक सुखद समय में शायद न सीखें। हम उस पर निर्भर रहना सीखते हैं। हम जीवन की गंभीरता के बारे में सोचते हैं। हम अनन्त मूल्यों को अपनाना और स्वर्ग की बाट जोहना सीखते हैं। जब हम इस तरह की बातें सुनते हैं, तो हमारे भीतर उन प्रियजनों को सँजोने की प्रेरणा मिलती है जो अब भी हमारे साथ हैं: “पीछे मुड़कर देखती हूँ, तो चाहती हूँ कि हमने साथ बिताए समय को हल्के में न लिया होता। काश, मैंने उसके व्यक्तित्व के गुणों को उन बातों के बजाय खूबियाँ समझा होता जो मुझे खटकती थीं।”

प्रियजनों को खोने वाले लोग अक्सर कुछ समय के लिए सबकी निगाहों के केंद्र में आ जाते हैं। बहुत-से लोग जानना चाहते हैं कि वे कैसी प्रतिक्रिया दे रहे हैं, खासकर जब मृत्यु किसी असामान्य परिस्थिति में हुई हो। एलिज़ाबेथ इलियट और उन चार अन्य महिलाओं के अनुभव पर विचार करें जो 1956 में इक्वाडोर के जंगलों में हत्यारों के हाथों अपने पतियों को खोकर विधवा हो गईं। या मैरी ट्रॉयर के बारे में सोचें, जिनके पति जॉन की 1981 में ग्वाटेमाला में गुरिल्लाओं ने हत्या कर दी थी, या 2006 में पेन्सिल्वेनिया के निकल माइन्स में मारी गई लड़कियों की माताओं के बारे में।

इन महिलाओं ने खुद को लगभग पूरी दुनिया की निगाहों की चकाचौंध में पाया। परमेश्वर के सामर्थ्यकारी अनुग्रह को दिखाने का उनका सबसे बड़ा अवसर शायद ऐसे समय आया जब वे उसे सबसे कम चाहती थीं। लेकिन क्षमा, निस्वार्थता और परमेश्वर पर भरोसे से भरी उनकी प्रतिक्रियाओं ने दुनिया को अचंभित कर दिया—कम-से-कम मीडिया का जितना ध्यान उन्हें मिला, उसके लिहाज़ से। सचमुच, पहाड़ी पर बसा नगर छिप नहीं सकता—मत्ती 5:14।

हालाँकि हम और हमारे जान-पहचान के लोग शायद ही कभी इतनी अधिक सार्वजनिक निगाहों का सामना करेंगे, फिर भी हमारे पास परमेश्वर के अनुग्रह को दिखाने का एक अनोखा अवसर है। अपने शोक के समय से बेहतर अवसर शायद हमें कठोर या खोज में लगे हृदयों को छूने के लिए कभी न मिले।

जब हम सुनते हैं कि हमारे प्रियजन की मृत्यु के कारण वास्तव में लोग परमेश्वर की ओर खिंचे आए हैं, तो इससे सांत्वना और अर्थ मिल सकता है। यह मृत्यु कोई निरर्थक त्रासदी नहीं थी; इसका उद्देश्य परमेश्वर की महिमा लाना था। दूसरे शब्दों में, परमेश्वर हमारे दुःखों को व्यर्थ नहीं जाने देता।

यह हमें लाज़र के बारे में यीशु के शब्द याद दिलाता है, जब उसने कहा, …यह बीमारी मृत्यु के लिए नहीं, बल्कि परमेश्वर की महिमा के लिए है, ताकि इसके द्वारा परमेश्वर के पुत्र की महिमा हो—यूहन्ना 11:4। शोक में पड़े लोगों के साथ व्यवहार करने में यीशु हमारा सिद्ध उदाहरण है। वह मरियम और मार्था के पास आया और उनकी बात सुनी। वह उनके साथ रोया, जबकि वह जानता था कि वह पूरी परिस्थिति को बदल सकता है—और फिर उसने लाज़र को जिलाकर ऐसा किया।

हम कैसे सहायता करें?

अपनी परिस्थिति के बीच परमेश्वर की महिमा करने में शोकाकुल बहन की सहायता करने में हमारी क्या भूमिका है? निम्नलिखित विधवाओं के विचारों पर ध्यान दें:

  • “जब एक प्रिय बहन मेरे पास बैठी और उसने कहा कि उसे मेरी परवाह है, तो उससे मुझे सहायता मिली। और उसकी शांत उपस्थिति में मैं महसूस कर सकी कि उसका प्रेम सच्चा था।”
  • “शोक अप्रत्याशित होता है और चौंका देता है। किसी का दिन अच्छा जा रहा हो, तभी कोई गीत सुनना, कोई खास खुशबू महसूस करना या कपड़ों की कोई जानी-पहचानी चीज़ देखना कोई याद जगा सकता है, और फिर आँसुओं की बाढ़ आ सकती है। अगर आपके साथ होते हुए ऐसा हो, तो कोई बात नहीं। आँसू ठीक हैं। आँसू चंगाई देते हैं। उसके साथ बने रहें और इस दौर से गुज़रने में उसकी मदद करें। उसके पास रहें; उसके साथ शोक करें। कुछ करने में गलती करना, कुछ भी न करने से बेहतर है। शायद आप समझ न पाएँ। कोई बात नहीं। परवाह दिखाने के लिए आपको स्वयं किसी क्षति का अनुभव करना ज़रूरी नहीं।”
  • “शोक थका देने वाला होता है और मानसिक रूप से निष्क्रिय कर देता है। इसलिए सिर्फ़ यह मत पूछिए कि आप क्या कर सकते हैं; उनकी किसी ज़रूरत को पहचानने की कोशिश कीजिए और उसे पूरा कीजिए। उदाहरण के लिए, ‘मैं मंगलवार शाम आपके यहाँ आकर नल ठीक करना चाहूँगा’ या ‘अगर आप ठीक महसूस कर रहे हों, तो हम खाना लेकर आना चाहेंगे।’”
  • “एक बात जो मेरे लिए बहुत मायने रखती थी, वह थी लोगों का हमारे प्रियजन की अच्छी यादें साझा करना, या उसके बारे में वे बातें बताना जिनकी वे क़द्र करते थे। आज भी, लगभग उन्नीस साल बाद, जब लोग ऐसा करते हैं तो मेरा दिल गर्माहट से भर जाता है।”
  • “मेरे पति की मृत्यु के बाद पहले दो महीनों तक हर दिन जो कार्ड आते रहे, वे सभी मेरे लिए बहुत मायने रखते थे। मैं हर दिन उनका इंतज़ार करती थी, और जिस पहले दिन कोई कार्ड नहीं आया, वह कठिन था।”
  • “जिस बात से मुझे सचमुच मदद मिली, वह थी किसी का मुझे अपनी आशीषों पर ध्यान देने के लिए कहना; यह बताना कि वे मेरे लिए प्रार्थना कर रहे हैं और उन्हें मेरी परवाह है। या उन्होंने मुझे अपने साथ चलने का निमंत्रण दिया, भले ही तब संख्या बराबर न रहती। एक और बात यह थी कि वे कॉफ़ी के लिए मिलने आ जाते थे या संदेश भेजते थे।”
  • “विधवाओं को अपनी शादी की सालगिरह और अपने पति की मृत्यु की तारीख पर हौसला-अफ़ज़ाई की ज़रूरत होती है। अगर कोई सचमुच याद रखे, तो यह बहुत मायने रखता है! विधवाओं के लिए भोज अच्छा रहता है। एक गुप्त बहन का होना भी अच्छा है। जब किसी ने मेरी बात ध्यान से सुनी और कामकाज तथा छोटे बच्चों की देखभाल में सहायता के लिए मौजूद रहा, तो उससे मदद मिली। सबसे बढ़कर, मैं जानती थी कि लोग हमारे लिए प्रार्थना कर रहे हैं।”

हम क्या कहें?

शोकाकुल मित्र से क्या कहें, यह सोचकर हम उलझन में पड़ सकते हैं। आख़िरकार, हम अय्यूब की पत्नी या उसके मित्रों जैसे नहीं बनना चाहते, जिनकी बातों ने अय्यूब की पीड़ा और बढ़ा दी। यहाँ कुछ विचार दिए गए हैं:

  • “उन्हें हमें यह बताने की ज़रूरत नहीं कि अब हम अकेले हैं। यह बात हमें पहले से मालूम है।”
  • “शोक किसी के परमेश्वर पर विश्वास को सचमुच झकझोर सकता है और उसे कुछ समय के लिए निष्क्रिय कर सकता है, खासकर अगर उसने पहले बहुत अधिक आघात न झेले हों। वे जितना परमेश्वर पर भरोसा रखना और अपने जीवन की इस नई वास्तविकता को स्वीकार करना चाहते हैं, कभी-कभी सदमे से उबरने और परमेश्वर से फिर बात कर पाने में ही समय लगता है। यह ठीक है। संभवतः उन्हें चंगाई मिलेगी और उनका विश्वास गहरा होगा, लेकिन उन्हें संघर्ष करने, जूझने और गहराई से शोक करने की जगह दें। सुनें और ‘सब बातें मिलकर भलाई ही को उत्पन्न करती हैं…’ या ‘कम-से-कम तुम्हारे पास…’ जैसी बातें कहकर उनके विश्वास को ‘ठीक’ करने से बचने की कोशिश करें।”
  • “शोक में डूबे व्यक्ति से यह पूछना कि वह कैसा है, उसे कठिन स्थिति में डाल सकता है। लोगों की भीड़ में पूछना शायद सबसे अच्छा समय न हो। शायद तब तक न पूछना बेहतर है, जब तक आप सचमुच जानना न चाहें और सुनने के लिए समय देने को तैयार न हों।”
  • “शुरुआती कठिन महीनों में तर्कसंगत ढंग से सोचना मुश्किल होता है। उन शुरुआती महीनों में मुझसे यह पूछे जाने पर कि मैं गुज़ारे के लिए क्या करूँगी, मुझे अच्छा नहीं लगा। पहले मुझे अपने शोक को समझने की ज़रूरत थी। मैं अपनी छोटी बेटियों की मदद करने की कोशिश भी कर रही थी, जो अपने प्यारे पिता को खोकर टूट गई थीं। उस फैसले के लिए इंतज़ार किया जा सकता था।”

निम्नलिखित अंश शोक से जुड़े दूसरे संघर्षों को उजागर करते हैं:

  • “हर कोई अलग तरह से शोक करता है; इसका कोई सही या गलत तरीका नहीं है। और यह कभी पूरी तरह दूर नहीं होता, भले ही मेरे सभी मित्रों का जीवन सामान्य रूप से चलता रहे—यह देखना बहुत पीड़ादायक है। छुट्टियाँ बहुत कठिन होती हैं। शादियों में जाना लगभग असंभव लगता है। यह दंपतियों की दुनिया है और केवल परमेश्वर के अनुग्रह से ही इसमें जाना संभव है। सच कहूँ, हर साल आने वाली सालगिरह की तारीखों से पहले के सप्ताह उन असली तारीखों से भी कठिन होते हैं।”
  • “मुझे बहुत जल्दी एहसास हुआ कि हम ऐसी दुनिया में रहते हैं जो बहुत हद तक जोड़ों के इर्द-गिर्द बनी है। जीवनसाथी को खोने पर इंसान यह समझने की कोशिश में रह जाता है कि अब वह कहाँ फिट बैठता है। जब मैं ऐसे समूह में होती हूँ जिसमें विधवाएँ और अविवाहित लोग शामिल हों, तो मैं उन लोगों की बहुत क़द्र करती हूँ जो मुझे शामिल महसूस कराने और अलग-थलग न पड़ने देने की कोशिश करते हैं।”
  • “शोक के लिए कोई समय-सीमा तय नहीं की जा सकती। हर किसी के लिए यह अलग होता है। ऐसा नहीं है कि इससे ‘उबर’ जाने पर फिर दर्द नहीं होगा। अगर शोक ठीक से किया जाए, तो घाव उतना कच्चा नहीं रहता और निशान बन जाता है। यह बिना हाथ या पैर के जीने की आदत डालने जैसा है। आप उसके न होने के साथ तालमेल बिठा लेते हैं, लेकिन उसकी कमी महसूस करना कभी बंद नहीं करते।”
  • “परिवार में मृत्यु या जीवनसाथी को खोना, जब तक स्वयं उसी से न गुज़रें, कल्पना से भी अधिक कठिन है। काश, हमें कलीसिया से अधिक सहारा मिला होता। हमारे लड़कों को अनुसरण करने के लिए पिता-जैसे किसी व्यक्ति की ज़रूरत है, जो उन्हें वह सिखाए जो पिता सिखाता।”
  • “हमारे बच्चे भी दूसरे बच्चों की तरह गलतियाँ करते हैं; उन्हें आलोचना नहीं, हौसला-अफ़ज़ाई चाहिए। उन्हें अपने कामकाज में मदद की भी ज़रूरत पड़ सकती है। काश, काम पर जाने के दौरान मुझे अपने सबसे छोटे बच्चे को इतना अकेला न छोड़ना पड़ता। बिल चुकाने के पैसे कहाँ से आएँगे, यह सोचकर एक से अधिक बार मुझे पसीना छूट गया, लेकिन मैं प्रभु का धन्यवाद करती हूँ कि पैसे हमेशा मिल जाते थे।”

हम उन शुरुआती दिनों और हफ्तों के बाद भी शोकाकुल लोगों का साथ देना कैसे याद रख सकते हैं? हम उनके जन्मदिनों, सालगिरहों और उनके प्रियजन की मृत्यु की तारीखों को अपने कैलेंडर में लिख सकते हैं। फिर हम सप्ताह का कोई खास दिन उनके लिए कुछ करने के लिए तय कर सकते हैं। अगर हम योजना बनाएँ, तो अपनी नेक मंशा को पूरा करने की संभावना अधिक होगी।

आख़िर में, हमें उन “विधवाओं” को भी याद रखना चाहिए जिनके पति मरे नहीं हैं। कभी-कभी हमारे बीच ऐसे लोग होते हैं जिनका जीवन वास्तविक मृत्यु से भी अधिक गहरे शोक से अस्त-व्यस्त हो जाता है। शायद उनके जीवन की यात्रा में विश्वासघात, परित्याग, कारावास या आत्महत्या हुई हो। उन्हें शायद “सामान्य” विधवा के साफ़ घाव से भी ईर्ष्या हो। या वे अपने शोक के साथ-साथ अपराधबोध से भी जूझ रहे हों।

अक्सर ये परिस्थितियाँ हमारे सहजता के दायरे से बहुत बाहर होती हैं। उनसे निपटने के कोई आसान जवाब नहीं हैं। लेकिन अगर हमें अवसर मिले, तो आइए ऐसी बहन से दूर न रहें। यदि हम परमेश्वर से माँगें, तो वह हमें परवाह दिखाने का रास्ता खोजने में मदद करेगा।

जब हम और हमारे प्रियजन परमेश्वर के साथ चलते रहें, तो आइए पहले बताए गए गीत के अंतिम पद का दृश्य हमारे जीवन में दिखाई दे:

“स्वामी, भय अब समाप्त हुआ, सृष्टि के तत्व मधुर शांति में हैं;
शांत झील में धरती का सूरज प्रतिबिंबित है,
और स्वर्ग मेरे हृदय में है।
ठहरिए, हे धन्य उद्धारकर्ता,
अब मुझे फिर कभी अकेला न छोड़िए;
और आनन्द से मैं उस धन्य बंदरगाह तक पहुँचूँगी,
और आनंदमय तट पर विश्राम करूँगी।”

आइए, एक विधवा के उद्धरण के साथ समाप्त करें:

“जब तक वे गुफा से बाहर आकर फिर से धूप महसूस न कर सकें, तब तक उनके साथ चलते रहें। कभी-कभी इसके लिए कठिन परिश्रम करना और मुश्किल हालात में उनके साथ शामिल होना पड़ सकता है, लेकिन उनके लिए आप ‘त्वचा पहने यीशु’ होंगे। उनकी चंगाई की ज़िम्मेदारी आपकी नहीं है; यह केवल यीशु कर सकता है। लेकिन आप उन्हें उसके पास ला सकते हैं।

उन मित्रों को याद कीजिए जो लकवे के मारे व्यक्ति को यीशु के पास लाए और उसे छत से नीचे उतारा। और देखो, लोग एक लकवे के मारे हुए मनुष्य को खाट पर लिटाकर उसके पास लाए; और यीशु ने उनका विश्वास देखकर उस लकवे के मारे हुए से कहा, हे पुत्र, ढाढ़स बाँध; तेरे पाप क्षमा हुए… और यीशु ने उनके विचार जानकर कहा, तुम अपने मन में बुरी बातें क्यों सोचते हो? क्योंकि कौन-सी बात कहना अधिक आसान है: तेरे पाप क्षमा हुए, या उठ और चल? परन्तु इसलिए कि तुम जानो कि मनुष्य के पुत्र को पृथ्वी पर पाप क्षमा करने का अधिकार है (तब उसने लकवे के मारे हुए से कहा), उठ, अपनी खाट उठा और अपने घर चला जा। और वह उठकर अपने घर चला गया। यह देखकर भीड़ चकित हुई और परमेश्वर की महिमा करने लगी, जिसने मनुष्यों को ऐसा अधिकार दिया है—मत्ती 9:2-8।

कितना सुंदर दृश्य है! इसी तरह, आप अपने शोक से ‘लकवाग्रस्त’ मित्र को यीशु के पास ले जा सकते हैं। उन्हें चंगा होते देखें, उनके शोक का बोझ अपने कंधों पर उठाएँ, और फिर उनके स्वर्गीय घर की ओर आगे बढ़ें। जब हम परमेश्वर को उनके हृदय में काम करते देखते हैं, तो हम सब मिलकर परमेश्वर की स्तुति कर सकते हैं!”

~इस लेख में उद्धरण चिह्नों के भीतर दिए गए अंश कई गुमनाम विधवाओं ने लेखिका के साथ साझा किए थे।

One day you may be walking along a seashore. You glance back to watch your footprints disappear with the next surge of foaming water. You love to hear the soothing swish of the breakers. You gaze at the graceful sweep of shoreline and glittering ocean way out to the horizon. Life is good.

Suddenly a huge wave sweeps in and lifts you off your feet. You struggle and flail to regain your footing. Or the wave may even carry you farther and slam you against a rock wall, leaving you stunned and gasping in pain.

This wave may be called grief, as expressed in the following stanza from the song by Mary A. Baker.

Master, with anguish of spirit
I bow in my grief today;
The depths of my sad heart are troubled;
Oh, waken and save, I pray!
Torrents of sin and of anguish
Sweep o’er my sinking soul!
And I perish! I perish, dear Master;
Oh hasten, and take control.

In the past year, many of us have lost loved ones. Perhaps it was a childhood friend, or someone from our church family, or even from our immediate family. Depending on how close we were, we felt drops, splashes, or even tidal waves of grief.

Our grief stems from the relationship we shared. We have invested in each other’s lives to some degree. We have loved, but now that love has nowhere to go. We could say that grief is the price of love.

Here is how one widow described grief: “At the sudden and untimely death of my husband, the feeling was one of overwhelming shock, disbelief, and even panic, as I faced an uncertain future without him at the age of 51. Looking back, I realize how merciful God is to allow us to be in a certain state of numbness and shock at a time like this, allowing the reality to sink in more slowly.”

How did she cope? She says, “I am also awed at how He provides the grace and strength to go through hard things in life that we never thought we would have to face. He walks with us as we go through the valley of grief, so we are never walking alone. The journey of grief is not the same for everyone. It is not over in a few months. For me, I still cried a year later. It took a long time for the pain to fade and for life to become meaningful again. But praise God, that time does come! It is best not to look too far into the future. We walk one day at a time with Jesus, knowing that the best is yet to come.”

Here are more experiences from those who have been there:

  • “I am still learning that when we say, ‘It’s all right, Lord,’ we need to leave it there, at Jesus’ feet.”
  • “Grieving people are very lonely, but there’s also an aloneness that comes from not having a place to belong. You may be in a room of people, and still feel utterly alone, because you’ve lost your sense of belonging, or your category of belonging has changed.”
  • “The presence of a grieving person can be painful for others. It’s a reminder that “bad” things can happen. So, at times they are not invited, which is painful. A grieving person wants to be invited, but at times when included they feel their lack of belonging anew and think they should have stayed at home. Most times, casual conversation can be difficult for them when their world has been violently shaken. Their hearts are heavy while the mood of others is lighthearted, making them feel even more despondent. Understandably, many people don’t know what to do when they see others grieving, so they default to doing nothing and walk away. Many friendships are lost after a loss, which is even more painful.”
  • “God was so close. He was always there. ‘Underneath are the everlasting arms’, and I felt them.”

God can use sorrow and grief to teach us what we might not learn in happier times. We learn to depend on Him. We think of the seriousness of life. We learn to embrace eternal values and anticipate heaven. We are motivated to cherish the loved ones we still have when we hear expressions such as this: “Looking back, I wish we would not have taken the time we had together for granted. I wish I would have recognized his personality traits as strengths rather than things that annoyed.”

Those who lose loved ones often find themselves in the limelight for a time. Many people want to know how they are responding, especially when the death is an unusual situation. Consider the experience of Elizabeth Elliot and the four others who were made widows in 1956 by jungle killers in Ecuador. Or think of Marie Troyer whose husband John was murdered by guerrillas in Guatemala in 1981, or the mothers of the girls killed in Nickel Mines, Pennsylvania in 2006.

These women found themselves in the glare of an almost worldwide spotlight. Their greatest opportunity to display God’s enabling grace likely came at a time when they wanted it least. But their responses of forgiveness, unselfishness, and trust in God amazed the world, at least considering the amount of media attention. Truly, A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid –Matthew 5:14.

While we and those we know will hardly face that level of exposure, we too have a unique platform to display God’s grace. We may never have a better opportunity to touch hardened or seeking hearts than in our own hour of grief.

When we hear that people have indeed been drawn to God through the death of our loved one, it can be a source of comfort and meaning. This death was not a senseless tragedy; it was meant to bring glory to God. In other words, God does not waste our sorrows.

It reminds us of Jesus’ words about Lazarus when he said, …This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God might be glorified thereby –John 11:4. Jesus is our perfect example for relating to those in sorrow. He came to Mary and Martha and listened. He cried with them even though He knew He could and then did transform the whole situation by raising Lazarus.

How do we help?

What is our part in helping a grieving sister glorify God in the midst of her situation? Consider the thoughts shared by the following widows:

  • “What helped was when a dear sister sat with me and told me she cared. And in her quietness, I could feel that her love was real.”
  • “Grief is surprising and unexpected. The person may be having a good day when they hear a song, smell a certain scent, or see a familiar article of clothing which triggers a memory followed by a flood of tears. If this happens when you’re with them, it’s okay. Tears are okay. Tears are healing. Stay present and help them through it. Press in; grieve with them. It’s better to err in doing something than in doing nothing. You may not understand. That’s okay. You don’t need to experience loss to show that you care.”
  • “Grief is exhausting and mentally debilitating. So don’t just ask what you can do; look for a need they may have and try to fill it. For example, ‘I’d like to come over Tuesday evening and fix your faucet’ or ‘We’d like to come and bring a meal if you’re up to it?’”
  • “One thing that meant a lot to me was when people shared pleasant memories of our loved one, or things they appreciated about him. Even today, almost nineteen years later, it still warms my heart when people do that.”
  • “It was all the cards that came every day for the first two months after my husband died. I looked forward to them every day, and the first day without a card was hard.”
  • “What really helped me was when someone told me to focus on my blessings; that they are praying for me, and they care. Or they invited me to go along even if the number was then lopsided. Another thing was when they stopped by for coffee breaks or when they sent a text.”
  • “Widows need encouragement on their anniversary date and on the date their husband died. It means a lot if someone ‘actually’ remembers! A widow’s supper is nice. So is having a secret sister. It helped when someone gave a listening ear and was there to help with the work and the young children. Most of all, I knew people were praying for us.”

What do we say?

We may struggle with what to say to a bereaved friend. After all, we do not want to be like Job’s wife or his friends whose words only increased Job’s suffering. Here are some perspectives:

  • “They need not tell us we are alone now. We know that already.”
  • “Grief may really shake someone’s faith in God, momentarily paralyzing them, especially if they haven’t experienced much trauma before. As much as they long to trust God and accept this new reality in their lives, sometimes it takes time to simply get through the shock and be able to talk to God again. This is okay. They will most likely find healing and deepen their faith, but give them space to struggle, wrestle, and grieve deeply. Listen and try to refrain from “fixing” their faith with words such as “All things work together for good…”, or “At least you…”
  • “Asking a grieving person how they are doing could put them in a difficult position. Asking in a crowd of people may not be the best time. It may be best not to ask unless you really want to know and are willing to take the time to listen.”
  • “It is hard to think rationally in those first hard months. I did not appreciate being asked those first months what I would do for a living. I first needed to process my grief. I was also trying to help my young daughters who were devastated at the loss of their beloved daddy. That decision could wait.”

The following excerpts reveal other struggles with grief:

  • “Everyone grieves differently; there is no right or wrong way. And it never goes away even though all my friends’ lives go on as normal, which is very painful to watch. Holidays are very hard. Attending weddings is almost not doable. This is a couple’s world and only by the grace of God is it possible. Actually, the weeks before the annual anniversary dates are harder than the actual days.”
  • “One thing I realized very quickly was that we live in a very couple-orientated world. At the loss of a spouse, one is left trying to figure out where they fit in. I deeply appreciate, when I’m in a group setting that includes widows and singles, that there are those who try to make me feel included and not the odd one out.”
  • “You can’t put a time limit on grief. It’s different for everyone. There’s no ‘getting over it’ so that it doesn’t hurt anymore. If grieved properly, the wound is not as raw, and it becomes a scar. It’s like getting used to living without an arm or a leg. You adjust to it not being there, but you never stop missing it.”
  • “Death in the family or losing a spouse is harder than one can imagine until they are going through the same thing. I wish we would have had more church support. Our boys need a father figure to follow, one to teach them what a dad would.”
  • “Our children make mistakes as other children do; they need encouragement, not criticism. Also, they could use a helping hand with their work. I wish I would not have needed to leave my youngest child alone so much when I went to work. I broke out in a sweat more than once wondering where the money was coming from to pay the bills, but I thank the Lord that it was always there.”

How can we remember to support the grieving beyond those first days and weeks? We could mark our calendars with the dates of their birthdays, anniversaries, and their loved one’s death date. Then we could designate a certain day of the week to do something for them. If we make a plan, we are more likely to carry out our good intentions.

Finally, we should also remember the “widows who aren’t”. Sometimes there are those among us whose life is racked by a grief worse than that of an actual death. Perhaps there was betrayal, abandonment, incarceration, or suicide in their life’s journey. They may almost envy the clean wound of the “normal” widow. Or they may struggle with guilt on top of their grief.

These situations are often located far outside our comfort zones. There are no easy answers of how to deal with them. But let us not stay aloof from such a sister if we have the opportunity. God will help us find a way to show we care if we ask Him.

As we, and those we love, keep walking with God, may we portray the scene in the final verse of the song mentioned earlier:

“Master, the terror is over, the elements sweetly rest;
Earth’s sun in the calm lake is mirrored,
And heaven’s within my breast.
Linger, O blessed Redeemer,
Leave me alone no more;
And with joy I shall make the blest harbor,
And rest on the blissful shore.”

Let’s conclude with a quote from a widow:

“Walk with them until they can come out of the cave and feel the sunshine again. It may require hard work and getting messy at times, but to them you will be Jesus ‘with skin on’. You are not responsible for their healing; only Jesus can do that. But you can bring them to Him.

Remember the friends that brought the paralyzed man to Jesus, lowering him through the roof. And, behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy; Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee … And Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts? For whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and walk? But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, (then saith he to the sick of the palsy,) Arise, take up thy bed, and go unto thine house. And he arose, and departed to his house. But when the multitudes saw it, they marvelled, and glorified God, which had given such power unto men –Matthew 9:2-8.

What a beautiful picture! In like manner, you can carry your grief-‘paralyzed’ friend to Jesus. Watch them be healed, shoulder their burden of grief, and then move on toward their heavenly home. As we see God doing a work in their heart, we can all praise God together!”

~In this article, the sections in quotation marks were shared with the author by a number of anonymous widows.

Siku moja huenda ukawa unatembea kando ya ufuo wa bahari. Unageuka nyuma kutazama nyayo zako zikifutwa na wimbi linalofuata la maji yenye povu. Unapenda kusikia sauti tulivu ya mawimbi yakivunjika ufukweni. Unatazama kwa kuvutiwa ukingo wa ufuo unaopinda kwa uzuri na bahari inayong’aa hadi mbali kwenye upeo wa macho. Maisha ni mazuri.

Ghafla wimbi kubwa linaingia kwa nguvu na kukuinua kutoka ardhini. Unahangaika na kupapasa-papasa ili usimame tena. Au wimbi hilo linaweza hata kukupeleka mbali zaidi na kukugonga kwenye ukuta wa mwamba, na kukuacha ukiwa umepigwa na butwaa na ukipumua kwa shida kwa sababu ya maumivu.

Wimbi hili linaweza kuitwa huzuni ya msiba, kama inavyoelezwa katika ubeti ufuatao wa wimbo wa Mary A. Baker.

Bwana, kwa uchungu wa roho yangu
Nainama katika maombolezo yangu leo;
Vilindi vya moyo wangu wenye huzuni vimetatizwa;
Ee, amka uniokoe, nakuomba!
Mafuriko ya dhambi na uchungu
Yanaifagia nafsi yangu inayozama!
Ninaangamia! Ninaangamia, Bwana mpendwa;
Ee, fanya haraka, uchukue udhibiti.

Mwaka uliopita, wengi wetu tumepoteza wapendwa wetu. Huenda alikuwa rafiki wa utotoni, au mtu wa familia yetu ya kanisa, au hata mtu wa familia yetu ya karibu. Kutegemea jinsi tulivyokuwa karibu, tulihisi matone, mipulizo ya maji, au hata mawimbi makubwa ya huzuni ya msiba.

Huzuni yetu ya msiba inatokana na uhusiano tuliokuwa nao. Kwa kiasi fulani tumeshiriki katika maisha ya kila mmoja wetu. Tumependa, lakini sasa upendo huo hauna pa kuelekezwa. Tunaweza kusema kwamba huzuni ya msiba ni gharama ya upendo.

Hivi ndivyo mjane mmoja alivyoeleza huzuni ya msiba: “Mume wangu alipokufa ghafla na kabla ya wakati wake, nilihisi mshtuko mkubwa sana, kutokuamini, na hata hofu, nilipokabili wakati ujao usio na uhakika bila yeye nikiwa na umri wa miaka 51. Ninapotazama nyuma, ninatambua jinsi Mungu alivyo na rehema kwa kuturuhusu kuwa katika hali fulani ya kufa ganzi na mshtuko wakati kama huu, akiruhusu ukweli uzidi kutuingia polepole.”

Alikabilianaje na hali hiyo? Anasema, “Pia ninastaajabishwa na jinsi Anavyotoa neema na nguvu za kustahimili mambo magumu maishani ambayo hatukuwahi kufikiri tungelazimika kukabiliana nayo. Anatembea pamoja nasi tunapopita katika bonde la huzuni ya msiba, kwa hiyo hatutembei peke yetu kamwe. Safari ya huzuni ya msiba si sawa kwa kila mtu. Haimaliziki baada ya miezi michache. Kwangu mimi, bado nililia mwaka mmoja baadaye. Ilichukua muda mrefu kwa maumivu kupungua na kwa maisha kuwa na maana tena. Lakini Mungu asifiwe, wakati huo hufika! Ni bora kutotazama mbali sana katika wakati ujao. Tunatembea siku moja baada ya nyingine pamoja na Yesu, tukijua kwamba yaliyo bora bado yanakuja.”

Haya hapa ni mambo mengine waliyopitia wale ambao wamewahi kukabili hali hiyo:

  • “Bado ninajifunza kwamba tunaposema, ‘Ni sawa, Bwana,’ tunahitaji kuliachia hapo, miguuni pa Yesu.”
  • “Watu waliofiwa huhisi upweke sana, lakini pia kuna upweke unaotokana na kutokuwa na mahali pa kujihisi kuwa sehemu yake. Unaweza kuwa katika chumba chenye watu, na bado ukahisi upweke kabisa, kwa sababu umepoteza hisia ya kuwa sehemu ya kundi fulani, au kundi ulilokuwa sehemu yake limebadilika.”
  • “Kuwepo kwa mtu aliye katika huzuni ya msiba kunaweza kuwaumiza wengine. Ni ukumbusho kwamba mambo ‘mabaya’ yanaweza kutokea. Kwa hiyo nyakati nyingine hawaalikwi, jambo ambalo linaumiza. Mtu aliye katika huzuni ya msiba hutaka kualikwa, lakini nyakati nyingine anapojumuishwa, huhisi tena kwamba si sehemu ya kundi na kufikiri kwamba alipaswa kubaki nyumbani. Mara nyingi, mazungumzo ya kawaida yanaweza kuwa magumu kwake wakati ulimwengu wake umetikiswa vikali. Mioyo yao ni mizito huku wengine wakiwa na furaha, na hilo huwafanya wakate tamaa hata zaidi. Inaeleweka kwamba watu wengi hawajui la kufanya wanapowaona wengine wakiwa katika huzuni ya msiba, kwa hiyo huishia kutofanya lolote na kuondoka. Urafiki mwingi hupotea baada ya kufiwa, jambo ambalo linaumiza zaidi.”
  • “Mungu alikuwa karibu sana. Alikuwepo daima. ‘Mikono ya milele iko chini yetu,’ nami niliihisi.”

Mungu anaweza kutumia huzuni na majonzi kutufundisha mambo ambayo huenda tusingejifunza nyakati zenye furaha zaidi. Tunajifunza kumtegemea. Tunatafakari uzito wa maisha. Tunajifunza kukumbatia mambo yenye thamani ya milele na kutarajia mbinguni. Tunachochewa kuwathamini wapendwa ambao bado tunao tunaposikia maneno kama haya: “Ninapotazama nyuma, natamani tusingechukulia kirahisi muda tuliokuwa pamoja. Natamani ningetambua sifa zake za tabia kuwa nguvu badala ya mambo yaliyoniudhi.”

Wale wanaopoteza wapendwa wao mara nyingi hujikuta wakiwa kwenye uangalizi wa umma kwa muda. Watu wengi hutaka kujua wanakabilianaje na hali hiyo, hasa kifo kinapotokea katika mazingira yasiyo ya kawaida. Fikiria yaliyowapata Elizabeth Elliot na wanawake wengine wanne waliokuwa wajane mwaka 1956 baada ya waume zao kuuawa na wauaji wa msituni nchini Ekuado. Au mfikirie Marie Troyer, ambaye mume wake John aliuawa na wapiganaji wa msituni nchini Guatemala mwaka 1981, au mama za wasichana waliouawa huko Nickel Mines, Pennsylvania, mwaka 2006.

Wanawake hawa walijikuta wakitazamwa sana na watu karibu kote ulimwenguni. Pengine fursa yao kubwa zaidi ya kuonyesha neema ya Mungu inayowatia nguvu ilikuja wakati ambao hawakuitaka kabisa. Lakini jinsi walivyosamehe, walivyojinyima na kumtumaini Mungu kuliushangaza ulimwengu, angalau kutokana na jinsi vyombo vya habari vilivyolipa jambo hilo uzito. Hakika, Mji uliowekwa juu ya kilima hauwezi kufichwa –Mathayo 5:14.

Ingawa sisi na wale tunaowajua huenda tusikabili kiwango hicho cha kuangaziwa, sisi pia tuna jukwaa la kipekee la kuonyesha neema ya Mungu. Huenda tusipate kamwe fursa bora zaidi ya kugusa mioyo iliyofanywa migumu au inayomtafuta Mungu kuliko katika saa yetu wenyewe ya huzuni ya msiba.

Tunaposikia kwamba kwa kweli watu wamevutwa kwa Mungu kupitia kifo cha mpendwa wetu, hilo linaweza kuwa chanzo cha faraja na maana. Kifo hiki hakikuwa msiba usio na maana; kilikusudiwa kumletea Mungu utukufu. Kwa maneno mengine, Mungu hapotezi bure huzuni zetu.

Hilo linatukumbusha maneno ya Yesu kuhusu Lazaro aliposema, …Ugonjwa huu si wa mauti, bali ni kwa ajili ya utukufu wa Mungu, ili Mwana wa Mungu atukuzwe kwa huo –Yohana 11:4. Yesu ndiye mfano wetu mkamilifu wa jinsi ya kuhusiana na walio na huzuni na jinsi ya kuitikia huzuni yao. Alikuja kwa Mariamu na Martha akawasikiliza. Alilia pamoja nao ingawa alijua kwamba angeweza na kisha alifanya hivyo kubadili hali nzima kwa kumfufua Lazaro.

Tunawezaje kusaidia?

Jukumu letu ni nini katika kumsaidia dada aliye katika huzuni ya msiba kumtukuza Mungu katikati ya hali yake? Tafakari mawazo yaliyoshirikishwa na wajane wafuatao:

  • “Kilichonisaidia ni dada mpendwa kukaa pamoja nami na kuniambia kwamba ananijali. Na katika ukimya wake, niliweza kuhisi kwamba upendo wake ulikuwa wa kweli.”
  • “Huzuni ya msiba huja bila kutarajiwa na hushangaza. Mtu anaweza kuwa na siku nzuri anaposikia wimbo, kunusa harufu fulani, au kuona nguo anayoifahamu ambayo huamsha kumbukumbu na kufuatiwa na machozi mengi. Hilo likitokea mkiwa pamoja, ni sawa. Kulia ni sawa. Machozi huleta uponyaji. Kaa naye na umsaidie apitie hali hiyo. Mkaribie; huzunika pamoja naye. Ni bora kukosea kwa kufanya jambo fulani kuliko kutofanya lolote. Huenda usielewe. Ni sawa. Huhitaji wewe mwenyewe kufiwa ili kuonyesha kwamba unajali.”
  • “Huzuni ya msiba huchosha na kudhoofisha uwezo wa kufikiri. Kwa hiyo usiulize tu unachoweza kufanya; tafuta hitaji ambalo huenda analo na ujaribu kulitosheleza. Kwa mfano, ‘Ningependa kuja jioni ya Jumanne kutengeneza bomba lako’ au ‘Tungependa kuja na kukuletea chakula ikiwa utakuwa tayari?’”
  • “Jambo moja lililonifanya nijisikie vizuri sana ni watu kushiriki kumbukumbu nzuri za mpendwa wetu, au mambo waliyothamini kumhusu. Hata leo, karibu miaka kumi na tisa baadaye, moyo wangu bado huchangamka watu wanapofanya hivyo.”
  • “Kadi zote zilizokuja kila siku kwa miezi miwili ya kwanza baada ya mume wangu kufariki ndizo zilizonisaidia. Nilizitarajia kila siku, na siku ya kwanza ambayo sikupokea kadi ilikuwa ngumu.”
  • “Kilichonisaidia sana ni mtu kuniambia niangazie baraka zangu; kwamba wananiombea na wanajali. Au walinialika niende pamoja nao hata kama idadi yetu haikuwa sawa pande zote. Jambo jingine lilikuwa walipopita kwa ajili ya mapumziko ya kahawa au walipotuma ujumbe mfupi.”
  • “Wajane wanahitaji kutiwa moyo siku ya kumbukumbu ya ndoa yao na siku ambayo mume wao alikufa. Ina maana kubwa mtu ‘anakumbuka kweli’! Chakula cha jioni cha wajane ni kizuri. Vivyo hivyo kuwa na dada wa siri. Nilisaidiwa mtu aliponisikiliza na kuwepo kunisaidia kazi na watoto wadogo. Zaidi ya yote, nilijua watu walikuwa wakituombea.”

Tuseme nini?

Huenda tukahangaika kujua la kumwambia rafiki aliyefiwa. Hata hivyo, hatutaki kuwa kama mke wa Ayubu au marafiki zake, ambao maneno yao yaliongeza tu mateso ya Ayubu. Haya hapa ni baadhi ya mitazamo:

  • “Hawahitaji kutuambia kwamba sasa tuko peke yetu. Tunajua hilo tayari.”
  • “Huzuni ya msiba inaweza kweli kutikisa imani ya mtu kwa Mungu, na kumfanya ashindwe kutenda kwa muda, hasa ikiwa hajawahi kupitia kiwewe kikubwa hapo awali. Ingawa anatamani sana kumtumaini Mungu na kuukubali ukweli huu mpya maishani mwake, nyakati nyingine huchukua muda kupita tu mshtuko huo na kuweza kuzungumza tena na Mungu. Hilo ni sawa. Uwezekano mkubwa atapata uponyaji na kuimarisha imani yake, lakini mpe nafasi ya kuhangaika, kushindana na hali hiyo, na kuomboleza kwa kina. Msikilize na ujaribu kujizuia ‘kurekebisha’ imani yake kwa maneno kama ‘Mambo yote hufanya kazi pamoja kwa wema…’ au ‘Angalau wewe…’”
  • “Kumuuliza mtu aliye katika huzuni ya msiba anaendeleaje kunaweza kumweka katika hali ngumu. Kumuuliza mbele ya kundi la watu huenda isiwe wakati mzuri zaidi. Huenda ni bora usiulize isipokuwa unataka kweli kujua na uko tayari kuchukua muda wa kusikiliza.”
  • “Ni vigumu kufikiri kwa busara katika miezi hiyo migumu ya kwanza. Sikufurahia kuulizwa katika miezi hiyo ya kwanza nitafanya kazi gani ili kujikimu. Kwanza nilihitaji kupitia huzuni yangu ya msiba. Pia nilikuwa nikijaribu kuwasaidia binti zangu wadogo ambao walikuwa wamehuzunika sana kwa kumpoteza baba yao mpendwa. Uamuzi huo ungeweza kusubiri.”

Dondoo zifuatazo zinaonyesha changamoto nyingine za huzuni ya msiba:

  • “Kila mtu huomboleza kwa namna tofauti; hakuna njia iliyo sahihi au isiyo sahihi. Na huzuni hiyo haiondoki kamwe, ingawa maisha ya marafiki zangu wote yanaendelea kama kawaida, jambo ambalo linaumiza sana kutazama. Sikukuu huwa ngumu sana. Kuhudhuria harusi karibu haiwezekani. Huu ni ulimwengu wa wanandoa, na ni kwa neema ya Mungu tu kwamba inawezekana. Kwa kweli, majuma kabla ya siku za kila mwaka za kumbukumbu huwa magumu zaidi kuliko siku zenyewe.”
  • “Jambo moja nililotambua haraka sana ni kwamba tunaishi katika ulimwengu unaowajali sana wanandoa. Mtu anapompoteza mwenzi wake, hubaki akijaribu kujua anafaa wapi. Ninathamini sana ninapokuwa katika kundi linalojumuisha wajane na watu wasio kwenye ndoa, na kuna watu wanaojitahidi kunifanya nijihisi nimejumuishwa wala si mtu wa pekee asiyeendana na wengine.”
  • “Huwezi kuweka kikomo cha muda kwa huzuni ya msiba. Ni tofauti kwa kila mtu. Hakuna ‘kuishinda’ ili isiendelee kuuma tena. Mtu akiomboleza ipasavyo, jeraha huwa si bichi sana, na hubaki kovu. Ni kama kuzoea kuishi bila mkono au mguu. Unazoea kutokuwepo kwake, lakini humwachi kamwe kumkosa.”
  • “Kifo katika familia au kumpoteza mwenzi ni jambo gumu zaidi kuliko mtu anavyoweza kuwazia mpaka yeye mwenyewe apitie hali hiyo. Natamani tungepata msaada zaidi kutoka kanisani. Wavulana wetu wanahitaji mtu wa kuwa mfano wa baba wa kumfuata, mtu wa kuwafundisha mambo ambayo baba angefundisha.”
  • “Watoto wetu hufanya makosa kama watoto wengine; wanahitaji kutiwa moyo, si kukosolewa. Pia, wanaweza kusaidiwa katika kazi zao. Natamani nisingelazimika kumwacha mtoto wangu mdogo peke yake mara nyingi nilipoenda kazini. Zaidi ya mara moja nilitokwa na jasho jingi nikijiuliza pesa za kulipa bili zingetoka wapi, lakini namshukuru Bwana kwamba zilikuwepo daima.”

Tunawezaje kukumbuka kuwategemeza walio katika huzuni ya msiba baada ya siku na majuma hayo ya kwanza? Tunaweza kuandika kwenye kalenda zetu tarehe za siku zao za kuzaliwa, kumbukumbu za ndoa zao na tarehe ya kifo cha mpendwa wao. Kisha tunaweza kuchagua siku fulani ya juma ya kuwafanyia jambo fulani. Tukipanga, kuna uwezekano mkubwa zaidi wa kutimiza nia zetu njema.

Mwisho, tunapaswa pia kuwakumbuka “wajane ambao si wajane”. Nyakati nyingine kuna watu miongoni mwetu ambao maisha yao yamekumbwa na huzuni kubwa kuliko ile ya kifo halisi. Huenda katika safari ya maisha yao kulikuwa na usaliti, kuachwa, kufungwa gerezani, au kujiua. Huenda karibu wakauonea wivu uchungu ulio wazi na unaoeleweka wa mjane wa “kawaida”. Au huenda wakahangaika na hatia pamoja na huzuni yao ya msiba.

Mara nyingi hali hizi ziko mbali sana na maeneo tunayojisikia vizuri. Hakuna majibu rahisi ya jinsi ya kukabiliana nazo. Lakini tusikae mbali na dada wa namna hiyo ikiwa tuna fursa ya kumsaidia. Mungu atatusaidia kupata njia ya kuonyesha kwamba tunajali tukimwomba.

Tunapoendelea kutembea pamoja na Mungu, sisi na wale tunaowapenda, na tuweze kuonyesha taswira iliyo katika ubeti wa mwisho wa wimbo uliotajwa mapema:

“Bwana, hofu imekwisha, nguvu za asili zimetulia kwa utulivu;
Jua linaakisiwa katika ziwa tulivu,
Na mbingu imo kifuani mwangu.
Kaa nami, Ee Mkombozi mwenye baraka,
Usiniache peke yangu tena;
Kwa furaha nitafika kwenye bandari yenye baraka,
Na kupumzika kwenye ufuo wenye furaha.”

Tumalizie kwa nukuu kutoka kwa mjane mmoja:

“Tembea pamoja nao mpaka waweze kutoka pangoni na kuhisi tena mwangaza wa jua. Huenda ikahitaji jitihada kubwa na nyakati nyingine kujitia katika hali ngumu, lakini kwao utakuwa Yesu ‘aliyevaa ngozi’. Huwajibiki kwa uponyaji wao; Yesu pekee ndiye awezaye kufanya hivyo. Lakini unaweza kuwaongoza kwake.

Kumbuka marafiki waliompeleka Yesu mtu aliyepooza, wakimshusha kupitia kwenye paa. Na tazama, wakamletea mtu aliyepooza, amelala kitandani; Yesu alipoiona imani yao akamwambia yule aliyepooza, Jipe moyo, mwanangu; umesamehewa dhambi zako… Yesu akijua mawazo yao akasema, Mbona mnawaza maovu mioyoni mwenu? Kwa maana ni lipi lililo rahisi, kusema, Umesamehewa dhambi zako; au kusema, Inuka, tembea? Lakini mpate kujua ya kwamba Mwana wa Adamu anayo mamlaka duniani kusamehe dhambi, (akamwambia yule aliyepooza,) Inuka, chukua kitanda chako, uende nyumbani kwako. Akaondoka, akaenda nyumbani kwake. Makutano walipoona hayo, walistaajabu, wakamtukuza Mungu aliyewapa wanadamu mamlaka kama hayo –Mathayo 9:2-8.

Ni taswira nzuri kama nini! Vivyo hivyo, unaweza kumpeleka Yesu rafiki yako ‘aliyepooza’ kwa huzuni ya msiba. Waangalie wanapoponywa, ubebe mzigo wao wa huzuni ya msiba, kisha uendelee nao katika safari kuelekea makao yao ya mbinguni. Tunapomwona Mungu akifanya kazi mioyoni mwao, sote tunaweza kumsifu Mungu pamoja!”

~Katika makala hii, sehemu zilizo ndani ya alama za nukuu zilishirikishwa na mwandishi na wajane kadhaa ambao hawakutaka majina yao yajulikane.
