And David said, What have I now done? Is there not a cause? –1 Samuel 17:29.

The story of David and Goliath took place over three millenniums ago and has been a perennial favorite of the young and old ever since. There is something about the plight of the underdog that we all relate to. Perhaps we subconsciously view ourselves in such odds and secretly hope that there will come a day when our own “ship will come in” in a similar fashion. Unfortunately, that sort of random success seems more akin to a Hollywood production than to real life. We see only the conflict between the young and the old, the shepherd and the warrior, and the heavy military weapons and the sling. Yet there were some preliminary principles that David embraced in his youth that made him a prime candidate for success. But these often go unheralded in our love for a climactic romantic victory.

If the only vision we have of ourselves comes from the social mirror about us, we will carry a warped inner perception similar to what we see as we glance into a trick mirror at a carnival. The social opinions and perceptions of our environment often cast an awkward and skewed description of our person before our eyes and ears. Sometimes it is unrealistically positive, building the person up in the eyes of the media when there is very little heroic character displayed.

The sports arena is probably the biggest offender in this. The individuals are praised who can run, throw, or shoot better than everyone else. But sporting talent adds little to their honest pure worth as a human. The other side of the coin produces an immense amount of negative and degrading input that seeks to thwart any effort to try. These comments are produced in copious showers by stressed parents, insecure siblings, frustrated bosses, and a host of other acquaintances struggling for identity in a “survival of the fittest” society. The input from these two camps is both disjointed, and out of proportion. To be told you are great will never produce greatness any more than a barrage of derogatory remarks will produce humility. Unfortunately, too often many of us allow these disproportionate projections to affect our thinking and chart our course.

The greatest and superior endowment given to mankind over the rest of creation is not found in his physical abilities, but in his mind. The most intelligent of animals can be trained to be responsible, but they cannot choose or direct that training. But as humans, we can write new programs for ourselves totally independent of our instincts or environmental training. Those of us who live in natural accordance with our instincts and conditioning, will scarcely rise above the animal kingdom. But those who will exercise and develop those endowments shall uniquely fill the role God has designed for them in their encounter with the giants. While David’s time and position were unique, the principles he embraced were universal. If I could teach my dog to yodel, it would prove that yodeling is achievable for dogs and open the possibility for others to do it too. Likewise, if David defeated Goliath by miracle alone, then there is no hope for us but to sit and wait for God to do the same for us. However, if principles were at the core of the victory, then there is an example for us to follow and a virtue to secure for use on our own battlefield.

As David arose early that morning and shouldered his pack of corn, bread, and cheese to take to his brothers, he had no idea what the day would bring forth. The Lord was his Shepherd, and he had no lack, but as he came upon the scene he was shocked at the sight. Both armies were positioned on opposite mountains and locked in a stalemate. To take your entire army down into the valley and fight the opposition uphill would leave you at a tremendous disadvantage. One that neither side was willing to risk. So, the Philistines evoked a common dimension of warfare proposing that two warriors would fight in the valley giving no advantage to either side. But the Philistines had a giant among their numbers that terrified the army of Israel. As David inquired into the situation as to why no one would confront the reproachful blasphemies of the infidel, he was met with a stiff rebuke from his oldest brother: …and Eliab’s anger was kindled against David, and he said, Why camest thou down hither? and with whom hast thou left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart; for thou art come down that thou mightest see the battle. And David said, What have I now done? Is there not a cause? –1 Samuel 17:28-29.

Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God –Hebrews 12:2. When a man has a cause set before him, he can endure almost anything. Some endure for a corruptible crown. King Saul had offered tax exempt wealth and son-in-law status, but the earthly dowry elicited no volunteers. While the thought of earthly prominence meant nothing to the tender heart of David, there was a jealous fire kindled by the blasphemous taunts of Goliath and he stepped forward by faith. But faith is not just a whim that may be inflated by an emotional tire pump. For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works [action] is dead also –James 2:26. Thus, with the cause clearly before him, and his God beside him, David offers to fight Goliath.

So David moved forward acting according to godly, uncorrupted principles…

A Caring Conscience is seated in the soul of man and determines what we care about. Many think that a conscience is only useful as a limiting guide. But the human conscience was also created to function in the reverse. When we are convicted that something is good and right, we pursue it with a passion. Thomas Edison said that genius is 1% inspiration and 99% perspiration. While this may be true enough, it is without question that the inspiration must arrive first. Jacob’s aspirations for Rachael made him forget the seven years of labor. Edison’s pursuit of a successful light bulb caused him to forget the thousands of elements that had failed.

Careless apathy is the opposite and is the result of a seared conscience. David was amazed that the blasphemous taunts of Goliath produced no cause for action on the part of God’s army. Give a man a reason to live and he will supply the how –Nietzke. As a holocaust prisoner in a Nazi concentration camp, Victor Frankl was commissioned to labor in the ward of the camp where prisoners were dying of typhus. He observed that when a person gave up hope, death was soon to follow. Likewise, for many of our day, when the hope of personal gain evaporates in the fray, so does the passion to overcome. Most workers today are more concerned about their paycheck than of doing a good and worthy job. Often when a man loses his feelings for his wife, he believes that he is incapable of loving her, but a man with a healthy conscience toward godly principles will act in loving fashion toward her regardless of his feelings or her response. The cause is aroused and fueled by the conscience and lays the foundation for passionate action.

An Honest Imagination belongs to the realm of the spirit and is driven by our conscience. Necessity is the mother of invention –Unknown. Some are waiting for life to be discovered while others are inventing it as they go. This is not a license to claim false ideals. David’s pursuit is honest for he was not warped by the media about him. He has met with success over the beasts (a lion and a bear) in the hills of Bethlehem and with God’s help, incurs no fear of contending with one (a man of war from his youth) in the valley of Elah.

As Saul reluctantly consents to David’s proposal, he proceeds to arm the lad in typical worldly fashion. While it may have been an honor to wear the armor of the king, David would have none of it: …I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them. And David put them off him –1 Samuel 17:39, choosing five stones instead. Knowing what others do and knowing what to do are not necessarily the same thing.

The cowering beliefs of the Israelite army were rooted in a pagan value system. Goliath was not the problem, but rather, faithless fear and the assumption that they needed to engage in the warfare on the terms of the world. Those that embrace a true and worthy cause will surely find the imagination to pursue it.

Goliath had automatically assumed that he would be in combat under his own terms. Insulted and angered he cries out: …Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field –1 Samuel 17:44. As a giant, speed and agility are not his forte and so he orders David to come to him. But Goliath has grossly overestimated his personal ability and underestimated his foe. According to some estimates, at six or seven revolutions per second, David’s sling had the stopping power of a 45 mm handgun, and the hand of a skillful slinger …could sling stones at an hair breadth, and not miss –Judges 20:16. It was not unusual for them to be able to hit birds in flight. Ancient ruins have uncovered tongs that were believed to be used by the military to remove embedded stones from wounded soldiers. If Goliath had a spear and David a pistol, we would not be so quick to believe that the larger man held the major advantage.

Faithful Action is inevitable when our bodies are subject to our soul and spirit, and they are under the direction of God’s Spirit. We are then free to act independently of our nature and other influences. When the lustful passions of the mortal body hold sway over our inner heart and mind, we are defeated before we take one step toward the enemy. As vessels of God’s design, with a moral free will, we have the divine ability to choose our course of action. Some believe that being proactive is merely taking the initiative. But initiative alone will not fit us for victory any more than it did for the sons of Sceva. The desire to dominate is no more noble than Goliath’s unbridled rage to destroy this young upstart. His adrenaline flowed as he scorned David’s youth, jumped to conclusions, was easily insulted, and marveled at the ignorance of others.

But David carried no such reactive mission. His endeavor was that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel. And all this assembly shall know that the LORD saveth not with sword and spear… –1 Samuel 17:47. Faithful action must be focused on yielding what you have, rather than obtaining what you don’t. If life erects concerns outside of our ability to change, it is fruitless to give them our attention. Joseph could not change his brothers’ reception, his master’s wife’s deception, the jail’s seclusion, or the butler’s delusion. The faith of the shepherd boy teaches us to stop lamenting over what we wanna-be and start being what we oughta-be. We need to stop looking for a miracle and start looking for an opportunity. It is not about overcoming extreme odds, but rather it is how we respond to a traffic jam, a disobedient child, an irate customer, or a demanding spouse. It is about owning a cause big enough to defuse selfish reaction and incite charitable pro-action.

Why would Japanese Kamikaze pilots die for a losing cause during World War Two? Why would Muslim terrorists blow themselves up? Why do Catholic Priests and Nuns take vows of celibacy and poverty? Is there no cause for the Christian that extends broader and deeper than the giants of this world? Is there not a cause that stirs our imagination and sanctifies our action? Or isn’t there even one that transforms our mundane work into a channel of grace for the service of the King of the Universe? How would history be different if Jesse would have spent his retirement like the elders of our day? God slays giants by the instruments we yield to him, from the needle of Dorcas… to the nail of Jael, from Zebedee’s boats of the business… to the boys of his bosom.

Shamgar had an oxgoad;
David had a sling;
Dorcus had a needle;
Rahab had a string;
Samson had a jawbone;
Moses had a rod;
Mary had some ointment;
And all were used for God!

Und David sprach: Was habe ich nun getan? Gibt es nicht einen Grund? –1. Samuel 17:29.

Die Geschichte von David und Goliat ereignete sich vor mehr als drei Jahrtausenden und ist seitdem bei Jung und Alt ein zeitloser Favorit. Irgendetwas an der Notlage des Außenseiters spricht uns alle an. Vielleicht sehen wir uns unbewusst in einer solchen Situation und hoffen insgeheim, dass sich eines Tages auch unser Glück wendet. Leider scheint ein solcher zufälliger Erfolg eher zu einer Hollywood-Produktion als zum wirklichen Leben zu passen. Wir sehen nur den Konflikt zwischen Jung und Alt, dem Hirten und dem Krieger, den schweren Waffen und der Schleuder. Doch es gab einige grundlegende Prinzipien, die David schon in seiner Jugend verinnerlicht hatte und die ihn zu einem vielversprechenden Kandidaten für den Erfolg machten. In unserer Liebe zu einem dramatischen, romantischen Sieg werden diese jedoch oft nicht gewürdigt.

Wenn unser einziges Bild von uns selbst aus dem sozialen Spiegel um uns herum stammt, entwickeln wir eine verzerrte innere Wahrnehmung, ähnlich dem Bild, das wir sehen, wenn wir auf einem Jahrmarkt in einen Zerrspiegel blicken. Die sozialen Meinungen und Wahrnehmungen unseres Umfelds zeichnen vor unseren Augen und Ohren oft ein unbeholfenes und verzerrtes Bild von uns. Manchmal ist es unrealistisch positiv und lässt einen Menschen in den Augen der Medien groß erscheinen, obwohl er kaum heldenhafte Charakterzüge zeigt.

Im Sport ist das vermutlich am ausgeprägtesten. Gepriesen werden diejenigen, die besser laufen, werfen oder schießen können als alle anderen. Doch sportliches Talent trägt wenig zum aufrichtigen, unverfälschten Wert eines Menschen bei. Die andere Seite der Medaille besteht aus einer ungeheuren Menge negativer und entwürdigender Botschaften, die jeden Versuch zu vereiteln suchen. Solche Bemerkungen prasseln in Strömen auf uns ein: von gestressten Eltern, verunsicherten Geschwistern, frustrierten Vorgesetzten und einer Vielzahl anderer Bekannter, die in einer „Überleben des Stärksten“-Gesellschaft um ihre Identität ringen. Die Botschaften aus diesen beiden Lagern sind widersprüchlich und unverhältnismäßig. Zu hören, man sei großartig, wird einen ebenso wenig großartig machen, wie eine Salve abfälliger Bemerkungen Demut hervorbringt. Leider lassen viele von uns allzu oft zu, dass solche unverhältnismäßigen Zuschreibungen unser Denken beeinflussen und unseren Weg bestimmen.

Die größte und überlegene Gabe, die der Mensch im Vergleich zum Rest der Schöpfung erhalten hat, findet sich nicht in seinen körperlichen Fähigkeiten, sondern in seinem Verstand. Die intelligentesten Tiere können dazu abgerichtet werden, sich verantwortungsvoll zu verhalten, aber sie können diese Abrichtung weder wählen noch lenken. Wir Menschen hingegen können neue Programme für uns selbst schreiben, völlig unabhängig von unseren Instinkten oder unserer durch die Umwelt geprägten Erziehung. Wer im Einklang mit seinen Instinkten und seiner Prägung lebt, wird sich kaum über das Tierreich erheben. Doch diejenigen, die diese Gaben einsetzen und entwickeln, werden in ihrer Begegnung mit den Riesen auf einzigartige Weise die Rolle ausfüllen, die Gott für sie vorgesehen hat. Davids Zeit und Stellung waren einzigartig, doch die Prinzipien, die er beherzigte, waren allgemeingültig. Wenn ich meinem Hund das Jodeln beibringen könnte, würde das beweisen, dass Hunde jodeln können, und auch für andere die Möglichkeit dazu eröffnen. Ebenso gäbe es für uns keine Hoffnung, außer untätig darauf zu warten, dass Gott dasselbe für uns tut, wenn David Goliat allein durch ein Wunder besiegt hätte. Wenn aber Prinzipien den Kern des Sieges ausmachten, dann haben wir ein Beispiel, dem wir folgen können, und eine Tugend, die wir uns aneignen können, um sie auf unserem eigenen Schlachtfeld einzusetzen.

Als David an jenem Morgen früh aufstand und seinen Sack mit Getreide, Brot und Käse auf die Schulter nahm, um ihn seinen Brüdern zu bringen, ahnte er nicht, was der Tag bringen würde. Der Herr war sein Hirte, und es fehlte ihm an nichts; doch als er zum Ort des Geschehens kam, war er erschüttert von dem, was er sah. Beide Heere standen auf gegenüberliegenden Bergen und waren in einer Pattsituation gefangen. Das ganze Heer ins Tal hinabzuführen und bergauf gegen den Feind zu kämpfen, hätte einen gewaltigen Nachteil bedeutet. Ein Risiko, zu dem keine Seite bereit war. Deshalb schlugen die Philister eine im Krieg übliche Lösung vor: Zwei Krieger sollten im Tal gegeneinander kämpfen, sodass keine Seite einen Vorteil hatte. Doch unter den Philistern war ein Riese, der das Heer Israels in Schrecken versetzte. Als David sich erkundigte, warum niemand den schmählichen Lästerungen des Ungläubigen entgegentreten wollte, wurde er von seinem ältesten Bruder scharf zurechtgewiesen: …und Eliabs Zorn entbrannte gegen David, und er sprach: Warum bist du hierhergekommen? Und bei wem hast du jene wenigen Schafe in der Wüste gelassen? Ich kenne deinen Hochmut und die Bosheit deines Herzens; denn du bist hergekommen, um den Kampf zu sehen. Und David sprach: Was habe ich nun getan? Gibt es nicht einen Grund? –1. Samuel 17:28-29.

…und auf Jesus sehen, den Anfänger und Vollender unseres Glaubens; der um der vor ihm liegenden Freude willen das Kreuz erduldete, die Schande verachtete und sich zur Rechten des Thrones Gottes gesetzt hat –Hebräer 12:2. Wenn ein Mensch ein Anliegen vor Augen hat, kann er beinahe alles ertragen. Manche erdulden es um eines vergänglichen Kranzes willen. König Saul hatte steuerbefreiten Reichtum und die Stellung als Schwiegersohn angeboten, doch die irdische Mitgift fand keine Freiwilligen. Die Aussicht auf irdisches Ansehen bedeutete dem sanftmütigen David nichts; doch Goliats gotteslästerliche Hohnreden entfachten in ihm ein eifersüchtiges Feuer, und im Glauben trat er vor. Glaube ist jedoch keine bloße Laune, die man mit einer emotionalen Luftpumpe aufblasen kann. Denn wie der Leib ohne Geist tot ist, so ist auch der Glaube ohne Werke [Taten] tot –Jakobus 2:26. So bot David, mit dem Anliegen klar vor Augen und seinem Gott an seiner Seite, an, gegen Goliat zu kämpfen.

David trat also vor und handelte nach gottgefälligen, unverfälschten Prinzipien…

Ein fürsorgliches Gewissen ist in der Seele des Menschen verankert und bestimmt, was uns am Herzen liegt. Viele meinen, ein Gewissen sei nur als begrenzender Wegweiser nützlich. Doch das menschliche Gewissen wurde auch geschaffen, um in umgekehrter Richtung zu wirken. Wenn wir davon überzeugt sind, dass etwas gut und recht ist, verfolgen wir es mit Leidenschaft. Thomas Edison sagte, Genie bestehe zu einem Prozent aus Inspiration und zu 99 Prozent aus Transpiration. Das mag durchaus stimmen; unbestreitbar ist jedoch, dass zuerst die Inspiration kommen muss. Jakobs Sehnsucht nach Rahel ließ ihn die sieben Jahre Arbeit vergessen. Edisons Streben nach einer funktionierenden Glühbirne ließ ihn die Tausenden gescheiterten Versuche vergessen.

Sorglose Gleichgültigkeit ist das Gegenteil davon und das Ergebnis eines abgestumpften Gewissens. David staunte, dass Goliats gotteslästerliche Hohnreden das Heer Gottes zu keinerlei Handeln bewegten. Gib einem Menschen einen Grund zu leben, und er wird das Wie herausfinden –Nietzke. Als Häftling in einem Konzentrationslager der Nazis wurde Victor Frankl zur Arbeit auf der Krankenstation des Lagers eingeteilt, wo Gefangene an Typhus starben. Er beobachtete, dass, wenn ein Mensch die Hoffnung aufgab, bald der Tod folgte. Ebenso schwindet bei vielen Menschen unserer Zeit die Leidenschaft, zu überwinden, wenn in der Auseinandersetzung die Hoffnung auf persönlichen Gewinn verfliegt. Den meisten heutigen Arbeitern ist ihr Gehalt wichtiger als gute und sinnvolle Arbeit. Wenn ein Mann die Zuneigung zu seiner Frau verliert, glaubt er oft, er könne sie nicht lieben; doch ein Mann mit einem gesunden Gewissen, das sich an göttlichen Prinzipien orientiert, wird ihr liebevoll begegnen, ungeachtet seiner Gefühle oder ihrer Reaktion. Das Gewissen weckt und nährt das Anliegen und legt so den Grund für leidenschaftliches Handeln.

Eine aufrichtige Vorstellungskraft gehört zum Bereich des Geistes und wird von unserem Gewissen gelenkt. Die Not ist die Mutter der Erfindung –unbekannt. Manche warten darauf, dass das Leben entdeckt wird, während andere es unterwegs selbst gestalten. Das ist keine Erlaubnis, falsche Ideale zu behaupten. Davids Streben ist aufrichtig, denn die Medien um ihn herum haben sein Bild nicht verzerrt. In den Hügeln von Bethlehem hat er sich gegenüber wilden Tieren – einem Löwen und einem Bären – bewährt; mit Gottes Hilfe fürchtet er sich nicht davor, im Tal Ela einem Mann entgegenzutreten, der von Jugend an ein Krieger ist.

Als Saul Davids Vorschlag widerwillig zustimmt, rüstet er den Jungen auf typisch weltliche Weise aus. Es mag eine Ehre gewesen sein, die Rüstung des Königs zu tragen, doch David wollte nichts davon wissen: …ich kann damit nicht gehen, denn ich habe es nicht erprobt. Und David legte es ab –1. Samuel 17:39, und wählte stattdessen fünf Steine. Zu wissen, was andere tun, und zu wissen, was man tun soll, ist nicht unbedingt dasselbe.

Die ängstlichen Überzeugungen des israelitischen Heeres wurzelten in einem heidnischen Wertesystem. Nicht Goliat war das Problem, sondern der glaubenslose Schrecken und die Annahme, man müsse den Kampf nach den Maßstäben der Welt aufnehmen. Wer sich einem wahrhaft würdigen Anliegen verschreibt, wird gewiss die Vorstellungskraft finden, es zu verfolgen.

Goliat hatte selbstverständlich angenommen, dass der Kampf nach seinen eigenen Bedingungen stattfinden würde. Beleidigt und erzürnt rief er: …Komm zu mir, und ich werde dein Fleisch den Vögeln des Himmels und den Tieren des Feldes geben –1. Samuel 17:44. Als Riese verfügt er nicht gerade über Schnelligkeit und Beweglichkeit und fordert David deshalb auf, zu ihm zu kommen. Doch Goliat überschätzte seine eigenen Fähigkeiten maßlos und unterschätzte seinen Gegner. Nach manchen Schätzungen hatte Davids Schleuder bei sechs oder sieben Umdrehungen pro Sekunde die Stoppwirkung einer 45-mm-Handfeuerwaffe, und die Hand eines geübten Schleuderers …konnte Steine auf eine Haarbreite genau schleudern und verfehlte nicht –Richter 20:16. Es war nicht ungewöhnlich, dass sie Vögel im Flug treffen konnten. In antiken Ruinen hat man Zangen gefunden, von denen man annimmt, dass sie vom Militär verwendet wurden, um eingebettete Steine aus verwundeten Soldaten zu entfernen. Hätte Goliat einen Speer und David eine Pistole gehabt, würden wir nicht so schnell glauben, dass der größere Mann den entscheidenden Vorteil hatte.

Treues Handeln ist unvermeidlich, wenn unser Leib unserer Seele und unserem Geist untergeordnet ist und diese unter der Leitung des Geistes Gottes stehen. Dann sind wir frei, unabhängig von unserer Natur und anderen Einflüssen zu handeln. Wenn die lüsternen Begierden des sterblichen Leibes über unser inneres Herz und unseren Verstand herrschen, sind wir besiegt, noch bevor wir einen Schritt auf den Feind zugehen. Als Gefäße nach Gottes Entwurf, ausgestattet mit einem freien moralischen Willen, haben wir die göttliche Fähigkeit, unseren Handlungsweg zu wählen. Manche glauben, proaktiv zu sein bedeute lediglich, die Initiative zu ergreifen. Doch Initiative allein macht uns ebenso wenig siegesfähig wie die Söhne des Skeva. Der Wunsch zu herrschen ist nicht edler als Goliats ungezügelte Wut, diesen jungen Emporkömmling zu vernichten. Sein Adrenalin strömte, als er Davids Jugend verspottete, voreilige Schlüsse zog, sich leicht beleidigen ließ und über die Unwissenheit anderer staunte.

Doch David handelte nicht aus einer solchen reaktiven Haltung heraus. Sein Ziel war, dass die ganze Erde erkennen möge, dass es einen Gott in Israel gibt. Und diese ganze Versammlung soll erkennen, dass der HERR nicht durch Schwert und Speer rettet… –1. Samuel 17:47. Treues Handeln muss darauf ausgerichtet sein, das einzusetzen, was man hat, statt zu erlangen, was man nicht hat. Wenn das Leben Sorgen aufwirft, die außerhalb unserer Fähigkeit liegen, sie zu verändern, ist es vergeblich, ihnen unsere Aufmerksamkeit zu schenken. Josef konnte weder die Reaktion seiner Brüder ändern noch die Täuschung der Frau seines Herrn, die Abgeschiedenheit des Gefängnisses oder den Irrtum des Mundschenks. Der Glaube des Hirtenjungen lehrt uns, nicht länger darüber zu klagen, was wir gern wären, sondern anzufangen, das zu sein, was wir sein sollten. Wir müssen aufhören, nach einem Wunder Ausschau zu halten, und anfangen, nach einer Gelegenheit zu suchen. Es geht nicht darum, überwältigende Widrigkeiten zu besiegen, sondern darum, wie wir auf einen Stau, ein ungehorsames Kind, einen wütenden Kunden oder einen fordernden Ehepartner reagieren. Es geht darum, sich einem Anliegen zu verschreiben, das groß genug ist, selbstsüchtige Reaktionen zu entschärfen und uneigennütziges Handeln anzustoßen.

Warum starben japanische Kamikaze-Piloten im Zweiten Weltkrieg für eine aussichtslose Sache? Warum sprengen sich muslimische Terroristen in die Luft? Warum legen katholische Priester und Nonnen Gelübde der Ehelosigkeit und Armut ab? Gibt es für Christen kein Anliegen, das weiter reicht und tiefer geht als die Riesen dieser Welt? Gibt es kein Anliegen, das unsere Vorstellungskraft anregt und unser Handeln heiligt? Gibt es nicht einmal eines, das unsere alltägliche Arbeit in einen Kanal der Gnade verwandelt, durch den wir dem König des Universums dienen? Wie wäre die Geschichte verlaufen, wenn Jesse seinen Ruhestand so verbracht hätte wie die Älteren unserer Tage? Gott besiegt Riesen durch die Werkzeuge, die wir ihm an die Hand geben: von der Nadel der Dorkas… bis zum Nagel Jaels, von den Geschäftsbooten des Zebedäus… bis zu den Kindern an seinem Herzen.

Schamgar hatte einen Ochsenstecken;
David hatte eine Schleuder;
Dorkas hatte eine Nadel;
Rahab hatte eine Schnur;
Simson hatte einen Kinnbacken;
Mose hatte einen Stab;
Maria hatte Salböl;
Und alles wurde für Gott eingesetzt!

One day you may be walking along a seashore. You glance back to watch your footprints disappear with the next surge of foaming water. You love to hear the soothing swish of the breakers. You gaze at the graceful sweep of shoreline and glittering ocean way out to the horizon. Life is good.

Suddenly a huge wave sweeps in and lifts you off your feet. You struggle and flail to regain your footing. Or the wave may even carry you farther and slam you against a rock wall, leaving you stunned and gasping in pain.

This wave may be called grief, as expressed in the following stanza from the song by Mary A. Baker.

Master, with anguish of spirit
I bow in my grief today;
The depths of my sad heart are troubled;
Oh, waken and save, I pray!
Torrents of sin and of anguish
Sweep o’er my sinking soul!
And I perish! I perish, dear Master;
Oh hasten, and take control.

In the past year, many of us have lost loved ones. Perhaps it was a childhood friend, or someone from our church family, or even from our immediate family. Depending on how close we were, we felt drops, splashes, or even tidal waves of grief.

Our grief stems from the relationship we shared. We have invested in each other’s lives to some degree. We have loved, but now that love has nowhere to go. We could say that grief is the price of love.

Here is how one widow described grief: “At the sudden and untimely death of my husband, the feeling was one of overwhelming shock, disbelief, and even panic, as I faced an uncertain future without him at the age of 51. Looking back, I realize how merciful God is to allow us to be in a certain state of numbness and shock at a time like this, allowing the reality to sink in more slowly.”

How did she cope? She says, “I am also awed at how He provides the grace and strength to go through hard things in life that we never thought we would have to face. He walks with us as we go through the valley of grief, so we are never walking alone. The journey of grief is not the same for everyone. It is not over in a few months. For me, I still cried a year later. It took a long time for the pain to fade and for life to become meaningful again. But praise God, that time does come! It is best not to look too far into the future. We walk one day at a time with Jesus, knowing that the best is yet to come.”

Here are more experiences from those who have been there:

  • “I am still learning that when we say, ‘It’s all right, Lord,’ we need to leave it there, at Jesus’ feet.”
  • “Grieving people are very lonely, but there’s also an aloneness that comes from not having a place to belong. You may be in a room of people, and still feel utterly alone, because you’ve lost your sense of belonging, or your category of belonging has changed.”
  • “The presence of a grieving person can be painful for others. It’s a reminder that “bad” things can happen. So, at times they are not invited, which is painful. A grieving person wants to be invited, but at times when included they feel their lack of belonging anew and think they should have stayed at home. Most times, casual conversation can be difficult for them when their world has been violently shaken. Their hearts are heavy while the mood of others is lighthearted, making them feel even more despondent. Understandably, many people don’t know what to do when they see others grieving, so they default to doing nothing and walk away. Many friendships are lost after a loss, which is even more painful.”
  • “God was so close. He was always there. ‘Underneath are the everlasting arms’, and I felt them.”

God can use sorrow and grief to teach us what we might not learn in happier times. We learn to depend on Him. We think of the seriousness of life. We learn to embrace eternal values and anticipate heaven. We are motivated to cherish the loved ones we still have when we hear expressions such as this: “Looking back, I wish we would not have taken the time we had together for granted. I wish I would have recognized his personality traits as strengths rather than things that annoyed.”

Those who lose loved ones often find themselves in the limelight for a time. Many people want to know how they are responding, especially when the death is an unusual situation. Consider the experience of Elizabeth Elliot and the four others who were made widows in 1956 by jungle killers in Ecuador. Or think of Marie Troyer whose husband John was murdered by guerrillas in Guatemala in 1981, or the mothers of the girls killed in Nickel Mines, Pennsylvania in 2006.

These women found themselves in the glare of an almost worldwide spotlight. Their greatest opportunity to display God’s enabling grace likely came at a time when they wanted it least. But their responses of forgiveness, unselfishness, and trust in God amazed the world, at least considering the amount of media attention. Truly, A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid –Matthew 5:14.

While we and those we know will hardly face that level of exposure, we too have a unique platform to display God’s grace. We may never have a better opportunity to touch hardened or seeking hearts than in our own hour of grief.

When we hear that people have indeed been drawn to God through the death of our loved one, it can be a source of comfort and meaning. This death was not a senseless tragedy; it was meant to bring glory to God. In other words, God does not waste our sorrows.

It reminds us of Jesus’ words about Lazarus when he said, …This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God might be glorified thereby –John 11:4. Jesus is our perfect example for relating to those in sorrow. He came to Mary and Martha and listened. He cried with them even though He knew He could and then did transform the whole situation by raising Lazarus.

How do we help?

What is our part in helping a grieving sister glorify God in the midst of her situation? Consider the thoughts shared by the following widows:

  • “What helped was when a dear sister sat with me and told me she cared. And in her quietness, I could feel that her love was real.”
  • “Grief is surprising and unexpected. The person may be having a good day when they hear a song, smell a certain scent, or see a familiar article of clothing which triggers a memory followed by a flood of tears. If this happens when you’re with them, it’s okay. Tears are okay. Tears are healing. Stay present and help them through it. Press in; grieve with them. It’s better to err in doing something than in doing nothing. You may not understand. That’s okay. You don’t need to experience loss to show that you care.”
  • “Grief is exhausting and mentally debilitating. So don’t just ask what you can do; look for a need they may have and try to fill it. For example, ‘I’d like to come over Tuesday evening and fix your faucet’ or ‘We’d like to come and bring a meal if you’re up to it?’”
  • “One thing that meant a lot to me was when people shared pleasant memories of our loved one, or things they appreciated about him. Even today, almost nineteen years later, it still warms my heart when people do that.”
  • “It was all the cards that came every day for the first two months after my husband died. I looked forward to them every day, and the first day without a card was hard.”
  • “What really helped me was when someone told me to focus on my blessings; that they are praying for me, and they care. Or they invited me to go along even if the number was then lopsided. Another thing was when they stopped by for coffee breaks or when they sent a text.”
  • “Widows need encouragement on their anniversary date and on the date their husband died. It means a lot if someone ‘actually’ remembers! A widow’s supper is nice. So is having a secret sister. It helped when someone gave a listening ear and was there to help with the work and the young children. Most of all, I knew people were praying for us.”

What do we say?

We may struggle with what to say to a bereaved friend. After all, we do not want to be like Job’s wife or his friends whose words only increased Job’s suffering. Here are some perspectives:

  • “They need not tell us we are alone now. We know that already.”
  • “Grief may really shake someone’s faith in God, momentarily paralyzing them, especially if they haven’t experienced much trauma before. As much as they long to trust God and accept this new reality in their lives, sometimes it takes time to simply get through the shock and be able to talk to God again. This is okay. They will most likely find healing and deepen their faith, but give them space to struggle, wrestle, and grieve deeply. Listen and try to refrain from “fixing” their faith with words such as “All things work together for good…”, or “At least you…”
  • “Asking a grieving person how they are doing could put them in a difficult position. Asking in a crowd of people may not be the best time. It may be best not to ask unless you really want to know and are willing to take the time to listen.”
  • “It is hard to think rationally in those first hard months. I did not appreciate being asked those first months what I would do for a living. I first needed to process my grief. I was also trying to help my young daughters who were devastated at the loss of their beloved daddy. That decision could wait.”

The following excerpts reveal other struggles with grief:

  • “Everyone grieves differently; there is no right or wrong way. And it never goes away even though all my friends’ lives go on as normal, which is very painful to watch. Holidays are very hard. Attending weddings is almost not doable. This is a couple’s world and only by the grace of God is it possible. Actually, the weeks before the annual anniversary dates are harder than the actual days.”
  • “One thing I realized very quickly was that we live in a very couple-orientated world. At the loss of a spouse, one is left trying to figure out where they fit in. I deeply appreciate, when I’m in a group setting that includes widows and singles, that there are those who try to make me feel included and not the odd one out.”
  • “You can’t put a time limit on grief. It’s different for everyone. There’s no ‘getting over it’ so that it doesn’t hurt anymore. If grieved properly, the wound is not as raw, and it becomes a scar. It’s like getting used to living without an arm or a leg. You adjust to it not being there, but you never stop missing it.”
  • “Death in the family or losing a spouse is harder than one can imagine until they are going through the same thing. I wish we would have had more church support. Our boys need a father figure to follow, one to teach them what a dad would.”
  • “Our children make mistakes as other children do; they need encouragement, not criticism. Also, they could use a helping hand with their work. I wish I would not have needed to leave my youngest child alone so much when I went to work. I broke out in a sweat more than once wondering where the money was coming from to pay the bills, but I thank the Lord that it was always there.”

How can we remember to support the grieving beyond those first days and weeks? We could mark our calendars with the dates of their birthdays, anniversaries, and their loved one’s death date. Then we could designate a certain day of the week to do something for them. If we make a plan, we are more likely to carry out our good intentions.

Finally, we should also remember the “widows who aren’t”. Sometimes there are those among us whose life is racked by a grief worse than that of an actual death. Perhaps there was betrayal, abandonment, incarceration, or suicide in their life’s journey. They may almost envy the clean wound of the “normal” widow. Or they may struggle with guilt on top of their grief.

These situations are often located far outside our comfort zones. There are no easy answers of how to deal with them. But let us not stay aloof from such a sister if we have the opportunity. God will help us find a way to show we care if we ask Him.

As we, and those we love, keep walking with God, may we portray the scene in the final verse of the song mentioned earlier:

“Master, the terror is over, the elements sweetly rest;
Earth’s sun in the calm lake is mirrored,
And heaven’s within my breast.
Linger, O blessed Redeemer,
Leave me alone no more;
And with joy I shall make the blest harbor,
And rest on the blissful shore.”

Let’s conclude with a quote from a widow:

“Walk with them until they can come out of the cave and feel the sunshine again. It may require hard work and getting messy at times, but to them you will be Jesus ‘with skin on’. You are not responsible for their healing; only Jesus can do that. But you can bring them to Him.

Remember the friends that brought the paralyzed man to Jesus, lowering him through the roof. And, behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy; Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee … And Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts? For whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and walk? But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, (then saith he to the sick of the palsy,) Arise, take up thy bed, and go unto thine house. And he arose, and departed to his house. But when the multitudes saw it, they marvelled, and glorified God, which had given such power unto men –Matthew 9:2-8.

What a beautiful picture! In like manner, you can carry your grief-‘paralyzed’ friend to Jesus. Watch them be healed, shoulder their burden of grief, and then move on toward their heavenly home. As we see God doing a work in their heart, we can all praise God together!”

~In this article, the sections in quotation marks were shared with the author by a number of anonymous widows.

Um dia, talvez você esteja caminhando pela praia. Você olha para trás e observa suas pegadas desaparecerem com a próxima onda de água espumante. Você gosta de ouvir o suave marulho das ondas. Contempla a graciosa curva da costa e o oceano cintilante que se estende até o horizonte. A vida é boa.

De repente, uma onda enorme chega e tira você do chão. Você luta e se debate para recuperar o equilíbrio. Ou a onda pode até carregá-lo mais para longe e arremessá-lo contra um paredão rochoso, deixando-o atordoado e ofegante de dor.

Essa onda pode ser chamada de pesar, como expresso na seguinte estrofe da canção de Mary A. Baker.

Mestre, com angústia no espírito
Curvo-me hoje em meu pesar;
As profundezas do meu triste coração se inquietam;
Ó, desperta e salva-me, eu te peço!
Torrentes de pecado e angústia
Varrem minha alma que afunda!
E pereço! Pereço, querido Mestre;
Ó, apressa-te e assume o controle.

No último ano, muitos de nós perdemos entes queridos. Talvez tenha sido um amigo de infância, alguém da família da igreja ou até mesmo da nossa família imediata. Dependendo de quão próximos éramos, sentimos gotas, respingos ou até ondas gigantes de pesar.

Nosso pesar nasce do relacionamento que compartilhávamos. Investimos uns na vida dos outros em certa medida. Amamos, mas agora esse amor não tem para onde ir. Poderíamos dizer que o pesar é o preço do amor.

Uma viúva descreveu assim o pesar: “Com a morte súbita e prematura de meu marido, senti um choque avassalador, incredulidade e até pânico, ao enfrentar um futuro incerto sem ele, aos 51 anos. Olhando para trás, percebo como Deus é misericordioso ao permitir que fiquemos em certo estado de entorpecimento e choque num momento como esse, permitindo que a realidade se instale mais lentamente.”

Como ela lidou com isso? Ela diz: “Também fico maravilhada com a maneira como Ele concede a graça e a força para atravessarmos momentos difíceis da vida que nunca pensamos que teríamos de enfrentar. Ele caminha conosco enquanto atravessamos o vale do pesar, por isso nunca caminhamos sozinhos. A jornada do pesar não é igual para todos. Não termina em poucos meses. No meu caso, ainda chorei um ano depois. A dor levou muito tempo para diminuir e para que a vida voltasse a ter sentido. Mas, louvado seja Deus, esse momento chega! É melhor não olhar muito longe para o futuro. Caminhamos um dia de cada vez com Jesus, sabendo que o melhor ainda está por vir.”

Aqui estão mais experiências de pessoas que passaram por isso:

  • “Ainda estou aprendendo que, quando dizemos: ‘Está tudo bem, Senhor’, precisamos deixar as coisas assim, aos pés de Jesus.”
  • “As pessoas enlutadas sentem muita solidão, mas também há uma solidão que vem de não ter um lugar a que pertençam. Você pode estar numa sala cheia de pessoas e ainda se sentir completamente só, porque perdeu seu senso de pertencimento, ou sua categoria de pertencimento mudou.”
  • “A presença de uma pessoa enlutada pode ser dolorosa para os outros. É um lembrete de que coisas ‘ruins’ podem acontecer. Por isso, às vezes, ela não é convidada, o que é doloroso. Uma pessoa enlutada quer ser convidada, mas, quando é incluída, às vezes volta a sentir que não pertence e pensa que deveria ter ficado em casa. Muitas vezes, uma conversa casual pode ser difícil para ela quando seu mundo foi violentamente abalado. Seu coração está pesado enquanto os outros estão descontraídos, o que a faz sentir-se ainda mais desanimada. É compreensível que muitas pessoas não saibam o que fazer quando veem outras de luto; por isso, acabam não fazendo nada e vão embora. Muitas amizades se perdem depois de uma perda, o que é ainda mais doloroso.”
  • “Deus esteve tão perto. Ele sempre esteve presente. ‘Por baixo estão os braços eternos’, e eu os senti.”

Deus pode usar a tristeza e o pesar para nos ensinar o que talvez não aprendêssemos em tempos mais felizes. Aprendemos a depender dele. Refletimos sobre a seriedade da vida. Aprendemos a abraçar os valores eternos e a aguardar o céu. Somos motivados a valorizar os entes queridos que ainda temos quando ouvimos declarações como esta: “Olhando para trás, gostaria de não ter dado por garantido o tempo que passamos juntos. Gostaria de ter reconhecido os traços da personalidade dele como qualidades, em vez de coisas que me irritavam.”

Quem perde entes queridos muitas vezes acaba em evidência por algum tempo. Muitas pessoas querem saber como estão reagindo, especialmente quando a morte ocorre em circunstâncias incomuns. Pense na experiência de Elizabeth Elliot e das outras quatro mulheres que ficaram viúvas em 1956 por causa de assassinos da selva no Equador. Ou pense em Marie Troyer, cujo marido, John, foi assassinado por guerrilheiros na Guatemala em 1981, ou nas mães das meninas mortas em Nickel Mines, Pensilvânia, em 2006.

Essas mulheres se viram sob os holofotes de uma atenção quase mundial. Sua maior oportunidade de demonstrar a graça capacitadora de Deus provavelmente chegou no momento em que menos a desejavam. Mas suas respostas de perdão, altruísmo e confiança em Deus maravilharam o mundo, ao menos levando em conta a atenção da mídia. De fato, Uma cidade situada sobre um monte não pode ficar escondida –Mateus 5:14.

Embora nós e as pessoas que conhecemos dificilmente enfrentemos esse nível de exposição, também temos uma plataforma singular para demonstrar a graça de Deus. Talvez nunca tenhamos uma oportunidade melhor de tocar corações endurecidos ou que buscam a Deus do que em nossa própria hora de pesar.

Quando ouvimos que pessoas foram realmente atraídas a Deus pela morte de nosso ente querido, isso pode ser uma fonte de consolo e significado. Essa morte não foi uma tragédia sem sentido; ela tinha o propósito de trazer glória a Deus. Em outras palavras, Deus não desperdiça nossas tristezas.

Isso nos lembra as palavras de Jesus sobre Lázaro, quando disse: …Esta enfermidade não é para a morte, mas para a glória de Deus, para que o Filho de Deus seja glorificado por ela –João 11:4. Jesus é nosso exemplo perfeito de como nos relacionar com os que estão tristes. Ele foi até Maria e Marta e as ouviu. Chorou com elas, embora soubesse que podia e depois de fato transformou toda a situação ao ressuscitar Lázaro.

Como podemos ajudar?

Qual é a nossa parte em ajudar uma irmã enlutada a glorificar a Deus em meio à sua situação? Consideremos os pensamentos compartilhados pelas seguintes viúvas:

  • “O que me ajudou foi uma querida irmã sentar-se comigo e dizer que se importava. E, em seu silêncio, eu podia sentir que seu amor era verdadeiro.”
  • “O pesar é surpreendente e inesperado. A pessoa pode estar tendo um bom dia quando ouve uma canção, sente determinado cheiro ou vê uma peça de roupa conhecida, o que desperta uma lembrança seguida por uma enxurrada de lágrimas. Se isso acontecer quando você estiver com ela, tudo bem. Chorar é permitido. As lágrimas curam. Permaneça presente e ajude-a a passar por isso. Aproxime-se; sofra com ela. É melhor errar por fazer algo do que por não fazer nada. Talvez você não entenda. Tudo bem. Você não precisa passar por uma perda para demonstrar que se importa.”
  • “O pesar é exaustivo e debilitante do ponto de vista mental. Portanto, não pergunte apenas o que pode fazer; procure uma necessidade que ela possa ter e tente atendê-la. Por exemplo: ‘Gostaria de passar aí na terça-feira à noite e consertar sua torneira’ ou ‘Gostaríamos de ir levar uma refeição, se você estiver disposta?’”
  • “Uma coisa que significou muito para mim foi quando as pessoas compartilharam lembranças agradáveis de nosso ente querido ou coisas que apreciavam nele. Até hoje, quase dezenove anos depois, ainda fico com o coração aquecido quando fazem isso.”
  • “Foram todos os cartões que chegaram todos os dias nos dois primeiros meses após a morte de meu marido. Eu os esperava ansiosamente todos os dias, e foi difícil o primeiro dia sem cartão.”
  • “O que realmente me ajudou foi alguém me dizer para me concentrar nas bênçãos; que estavam orando por mim e se importavam comigo. Ou me convidarem para acompanhá-los, mesmo que assim o número de pessoas ficasse desigual. Outra coisa foi passarem para tomar um café ou me enviarem uma mensagem.”
  • “As viúvas precisam de encorajamento no aniversário de casamento e na data da morte do marido. Significa muito quando alguém ‘realmente’ se lembra! Um jantar para viúvas é bom. Ter uma irmã secreta também. Ajudou quando alguém me ouviu e estava disponível para ajudar com as tarefas e as crianças pequenas. Acima de tudo, eu sabia que as pessoas estavam orando por nós.”

O que devemos dizer?

Talvez tenhamos dificuldade para saber o que dizer a um amigo enlutado. Afinal, não queremos ser como a esposa de Jó ou seus amigos, cujas palavras apenas aumentaram o sofrimento de Jó. Aqui estão algumas perspectivas:

  • “Não precisam nos dizer que agora estamos sozinhos. Já sabemos disso.”
  • “O pesar pode realmente abalar a fé de alguém em Deus, paralisando essa pessoa por um tempo, especialmente se ela não passou por muitos traumas antes. Por mais que deseje confiar em Deus e aceitar essa nova realidade em sua vida, às vezes é preciso algum tempo simplesmente para superar o choque e conseguir falar com Deus novamente. Tudo bem. Muito provavelmente, a pessoa encontrará cura e sua fé se aprofundará, mas dê espaço para que ela lute, se debata e sofra profundamente. Escute e tente não ‘consertar’ sua fé com frases como ‘Todas as coisas cooperam para o bem…’ ou ‘Pelo menos você…’”
  • “Perguntar a uma pessoa enlutada como ela está pode colocá-la numa situação difícil. Perguntar diante de um grupo de pessoas talvez não seja o melhor momento. Talvez seja melhor não perguntar, a menos que você realmente queira saber e esteja disposto a dedicar tempo para ouvir.”
  • “É difícil pensar racionalmente naqueles primeiros meses difíceis. Não gostei que me perguntassem, naqueles primeiros meses, o que eu faria para ganhar a vida. Primeiro, eu precisava processar meu pesar. Também estava tentando ajudar minhas filhas pequenas, devastadas pela perda do querido pai. Essa decisão podia esperar.”

Os trechos a seguir revelam outras dificuldades relacionadas ao pesar:

  • “Cada um vive o pesar de maneira diferente; não há jeito certo ou errado. E ele nunca vai embora, embora a vida de todos os meus amigos continue normalmente, o que é muito doloroso de assistir. Os feriados são muito difíceis. Ir a casamentos é quase impossível. Este é um mundo de casais, e só pela graça de Deus isso é possível. Na verdade, as semanas que antecedem as datas anuais de aniversário são mais difíceis do que os próprios dias.”
  • “Uma coisa que percebi muito depressa foi que vivemos num mundo muito voltado para casais. Com a perda do cônjuge, a pessoa fica tentando descobrir onde se encaixa. Aprecio profundamente, quando estou num grupo que inclui viúvas e pessoas solteiras, aqueles que tentam fazer com que eu me sinta incluída e não deslocada.”
  • “Não se pode impor um limite de tempo ao pesar. É diferente para cada pessoa. Não existe ‘superar’ a situação de modo que ela já não doa. Quando se vive o pesar como é preciso, a ferida não fica tão exposta e se transforma numa cicatriz. É como se acostumar a viver sem um braço ou uma perna. Você se adapta à ausência, mas nunca deixa de sentir falta.”
  • “A morte na família ou a perda do cônjuge é mais difícil do que se pode imaginar até passar pela mesma situação. Gostaria que tivéssemos recebido mais apoio da igreja. Nossos meninos precisam de uma figura paterna que possam seguir, alguém que lhes ensine o que um pai ensinaria.”
  • “Nossos filhos cometem erros como as outras crianças; precisam de encorajamento, não de críticas. Também poderiam receber ajuda com as tarefas. Gostaria de não ter precisado deixar tanto sozinha minha filha mais nova quando ia trabalhar. Mais de uma vez comecei a suar frio, imaginando de onde viria o dinheiro para pagar as contas, mas agradeço ao Senhor porque o dinheiro sempre esteve disponível.”

Como podemos nos lembrar de apoiar os enlutados depois dos primeiros dias e semanas? Poderíamos marcar em nossos calendários as datas de seus aniversários, aniversários de casamento e a data da morte de seu ente querido. Então poderíamos escolher um dia específico da semana para fazer algo por eles. Se fizermos um plano, é mais provável que cumpramos nossas boas intenções.

Por fim, também devemos nos lembrar das “viúvas que não são”. Às vezes, há entre nós pessoas cuja vida é atormentada por um pesar pior do que o de uma morte de fato. Talvez tenham passado por traição, abandono, encarceramento ou suicídio ao longo de sua vida. Talvez até invejem a ferida limpa da viúva “normal”. Ou talvez lutem contra a culpa além do pesar.

Essas situações muitas vezes ficam bem fora da nossa zona de conforto. Não há respostas fáceis sobre como lidar com elas. Mas não nos afastemos de uma irmã assim se tivermos oportunidade. Deus nos ajudará a encontrar uma maneira de demonstrar que nos importamos, se pedirmos a ele.

Enquanto nós e aqueles que amamos continuamos caminhando com Deus, que possamos retratar a cena do verso final da canção mencionada anteriormente:

“Mestre, o terror passou, os elementos repousam suavemente;
O sol da Terra reflete-se no lago sereno,
E o céu está dentro do meu peito.
Permanece, ó bendito Redentor,
Não me deixes mais sozinha;
E, com alegria, chegarei ao porto bendito,
E descansarei na praia de bem-aventurança.”

Concluamos com uma citação de uma viúva:

“Caminhe com elas até que consigam sair da caverna e sentir novamente o calor do sol. Talvez seja necessário muito esforço e, às vezes, lidar com situações difíceis, mas, para elas, você será Jesus ‘com pele’. Você não é responsável pela cura delas; só Jesus pode fazer isso. Mas você pode levá-las até ele.

Lembre-se dos amigos que levaram o paralítico a Jesus, descendo-o pelo telhado. E eis que lhe trouxeram um paralítico deitado numa cama; e Jesus, vendo a fé deles, disse ao paralítico: Filho, tem bom ânimo; os teus pecados estão perdoados… E Jesus, conhecendo os pensamentos deles, disse: Por que pensais mal em vossos corações? Pois o que é mais fácil, dizer: Os teus pecados estão perdoados; ou dizer: Levanta-te e anda? Mas, para que saibais que o Filho do Homem tem poder na terra para perdoar pecados (disse então ao paralítico): Levanta-te, toma a tua cama e vai para tua casa. E ele se levantou e foi para sua casa. Vendo isso, as multidões se maravilharam e glorificaram a Deus, que dera tal poder aos homens –Mateus 9:2-8.

Que imagem linda! Da mesma maneira, você pode levar a Jesus seu amigo ‘paralisado’ pelo pesar. Veja-as serem curadas, ajude-as a carregar o fardo do pesar e, então, siga com elas em direção ao lar celestial. Ao vermos Deus realizando uma obra em seu coração, todos podemos louvar a Deus juntos!”

~Neste artigo, os trechos entre aspas foram compartilhados com a autora por várias viúvas anônimas.

Pride is something that everyone must deal with. It is something that naturally tends to come into our lives and stay. Like many other things, it is very deceitful, because it is commonly accepted by the world in which we live. People today are proud of being proud. Americans are proud of their country, their jobs, their children, their lawns, their sports teams, their vehicles, their ambitions, their goals, their looks, their friends, their homes, and the list could go on. If we think about it, the carnal man is proud of just about anything. People stand and proclaim they are proud and boast of their great accomplishments. People look at something someone has done and proclaim to the doer, “You should be proud of yourself!”

There is one problem; God hates pride! God actually despises the proud. In Psalms, it says that God will cut off …the tongue that speaketh proud things –Psalm 12:3. And in Job it says He will …behold every one that is proud, and abase [put down or make low] him –Job 40:11. Psalms 40:4 says He will not respect the proud and in Psalm 119: Thou hast rebuked the proud that are cursed, which do err from thy commandments –Psalm 119:21. In Proverbs, we read that: The LORD will destroy the house of the proud… –Proverbs 15:25, and that Every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to the LORD… –Proverbs 16:5. In Malachi, it says that …behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud… –Malachi 4:1. Finally, James states that …God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble –James 4:6.

As we can see, the Bible is very clear on pride, and the people who are proud. There is no room for pride in our hearts or lives. So, what do we do with this? Are we proud? Do we boast as the world does?

I would like to call attention to a hidden form of pride that can slip into our lives, sometimes unnoticed. We will call it false humility. If we have a false humility, would it not actually be a form of pride?

Let us look first at Law and Grace. Someone that is under the law does not desire to do what he must do, but rather, he does it because of the law. For example, the law states that we should not kill, yet (according to the law) we are allowed to be angry. Someone can hate another and even desire to kill him, but if they resist the temptation to kill, they have indeed kept the law. Many people today who claim to be Christians, are actually under the law. They do all that they do because of a law, or an order from their authority. We can see this clearly when people push the law, doing the least that is required, but still technically keeping the law.

The head covering is a good example. A woman who desires to cover her head because of what the Bible teaches, will indeed cover her head. She does not need to be reminded to do it or be admonished for doing it half-heartedly. On the other hand, there are Christians that cover their heads; however, the actual covering continues to get smaller, and less noticeable. Some even put it all the way on the back of the head and color it the same as their hair, trying to keep it from being noticed by the uncovered public. This clearly reveals the heart; they are simply complying with the law.

This type of thinking can go for many things. One more would be adornment. The bible says that the adornment should not be outward. Many Christians will not adorn themselves with flashy eye-catching things, however there are no standards about adorning homes, vehicles, and such like. So, a plain, unadorned person gets out of their adorned vehicle and walks into their very adorned home. This shows where the heart is—under the law.

Now let us look at grace. It is the power of God in the life of a human being. It causes one to actually love their enemies, to do good to those who mistreat them. It causes one to love their God with all their heart and obey God’s commands because of a passionate love for Him. The law is no longer needed because the heart is new; it desires to live for God. When someone does evil to you, you do not think about getting even. In fact, you do not even get angry. You are a new creature and because of this power—grace from God—you love him that has done you wrong. Forgiving is not a problem; helping others is natural. You are not your own and you desire to be all you can be for your Savior who died for you.

What does this have to do with pride or humility?

The Bible says that …the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ –John 1:17. It does not take God’s Spirit in our lives for us to obey the law—we can do that on our own. Therefore, we can become proud by doing things for God because WE did them. When we did not allow our anger to spew out when disagreeing with a neighbor, we think well of ourselves, and we can become proud. However, when we actually love our neighbor that has a problem with us, we cannot become proud because it was grace; it was the power of God that caused this, not ourselves. Therefore, we marvel at God and his abundant grace.

It would be foolish for someone to be proud of something that God clearly did! If Lazarus walked around boasting of himself for being raised from the dead, people would question his sanity, saying, “You did nothing! It was Jesus that did everything.”

I’m not trying to say that the Christian does nothing. No, we must humbly obey the commandments of God and walk in His ways. However, I am saying that we cannot boast in ourselves because it is God that enables us to obey His commandments.

Let us look at the popular story of David and Goliath. David went to the army to take provisions to his brothers who were fighting there. As he approached, he marveled at what he saw, a large man challenging his people! David seemed a bit shocked, and aggrieved as he asked, …who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God? –1 Samuel 17:26.

What does David’s oldest brother Eliab say to him? “I know thy pride.”

Eliab thought the attitude of David was prideful, and we can see why. A ruddy youth walks up from tending sheep and wonders why someone is not taking care of this large man. It sounds a bit off. But what was David thinking? He was only thinking about what God could, and most likely, wanted to do! He did not think for a moment that he himself could do anything in this situation.

He is then brought before King Saul: And Saul said to David, Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth –1 Samuel 17:33.

David responded, … Thy servant kept his father’s sheep, and there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock: And I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth: and when he arose against me, I caught him by his beard, and smote him, and slew him. Thy servant slew both the lion and the bear: and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, seeing he hath defied the armies of the living God –1 Samuel 17:34-36.

David here is super confident, but why?! David said moreover, The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine… –1 Samuel 17:37.

Clearly his confidence is because the Lord is fighting for him. David was not concerned that he was “but a youth” and he did not understand why people questioned him. He was only thinking about what God was going to do! However, Eliab saw David’s confidence as pride. Possibly God had not worked in Eliab’s life. Maybe he did not know of the power of God; therefore, to him it looked like foolish pride.

And Saul armed David with his armour, and he put an helmet of brass upon his head; also he armed him with a coat of mail. And David girded his sword upon his armour, and he assayed to go; for he had not proved it. And David said unto Saul, I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them. And David put them off him –1 Samuel 17:38-39.

So, David chose to not wear the armor; it would only have been a hindrance. Rather, he chose some stones then he ran out to fight the giant. Of course, the giant also did not understand. When he …saw David, he disdained him: for he was but a youth … And the Philistine said unto David, Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods. And the Philistine said to David, Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field –1 Samuel 17:42-44.

Then David said …Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied. This day will the LORD deliver thee into mine hand; and I will smite thee … that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel –1 Samuel 17:45-46.

Notice then what David did. He killed the giant, cut off his head, and took his head back to Jerusalem. What do you think Eliab thought now? Here is the younger brother marching around the streets of Jerusalem with the head of the defeated giant! King Saul calls for David and he goes to see Saul, still holding the severed head.

Why was David not proud? Because he knew it was not he himself that did it. It was God who had done a marvelous work! He was simply testifying of the grace of God.

When we do a work on our own, we cannot boast of it because we did it. It would be pride, so we remain silent and call it humility, even if we desire others to see it. However, when it is a super-natural work of God, we now must boast of what God has done! We are called to this.

Is God working in your life? Are you confused as to whether it is you or God? Ask yourself a question, “Am I doing things that people who are not relying on God can still do?” If we are not doing anything differently than the world, then God is not working in our life. It is that simple. No one enjoys getting angry. I spent most of my childhood and teenage years going to anger management classes where counselors tried to teach us how to control our anger. The unregenerate heart can learn to hide anger, but only God can change the heart. I never heard a counselor teach us how to love people instead of getting angry with them, since it is impossible! It is only a work of the living God in one’s life, and in that work, we must boast! We testify of the outpouring of the grace of God in our lives. When someone believes it is pride, just like Eliab did, it’s because they only see the working of the Law, where all is done by man’s feeble attempts.

Let us look at an example to help us understand. If you decide to build a house, every day you put on your nail bag and get to work. It takes you time and energy, but finally the house is finished. You are standing in front of the newly constructed home with a friend. “Wow,” he states, “This house is beautiful! It looks perfectly built!”

Your cheeks blush a little and you begin to point out the flaws that you know, “No, it’s not perfect, you see that over there? I messed up on that gable…. And the siding over there… it’s not exactly straight.” We do this because we want to be humble! If we would say, “Yes, it is a beautiful house; I did a great job building it!” it would be prideful, right?

Now, what if you wanted to build a house and you realize you are not able to build it; you need God’s help. You pray for help then bam, the house is built! You never even put on your nail bag; the house miraculously appeared. God built it. Now how would the conversation go with your friend? Would you still point out all the flaws? NO! You would boast of its perfection, boldly proclaiming what the Lord had done.

When God does a work in our lives, it is not pride to tell people about it. It takes humility to say that we did not do it, but that God did! However, the devil wants us to quiet down and say it is humility like Eliab wanted David to do. We need men and women today that can boldly proclaim what God is doing in their lives!

Instead, it seems we have many defeated people that actually believe it is godly to talk down about ourselves, to act as if we are a defeated sinner trying to struggle through this earthly existence. “Rise up, Oh man of God! Be done with lesser things!”

I realize one could ask, “So, we should go around boasting about how righteous we are?” To this question, I will paint another picture. A poor criminal who has only known the city streets as home, steals and robs just to get by. He knows he is a bad person, yet he knows nothing else. One day God reveals himself to this man. In a dark alley he repents of his sin and gives his life to the Lord. God saves him, transforms him, converts him. He leaves that alley a new person! He has joy in his heart and peace in his soul!

What do you expect him to tell his friends? Um, the siding over there is not straight, the windows are too small….

NO, certainly not! Rather, he would say I’m perfect! God has done a great work, look at me! I’ve been saved by the power of God! By the blood of Jesus! All this as he skips down the road in the beauty of holiness.

교만은 누구나 다루어야 하는 문제입니다. 교만은 자연스럽게 우리 삶에 들어와 자리를 잡는 경향이 있습니다. 다른 많은 것들과 마찬가지로, 교만은 우리가 사는 세상에서 흔히 받아들여지기 때문에 매우 기만적입니다. 오늘날 사람들은 자신이 교만한 것을 자랑스러워합니다. 미국인들은 자국과 직업, 자녀, 잔디밭, 스포츠팀, 자동차, 야망, 목표, 외모, 친구, 집을 자랑스러워하며, 목록은 계속 이어질 수 있습니다. 생각해 보면 육적인 사람은 거의 무엇이든 자랑스러워합니다. 사람들은 일어서서 자신이 자랑스럽다고 선언하고 자신의 대단한 업적을 자랑합니다. 사람들은 누군가가 한 일을 보고 그 사람에게 “자신을 자랑스러워해야죠!”라고 말합니다.

한 가지 문제가 있습니다. 하나님께서는 교만을 미워하십니다! 하나님께서는 실제로 교만한 자를 몹시 싫어하십니다. 시편에는 하나님께서 …교만한 말을 하는 혀를 끊으시리로다 –시편 12:3.라고 기록되어 있습니다. 욥기에는 그분께서 …모든 교만한 자를 살펴보시고 그를 낮추시리라 [끌어내리거나 낮추시리라] –욥기 40:11.라고 기록되어 있습니다. 시편 40:4은 그분께서 교만한 자를 돌아보지 않으신다고 말하며, 시편 119편에는 주께서 저주를 받은 교만한 자들을 책망하셨나이다 그들은 주의 계명에서 벗어났나이다 –시편 119:21.라고 기록되어 있습니다. 잠언에는 여호와께서 교만한 자의 집을 허무시리라… –잠언 15:25, 그리고 마음이 교만한 자는 모두 여호와께 가증하니… –잠언 16:5.라고 기록되어 있습니다. 말라기에는 …보라, 화덕처럼 타는 날이 오나니 모든 교만한 자… –말라기 4:1.라고 기록되어 있습니다. 마지막으로 야고보는 …하나님은 교만한 자를 대적하시되 겸손한 자들에게는 은혜를 주시느니라 –야고보서 4:6.라고 말합니다.

보시다시피 성경은 교만과 교만한 사람들에 대해 매우 분명하게 말합니다. 우리의 마음과 삶에 교만이 들어설 자리는 없습니다. 그렇다면 우리는 이 문제를 어떻게 해야 할까요? 우리는 교만합니까? 세상 사람들처럼 자랑합니까?

때로는 알아차리지 못하는 사이 우리 삶에 스며들 수 있는, 감춰진 형태의 교만에 주의를 환기하고 싶습니다. 이것을 거짓된 겸손이라고 부르겠습니다. 거짓된 겸손을 지닌다면, 그것도 사실 교만의 한 형태가 아니겠습니까?

먼저 율법과 은혜를 살펴봅시다. 율법 아래 있는 사람은 마땅히 해야 할 일을 하고 싶어서 하는 것이 아니라 율법 때문에 합니다. 예를 들어, 율법은 살인하지 말라고 하지만 (율법에 따르면) 화를 내는 것은 허용됩니다. 누군가 다른 사람을 미워하고 심지어 그를 죽이고 싶어 할 수도 있지만, 살인의 유혹을 물리친다면 그는 실제로 율법을 지킨 것입니다. 오늘날 그리스도인이라고 주장하는 많은 사람은 실제로 율법 아래 있습니다. 그들은 율법이나 권위자의 명령 때문에 모든 일을 합니다. 사람들이 율법을 밀어붙이며 요구되는 최소한만 하면서도 기술적으로는 율법을 지키는 모습을 보면 이를 분명히 알 수 있습니다.

머리 가리개가 좋은 예입니다. 성경의 가르침 때문에 머리를 가리고자 하는 여성은 실제로 머리를 가릴 것입니다. 그렇게 하라는 말을 듣거나, 마음을 다하지 않고 한다고 훈계를 받을 필요가 없습니다. 반면 머리를 가리는 그리스도인들 가운데 실제 가리개를 계속 더 작고 눈에 덜 띄게 만드는 이들이 있습니다. 어떤 이들은 가리개를 머리 뒤쪽에 바짝 붙여 놓고 머리카락과 같은 색으로 칠해, 머리를 가리지 않은 사람들에게 들키지 않으려 하기도 합니다. 이는 마음을 분명히 드러냅니다. 그들은 그저 율법을 따르고 있을 뿐입니다.

이런 생각은 여러 가지 일에 적용될 수 있습니다. 장식도 그중 하나입니다. 성경은 장식이 외적인 것이어서는 안 된다고 말합니다. 많은 그리스도인은 화려하고 눈길을 끄는 것으로 자신을 꾸미지 않지만, 집이나 자동차 등을 꾸미는 데에는 아무런 기준이 없습니다. 그래서 꾸밈없이 수수한 사람이 장식이 화려한 차에서 내려 장식이 가득한 집으로 걸어 들어갑니다. 이는 마음이 어디에 있는지, 곧 율법 아래 있음을 보여 줍니다.

이제 은혜를 살펴봅시다. 은혜는 한 인간의 삶 속에 임하는 하나님의 능력입니다. 은혜는 사람이 실제로 원수를 사랑하고 자신을 박대하는 이들에게 선을 행하게 합니다. 하나님을 온 마음으로 사랑하고, 하나님을 향한 열렬한 사랑 때문에 그분의 명령에 순종하게 합니다. 마음이 새로워져 하나님을 위해 살고자 하므로 더는 율법이 필요하지 않습니다. 누군가가 여러분에게 악을 행할 때 보복할 생각을 하지 않습니다. 사실 화조차 내지 않습니다. 여러분은 새 피조물이며, 하나님의 은혜라는 이 능력으로 여러분에게 잘못한 사람을 사랑합니다. 용서하는 것은 어려운 일이 아니며, 다른 사람을 돕는 일은 자연스럽습니다. 여러분은 자신의 것이 아니며, 여러분을 위해 죽으신 구주를 위해 할 수 있는 모든 일을 하고자 합니다.

이것이 교만이나 겸손과 무슨 관계가 있을까요?

성경은 …율법은 모세로 말미암아 주어진 것이요 은혜와 진리는 예수 그리스도로 말미암아 온 것이라 –요한복음 1:17.라고 말합니다. 율법에 순종하는 데 우리 삶 속 하나님의 영이 필요한 것은 아닙니다. 우리는 스스로 그렇게 할 수 있습니다. 그러므로 우리가 하나님을 위해 어떤 일을 하고 그것을 우리가 했다고 생각하면 교만해질 수 있습니다. 이웃과 의견이 다를 때 화를 터뜨리지 않았으면 우리는 스스로를 좋게 여기고 교만해질 수 있습니다. 그러나 우리에게 문제를 제기하는 이웃을 실제로 사랑할 때는 교만해질 수 없습니다. 그것은 은혜였고, 우리 자신이 아니라 하나님의 능력이 그렇게 하게 했기 때문입니다. 그러므로 우리는 하나님과 그분의 풍성한 은혜에 경탄합니다.

하나님께서 분명히 하신 일을 두고 누군가가 자랑스러워한다면 어리석은 일일 것입니다! 나사로가 죽은 자 가운데서 살아난 일을 자기 공로인 양 자랑하며 돌아다녔다면, 사람들은 그의 정신이 온전한지 의심하며 이렇게 말했을 것입니다. “당신은 아무것도 하지 않았어요! 모든 일을 하신 분은 예수님이었어요.”

그리스도인이 아무것도 하지 않는다고 말하려는 것은 아닙니다. 아닙니다. 우리는 겸손히 하나님의 계명에 순종하고 그분의 길을 걸어야 합니다. 그러나 우리 자신을 자랑할 수는 없다고 말하는 것입니다. 우리가 그분의 계명에 순종할 수 있도록 하시는 분은 하나님이시기 때문입니다.

다윗과 골리앗의 잘 알려진 이야기를 살펴봅시다. 다윗은 그곳에서 싸우고 있던 형들에게 식량을 가져다주려고 군대에 갔습니다. 다가가던 중 그는 자기 백성을 위협하는 거인을 보고 놀랐습니다! 다윗은 다소 충격을 받고 마음이 상한 듯 이렇게 물었습니다. …이 할례 받지 않은 블레셋 사람이 누구이기에 살아 계신 하나님의 군대를 모욕하나이까? –사무엘상 17:26.

다윗의 맏형 엘리압은 그에게 뭐라고 말합니까? “나는 네 교만을 안다.”

엘리압은 다윗의 태도가 교만하다고 생각했고, 그럴 만한 이유도 있어 보입니다. 양을 치던 붉은 기운이 도는 소년이 다가와서는 왜 누군가 저 거인을 처리하지 않느냐고 의아해합니다. 조금 이상하게 들립니다. 하지만 다윗은 무슨 생각을 하고 있었을까요? 그는 오직 하나님께서 무엇을 하실 수 있고, 아마도 무엇을 하시기를 원하시는지만 생각하고 있었습니다! 이 상황에서 자신이 무언가를 할 수 있으리라고는 잠시도 생각하지 않았습니다.

그는 사울 왕 앞으로 불려갑니다. 사울이 다윗에게 말했습니다. “네가 저 블레셋 사람과 싸우러 나갈 수 없으니, 너는 아직 소년이요 그는 어려서부터 용사임이니라 –사무엘상 17:33.”

다윗이 대답했습니다. “주의 종이 아버지의 양을 지킬 때 사자와 곰이 와서 양 떼에서 새끼 양을 물어 갔습니다. 내가 그 뒤를 따라가서 그것들을 쳐서 그 입에서 새끼 양을 건져냈습니다. 그것들이 나를 향해 덤벼들 때면 내가 그 수염을 잡고 쳐서 죽였습니다. 주의 종이 사자와 곰을 모두 죽였습니다. 이 할례 받지 않은 블레셋 사람도 그중 하나처럼 될 것입니다. 살아 계신 하나님의 군대를 모욕했기 때문입니다 –사무엘상 17:34-36.

다윗은 여기서 대단히 자신만만한데, 왜 그랬을까요?! 다윗이 또 말했습니다. “나를 사자의 발톱과 곰의 발톱에서 건져 내신 여호와께서 이 블레셋 사람의 손에서도 나를 건져 내시리이다… –사무엘상 17:37.

다윗의 자신감은 분명 주님께서 그를 위해 싸우신다는 데서 비롯되었습니다. 다윗은 자신이 “아직 소년”이라는 사실을 염려하지 않았고, 사람들이 왜 자신에게 의문을 제기하는지 이해하지 못했습니다. 그는 오직 하나님께서 무엇을 하실지 생각하고 있었습니다! 그러나 엘리압은 다윗의 자신감을 교만으로 보았습니다. 어쩌면 하나님께서 엘리압의 삶에서는 일하지 않으셨을지도 모릅니다. 그는 하나님의 능력을 알지 못했을 수도 있습니다. 그래서 그에게는 어리석은 교만처럼 보였을 것입니다.

사울이 자기 갑옷으로 다윗을 무장시키고, 그의 머리에 놋 투구를 씌웠으며, 갑옷을 입혔습니다. 다윗은 갑옷 위에 칼을 차고 나아가 보려 했지만, 그것을 시험해 본 적이 없었습니다. 다윗이 사울에게 말했습니다. “이것을 입고는 갈 수 없습니다. 이것들을 시험해 본 적이 없습니다.” 다윗은 그것들을 벗었습니다 –사무엘상 17:38-39.

그래서 다윗은 갑옷을 입지 않기로 했습니다. 오히려 방해만 되었을 것입니다. 대신 돌 몇 개를 골라 거인과 싸우려고 달려 나갔습니다. 물론 거인도 이해하지 못했습니다. 그가 …다윗을 보고 업신여겼으니, 이는 그가 소년이었기 때문이라… 블레셋 사람이 다윗에게 말했습니다. “네가 막대기를 가지고 내게 오다니, 내가 개냐?” 블레셋 사람은 자기 신들의 이름으로 다윗을 저주했습니다. 또 다윗에게 말했습니다. “내게로 오라. 내가 네 살을 공중의 새와 들짐승에게 주리라” –사무엘상 17:42-44.

그러자 다윗이 말했습니다. …너는 칼과 창과 방패를 가지고 내게 오지만, 나는 네가 모욕한 이스라엘 군대의 하나님, 만군의 여호와의 이름으로 네게 가노라. 오늘 여호와께서 너를 내 손에 넘기시리니 내가 너를 쳐서… 온 땅으로 이스라엘에 하나님이 계신 줄 알게 하리라 –사무엘상 17:45-46.

그런 다음 다윗이 한 일을 주목하십시오. 그는 거인을 죽이고 머리를 베어 예루살렘으로 가져갔습니다. 이제 엘리압은 무슨 생각을 했을까요? 막내 동생이 패배한 거인의 머리를 들고 예루살렘 거리를 행진하고 있습니다! 사울 왕이 다윗을 부르자 다윗은 잘린 머리를 여전히 들고 사울을 만나러 갔습니다.

다윗은 왜 교만하지 않았을까요? 그 일을 한 사람이 자기 자신이 아니라는 것을 알았기 때문입니다. 놀라운 일을 하신 분은 하나님이셨습니다! 그는 그저 하나님의 은혜를 증언하고 있었을 뿐입니다.

우리가 스스로 어떤 일을 해냈다면, 우리가 한 일이므로 그것을 자랑할 수 없습니다. 그것은 교만일 것이므로 우리는 침묵하고 그것을 겸손이라고 부릅니다. 다른 사람들이 알아주기를 바라더라도 말입니다. 그러나 하나님의 초자연적인 역사라면, 이제 우리는 하나님께서 하신 일을 자랑해야 합니다! 우리는 그렇게 하도록 부름받았습니다.

하나님께서 여러분의 삶에서 일하고 계십니까? 그것이 여러분의 일인지 하나님의 일인지 혼란스럽습니까? 스스로에게 이렇게 물어보십시오. “하나님을 의지하지 않는 사람들도 여전히 할 수 있는 일을 내가 하고 있는가?” 우리가 세상과 다르게 아무것도 하지 않는다면, 하나님께서 우리 삶에서 일하고 계시지 않는 것입니다. 아주 간단합니다. 화내기를 좋아하는 사람은 없습니다. 저는 어린 시절과 십 대 시절의 대부분을 분노 조절 수업을 받으며 보냈습니다. 상담사들은 우리에게 분노를 다스리는 법을 가르치려 했습니다. 거듭나지 않은 마음도 분노를 숨기는 법은 배울 수 있지만, 마음을 바꾸실 수 있는 분은 하나님뿐입니다. 상담사가 사람들에게 화내는 대신 사랑하는 법을 가르치는 것은 한 번도 듣지 못했습니다. 그것은 불가능하니까요! 그것은 오직 살아 계신 하나님께서 한 사람의 삶 속에서 행하시는 역사이며, 우리는 그 역사에 대해 자랑해야 합니다! 우리 삶에 하나님의 은혜가 부어졌음을 증언하는 것입니다. 엘리압이 그랬던 것처럼 누군가 그것을 교만이라고 여긴다면, 모든 일을 인간의 연약한 노력으로 이루는 율법의 역사만 보기 때문입니다.

이해를 돕기 위해 예를 하나 살펴봅시다. 여러분이 집을 짓기로 했다면, 매일 못주머니를 차고 일을 시작합니다. 시간과 힘이 들지만 마침내 집이 완성됩니다. 새로 지은 집 앞에 친구와 함께 서 있습니다. 친구가 “와,” 하고 말합니다. “정말 아름다운 집이네요! 완벽하게 지은 것 같아요!”

여러분은 얼굴을 조금 붉히며 자신이 아는 흠을 지적하기 시작합니다. “아니에요, 완벽하진 않아요. 저기 보이죠? 박공 부분을 제가 잘못했어요…. 그리고 저기 외벽은… 정확히 똑바르지 않아요.” 우리는 겸손해 보이고 싶어서 이렇게 합니다! “네, 아름다운 집이죠. 제가 정말 잘 지었어요!”라고 말한다면 교만하겠지요?

그런데 집을 짓고 싶지만 자신은 지을 수 없다는 사실을 깨닫고 하나님의 도움이 필요하다면 어떨까요? 도움을 구하며 기도한 뒤, 쾅, 집이 지어졌습니다! 못주머니를 차 본 적도 없는데 집이 기적처럼 나타났습니다. 하나님께서 지으셨습니다. 이제 친구와의 대화는 어떨까요? 여전히 흠을 하나하나 지적하겠습니까? 아닙니다! 집의 완전함을 자랑하며 주님께서 하신 일을 담대히 선포할 것입니다.

하나님께서 우리 삶 속에서 어떤 일을 하실 때, 사람들에게 그것을 말하는 것은 교만이 아닙니다. 우리가 한 일이 아니라 하나님께서 하셨다고 말하려면 겸손이 필요합니다! 그러나 마귀는 우리가 조용히 하고 그것을 겸손이라고 말하기를 원합니다. 엘리압이 다윗에게 그렇게 하기를 원했던 것처럼 말입니다. 오늘날 우리는 하나님께서 자기 삶에서 하시는 일을 담대히 선포할 남녀가 필요합니다!

그 대신, 자신을 깎아내리고 마치 패배한 죄인인 양 이 땅의 삶을 힘겹게 견디려 애쓰는 것이 경건한 일이라고 실제로 믿는 사람들이 많이 있는 듯합니다. “일어서라, 하나님의 사람이여! 하찮은 일은 이제 그만두라!”

누군가는 “그렇다면 우리가 얼마나 의로운지 자랑하며 다녀야 한다는 말입니까?”라고 물을 수 있음을 압니다. 이 질문에 답하기 위해 또 다른 장면을 그려 보겠습니다. 도시의 거리만을 집으로 알고 살아온 가난한 범죄자가 먹고살기 위해 도둑질하고 강도질합니다. 그는 자신이 나쁜 사람이라는 것을 알지만, 달리 살아갈 길을 모릅니다. 어느 날 하나님께서 이 사람에게 자신을 드러내십니다. 어두운 골목에서 그는 죄를 회개하고 자신의 삶을 주님께 드립니다. 하나님께서 그를 구원하시고 변화시키시며 회심하게 하십니다. 그는 골목을 떠날 때 새로운 사람이 되어 있습니다! 마음에는 기쁨이, 영혼에는 평안이 있습니다!

그가 친구들에게 무엇이라고 말하리라 기대하십니까? 음, 저기 외벽이 똑바르지 않고, 창문이 너무 작고… 그런 말을 할까요?

아닙니다, 결코 그렇지 않습니다! 오히려 “나는 완전해요! 하나님께서 놀라운 일을 하셨으니 나를 보세요! 하나님의 능력으로 구원받았어요! 예수님의 보혈로요!”라고 말할 것입니다. 그러면서 거룩함의 아름다움 가운데 길을 따라 깡충깡충 뛰어갈 것입니다.

The storm was dark and threatening,
Dark clouds billowed o’er head.
Lightning flashed around me,
Fears gripped and filled me with dread.

Thunder rolled out its forebodings.
My heart felt heavy and numb.
All around the storm was raging,
The turmoil inside struck me dumb.

Not only was the danger around me,
But just as real was the peril within.
I trembled as I looked at the future,
Not knowing how next to begin.

What lay behind the fog?
The wind whistled in my ears.
Suggesting questions, tripping my feet,
And ladening me down with fears.

This storm had removed all signs of the path,
That one time I had thought I could see.
Now, all the familiar was gone to my eyes,
Each step taken hesitatingly.

At the end of myself, I cried out in fear...
"Lord, come unto me! Tarry not, oh my King!"
Silence reigned heavy, I felt all alone,
Only to hope did I cling.

Then a still, but strong voice spoke in my ear,
"My precious child, look up."
Why such a request? When engulfed as I was,
In the fog that refused to break up.

Still in hope, I lifted my eyes,
Trembling at the dark clouds around.
Yet as I looked, I saw something more,
A treasure in the sky there was found.

Amidst all the dark and threatening clouds,
There it was! A cleft of light!
A rainbow shone through, of loveliest hue,
A beacon amidst this dark night.

"My child, fear not, you were never alone.
Not for a second could I leave your side.
Though the path is obscure, and there is much to endure,
Do not doubt that in Me you can hide."

"Yes, for now, you walk amidst trials,
Fears threaten both inside and out.
You wonder and question what is next to be done,
Dangers seem to laugh and flout."

"But here I have placed My rainbow,
That amidst all the darkness and fear,
You can see that My promise is certain.
I will never forsake, but always be near."

"If you keep your eyes on this promise,
My light will guide your way.
The fears and dangers surrounding,
Will then be held at bay."

"This promise can also open to you,
The secrets that are hid 'midst the storm.
For My strength and power are manifest,
When these to My will conform."

"So, My child, gaze long at the rainbow.
Ponder the message it brings.
Though all around you is angry and wild,
Remember the promise that it sings."

~by Adrianna Fanton
