Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh… –Matthew 19:6.

The marriage relationship was authored by God in the very beginning of time. God also offered to bless the marriage (Genesis 1:28) of the man and woman entering into it, if they desired to maintain its beauty and holiness. Since then, Satan has attempted, in every way possible, to corrupt and destroy the existence of Holy Matrimony. As early as Genesis 4:19, mankind was using polygamy to corrupt God's design of marriage. In Leviticus chapters 21 and 22, a plan, called a divorce, was put in place to legally dissolve the “first love”. This also included the option to remarry. When it was first developed as a practice, the call for divorce was initiated by man, not God, and was for the purpose of dissolving what was understood up until that time to be a lifelong commitment.

In this article we want to look at a number of points:

  • What does the Bible teach about marriage? Does the first marriage carry any special position with God?
  • What does the Bible teach about divorce? Does God recognize divorce as terminating the original marriage vow while either spouse is still living?
  • What does the Bible teach about the reuniting of a separated or divorced first marriage?

It is the desire of this study to be comprehensive, while allowing the scriptures to be their own interpreter, thus keeping commentary to a minimum. The purpose of this writing is to encourage diligence with prayer in seeking the will of God through a study of His Word. The desire of the writer has been to prayerfully consider all relevant scriptures and the context for which they were written.

What does the Bible teach about God's view of the first marriage?

At least five times in the Old Testament, the first marriage is described by the Lord as exclusive and lifelong. This same view was supported by Jesus and the apostles in the New Testament.

  1. Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth –Proverbs 5:18. Note the attention given to the wife of thy youth.

  2. For the LORD hath called thee as a woman forsaken and grieved in spirit, and a wife of youth, when thou wast refused, saith thy God –Isaiah 54:6. Being a wife of one’s youth and then later refused, intensified the grieving of this forsaken woman.

  3. Yet ye say, Wherefore? Because the LORD hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth, against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant. And did not he make one? Yet had he the residue of the spirit. And wherefore one? That he might seek a godly seed. Therefore take heed to your spirit, and let none deal treacherously against the wife of his youth. For the LORD, the God of Israel, saith that he hateth putting away: for one covereth violence with his garment, saith the LORD of hosts: therefore take heed to your spirit, that ye deal not treacherously. –Malachi 2:14-16. And why are they made one, exclusive to each other? To raise up a godly seed unto the Lord. Even though God hates putting away, men still try to cover it with a garment of civil, legal acceptance called "divorce".

  4. Matthew 19:3-12: V.4 In the beginning… Jesus, when asked by the Pharisees about this issue, takes them back to original intent of His Father when He chides them… And he answered and said unto them, Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female –Matthew 19:4. He then goes on to remind them of the Scriptures teaching that …a man [shall] leave [his] father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh? Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder –Matthew 19:5-6. Don't equate man’s authority (the civil court) with God’s authority when it comes to deciding what the facts are concerning marriage, divorce, and remarriage. We need to remember that it is God who has joined each marriage together in Heaven and has recorded them in the Book of Life.

  5. For the woman which hath an husband is bound by the law to her husband so long as he liveth; but if the husband be dead, she is loosed from the law of her husband. So then if, while her husband liveth, she be married to another man, she shall be called an adulteress: but if her husband be dead, she is free from that law; so that she is no adulteress, though she be married to another man –Romans 7:2-3. Again, this is pointing back to the beginning in order to establish a basis of Truth.

Only the death of either spouse will terminate the initial marriage covenant in the heavenly records. And once this life is over, only the heavenly records will matter—for all of eternity.

There are several exceptions to the Biblical ideal:

  • Defraud [deprive, keep back] ye not one the other, except it be with consent for a time, that ye may give yourselves to fasting and prayer; and come together again, that Satan tempt you not for your incontinency [lack of self-restraint] –1 Corinthians 7:5. So, restraining the marriage relationship for a time with voluntary consent from both husband and wife when there is a need for seeking God’s favor or guidance on a matter of great importance, may in some circumstances find God’s blessing. However, this should only be engaged in with a clear understanding and commitment by both spouses involved, about when and how to come together again, lest Satan tempt you. This exception has three clear qualifiers… 1) with consent, 2) for a time, & 3) for the purpose of giving yourselves to prayer and fasting.

  • And unto the married I command, yet not I, but the Lord, Let not the wife depart from her husband: But and if she depart, let her remain unmarried, or be reconciled to her husband: and let not the husband put away his wife –1 Corinthians 7:10-11. This is the Scriptural passage that frees the innocent spouse from biblical guilt when the other spouse is the one who chose to part ways. However, the teaching still remains that they shall not marry another “so long as the original partner remains alive”.

What does the Bible teach about God's view of divorce?

It hath been said, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement: But I say unto you, That whosoever shall put away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, causeth her to commit adultery: and whosoever shall marry her that is divorced committeth adultery –Matthew 5:31-32. As Jesus taught the people in His Sermon on the Mount, one of the many things that He kept focusing on was this issue of God’s original plan for marriage.

“Saving for the cause of fornication” Fornication is any type of immorality prior to marriage. Modern-day Christianity, at times, struggles with this idea since the customs of the ancient Jewish culture have long since been forgotten. In Jewish culture, the betrothal period was considered almost as binding as the marriage ceremony itself, so much so that to end a betrothal required a “divorce”. With this as a foundational understanding, fornication here is speaking of immorality during the espousal or betrothal period. If any unfaithfulness was discovered, a writing of divorcement was required to break the betrothal, espousal, or engagement. This specific aspect of divorce was not criticized by Jesus. Even though they were not permitted to engage in the physical relationship of marriage during the betrothal period, they were still referred to as husband and wife. Finally, the reason this is referred to as fornication instead of adultery is because that during the betrothal period the marriage of the two has not yet taken place, nor has their relationship been consummated physically. Thus, just prior to the point in time when they are considered by God as being married, any outside relationship would be fornication, while just after they are considered married, any similar relationship would be adultery.

We have an excellent biblical example of this type of situation with Joseph & Mary in the following verses: Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost. Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily –Matthew 1:18, 19.

So, biblically speaking, divorce can put asunder the first marriage according to civil law but cannot terminate a first marriage before God. A divorced person remains the companion of their first marriage (as long as the other spouse is alive) even when remarrying, whether they are legally divorced or not, thus resulting in biblical adultery for both parties. However, when divorce is allowed to be recognized as being legitimate in breaking or annulling the initial marriage covenant, we have thereby removed the specific reason by which God calls subsequent marriages adultery.

In Matthew 19:3-10, Jesus is teaching the same lesson as in Matthew 5:31-32. However, Matthew 19:3-10 was initiated from an attempt by the Pharisees to trap Jesus with a question: They say unto him, Why did Moses then command to give a writing of divorcement, and to put her away? –Matthew 19:7. Jesus then responds further and says, …Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so –Matthew 19:8.

Also, in Mark it is written, But from the beginning of the creation God made them male and female. For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife; And they twain shall be one flesh: so then they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder –Mark 10:6-9.

Thus, divorce, with all its regulations, is man's attempt to use civil law to terminate that which from the beginning was understood to be until the death of either spouse.

What does the Bible teach about the reuniting of a separated or a divorced first marriage?

He saith unto them, Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so –Matthew 19:8. Here Jesus is teaching the initial mind of His Father. In the law, Moses taught that… When a man hath taken a wife, and married her, and it come to pass that she find no favour in his eyes, because he hath found some uncleanness in her: then let him write her a bill of divorcement, and give it in her hand, and send her out of his house. And when she is departed out of his house, she may go and be another man's wife. And if the latter husband hate her, and write her a bill of divorcement, and giveth it in her hand, and sendeth her out of his house; or if the latter husband die, which took her to be his wife; Her former husband, which sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife… –Deuteronomy 24:1-4.

This is Moses' teaching regarding permission and qualifications for divorce which Jesus explained was because of the hardness of their hearts. Jesus further clarified this by saying, but from the beginning it was not so –Matthew 19:8.

Perhaps Jeremiah also is referring to Moses' writing in Deuteronomy 24:1-4 when he says, They say, If a man put away his wife, and she go from him, and become another man's, shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted? but thou hast played the harlot with many lovers; yet return again to me, saith the LORD –Jeremiah 3:1. The remainder of Jeremiah chapter 3 speaks of God receiving them back if they repent. God pleads for them to (v.13) "acknowledge thine iniquity" (repent), and repeatedly calls for their return (v.14-)

God invited Israel back into fellowship with Him on the basis of acknowledging her sin and changing her ways, giving no heed to the instruction that Moses gave in Deuteronomy 24:1-4, because "from the beginning it was not so."

In Jeremiah 3:8, the Lord had put her (Israel) away and given her a bill of divorcement. But in verses 1 and 12, He invites her to return and in verse 14 He offers the terms of reconciliation. In Malachi it is written, Judah hath dealt treacherously, and an abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem; for Judah hath profaned the holiness of the LORD which he loved, and hath married the daughter of a strange god –Malachi 2:11.

God's divorcing of Israel and Israel's subsequent remarriage to a strange god in no way interfered with them returning to their first marriage. Instead, the Lord invited them back if they would repent, Jeremiah 3:13-14. By the time of Deuteronomy chapter 24 and through most of the Old Testament, divorce was the accepted normal, with mankind attempting to put some regulations on it, "but from the beginning it was not so."

In the book of Hosea, we have a biblical example of the reuniting of a separated or divorced first marriage: … And the LORD said to Hosea, Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms and children of whoredoms: for the land hath committed great whoredom, departing from the LORD –Hosea 1:2 (see also Hosea 2:5).

Sometime after Hosea marries her, she resorts to the life of a "harlot'' (Hosea 3:3) and goes after other "lovers" (2:7). When she refers to Hosea as "my first husband" (2:7), it is evidence that she likely remarried after deserting Hosea. (2:14) By Hosea patiently "alluring her and speaking comfortably to her" (2:19-20), Hosea betrothed her again and Gomer apparently responded (2:20) "in faithfulness” and came to "know the Lord." (3:3) Eventually, Hosea and Gomer both reunited with a commitment of faithfulness to each other.

Restoration to the initial God-ordained commitment is the goal, reconciliation is the process, and a repentant heart before the Lord for His mercy and forgiveness is the means (see Hosea 3:5).

John 4:1-42 is a scripture that some would interpret as objecting to the reuniting of a first marriage after a separation or divorce, because of Jesus' reply to the woman. After she said …I have no husband. Jesus said unto her, Thou hast well said, I have no husband: For thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband: in that saidst thou truly –John 4:17-18.

Some would interpret Jesus to be saying, "You are right woman, none of your five former husbands of which you have divorced or put away (including your first one) are your husband, and neither is the one you have now. Some commentators and others refer to this woman as a five-time divorcee and currently living with a man in an unmarried state. However, I find no evidence in this account that this woman was living an unholy life.

Jesus' purpose of this account is to reveal Himself as the "Messias" with "Living Water" to this woman and many more in Sychar. Jesus says nothing to fault or correct her, which He typically would when meeting with sin. All five husbands could have been passed away and the one she was now seeing, just a friend, perhaps anticipating marriage. Also, we don't know since it doesn't say, but she seemed to be a woman of respect and influence in the city, which would have been unlikely with an ongoing reputation of immorality. Jesus would surely have said something to inform her of her sin, when making available His Living Water. So, to use this account and say that all five husbands are adulterous and still classified as God-recorded husbands does not agree with the rest of Scripture. Nor does it support the context of the statement: he whom thou now hast is not thy husband. To claim that this story is a display of an immoral lifestyle with no known biblical evidence is close to “adding to” or “taking away” from the Scriptures. (See Revelation 22:18)

In conclusion… In our world today and in history past, mankind has attempted to equate subsequent marriages following a divorce, to the level of the initial marriage covenant. This has confused the emphasis and intent God has put on the initial marriage covenant. God's Word teaches that the Lord has always respected repentance in the restoration of any initial God-blessed covenant. For the Lord to bless and prosper the reconciling of any struggling relationship, He requires a broken, contrite spirit of humility and repentance with submission.

The context of 1 Corinthians 7:10-16 is that of a believer being in a covenant relationship with a spouse who is an unbeliever. In verse 15, the remaining believing spouse is not under obligation to denounce their walk of faith to continue a marriage relationship, neither are they free to remarry (verse 11) in the event of the unbelieving spouse leaving. If verse 15 is speaking of the marriage covenant, then verse 39 would contradict verse 15 and the will of God according to the rest of Scripture, (see Matthew 19:5 and 1 Corinthians 7:10). Living separately limits influence to the family and is a negative witness to the community, thus the believing spouse will always have a much greater impact for the Lord by staying true to the “initial marriage commitment” as challenging as that may be.

The Word of God holds the initial marriage covenant exclusively binding and honorable. Any subsequent marriage vow while either spouse is living is considered by our Lord as the sin of lust and adultery and must be repented of if we wish to seek God’s forgiveness.

Therefore, repentance and forgiveness by both spouses, with the desire to reunite and honor their initial God-blessed marriage covenant, is not a desire of the flesh but is the work of the Holy Spirit deep within the heart of the sinner. When there is a godly desire to repent and reconcile a broken relationship, we should fall on our knees in support and sincere gratitude to our Heavenly Father.

Jesus has offered to come between and restore struggling relationships that through humility and repentance seek forgiveness, thus returning to full service for their Lord resulting in eternal joy. He says: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them –Matthew 18:20. And Paul says, But if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also quicken your mortal bodies by his Spirit that dwelleth in you –Romans 8:11.

Karena itu mereka bukan lagi dua, melainkan satu daging… –Matius 19:6.

Ikatan pernikahan ditetapkan oleh Allah pada awal mula waktu. Allah juga menawarkan berkat-Nya atas pernikahan (Kejadian 1:28) pria dan wanita yang memasukinya, jika mereka ingin mempertahankan keindahan dan kekudusannya. Sejak saat itu, Iblis telah berusaha dengan segala cara untuk merusak dan menghancurkan keberadaan Pernikahan Kudus. Sejak Kejadian 4:19, umat manusia telah menggunakan poligami untuk merusak rancangan Allah tentang pernikahan. Dalam Imamat pasal 21 dan 22, sebuah cara yang disebut perceraian diberlakukan untuk mengakhiri “cinta pertama” secara hukum. Cara ini juga mencakup pilihan untuk menikah lagi. Ketika praktik ini pertama kali dikembangkan, tuntutan untuk bercerai dimulai oleh manusia, bukan Allah, dan bertujuan untuk membubarkan apa yang hingga saat itu dipahami sebagai komitmen seumur hidup.

Dalam artikel ini kita ingin membahas sejumlah hal:

  • Apa yang diajarkan Alkitab tentang pernikahan? Apakah pernikahan pertama memiliki kedudukan khusus di hadapan Allah?
  • Apa yang diajarkan Alkitab tentang perceraian? Apakah Allah mengakui perceraian sebagai pengakhiran ikrar pernikahan yang semula selama salah satu pasangan masih hidup?
  • Apa yang diajarkan Alkitab tentang bersatunya kembali pasangan dalam pernikahan pertama yang terpisah atau telah bercerai?

Tujuan kajian ini adalah menyeluruh, sambil membiarkan Kitab Suci menafsirkan dirinya sendiri, sehingga komentar dapat dibatasi seminimal mungkin. Tulisan ini dimaksudkan untuk mendorong ketekunan dalam doa saat mencari kehendak Allah melalui pengkajian Firman-Nya. Penulis berusaha dengan doa mempertimbangkan semua ayat yang relevan serta konteks penulisannya.

Apa yang diajarkan Alkitab tentang pandangan Allah terhadap pernikahan pertama?

Setidaknya lima kali dalam Perjanjian Lama, pernikahan pertama digambarkan oleh Tuhan sebagai ikatan eksklusif dan seumur hidup. Pandangan yang sama didukung oleh Yesus dan para rasul dalam Perjanjian Baru.

  1. Biarlah mata airmu diberkati, dan bersukacitalah dengan istri masa mudamu –Amsal 5:18. Perhatikan penekanan pada istri masa mudamu.

  2. Sebab TUHAN telah memanggil engkau seperti seorang perempuan yang ditinggalkan dan berdukacita dalam roh, seperti istri masa muda yang ditolak, firman Allahmu –Yesaya 54:6. Menjadi istri sejak masa muda, lalu kemudian ditolak, menambah dukacita perempuan yang ditinggalkan ini.

  3. Dan kamu bertanya: “Mengapa?” Karena TUHAN menjadi saksi antara engkau dan istri masa mudamu, yang terhadapnya engkau telah berlaku tidak setia, padahal dialah teman hidupmu dan istri ikatan perjanjianmu. Bukankah Dia menjadikan mereka satu? Namun, Dia memiliki kelebihan roh. Dan mengapa satu? Supaya mereka mencari keturunan yang saleh. Jadi jagalah dirimu dalam rohmu, dan janganlah seorang pun berlaku tidak setia terhadap istri masa mudanya. Sebab TUHAN, Allah Israel, berfirman bahwa Dia membenci perceraian: orang menutupi pakaiannya dengan kekerasan, firman TUHAN semesta alam. Jadi jagalah dirimu dalam rohmu, dan janganlah berlaku tidak setia. –Maleakhi 2:14-16. Dan mengapa mereka dijadikan satu, eksklusif satu bagi yang lain? Untuk membangkitkan keturunan yang saleh bagi Tuhan. Walaupun Allah membenci perceraian, manusia tetap berusaha menutupinya dengan pakaian penerimaan sipil dan hukum yang disebut “perceraian”.

  4. Matius 19:3-12: Ayat 4, “Pada mulanya…” Ketika orang Farisi bertanya kepada Yesus tentang persoalan ini, Dia membawa mereka kembali kepada maksud semula Bapa-Nya dengan menegur mereka… Jawab-Nya: “Tidakkah kamu baca, bahwa Ia yang menciptakan manusia sejak semula menjadikan mereka laki-laki dan perempuan” –Matius 19:4. Kemudian Dia mengingatkan mereka akan ajaran Kitab Suci bahwa …seorang laki-laki akan meninggalkan ayah dan ibunya dan bersatu dengan istrinya, sehingga keduanya menjadi satu daging. Jadi mereka bukan lagi dua, melainkan satu daging. Karena itu, apa yang telah dipersatukan Allah, tidak boleh diceraikan manusia –Matius 19:5-6. Jangan samakan wewenang manusia (pengadilan sipil) dengan wewenang Allah dalam menentukan fakta tentang pernikahan, perceraian, dan pernikahan kembali. Kita perlu ingat bahwa Allahlah yang telah mempersatukan setiap pasangan dalam pernikahan di Surga dan mencatatnya dalam Kitab Kehidupan.

  5. Seorang istri terikat oleh hukum kepada suaminya selama suaminya hidup; tetapi jika suaminya meninggal, ia bebas dari hukum yang mengikatnya kepada suaminya. Jadi, selama suaminya masih hidup, jika ia menjadi istri orang lain, ia akan disebut pezina; tetapi jika suaminya meninggal, ia bebas dari hukum itu, sehingga ia bukan pezina, sekalipun ia menjadi istri orang lain –Roma 7:2-3. Sekali lagi, ini menunjuk kembali kepada permulaan untuk menetapkan dasar Kebenaran.

Hanya kematian salah satu pasangan yang akan mengakhiri perjanjian pernikahan mula-mula dalam catatan surgawi. Dan setelah kehidupan ini berakhir, hanya catatan surgawilah yang akan berarti—untuk selama-lamanya.

Ada beberapa pengecualian terhadap cita-cita Alkitab:

  • Janganlah kamu saling mengurangi hak [merampas, menahan], kecuali dengan persetujuan bersama untuk sementara waktu, supaya kamu dapat mengabdikan diri untuk berdoa dan berpuasa; kemudian hendaklah kamu bersatu kembali, supaya Iblis jangan mencobai kamu karena kamu tidak dapat menguasai diri [kurang mampu menahan diri] –1 Korintus 7:5. Jadi, menahan hubungan pernikahan untuk sementara waktu dengan persetujuan sukarela dari suami dan istri, ketika ada kebutuhan untuk mencari perkenanan atau petunjuk Allah mengenai suatu perkara yang sangat penting, dalam keadaan tertentu dapat memperoleh berkat Allah. Namun, hal ini hanya boleh dilakukan apabila kedua pasangan yang terlibat memiliki pemahaman dan komitmen yang jelas tentang kapan dan bagaimana mereka akan bersatu kembali, agar Iblis tidak mencobai mereka. Pengecualian ini memiliki tiga syarat yang jelas… 1) dengan persetujuan, 2) untuk sementara waktu, dan 3) dengan tujuan mengabdikan diri untuk berdoa dan berpuasa.

  • Kepada orang-orang yang telah menikah aku perintahkan, bukan aku, melainkan Tuhan: Janganlah istri berpisah dari suaminya. Tetapi jika ia berpisah, hendaklah ia tetap tidak menikah, atau berdamai kembali dengan suaminya; dan janganlah suami menceraikan istrinya –1 Korintus 7:10-11. Ini adalah ayat Kitab Suci yang membebaskan pasangan yang tidak bersalah dari kesalahan menurut Alkitab ketika pasangan yang lain memilih untuk berpisah. Namun, ajaran yang tetap berlaku adalah bahwa mereka tidak boleh menikah dengan orang lain “selama pasangan semula masih hidup”.

Apa yang diajarkan Alkitab tentang pandangan Allah terhadap perceraian?

Telah dikatakan: “Siapa yang menceraikan istrinya harus memberikan surat cerai kepadanya.” Tetapi Aku berkata kepadamu: Setiap orang yang menceraikan istrinya, kecuali karena zinah, menjadikan istrinya berbuat zinah; dan siapa yang menikahi perempuan yang diceraikan itu berbuat zinah –Matius 5:31-32. Ketika Yesus mengajar orang banyak dalam Khotbah di Bukit, salah satu dari banyak hal yang terus menjadi perhatian-Nya adalah rancangan semula Allah bagi pernikahan.

“Kecuali karena zinah” Zinah dalam pengertian ini adalah segala jenis amoralitas sebelum pernikahan. Kekristenan masa kini terkadang bergumul dengan gagasan ini karena adat istiadat budaya Yahudi kuno telah lama dilupakan. Dalam budaya Yahudi, masa pertunangan dianggap hampir mengikat seperti upacara pernikahan itu sendiri, sedemikian rupa sehingga mengakhiri pertunangan memerlukan “perceraian”. Dengan pemahaman dasar ini, zinah di sini mengacu pada amoralitas selama masa peminangan atau pertunangan. Jika ditemukan ketidaksetiaan, surat cerai diperlukan untuk memutuskan hubungan peminangan, pertunangan, atau ikatan tunangan. Aspek perceraian yang khusus ini tidak dikecam oleh Yesus. Walaupun mereka tidak diizinkan menjalani hubungan fisik sebagai suami istri selama masa pertunangan, mereka tetap disebut suami dan istri. Akhirnya, alasan hal ini disebut zinah dan bukan perzinaan adalah karena selama masa pertunangan, pernikahan keduanya belum berlangsung dan hubungan mereka belum disempurnakan secara fisik. Jadi, tepat sebelum saat mereka dianggap oleh Allah telah menikah, hubungan dengan orang lain adalah zinah, sedangkan tepat setelah mereka dianggap menikah, hubungan serupa adalah perzinaan.

Kita memiliki contoh Alkitab yang sangat baik mengenai keadaan seperti ini dalam ayat-ayat berikut tentang Yusuf dan Maria: Kelahiran Yesus Kristus adalah seperti berikut: Ketika ibu-Nya, Maria, bertunangan dengan Yusuf, sebelum mereka hidup sebagai suami istri, ternyata ia mengandung dari Roh Kudus. Karena Yusuf, suaminya, seorang yang benar dan tidak mau mencemarkan nama istrinya di depan umum, bermaksud menceraikannya dengan diam-diam –Matius 1:18, 19.

Jadi, menurut Alkitab, perceraian dapat memisahkan pernikahan pertama menurut hukum sipil, tetapi tidak dapat mengakhiri pernikahan pertama di hadapan Allah. Orang yang bercerai tetap merupakan pasangan dalam pernikahan pertamanya (selama pasangan yang lain masih hidup), bahkan ketika menikah lagi, terlepas dari apakah mereka bercerai secara hukum atau tidak, sehingga keduanya melakukan perzinaan menurut Alkitab. Namun, jika perceraian diakui sah untuk memutuskan atau membatalkan perjanjian pernikahan mula-mula, dengan demikian kita telah menghapus alasan khusus yang membuat Allah menyebut pernikahan-pernikahan berikutnya sebagai perzinaan.

Dalam Matius 19:3-10, Yesus mengajarkan pelajaran yang sama seperti dalam Matius 5:31-32. Namun, Matius 19:3-10 diawali dengan upaya orang Farisi untuk menjebak Yesus melalui sebuah pertanyaan: Kata mereka kepada-Nya: “Kalau begitu, mengapa Musa memerintahkan untuk memberikan surat cerai dan menceraikan dia?” –Matius 19:7. Lalu Yesus menjawab lebih lanjut dan berkata, …Musa mengizinkan kamu menceraikan istrimu karena kekerasan hatimu, tetapi sejak semula tidaklah demikian –Matius 19:8.

Juga, dalam Markus tertulis, Tetapi sejak awal penciptaan Allah menjadikan mereka laki-laki dan perempuan. Sebab itu seorang laki-laki akan meninggalkan ayah dan ibunya dan bersatu dengan istrinya, sehingga keduanya menjadi satu daging. Jadi mereka bukan lagi dua, melainkan satu daging. Karena itu, apa yang telah dipersatukan Allah, tidak boleh diceraikan manusia –Markus 10:6-9.

Jadi, perceraian, dengan segala peraturannya, adalah upaya manusia menggunakan hukum sipil untuk mengakhiri sesuatu yang sejak semula dipahami berlangsung sampai salah satu pasangan meninggal.

Apa yang diajarkan Alkitab tentang bersatunya kembali pernikahan pertama yang terpisah atau telah bercerai?

Yesus berkata kepada mereka: “Musa mengizinkan kamu menceraikan istrimu karena kekerasan hatimu, tetapi sejak semula tidaklah demikian” –Matius 19:8. Di sini Yesus mengajarkan kehendak awal Bapa-Nya. Dalam hukum Taurat, Musa mengajarkan bahwa… Apabila seseorang mengambil seorang perempuan menjadi istri dan menikahinya, lalu perempuan itu tidak lagi mendapat kasih di matanya, karena ia menemukan sesuatu yang tidak senonoh padanya, maka hendaklah ia menulis surat cerai, menyerahkannya ke tangan perempuan itu, dan menyuruhnya pergi dari rumahnya. Setelah perempuan itu pergi dari rumahnya, ia boleh menjadi istri laki-laki lain. Jika suami yang kemudian membencinya, menulis surat cerai, menyerahkannya ke tangannya, dan menyuruhnya pergi dari rumahnya; atau jika suami yang kemudian itu meninggal, yang telah mengambilnya menjadi istrinya; maka suaminya yang dahulu, yang telah menyuruhnya pergi, tidak boleh mengambilnya kembali menjadi istrinya… –Ulangan 24:1-4.

Inilah ajaran Musa mengenai izin dan persyaratan perceraian, yang dijelaskan Yesus terjadi karena kekerasan hati mereka. Yesus memperjelas hal ini dengan berkata, tetapi sejak semula tidaklah demikian –Matius 19:8.

Mungkin Yeremia juga merujuk pada tulisan Musa dalam Ulangan 24:1-4 ketika ia berkata, Mereka berkata: “Jika seseorang menceraikan istrinya, lalu perempuan itu pergi darinya dan menjadi milik laki-laki lain, apakah ia akan kembali lagi kepadanya? Bukankah negeri itu akan sangat tercemar? Tetapi engkau telah berzinah dengan banyak kekasih, namun kembalilah lagi kepada-Ku, demikianlah firman TUHAN –Yeremia 3:1. Bagian selanjutnya dari Yeremia pasal 3 berbicara tentang Allah menerima mereka kembali jika mereka bertobat. Allah memohon agar mereka (ayat 13) “mengakui kesalahanmu” (bertobat), dan berulang kali memanggil mereka untuk kembali (ayat 14-).

Allah mengundang Israel kembali ke dalam persekutuan dengan-Nya dengan syarat mengakui dosanya dan mengubah jalannya, tanpa mengindahkan perintah yang Musa berikan dalam Ulangan 24:1-4, karena “sejak semula tidaklah demikian.”

Dalam Yeremia 3:8, Tuhan telah menceraikan dia (Israel) dan memberinya surat cerai. Namun, dalam ayat 1 dan 12, Dia mengundangnya untuk kembali, dan dalam ayat 14 Dia menawarkan syarat-syarat pendamaian. Dalam Maleakhi tertulis, Yehuda telah berlaku tidak setia, dan suatu kekejian dilakukan di Israel dan di Yerusalem; sebab Yehuda telah menajiskan kekudusan TUHAN yang dikasihi-Nya, dan telah menikahi anak perempuan allah asing –Maleakhi 2:11.

Perceraian Israel oleh Allah dan pernikahan Israel sesudahnya dengan allah asing sama sekali tidak menghalangi mereka untuk kembali kepada pernikahan pertama mereka. Sebaliknya, Tuhan mengundang mereka kembali jika mereka mau bertobat, Yeremia 3:13-14. Pada masa Ulangan pasal 24 dan sepanjang sebagian besar Perjanjian Lama, perceraian diterima sebagai hal yang biasa, sementara manusia berusaha menetapkan sejumlah aturan atasnya, “tetapi sejak semula tidaklah demikian.”

Dalam kitab Hosea, kita memiliki contoh Alkitab tentang bersatunya kembali pernikahan pertama yang terpisah atau telah bercerai: … Berfirmanlah TUHAN kepada Hosea: “Pergilah, kawinilah seorang perempuan sundal dan dapatkanlah anak-anak sundal, sebab negeri ini telah bersundal dengan meninggalkan TUHAN” –Hosea 1:2 (lihat juga Hosea 2:5).

Beberapa waktu setelah Hosea menikahinya, perempuan itu kembali menjalani kehidupan sebagai “pelacur” (Hosea 3:3) dan mengejar “kekasih-kekasih” lain (2:7). Ketika ia menyebut Hosea sebagai “suamiku yang pertama” (2:7), itu merupakan bukti bahwa kemungkinan besar ia menikah lagi setelah meninggalkan Hosea. (2:14) Dengan sabar Hosea “membujuknya dan berbicara dengan lembut kepadanya” (2:19-20), lalu Hosea bertunangan dengannya kembali dan Gomer tampaknya menanggapi (2:20) “dengan setia” dan datang untuk “mengenal TUHAN.” (3:3) Akhirnya, Hosea dan Gomer bersatu kembali dengan komitmen untuk setia satu sama lain.

Pemulihan kepada komitmen semula yang ditetapkan Allah adalah tujuannya, rekonsiliasi adalah prosesnya, dan hati yang bertobat di hadapan Tuhan untuk menerima belas kasihan dan pengampunan-Nya adalah sarananya (lihat Hosea 3:5).

Yohanes 4:1-42 adalah ayat yang ditafsirkan sebagian orang sebagai penolakan terhadap bersatunya kembali pernikahan pertama setelah perpisahan atau perceraian, karena jawaban Yesus kepada perempuan itu. Setelah ia berkata …“Aku tidak mempunyai suami.” Kata Yesus kepadanya: “Tepat katamu bahwa engkau tidak mempunyai suami, sebab engkau sudah mempunyai lima suami, dan yang ada sekarang padamu bukanlah suamimu. Dalam hal ini engkau berkata benar” –Yohanes 4:17-18.

Sebagian orang menafsirkan perkataan Yesus sebagai berikut: “Benar, perempuan, tak satu pun dari lima mantan suamimu yang telah engkau ceraikan atau tinggalkan (termasuk yang pertama) adalah suamimu, dan laki-laki yang sekarang bersamamu juga bukan.” Beberapa penafsir dan orang lain menyebut perempuan ini sebagai orang yang telah bercerai lima kali dan kini hidup bersama seorang laki-laki tanpa menikah. Namun, saya tidak menemukan bukti dalam kisah ini bahwa perempuan ini menjalani kehidupan yang tidak kudus.

Tujuan Yesus dalam kisah ini adalah menyatakan diri-Nya kepada perempuan ini dan banyak orang lain di Sikhar sebagai “Mesias” yang memiliki “Air Hidup”. Yesus tidak mengatakan apa pun untuk menyalahkan atau mengoreksinya, sesuatu yang biasanya Dia lakukan ketika berhadapan dengan dosa. Kelima suaminya mungkin semuanya telah meninggal, dan laki-laki yang sekarang ditemuinya mungkin hanya seorang teman, barangkali dengan harapan untuk menikah. Kita juga tidak tahu karena kisah ini tidak menjelaskannya, tetapi perempuan itu tampaknya dihormati dan berpengaruh di kota itu, sesuatu yang tidak mungkin terjadi jika ia terus-menerus dikenal karena amoralitas. Yesus tentu akan mengatakan sesuatu untuk memberitahunya tentang dosanya ketika menawarkan Air Hidup-Nya. Jadi, menggunakan kisah ini dan mengatakan bahwa kelima suaminya semuanya berzina dan masih digolongkan sebagai suami yang tercatat oleh Allah tidak selaras dengan bagian Kitab Suci lainnya. Hal itu juga tidak mendukung konteks pernyataan ini: yang ada sekarang padamu bukanlah suamimu. Mengklaim bahwa kisah ini menggambarkan gaya hidup amoral tanpa bukti Alkitab yang diketahui hampir sama dengan “menambah-nambahi” atau “mengurangi” Kitab Suci. (Lihat Wahyu 22:18)

Kesimpulannya… Di dunia kita saat ini dan sepanjang sejarah, manusia telah berusaha menyamakan pernikahan-pernikahan berikutnya setelah perceraian dengan perjanjian pernikahan mula-mula. Hal ini telah mengaburkan penekanan dan maksud yang diberikan Allah pada perjanjian pernikahan mula-mula. Firman Allah mengajarkan bahwa Tuhan senantiasa menghargai pertobatan dalam pemulihan setiap perjanjian mula-mula yang diberkati Allah. Agar Tuhan memberkati dan memajukan pendamaian dalam hubungan yang bermasalah, Dia mensyaratkan roh kerendahan hati dan pertobatan yang hancur dan remuk, disertai ketundukan.

Konteks 1 Korintus 7:10-16 adalah seorang percaya yang berada dalam hubungan perjanjian dengan pasangan yang tidak percaya. Dalam ayat 15, pasangan yang percaya dan tetap tinggal itu tidak berkewajiban menyangkal kehidupan imannya demi melanjutkan hubungan pernikahan; mereka juga tidak bebas menikah lagi (ayat 11) jika pasangan yang tidak percaya itu pergi. Jika ayat 15 berbicara tentang perjanjian pernikahan, maka ayat 39 akan bertentangan dengan ayat 15 dan kehendak Allah menurut bagian Kitab Suci lainnya (lihat Matius 19:5 dan 1 Korintus 7:10). Hidup terpisah membatasi pengaruh terhadap keluarga dan menjadi kesaksian negatif bagi masyarakat. Karena itu, pasangan yang percaya akan selalu membawa dampak yang jauh lebih besar bagi Tuhan dengan tetap setia pada “komitmen pernikahan mula-mula”, betapa pun beratnya hal itu.

Firman Allah menyatakan bahwa perjanjian pernikahan mula-mula mengikat secara eksklusif dan terhormat. Setiap ikrar pernikahan berikutnya selama salah satu pasangan masih hidup dipandang oleh Tuhan kita sebagai dosa hawa nafsu dan perzinaan, dan harus ditaubati jika kita ingin mencari pengampunan Allah.

Karena itu, pertobatan dan pengampunan oleh kedua pasangan, disertai keinginan untuk bersatu kembali dan menghormati perjanjian pernikahan mula-mula yang diberkati Allah, bukanlah keinginan daging, melainkan pekerjaan Roh Kudus jauh di dalam hati orang berdosa. Ketika ada keinginan saleh untuk bertobat dan mendamaikan hubungan yang rusak, kita patut berlutut untuk menyatakan dukungan dan rasa syukur yang tulus kepada Bapa Surgawi kita.

Yesus telah menawarkan diri untuk hadir di antara dan memulihkan hubungan yang bermasalah, yang melalui kerendahan hati dan pertobatan mencari pengampunan, sehingga kembali melayani Tuhan mereka sepenuhnya dan memperoleh sukacita kekal. Dia berkata: Sebab di mana dua atau tiga orang berkumpul dalam nama-Ku, di situ Aku ada di tengah-tengah mereka –Matius 18:20. Dan Paulus berkata, Jika Roh Dia, yang telah membangkitkan Yesus dari antara orang mati, diam di dalam kamu, maka Dia, yang telah membangkitkan Kristus dari antara orang mati, akan menghidupkan juga tubuhmu yang fana oleh Roh-Nya yang diam di dalam kamu –Roma 8:11.

In October of 2020, a 90-year-old woman named Nancy Russell, who was a resident of a nursing home in Toronto, Canada, expressed a desire to have a doctor help her kill herself. She felt that the isolation of the previous several months was more than she could endure, and she saw no end to it.

Nancy Russell did not have dementia. She did not have any condition that would normally be considered terminal. However, in Canada, it is not necessary to have a terminal condition to ask for help to go through with physician-assisted suicide. Canada calls this procedure “Medical Assistance in Dying” (MAID). The name implies that it is about comfort care, but the reality is that it is anything but comfort care.

A geriatrician heard her story and agreed to help her. She was discharged to spend the next week with her family. At the end of that time, she was given a lethal injection with her family present. This is not an isolated case. In 2020 there were 7,595 people who killed themselves with a doctor’s assistance.

As I consider these sobering statistics, I feel a great sadness. There is a sense in which many families abandon their elderly or ill family members. COVID has only seemed to worsen this problem. An even larger issue is that our society no longer values the lives of older individuals.

A society that no longer values all human lives as important, begins to allow things like physician-assisted suicide, and even euthanasia. Euthanasia is when someone administers medication to another person for the purpose of killing that other person, while assisted suicide is when one person provides medication to another person that they then “self ”-administer, thereby killing themselves.

It is helpful to review how we, as Christians, approach end-of-life situations and try to understand where the world around us has gone so terribly wrong.

Made in the Image of God

So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them –Genesis 1:27. And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul –Genesis 2:7.

God put the life into Adam and Eve during Creation. He molded Adam from the dust of the earth and made Eve from Adam’s rib. It was God Himself who breathed into them the breath of life. More than that, He stamped on them His own image.

Humans do not have value because of services they do for others. They are not worth something because of their intelligence or talents. Rather, humans have value because God created them for a purpose. He values each one of them.

For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life –John 3:16. Considered by some as the most well-known passage of Scripture, this verse makes it clear that every single one of us is valuable to God and worthy of His redemption. Whosoever means “every one of us”.

There are many other verses like Jeremiah 1:4-5 and Psalm 139:13-15 that speak of God’s foreknowledge in our creation. God didn’t simply plan to bring Adam and Eve into this world and then let things go on their own from that point. Instead, He guides the conception and development of each one who is born. We may not understand all of God’s purposes, but we can say with certainty that God does not make mistakes.

Quality of Life

Much of the ethics surrounding end-of-life issues has to do with concepts like “quality of life” and “dignity”. Quality of life is the extent to which someone can enjoy their normal, everyday activities. Dignity refers to people feeling that they are being given adequate levels of respect.

Many people feel that both of these things—quality of life and dignity—decline when someone gets a severe and debilitating illness. Those with such illnesses who do not have a personal relationship with Jesus may feel that they have reached the point where they don’t want to continue living.

It is a dangerous position when people believe that lives are only worth living when things are easy and when the quality of life is high.

We, as followers of Christ, understand that suffering will come to all of us. It brings glory to God when we suffer with a meek and quiet spirit. More than that, it teaches other people the power of a God-transformed life. We cannot bear these trials alone. And we don’t need to because God’s Spirit is with us and gives us the strength to endure faithfully until the end.

Leaving Our Lives in God’s Hands

Christians should not be fatalistic. We do not believe that regardless of what we do, we are certain to die on a pre-determined day.

It seems likely that, while there is a maximum life span for each one of us, we can shorten that considerably through poor decisions.

Someone who drives while intoxicated, or who uses street drugs, may not have a long life, unless they mend their ways. To a lesser extent, someone who eats poorly and refuses to exercise may also shorten his lifespan and have considerably worse health than someone who chooses a healthy lifestyle.

Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months are with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass –Job 14:5. Our days are in God’s hands. It is not our place to do something to deliberately shorten them.

One of the Ten Commandments is: Thou shalt not kill – Exodus 20:13. Certainly this command would forbid doctors from purposely taking the life of their patient. It would also be a command against someone ending their own life.

It is far better if we can leave our days and hours in God’s hands. We have but to serve Him the best we can with what time we have. We do not get to choose the amount of time that is allotted to us.

End of Life

It is difficult to make sweeping statements about what someone can or should experience at the end of their life. Some terminal illnesses, like cancer with bony metastases, can cause large amounts of pain. On the other hand, some diseases, like kidney failure or dementia, cause very little pain, if any.

Some people would rather not pursue aggressive treatments. Chemotherapy, dialysis, and many other modern treatments have side effects, some of which can be quite negative. Choosing not to take treatment for a disease is different from choosing to actively end our lives.

It is also important that it should be an individual person’s own decision and not one that is foisted on them. In Sweden during COVID, the government made the decision that elderly residents of nursing facilities would not be treated for COVID. Many were not even given oxygen, but simply started on Morphine and sedatives to “make them comfortable” as they waited for the end.

Do Not Act in Fear

Many of the decisions that people make as they face a terminal diagnosis are made out of fear. They may be fearful of medication side effects, fearful of death, or simply fearful of being a burden to families.

Christians should not act out of such motivations. For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind –2 Timothy 1:7.

As God’s children, we are not afraid of death. But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope. For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him –1 Thessalonians 4:13-14.

We understand that our Savior has had victory over death and that he has taken away its sting. Jesus won a victory over death and the grave, so that we too can live without fear.

We may choose to take aggressive treatments, but we won’t be motivated by a desperate attempt to stave off death.

Rely On God’s Strength

I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me –Philippians 4:13. This verse comes after the Apostle Paul spends time talking about how he is able to be content in any situation, both in times of plenty and in times of need.

We see clearly in his life that he put this very thing into practice. He experienced stonings, beatings, and shipwreck. One needs to believe that his body complained every evening when he would lie down to sleep, telling him of all the privations it had suffered.

It wasn’t ibuprofen or Tylenol that got him through these times (those wouldn’t be invented for many centuries). Rather, it was the strength which his relationship with God gave him. That same strength is available to us today, no matter what we are facing, even a terminal illness.

Understand that There Will Likely be Pain

One of the choices that people can make at the end of life is to accept palliative care. This is a type of care that is specifically designed to treat the pain and other symptoms, usually of a terminally ill patient (to keep them comfortable, not to try to cure them). This is the sort of care that is offered by hospice programs.

The doctors and nurses in hospice programs are focused primarily on eliminating pain rather than seeking a cure for the individual. Consequently, they rely very much on patients being honest about their pain levels so they can give the doses that patients feel that they need to control their pain.

Of course, this is challenging. Many times, the only way to completely eliminate pain is for a person to be so heavily medicated with pain medication that they are not able to relate to the people around them. As always, there needs to be some balance between controlling the pain and not having so much medicine that the individual is groggy and sleepy.

God is Glorified in Our Suffering

For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory; While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal –2 Corinthians 4:17-18.

None of us enjoys suffering and we certainly do not seek it out. When we go through suffering, the world around us sees how we deal with it, and they can tell if there is something different about us.

We know that Jesus suffered much during His trial and crucifixion. Whatever suffering we go through is tiny compared with that.

Most important is that we keep our eyes on our Savior. He is the one that gives us strength to endure to the end. He is always faithful.

Conclusion

The world is a dark place these days. The value of life seems to have diminished over time. More and more countries are allowing doctors to prescribe medications that allow patients to end their own lives, while others go so far as to even allow doctors to administer medications that will kill their patients.

It is important that we continue to value human life and that we glorify God in everything we face—even if we are dealing with a terminal illness.

If we are responsible for caring for someone in this situation, it is very important that we affirm their value and make certain that they understand that they are not a burden. God values their lives and so should we. This support will help them as they struggle with the limitations that their health has put upon them.

None of us will live forever, but the things we do here have eternal consequences for us and for those we influence.

Pada bulan Oktober 2020, seorang perempuan berusia 90 tahun bernama Nancy Russell, yang tinggal di sebuah panti jompo di Toronto, Kanada, menyatakan keinginannya agar seorang dokter membantunya mengakhiri hidup. Ia merasa bahwa keterasingan selama beberapa bulan sebelumnya lebih daripada yang sanggup ia tanggung, dan ia tidak melihat kapan keadaan itu akan berakhir.

Nancy Russell tidak menderita demensia. Ia tidak memiliki kondisi apa pun yang biasanya dianggap sebagai penyakit terminal. Namun, di Kanada, seseorang tidak perlu memiliki kondisi terminal untuk meminta bantuan dokter agar dapat melakukan bunuh diri dengan bantuan dokter. Kanada menyebut prosedur ini “Bantuan Medis untuk Mengakhiri Hidup” (MAID). Nama itu menyiratkan bahwa prosedur ini berkaitan dengan perawatan yang memberi kenyamanan, tetapi kenyataannya sama sekali bukan perawatan yang memberi kenyamanan.

Seorang dokter geriatri mendengar kisahnya dan setuju untuk membantunya. Ia dipulangkan agar dapat menghabiskan pekan berikutnya bersama keluarganya. Pada akhir pekan itu, ia diberi suntikan mematikan dengan keluarganya hadir. Ini bukan kasus yang terisolasi. Pada tahun 2020, ada 7.595 orang yang mengakhiri hidup dengan bantuan dokter.

Saat merenungkan statistik yang menyedihkan ini, saya merasakan kesedihan yang mendalam. Ada benarnya bahwa banyak keluarga mengabaikan anggota keluarga mereka yang lanjut usia atau sakit. COVID tampaknya hanya memperburuk masalah ini. Persoalan yang lebih besar lagi adalah masyarakat kita tidak lagi menghargai kehidupan orang-orang lanjut usia.

Masyarakat yang tidak lagi menghargai semua kehidupan manusia sebagai sesuatu yang penting mulai membiarkan hal-hal seperti bunuh diri dengan bantuan dokter, bahkan eutanasia. Eutanasia terjadi ketika seseorang memberikan obat kepada orang lain dengan tujuan membunuh orang tersebut, sedangkan bunuh diri dengan bantuan dokter terjadi ketika seseorang memberikan obat kepada orang lain, lalu orang itu menggunakan sendiri obat tersebut sehingga mengakhiri hidupnya.

Ada baiknya kita meninjau bagaimana kita, sebagai orang Kristen, menghadapi situasi menjelang akhir hayat dan berusaha memahami di mana dunia di sekitar kita telah sangat menyimpang.

Diciptakan Menurut Gambar Allah

Maka Allah menciptakan manusia itu menurut gambar-Nya, menurut gambar Allah diciptakan-Nya dia; laki-laki dan perempuan diciptakan-Nya mereka –Kejadian 1:27. Lalu TUHAN Allah membentuk manusia itu dari debu tanah dan mengembuskan napas hidup ke dalam hidungnya; demikianlah manusia itu menjadi makhluk yang hidup –Kejadian 2:7.

Allah memberikan kehidupan kepada Adam dan Hawa pada saat Penciptaan. Dia membentuk Adam dari debu tanah dan menjadikan Hawa dari tulang rusuk Adam. Allah sendiri mengembuskan napas hidup ke dalam diri mereka. Lebih dari itu, Dia mencapkan gambar-Nya sendiri pada mereka.

Manusia tidak bernilai karena jasa yang mereka berikan kepada orang lain. Mereka tidak berharga karena kecerdasan atau bakat mereka. Sebaliknya, manusia bernilai karena Allah menciptakan mereka untuk suatu tujuan. Allah menghargai setiap orang dari mereka.

Karena begitu besar kasih Allah akan dunia ini, sehingga Ia telah mengaruniakan Anak-Nya yang tunggal, supaya setiap orang yang percaya kepada-Nya tidak binasa, melainkan beroleh hidup yang kekal –Yohanes 3:16. Ayat ini, yang dianggap oleh sebagian orang sebagai bagian Kitab Suci yang paling dikenal, menegaskan bahwa setiap kita berharga bagi Allah dan layak menerima penebusan-Nya. “Setiap orang” berarti “kita semua”.

Ada banyak ayat lain, seperti Yeremia 1:4-5 dan Mazmur 139:13-15, yang berbicara tentang pengetahuan Allah sebelumnya mengenai penciptaan kita. Allah tidak sekadar merencanakan untuk membawa Adam dan Hawa ke dunia ini lalu membiarkan segala sesuatu berjalan sendiri sejak saat itu. Sebaliknya, Dia membimbing konsepsi dan perkembangan setiap orang yang dilahirkan. Kita mungkin tidak memahami semua maksud Allah, tetapi kita dapat mengatakan dengan pasti bahwa Allah tidak membuat kesalahan.

Kualitas Hidup

Banyak etika seputar persoalan akhir hayat berkaitan dengan konsep seperti “kualitas hidup” dan “martabat”. Kualitas hidup adalah sejauh mana seseorang dapat menikmati kegiatan sehari-hari yang biasa dilakukannya. Martabat mengacu pada perasaan bahwa orang diperlakukan dengan rasa hormat yang semestinya.

Banyak orang merasa bahwa kedua hal ini—kualitas hidup dan martabat—menurun ketika seseorang menderita penyakit parah yang melemahkan tubuh. Mereka yang menderita penyakit semacam itu dan tidak memiliki hubungan pribadi dengan Yesus mungkin merasa telah sampai pada titik ketika mereka tidak ingin terus hidup.

Ini merupakan sikap yang berbahaya: percaya bahwa hidup hanya layak dijalani ketika keadaan mudah dan kualitas hidup tinggi.

Kita, sebagai pengikut Kristus, memahami bahwa kita semua akan mengalami penderitaan. Allah dimuliakan ketika kita menderita dengan roh yang lemah lembut dan tenang. Lebih dari itu, penderitaan mengajarkan kepada orang lain kuasa hidup yang diubahkan Allah. Kita tidak dapat menanggung ujian ini sendirian. Dan kita tidak perlu melakukannya, karena Roh Allah menyertai kita dan memberi kita kekuatan untuk bertahan dengan setia sampai akhir.

Menyerahkan Hidup Kita ke dalam Tangan Allah

Orang Kristen tidak seharusnya bersikap fatalistis. Kita tidak percaya bahwa apa pun yang kita lakukan, kita pasti mati pada hari yang telah ditentukan sebelumnya.

Tampaknya masuk akal bahwa, meskipun masing-masing dari kita memiliki batas usia maksimum, kita dapat memperpendeknya secara drastis melalui keputusan yang buruk.

Seseorang yang mengemudi dalam keadaan mabuk atau menggunakan narkoba jalanan mungkin tidak akan berumur panjang, kecuali jika ia memperbaiki perilakunya. Dalam kadar yang lebih ringan, seseorang yang makan dengan buruk dan menolak berolahraga juga dapat memperpendek usianya dan memiliki kesehatan yang jauh lebih buruk daripada orang yang memilih gaya hidup sehat.

Jikalau hari-harinya sudah pasti, dan jumlah bulannya sudah tentu pada-Mu, dan batas-batasnya sudah Kautetapkan, sehingga tidak dapat dilampauinya –Ayub 14:5. Hari-hari kita berada di tangan Allah. Bukanlah hak kita untuk melakukan sesuatu yang sengaja memperpendeknya.

Salah satu dari Sepuluh Perintah Allah berbunyi: Jangan membunuh – Keluaran 20:13. Tentunya perintah ini melarang dokter mengambil nyawa pasiennya dengan sengaja. Perintah ini juga melarang seseorang mengakhiri hidupnya sendiri.

Jauh lebih baik jika kita menyerahkan hari-hari dan jam-jam hidup kita ke dalam tangan Allah. Kita hanya perlu melayani-Nya sebaik mungkin dengan waktu yang kita miliki. Kita tidak berhak memilih berapa lama waktu yang diberikan kepada kita.

Akhir Hayat

Sulit untuk membuat pernyataan yang berlaku umum tentang apa yang dapat atau seharusnya dialami seseorang menjelang akhir hayatnya. Beberapa penyakit terminal, seperti kanker dengan metastasis ke tulang, dapat menyebabkan rasa sakit yang hebat. Di sisi lain, beberapa penyakit, seperti gagal ginjal atau demensia, hanya menimbulkan sedikit rasa sakit, jika ada.

Beberapa orang lebih memilih untuk tidak menjalani pengobatan agresif. Kemoterapi, dialisis, dan banyak pengobatan modern lainnya memiliki efek samping, beberapa di antaranya bisa sangat buruk. Memilih untuk tidak menjalani pengobatan suatu penyakit berbeda dengan memilih untuk secara aktif mengakhiri hidup kita.

Penting juga bahwa keputusan itu merupakan keputusan orang yang bersangkutan sendiri, bukan keputusan yang dipaksakan kepadanya. Di Swedia selama COVID, pemerintah memutuskan bahwa penghuni panti jompo yang lanjut usia tidak akan diobati untuk COVID. Banyak di antara mereka bahkan tidak diberi oksigen, tetapi langsung diberi morfin dan obat penenang agar “merasa nyaman” sambil menunggu ajal.

Jangan Bertindak karena Takut

Banyak keputusan yang dibuat orang ketika menghadapi diagnosis penyakit terminal didasarkan pada rasa takut. Mereka mungkin takut akan efek samping obat, takut akan kematian, atau sekadar takut menjadi beban bagi keluarga.

Orang Kristen tidak seharusnya bertindak berdasarkan dorongan seperti itu. Sebab Allah memberikan kepada kita bukan roh ketakutan, melainkan roh yang membangkitkan kekuatan, kasih dan ketertiban –2 Timotius 1:7.

Sebagai anak-anak Allah, kita tidak takut akan kematian. Selanjutnya kami tidak mau, saudara-saudara, bahwa kamu tidak mengetahui tentang mereka yang meninggal, supaya kamu jangan berdukacita seperti orang-orang lain yang tidak mempunyai pengharapan. Karena jikalau kita percaya, bahwa Yesus telah mati dan telah bangkit, maka kita percaya juga bahwa mereka yang telah meninggal dalam Yesus akan dikumpulkan Allah bersama-sama dengan Dia –1 Tesalonika 4:13-14.

Kita memahami bahwa Juru Selamat kita telah menang atas kematian dan telah menghilangkan sengatnya. Yesus menang atas kematian dan kubur, sehingga kita pun dapat hidup tanpa rasa takut.

Kita mungkin memilih menjalani pengobatan agresif, tetapi kita tidak akan didorong oleh upaya putus asa untuk menunda kematian.

Bersandar pada Kekuatan Allah

Segala perkara dapat kutanggung di dalam Dia yang memberi kekuatan kepadaku –Filipi 4:13. Ayat ini muncul setelah Rasul Paulus berbicara tentang bagaimana ia dapat merasa cukup dalam keadaan apa pun, baik pada masa kelimpahan maupun pada masa kekurangan.

Kita melihat dengan jelas dalam kehidupannya bahwa ia menerapkan hal ini. Ia mengalami perajaman, pemukulan, dan karam kapal. Kita dapat membayangkan bahwa setiap malam, ketika berbaring untuk tidur, tubuhnya mengeluh dan mengingatkannya akan segala penderitaan yang telah dialaminya.

Bukan ibuprofen atau Tylenol yang membantunya melewati masa-masa itu (obat-obat tersebut baru ditemukan berabad-abad kemudian). Sebaliknya, kekuatan itu berasal dari hubungannya dengan Allah. Kekuatan yang sama tersedia bagi kita saat ini, apa pun yang kita hadapi, bahkan penyakit terminal.

Pahami bahwa Rasa Sakit Kemungkinan Akan Ada

Salah satu pilihan yang dapat diambil orang menjelang akhir hayat adalah menerima perawatan paliatif. Ini adalah jenis perawatan yang secara khusus dirancang untuk mengobati rasa sakit dan gejala lainnya, biasanya bagi pasien yang sakit terminal (agar mereka merasa nyaman, bukan untuk berusaha menyembuhkan mereka). Program hospis menyediakan jenis perawatan ini.

Dokter dan perawat dalam program hospis terutama berfokus pada menghilangkan rasa sakit, bukan mencari kesembuhan bagi pasien. Karena itu, mereka sangat mengandalkan pasien untuk bersikap jujur mengenai tingkat rasa sakit yang dialami, agar mereka dapat memberikan dosis yang dirasa pasien perlu untuk mengendalikan rasa sakitnya.

Tentu saja, ini tidak mudah. Sering kali, satu-satunya cara untuk menghilangkan rasa sakit sepenuhnya adalah dengan memberi seseorang obat pereda nyeri dalam dosis yang begitu tinggi sehingga ia tidak mampu berinteraksi dengan orang-orang di sekitarnya. Seperti biasa, perlu ada keseimbangan antara mengendalikan rasa sakit dan menghindari pemberian obat yang terlalu banyak sehingga orang tersebut linglung dan mengantuk.

Allah Dimuliakan dalam Penderitaan Kita

Sebab penderitaan ringan yang sekarang ini menghasilkan bagi kami kemuliaan kekal yang jauh lebih besar dan jauh lebih berbobot, sementara kami tidak memperhatikan hal-hal yang kelihatan, melainkan hal-hal yang tidak kelihatan; sebab hal-hal yang kelihatan adalah sementara, sedangkan hal-hal yang tidak kelihatan adalah kekal –2 Korintus 4:17-18.

Tak seorang pun dari kita menikmati penderitaan, dan tentu saja kita tidak mencarinya. Ketika kita mengalami penderitaan, dunia di sekitar kita melihat bagaimana kita menghadapinya, dan mereka dapat mengetahui apakah ada sesuatu yang berbeda dalam diri kita.

Kita tahu bahwa Yesus banyak menderita selama pengadilan dan penyaliban-Nya. Penderitaan apa pun yang kita alami sangat kecil dibandingkan dengan itu.

Yang terpenting, kita harus terus memandang kepada Juru Selamat kita. Dialah yang memberi kita kekuatan untuk bertahan sampai akhir. Dia selalu setia.

Kesimpulan

Dunia adalah tempat yang kelam pada masa ini. Nilai kehidupan tampaknya telah berkurang seiring waktu. Semakin banyak negara mengizinkan dokter meresepkan obat yang memungkinkan pasien mengakhiri hidup mereka sendiri, sementara negara-negara lain bahkan mengizinkan dokter memberikan obat yang akan membunuh pasien mereka.

Penting bagi kita untuk terus menghargai kehidupan manusia dan memuliakan Allah dalam segala hal yang kita hadapi—bahkan jika kita sedang mengidap penyakit terminal.

Jika kita bertanggung jawab merawat seseorang dalam situasi seperti ini, sangatlah penting bagi kita untuk menegaskan bahwa dirinya berharga dan memastikan ia memahami bahwa dirinya bukan beban. Allah menghargai hidupnya, dan kita pun seharusnya demikian. Dukungan ini akan membantu mereka menghadapi keterbatasan yang ditimbulkan oleh kondisi kesehatan mereka.

Tak seorang pun dari kita akan hidup selamanya, tetapi hal-hal yang kita lakukan di sini memiliki konsekuensi kekal bagi kita dan bagi orang-orang yang kita pengaruhi.

In October of 2020, a 90-year-old woman named Nancy Russell, who was a resident of a nursing home in Toronto, Canada, expressed a desire to have a doctor help her kill herself. She felt that the isolation of the previous several months was more than she could endure, and she saw no end to it.

Nancy Russell did not have dementia. She did not have any condition that would normally be considered terminal. However, in Canada, it is not necessary to have a terminal condition to ask for help to go through with physician-assisted suicide. Canada calls this procedure “Medical Assistance in Dying” (MAID). The name implies that it is about comfort care, but the reality is that it is anything but comfort care.

A geriatrician heard her story and agreed to help her. She was discharged to spend the next week with her family. At the end of that time, she was given a lethal injection with her family present. This is not an isolated case. In 2020 there were 7,595 people who killed themselves with a doctor’s assistance.

As I consider these sobering statistics, I feel a great sadness. There is a sense in which many families abandon their elderly or ill family members. COVID has only seemed to worsen this problem. An even larger issue is that our society no longer values the lives of older individuals.

A society that no longer values all human lives as important, begins to allow things like physician-assisted suicide, and even euthanasia. Euthanasia is when someone administers medication to another person for the purpose of killing that other person, while assisted suicide is when one person provides medication to another person that they then “self ”-administer, thereby killing themselves.

It is helpful to review how we, as Christians, approach end-of-life situations and try to understand where the world around us has gone so terribly wrong.

Made in the Image of God

So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them –Genesis 1:27. And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul –Genesis 2:7.

God put the life into Adam and Eve during Creation. He molded Adam from the dust of the earth and made Eve from Adam’s rib. It was God Himself who breathed into them the breath of life. More than that, He stamped on them His own image.

Humans do not have value because of services they do for others. They are not worth something because of their intelligence or talents. Rather, humans have value because God created them for a purpose. He values each one of them.

For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life –John 3:16. Considered by some as the most well-known passage of Scripture, this verse makes it clear that every single one of us is valuable to God and worthy of His redemption. Whosoever means “every one of us”.

There are many other verses like Jeremiah 1:4-5 and Psalm 139:13-15 that speak of God’s foreknowledge in our creation. God didn’t simply plan to bring Adam and Eve into this world and then let things go on their own from that point. Instead, He guides the conception and development of each one who is born. We may not understand all of God’s purposes, but we can say with certainty that God does not make mistakes.

Quality of Life

Much of the ethics surrounding end-of-life issues has to do with concepts like “quality of life” and “dignity”. Quality of life is the extent to which someone can enjoy their normal, everyday activities. Dignity refers to people feeling that they are being given adequate levels of respect.

Many people feel that both of these things—quality of life and dignity—decline when someone gets a severe and debilitating illness. Those with such illnesses who do not have a personal relationship with Jesus may feel that they have reached the point where they don’t want to continue living.

It is a dangerous position when people believe that lives are only worth living when things are easy and when the quality of life is high.

We, as followers of Christ, understand that suffering will come to all of us. It brings glory to God when we suffer with a meek and quiet spirit. More than that, it teaches other people the power of a God-transformed life. We cannot bear these trials alone. And we don’t need to because God’s Spirit is with us and gives us the strength to endure faithfully until the end.

Leaving Our Lives in God’s Hands

Christians should not be fatalistic. We do not believe that regardless of what we do, we are certain to die on a pre-determined day.

It seems likely that, while there is a maximum life span for each one of us, we can shorten that considerably through poor decisions.

Someone who drives while intoxicated, or who uses street drugs, may not have a long life, unless they mend their ways. To a lesser extent, someone who eats poorly and refuses to exercise may also shorten his lifespan and have considerably worse health than someone who chooses a healthy lifestyle.

Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months are with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass –Job 14:5. Our days are in God’s hands. It is not our place to do something to deliberately shorten them.

One of the Ten Commandments is: Thou shalt not kill – Exodus 20:13. Certainly this command would forbid doctors from purposely taking the life of their patient. It would also be a command against someone ending their own life.

It is far better if we can leave our days and hours in God’s hands. We have but to serve Him the best we can with what time we have. We do not get to choose the amount of time that is allotted to us.

End of Life

It is difficult to make sweeping statements about what someone can or should experience at the end of their life. Some terminal illnesses, like cancer with bony metastases, can cause large amounts of pain. On the other hand, some diseases, like kidney failure or dementia, cause very little pain, if any.

Some people would rather not pursue aggressive treatments. Chemotherapy, dialysis, and many other modern treatments have side effects, some of which can be quite negative. Choosing not to take treatment for a disease is different from choosing to actively end our lives.

It is also important that it should be an individual person’s own decision and not one that is foisted on them. In Sweden during COVID, the government made the decision that elderly residents of nursing facilities would not be treated for COVID. Many were not even given oxygen, but simply started on Morphine and sedatives to “make them comfortable” as they waited for the end.

Do Not Act in Fear

Many of the decisions that people make as they face a terminal diagnosis are made out of fear. They may be fearful of medication side effects, fearful of death, or simply fearful of being a burden to families.

Christians should not act out of such motivations. For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind –2 Timothy 1:7.

As God’s children, we are not afraid of death. But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope. For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him –1 Thessalonians 4:13-14.

We understand that our Savior has had victory over death and that he has taken away its sting. Jesus won a victory over death and the grave, so that we too can live without fear.

We may choose to take aggressive treatments, but we won’t be motivated by a desperate attempt to stave off death.

Rely On God’s Strength

I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me –Philippians 4:13. This verse comes after the Apostle Paul spends time talking about how he is able to be content in any situation, both in times of plenty and in times of need.

We see clearly in his life that he put this very thing into practice. He experienced stonings, beatings, and shipwreck. One needs to believe that his body complained every evening when he would lie down to sleep, telling him of all the privations it had suffered.

It wasn’t ibuprofen or Tylenol that got him through these times (those wouldn’t be invented for many centuries). Rather, it was the strength which his relationship with God gave him. That same strength is available to us today, no matter what we are facing, even a terminal illness.

Understand that There Will Likely be Pain

One of the choices that people can make at the end of life is to accept palliative care. This is a type of care that is specifically designed to treat the pain and other symptoms, usually of a terminally ill patient (to keep them comfortable, not to try to cure them). This is the sort of care that is offered by hospice programs.

The doctors and nurses in hospice programs are focused primarily on eliminating pain rather than seeking a cure for the individual. Consequently, they rely very much on patients being honest about their pain levels so they can give the doses that patients feel that they need to control their pain.

Of course, this is challenging. Many times, the only way to completely eliminate pain is for a person to be so heavily medicated with pain medication that they are not able to relate to the people around them. As always, there needs to be some balance between controlling the pain and not having so much medicine that the individual is groggy and sleepy.

God is Glorified in Our Suffering

For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory; While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal –2 Corinthians 4:17-18.

None of us enjoys suffering and we certainly do not seek it out. When we go through suffering, the world around us sees how we deal with it, and they can tell if there is something different about us.

We know that Jesus suffered much during His trial and crucifixion. Whatever suffering we go through is tiny compared with that.

Most important is that we keep our eyes on our Savior. He is the one that gives us strength to endure to the end. He is always faithful.

Conclusion

The world is a dark place these days. The value of life seems to have diminished over time. More and more countries are allowing doctors to prescribe medications that allow patients to end their own lives, while others go so far as to even allow doctors to administer medications that will kill their patients.

It is important that we continue to value human life and that we glorify God in everything we face—even if we are dealing with a terminal illness.

If we are responsible for caring for someone in this situation, it is very important that we affirm their value and make certain that they understand that they are not a burden. God values their lives and so should we. This support will help them as they struggle with the limitations that their health has put upon them.

None of us will live forever, but the things we do here have eternal consequences for us and for those we influence.
