نسمع كل هذا الحديث، عن بهاء المجد وجماله
والكتاب المقدس يتكلم ويروي قصته بنفسه.
هناك مكان في الأعالي، لا تعب فيه ولا خصام.
لكن الكنيسة قد تنسى تلك الحياة،
إن كان حضور الله يشرق كالشمس،
فالغناء العذب يشمل الجميع.
إن كانت السماء حقيقة، فسأطرح سؤالًا:
لماذا كل هذا التركيز على حياة لن تدوم؟
نبني قصورنا هنا على هذه الأرض،
ولا بد أننا نسينا كم أن قيمتها ضئيلة.
ننظر إلى ما نملك ونقول إننا مباركون،
وننسى أنه عما قريب سيحترق مع سائر الأشياء.
الكنوز ثمينة، وهذا ما نتفق عليه.
لكن أودعوها في السماء حيث تبقى إلى الأبد.
أَنَفقد حياتنا من أجل الرب الصالح؟
عندئذ نربح الأبدية وننعم بالسماء.
أم نحب حياتنا، والكتاب المقدس واضح
بأننا سنفقد فرصتنا في السماء الغالية.
إن كانت السماء حقيقة، فلا بد أننا مرتبكون،
إذ يبدو أن هذه الحياة هي ما يسلّينا.
إن كانت السماء تنتظرنا، وكنا نعلم أننا سنذهب إليها،
فلماذا نخاف حين يوجه الموت ضربته؟
حين تكون الحياة الآتية هي السماء، والأبدية معه،
يكون الموت بدايةً، فلماذا يبدو كئيبًا؟
يخبرنا الكتاب المقدس أن حياتنا ليست إلا بخارًا.
فلنتعقل بحكمة ونحوّل أنظارنا.

And David said, What have I now done? Is there not a cause? –1 Samuel 17:29.

The story of David and Goliath took place over three millenniums ago and has been a perennial favorite of the young and old ever since. There is something about the plight of the underdog that we all relate to. Perhaps we subconsciously view ourselves in such odds and secretly hope that there will come a day when our own “ship will come in” in a similar fashion. Unfortunately, that sort of random success seems more akin to a Hollywood production than to real life. We see only the conflict between the young and the old, the shepherd and the warrior, and the heavy military weapons and the sling. Yet there were some preliminary principles that David embraced in his youth that made him a prime candidate for success. But these often go unheralded in our love for a climactic romantic victory.

If the only vision we have of ourselves comes from the social mirror about us, we will carry a warped inner perception similar to what we see as we glance into a trick mirror at a carnival. The social opinions and perceptions of our environment often cast an awkward and skewed description of our person before our eyes and ears. Sometimes it is unrealistically positive, building the person up in the eyes of the media when there is very little heroic character displayed.

The sports arena is probably the biggest offender in this. The individuals are praised who can run, throw, or shoot better than everyone else. But sporting talent adds little to their honest pure worth as a human. The other side of the coin produces an immense amount of negative and degrading input that seeks to thwart any effort to try. These comments are produced in copious showers by stressed parents, insecure siblings, frustrated bosses, and a host of other acquaintances struggling for identity in a “survival of the fittest” society. The input from these two camps is both disjointed, and out of proportion. To be told you are great will never produce greatness any more than a barrage of derogatory remarks will produce humility. Unfortunately, too often many of us allow these disproportionate projections to affect our thinking and chart our course.

The greatest and superior endowment given to mankind over the rest of creation is not found in his physical abilities, but in his mind. The most intelligent of animals can be trained to be responsible, but they cannot choose or direct that training. But as humans, we can write new programs for ourselves totally independent of our instincts or environmental training. Those of us who live in natural accordance with our instincts and conditioning, will scarcely rise above the animal kingdom. But those who will exercise and develop those endowments shall uniquely fill the role God has designed for them in their encounter with the giants. While David’s time and position were unique, the principles he embraced were universal. If I could teach my dog to yodel, it would prove that yodeling is achievable for dogs and open the possibility for others to do it too. Likewise, if David defeated Goliath by miracle alone, then there is no hope for us but to sit and wait for God to do the same for us. However, if principles were at the core of the victory, then there is an example for us to follow and a virtue to secure for use on our own battlefield.

As David arose early that morning and shouldered his pack of corn, bread, and cheese to take to his brothers, he had no idea what the day would bring forth. The Lord was his Shepherd, and he had no lack, but as he came upon the scene he was shocked at the sight. Both armies were positioned on opposite mountains and locked in a stalemate. To take your entire army down into the valley and fight the opposition uphill would leave you at a tremendous disadvantage. One that neither side was willing to risk. So, the Philistines evoked a common dimension of warfare proposing that two warriors would fight in the valley giving no advantage to either side. But the Philistines had a giant among their numbers that terrified the army of Israel. As David inquired into the situation as to why no one would confront the reproachful blasphemies of the infidel, he was met with a stiff rebuke from his oldest brother: …and Eliab’s anger was kindled against David, and he said, Why camest thou down hither? and with whom hast thou left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart; for thou art come down that thou mightest see the battle. And David said, What have I now done? Is there not a cause? –1 Samuel 17:28-29.

Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God –Hebrews 12:2. When a man has a cause set before him, he can endure almost anything. Some endure for a corruptible crown. King Saul had offered tax exempt wealth and son-in-law status, but the earthly dowry elicited no volunteers. While the thought of earthly prominence meant nothing to the tender heart of David, there was a jealous fire kindled by the blasphemous taunts of Goliath and he stepped forward by faith. But faith is not just a whim that may be inflated by an emotional tire pump. For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works [action] is dead also –James 2:26. Thus, with the cause clearly before him, and his God beside him, David offers to fight Goliath.

So David moved forward acting according to godly, uncorrupted principles…

A Caring Conscience is seated in the soul of man and determines what we care about. Many think that a conscience is only useful as a limiting guide. But the human conscience was also created to function in the reverse. When we are convicted that something is good and right, we pursue it with a passion. Thomas Edison said that genius is 1% inspiration and 99% perspiration. While this may be true enough, it is without question that the inspiration must arrive first. Jacob’s aspirations for Rachael made him forget the seven years of labor. Edison’s pursuit of a successful light bulb caused him to forget the thousands of elements that had failed.

Careless apathy is the opposite and is the result of a seared conscience. David was amazed that the blasphemous taunts of Goliath produced no cause for action on the part of God’s army. Give a man a reason to live and he will supply the how –Nietzke. As a holocaust prisoner in a Nazi concentration camp, Victor Frankl was commissioned to labor in the ward of the camp where prisoners were dying of typhus. He observed that when a person gave up hope, death was soon to follow. Likewise, for many of our day, when the hope of personal gain evaporates in the fray, so does the passion to overcome. Most workers today are more concerned about their paycheck than of doing a good and worthy job. Often when a man loses his feelings for his wife, he believes that he is incapable of loving her, but a man with a healthy conscience toward godly principles will act in loving fashion toward her regardless of his feelings or her response. The cause is aroused and fueled by the conscience and lays the foundation for passionate action.

An Honest Imagination belongs to the realm of the spirit and is driven by our conscience. Necessity is the mother of invention –Unknown. Some are waiting for life to be discovered while others are inventing it as they go. This is not a license to claim false ideals. David’s pursuit is honest for he was not warped by the media about him. He has met with success over the beasts (a lion and a bear) in the hills of Bethlehem and with God’s help, incurs no fear of contending with one (a man of war from his youth) in the valley of Elah.

As Saul reluctantly consents to David’s proposal, he proceeds to arm the lad in typical worldly fashion. While it may have been an honor to wear the armor of the king, David would have none of it: …I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them. And David put them off him –1 Samuel 17:39, choosing five stones instead. Knowing what others do and knowing what to do are not necessarily the same thing.

The cowering beliefs of the Israelite army were rooted in a pagan value system. Goliath was not the problem, but rather, faithless fear and the assumption that they needed to engage in the warfare on the terms of the world. Those that embrace a true and worthy cause will surely find the imagination to pursue it.

Goliath had automatically assumed that he would be in combat under his own terms. Insulted and angered he cries out: …Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field –1 Samuel 17:44. As a giant, speed and agility are not his forte and so he orders David to come to him. But Goliath has grossly overestimated his personal ability and underestimated his foe. According to some estimates, at six or seven revolutions per second, David’s sling had the stopping power of a 45 mm handgun, and the hand of a skillful slinger …could sling stones at an hair breadth, and not miss –Judges 20:16. It was not unusual for them to be able to hit birds in flight. Ancient ruins have uncovered tongs that were believed to be used by the military to remove embedded stones from wounded soldiers. If Goliath had a spear and David a pistol, we would not be so quick to believe that the larger man held the major advantage.

Faithful Action is inevitable when our bodies are subject to our soul and spirit, and they are under the direction of God’s Spirit. We are then free to act independently of our nature and other influences. When the lustful passions of the mortal body hold sway over our inner heart and mind, we are defeated before we take one step toward the enemy. As vessels of God’s design, with a moral free will, we have the divine ability to choose our course of action. Some believe that being proactive is merely taking the initiative. But initiative alone will not fit us for victory any more than it did for the sons of Sceva. The desire to dominate is no more noble than Goliath’s unbridled rage to destroy this young upstart. His adrenaline flowed as he scorned David’s youth, jumped to conclusions, was easily insulted, and marveled at the ignorance of others.

But David carried no such reactive mission. His endeavor was that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel. And all this assembly shall know that the LORD saveth not with sword and spear… –1 Samuel 17:47. Faithful action must be focused on yielding what you have, rather than obtaining what you don’t. If life erects concerns outside of our ability to change, it is fruitless to give them our attention. Joseph could not change his brothers’ reception, his master’s wife’s deception, the jail’s seclusion, or the butler’s delusion. The faith of the shepherd boy teaches us to stop lamenting over what we wanna-be and start being what we oughta-be. We need to stop looking for a miracle and start looking for an opportunity. It is not about overcoming extreme odds, but rather it is how we respond to a traffic jam, a disobedient child, an irate customer, or a demanding spouse. It is about owning a cause big enough to defuse selfish reaction and incite charitable pro-action.

Why would Japanese Kamikaze pilots die for a losing cause during World War Two? Why would Muslim terrorists blow themselves up? Why do Catholic Priests and Nuns take vows of celibacy and poverty? Is there no cause for the Christian that extends broader and deeper than the giants of this world? Is there not a cause that stirs our imagination and sanctifies our action? Or isn’t there even one that transforms our mundane work into a channel of grace for the service of the King of the Universe? How would history be different if Jesse would have spent his retirement like the elders of our day? God slays giants by the instruments we yield to him, from the needle of Dorcas… to the nail of Jael, from Zebedee’s boats of the business… to the boys of his bosom.

Shamgar had an oxgoad;
David had a sling;
Dorcus had a needle;
Rahab had a string;
Samson had a jawbone;
Moses had a rod;
Mary had some ointment;
And all were used for God!

Och David sade: Vad har jag nu gjort? Finns det inte ett skäl? –1 Samuelsboken 17:29.

Berättelsen om David och Goljat utspelade sig för över tre tusen år sedan och har sedan dess varit en ständig favorit bland både unga och gamla. Det är något med den svages utsatta läge som vi alla kan känna igen oss i. Kanske ser vi omedvetet oss själva i sådana odds och hoppas i hemlighet att vår egen ”lyckans dag” en dag ska komma på ett liknande sätt. Tyvärr verkar sådan slumpmässig framgång höra mer hemma i en Hollywoodproduktion än i verkliga livet. Vi ser bara konflikten mellan den unge och den gamle, herden och krigaren, de tunga vapnen och slungan. Men det fanns några grundläggande principer som David tog till sig i sin ungdom och som gjorde honom till en utmärkt kandidat för framgång. Dessa förblir dock ofta ouppmärksammade i vår kärlek till en romantisk seger i sista stund.

Om den enda bild vi har av oss själva kommer från den sociala spegeln omkring oss, får vi en förvrängd inre uppfattning, liknande den vi ser när vi kastar en blick i en förvrängande spegel på ett tivoli. Omgivningens sociala åsikter och uppfattningar ger oss ofta en klumpig och skev beskrivning av oss själva, som vi hör och ser. Ibland är den orealistiskt positiv och framställer en person som stor i mediernas ögon, trots att personen visar mycket lite hjältemod.

Idrottsarenan är förmodligen den värsta boven i detta avseende. De individer som kan springa, kasta eller skjuta bättre än alla andra hyllas. Men idrottstalang bidrar föga till deras verkliga, oförvanskade värde som människor. Myntets andra sida ger upphov till en enorm mängd negativ och nedvärderande påverkan som vill motverka varje försök att ens försöka. Sådana kommentarer haglar från stressade föräldrar, osäkra syskon, frustrerade chefer och en mängd andra bekanta som kämpar för att finna sin identitet i ett samhälle där den starkaste överlever. Påverkan från dessa två läger är både osammanhängande och oproportionerlig. Att få höra att man är fantastisk skapar inte storhet, lika lite som en salva nedsättande kommentarer skapar ödmjukhet. Tyvärr låter alltför många av oss dessa oproportionerliga projektioner påverka vårt tänkande och styra vår kurs.

Den största och främsta gåva som människan fått framför resten av skapelsen finns inte i hennes fysiska förmågor, utan i hennes sinne. De mest intelligenta djuren kan tränas att ta ansvar, men de kan inte själva välja eller styra träningen. Men som människor kan vi skriva nya program för oss själva, helt oberoende av våra instinkter eller den träning vi fått av vår omgivning. De av oss som lever i naturlig överensstämmelse med våra instinkter och vår betingning kommer knappast att höja oss över djurriket. Men de som utövar och utvecklar dessa gåvor kommer på ett unikt sätt att fylla den roll Gud har utformat för dem när de möter jättarna. Davids tid och ställning var unika, men principerna han tog till sig var universella. Om jag kunde lära min hund att joddla skulle det visa att hundar kan lära sig att joddla och öppna möjligheten för andra att göra detsamma. Om David däremot besegrade Goljat enbart genom ett mirakel, då finns det inget hopp för oss annat än att sitta och vänta på att Gud ska göra detsamma för oss. Men om segern vilade på principer finns det ett exempel för oss att följa och en dygd att tillägna oss för bruk på vårt eget slagfält.

När David steg upp tidigt den morgonen och tog sin packning med säd, bröd och ost på axeln för att ta med till sina bröder, hade han ingen aning om vad dagen skulle föra med sig. Herren var hans herde, och honom fattades inget, men när han kom fram till platsen blev han chockad av det han såg. Båda arméerna stod på var sitt berg och hade hamnat i ett dödläge. Om man förde ner hela sin armé i dalen för att strida mot fienden i uppförsbacke skulle man hamna i ett mycket stort underläge. Ingen av sidorna var villig att ta den risken. Därför föreslog filistéerna en vanlig form av krigföring: två krigare skulle strida i dalen, så att ingen sida fick något övertag. Men bland filistéerna fanns en jätte som skrämde Israels armé. När David frågade varför ingen konfronterade den otrognas skymfliga hädelser fick han en skarp tillrättavisning av sin äldste bror: …och Eliabs vrede upptändes mot David, och han sade: Varför har du kommit hit? Och hos vem har du lämnat de få fåren i öknen? Jag känner din stolthet och ditt hjärtas ondska; du har kommit hit för att se striden. Och David sade: Vad har jag nu gjort? Finns det inte ett skäl? –1 Samuelsboken 17:28-29.

…och se på Jesus, trons upphovsman och fullkomnare; som för den glädje som låg framför honom uthärdade korset utan att bry sig om skammen och nu sitter på Guds trons högra sida –Hebreerbrevet 12:2. När en människa har ett mål framför sig kan hon uthärda nästan vad som helst. Somliga uthärdar för en förgänglig krona. Kung Saul hade erbjudit skattefri rikedom och en plats som kunglig svärson, men den jordiska hemgiften lockade ingen att ställa upp. Tanken på jordisk ställning betydde inget för Davids ömma hjärta, men Goljats hädiska hån tände en svartsjuk eld inom honom, och han trädde fram i tro. Men tro är inte bara ett infall som kan blåsas upp med en känslomässig luftpump. För liksom kroppen utan anden är död, så är också tron utan gärningar [handling] också död –Jakobsbrevet 2:26. Med målet tydligt framför sig och sin Gud vid sin sida erbjuder sig David därför att strida mot Goljat.

David gick alltså framåt och handlade enligt gudomliga, oförvanskade principer…

Ett omsorgsfullt samvete finns i människans själ och avgör vad vi bryr oss om. Många tror att samvetet bara är användbart som en begränsande vägvisare. Men det mänskliga samvetet skapades också för att fungera åt motsatt håll. När vi är övertygade om att något är gott och rätt, strävar vi efter det med passion. Thomas Edison sade att genialitet består av 1 % inspiration och 99 % transpiration. Det må vara sant nog, men det råder inget tvivel om att inspirationen måste komma först. Jakobs längtan efter Rakel fick honom att glömma de sju arbetsåren. Edisons strävan efter en fungerande glödlampa fick honom att glömma de tusentals beståndsdelar som hade misslyckats.

Likgiltig apati är motsatsen och är ett resultat av ett avtrubbat samvete. David förundrades över att Goljats hädiska hån inte gav Guds armé någon anledning att handla. Ge en människa en anledning att leva, så kommer hon att hitta ett sätt –Nietzke. Som fånge i ett nazistiskt koncentrationsläger fick Victor Frankl i uppdrag att arbeta på den avdelning där fångarna dog i tyfus. Han lade märke till att när någon gav upp hoppet följde snart döden. På samma sätt försvinner också passionen att övervinna hos många i vår tid när hoppet om personlig vinning försvinner i striden. De flesta arbetare i dag bryr sig mer om lönechecken än om att göra ett gott och värdefullt arbete. När en man förlorar sina känslor för sin hustru tror han ofta att han inte längre kan älska henne. Men en man med ett sunt samvete inför gudfruktiga principer kommer att handla kärleksfullt mot henne, oavsett vad han känner eller hur hon svarar. Samvetet väcker och ger näring åt målet, och lägger grunden för passionerat handlande.

En ärlig föreställningsförmåga hör till andens område och drivs av vårt samvete. Nöden är uppfinningarnas moder –Okänd. Somliga väntar på att livet ska upptäckas, medan andra uppfinner det medan de går. Det är inte en licens att hävda falska ideal. Davids strävan är ärlig, för han hade inte blivit förvrängd av medierna omkring sig. Han hade lyckats besegra vilddjuren (ett lejon och en björn) i Betlehems kullar och fruktade inte, med Guds hjälp, att möta en (en krigsman från sin ungdom) i Ela-dalen.

När Saul motvilligt går med på Davids förslag går han vidare med att beväpna ynglingen på typiskt världsligt vis. Även om det kunde ha varit en ära att bära kungens rustning ville David inte ha något av den: …Jag kan inte gå i dessa, för jag har inte prövat dem. Och David tog av sig dem –1 Samuelsboken 17:39, och valde i stället fem stenar. Att veta vad andra gör och att veta vad man själv bör göra är inte nödvändigtvis samma sak.

Israels armés räddhågade föreställningar hade sina rötter i ett hedniskt värdesystem. Goljat var inte problemet; problemet var snarare den troslösa rädslan och antagandet att de måste föra krig på världens villkor. De som tar sig an ett sant och värdefullt mål kommer säkert att finna den föreställningsförmåga som krävs för att sträva efter det.

Goljat hade automatiskt utgått från att striden skulle ske på hans villkor. Förolämpad och vred ropar han: …Kom hit till mig, så ska jag ge ditt kött åt himlens fåglar och markens djur –1 Samuelsboken 17:44. Som jätte saknar han snabbhet och smidighet, och därför befaller han David att komma till honom. Men Goljat har grovt överskattat sin egen förmåga och underskattat sin motståndare. Enligt vissa uppskattningar hade Davids slunga, med sex eller sju varv per sekund, samma stoppkraft som en 45 mm pistol, och en skicklig slungares hand …kunde slunga stenar på ett hårstrås bredd och inte missa –Domarboken 20:16. Det var inte ovanligt att de kunde träffa fåglar i flykten. I forntida ruiner har man hittat tänger som tros ha använts av militären för att avlägsna stenar som trängt in i sårade soldater. Om Goljat hade ett spjut och David en pistol skulle vi inte så snabbt tro att den större mannen hade det stora övertaget.

Trofast handling är oundviklig när våra kroppar underställs vår själ och ande, och de står under Guds Andes ledning. Då är vi fria att handla oberoende av vår natur och andra inflytanden. När den dödliga kroppens lustfyllda begär får makt över vårt inre hjärta och sinne är vi besegrade innan vi ens tar ett steg mot fienden. Som kärl utformade av Gud, med en moraliskt fri vilja, har vi en gudomlig förmåga att välja vårt handlingssätt. Somliga tror att initiativkraft helt enkelt handlar om att ta initiativet. Men initiativ räcker inte ensamt för att göra oss redo för seger, lika lite som det gjorde det för Skevas söner. Önskan att härska är inte ädlare än Goljats tygellösa raseri över att förgöra denna unge uppkomling. Hans adrenalin flödade när han föraktade Davids ungdom, drog förhastade slutsatser, lätt blev förolämpad och förundrades över andras okunnighet.

Men David drevs inte av någon sådan reaktiv avsikt. Hans mål var att hela jorden skulle veta att det finns en Gud i Israel. Och hela denna församling ska veta att Herren inte frälsar med svärd och spjut… –1 Samuelsboken 17:47. Trofast handling måste inriktas på att ge det man har, snarare än att skaffa det man saknar. Om livet skapar bekymmer som ligger utanför vår förmåga att förändra, är det fruktlöst att ägna dem vår uppmärksamhet. Josef kunde inte förändra hur hans bröder tog emot honom, sin herres hustrus svek, fängelsets isolering eller munskänkens villfarelse. Herdegossens tro lär oss att sluta sörja över vad vi skulle vilja vara och börja vara det vi borde vara. Vi måste sluta leta efter ett mirakel och börja leta efter en möjlighet. Det handlar inte om att övervinna osannolikt stora odds, utan om hur vi reagerar på en trafikstockning, ett olydigt barn, en ursinnig kund eller en krävande make eller maka. Det handlar om att äga ett mål som är stort nog att avväpna själviska reaktioner och väcka osjälviskt handlande.

Varför dog japanska kamikazepiloter för en förlorad sak under andra världskriget? Varför spränger muslimska terrorister sig själva i luften? Varför avlägger katolska präster och nunnor löften om celibat och fattigdom? Finns det ingen sak för den kristne som sträcker sig vidare och djupare än denna världens jättar? Finns det inte ett mål som väcker vår föreställningsförmåga och helgar våra handlingar? Eller finns det inte ens ett mål som förvandlar vårt vardagliga arbete till en nådens kanal i tjänst för universums Konung? Hur skulle historien ha sett annorlunda ut om Isai hade ägnat sin pension åt samma saker som vår tids äldre? Gud fäller jättar genom de redskap vi räcker honom, från Dorkas nål… till Jaels spik, från Sebedaios båtar i hans verksamhet… till pojkarna i hans famn.

Samgar hade en oxpik;
David hade en slunga;
Dorkas hade en nål;
Rahab hade ett snöre;
Simson hade ett käkben;
Mose hade en stav;
Maria hade lite salva;
Och allt användes för Gud!

In October of 2020, a 90-year-old woman named Nancy Russell, who was a resident of a nursing home in Toronto, Canada, expressed a desire to have a doctor help her kill herself. She felt that the isolation of the previous several months was more than she could endure, and she saw no end to it.

Nancy Russell did not have dementia. She did not have any condition that would normally be considered terminal. However, in Canada, it is not necessary to have a terminal condition to ask for help to go through with physician-assisted suicide. Canada calls this procedure “Medical Assistance in Dying” (MAID). The name implies that it is about comfort care, but the reality is that it is anything but comfort care.

A geriatrician heard her story and agreed to help her. She was discharged to spend the next week with her family. At the end of that time, she was given a lethal injection with her family present. This is not an isolated case. In 2020 there were 7,595 people who killed themselves with a doctor’s assistance.

As I consider these sobering statistics, I feel a great sadness. There is a sense in which many families abandon their elderly or ill family members. COVID has only seemed to worsen this problem. An even larger issue is that our society no longer values the lives of older individuals.

A society that no longer values all human lives as important, begins to allow things like physician-assisted suicide, and even euthanasia. Euthanasia is when someone administers medication to another person for the purpose of killing that other person, while assisted suicide is when one person provides medication to another person that they then “self ”-administer, thereby killing themselves.

It is helpful to review how we, as Christians, approach end-of-life situations and try to understand where the world around us has gone so terribly wrong.

Made in the Image of God

So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them –Genesis 1:27. And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul –Genesis 2:7.

God put the life into Adam and Eve during Creation. He molded Adam from the dust of the earth and made Eve from Adam’s rib. It was God Himself who breathed into them the breath of life. More than that, He stamped on them His own image.

Humans do not have value because of services they do for others. They are not worth something because of their intelligence or talents. Rather, humans have value because God created them for a purpose. He values each one of them.

For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life –John 3:16. Considered by some as the most well-known passage of Scripture, this verse makes it clear that every single one of us is valuable to God and worthy of His redemption. Whosoever means “every one of us”.

There are many other verses like Jeremiah 1:4-5 and Psalm 139:13-15 that speak of God’s foreknowledge in our creation. God didn’t simply plan to bring Adam and Eve into this world and then let things go on their own from that point. Instead, He guides the conception and development of each one who is born. We may not understand all of God’s purposes, but we can say with certainty that God does not make mistakes.

Quality of Life

Much of the ethics surrounding end-of-life issues has to do with concepts like “quality of life” and “dignity”. Quality of life is the extent to which someone can enjoy their normal, everyday activities. Dignity refers to people feeling that they are being given adequate levels of respect.

Many people feel that both of these things—quality of life and dignity—decline when someone gets a severe and debilitating illness. Those with such illnesses who do not have a personal relationship with Jesus may feel that they have reached the point where they don’t want to continue living.

It is a dangerous position when people believe that lives are only worth living when things are easy and when the quality of life is high.

We, as followers of Christ, understand that suffering will come to all of us. It brings glory to God when we suffer with a meek and quiet spirit. More than that, it teaches other people the power of a God-transformed life. We cannot bear these trials alone. And we don’t need to because God’s Spirit is with us and gives us the strength to endure faithfully until the end.

Leaving Our Lives in God’s Hands

Christians should not be fatalistic. We do not believe that regardless of what we do, we are certain to die on a pre-determined day.

It seems likely that, while there is a maximum life span for each one of us, we can shorten that considerably through poor decisions.

Someone who drives while intoxicated, or who uses street drugs, may not have a long life, unless they mend their ways. To a lesser extent, someone who eats poorly and refuses to exercise may also shorten his lifespan and have considerably worse health than someone who chooses a healthy lifestyle.

Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months are with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass –Job 14:5. Our days are in God’s hands. It is not our place to do something to deliberately shorten them.

One of the Ten Commandments is: Thou shalt not kill – Exodus 20:13. Certainly this command would forbid doctors from purposely taking the life of their patient. It would also be a command against someone ending their own life.

It is far better if we can leave our days and hours in God’s hands. We have but to serve Him the best we can with what time we have. We do not get to choose the amount of time that is allotted to us.

End of Life

It is difficult to make sweeping statements about what someone can or should experience at the end of their life. Some terminal illnesses, like cancer with bony metastases, can cause large amounts of pain. On the other hand, some diseases, like kidney failure or dementia, cause very little pain, if any.

Some people would rather not pursue aggressive treatments. Chemotherapy, dialysis, and many other modern treatments have side effects, some of which can be quite negative. Choosing not to take treatment for a disease is different from choosing to actively end our lives.

It is also important that it should be an individual person’s own decision and not one that is foisted on them. In Sweden during COVID, the government made the decision that elderly residents of nursing facilities would not be treated for COVID. Many were not even given oxygen, but simply started on Morphine and sedatives to “make them comfortable” as they waited for the end.

Do Not Act in Fear

Many of the decisions that people make as they face a terminal diagnosis are made out of fear. They may be fearful of medication side effects, fearful of death, or simply fearful of being a burden to families.

Christians should not act out of such motivations. For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind –2 Timothy 1:7.

As God’s children, we are not afraid of death. But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope. For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him –1 Thessalonians 4:13-14.

We understand that our Savior has had victory over death and that he has taken away its sting. Jesus won a victory over death and the grave, so that we too can live without fear.

We may choose to take aggressive treatments, but we won’t be motivated by a desperate attempt to stave off death.

Rely On God’s Strength

I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me –Philippians 4:13. This verse comes after the Apostle Paul spends time talking about how he is able to be content in any situation, both in times of plenty and in times of need.

We see clearly in his life that he put this very thing into practice. He experienced stonings, beatings, and shipwreck. One needs to believe that his body complained every evening when he would lie down to sleep, telling him of all the privations it had suffered.

It wasn’t ibuprofen or Tylenol that got him through these times (those wouldn’t be invented for many centuries). Rather, it was the strength which his relationship with God gave him. That same strength is available to us today, no matter what we are facing, even a terminal illness.

Understand that There Will Likely be Pain

One of the choices that people can make at the end of life is to accept palliative care. This is a type of care that is specifically designed to treat the pain and other symptoms, usually of a terminally ill patient (to keep them comfortable, not to try to cure them). This is the sort of care that is offered by hospice programs.

The doctors and nurses in hospice programs are focused primarily on eliminating pain rather than seeking a cure for the individual. Consequently, they rely very much on patients being honest about their pain levels so they can give the doses that patients feel that they need to control their pain.

Of course, this is challenging. Many times, the only way to completely eliminate pain is for a person to be so heavily medicated with pain medication that they are not able to relate to the people around them. As always, there needs to be some balance between controlling the pain and not having so much medicine that the individual is groggy and sleepy.

God is Glorified in Our Suffering

For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory; While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal –2 Corinthians 4:17-18.

None of us enjoys suffering and we certainly do not seek it out. When we go through suffering, the world around us sees how we deal with it, and they can tell if there is something different about us.

We know that Jesus suffered much during His trial and crucifixion. Whatever suffering we go through is tiny compared with that.

Most important is that we keep our eyes on our Savior. He is the one that gives us strength to endure to the end. He is always faithful.

Conclusion

The world is a dark place these days. The value of life seems to have diminished over time. More and more countries are allowing doctors to prescribe medications that allow patients to end their own lives, while others go so far as to even allow doctors to administer medications that will kill their patients.

It is important that we continue to value human life and that we glorify God in everything we face—even if we are dealing with a terminal illness.

If we are responsible for caring for someone in this situation, it is very important that we affirm their value and make certain that they understand that they are not a burden. God values their lives and so should we. This support will help them as they struggle with the limitations that their health has put upon them.

None of us will live forever, but the things we do here have eternal consequences for us and for those we influence.

Mnamo Oktoba 2020, mwanamke mwenye umri wa miaka 90 aliyeitwa Nancy Russell, aliyekuwa mkazi wa makao ya kuwatunzia wazee huko Toronto, Kanada, alionyesha nia ya kutaka daktari amsaidie kujiua. Alihisi kwamba kutengwa kwa miezi kadhaa iliyotangulia kulikuwa zaidi ya alivyoweza kuvumilia, naye hakuona mwisho wake.

Nancy Russell hakuwa na shida ya akili ya kupoteza kumbukumbu. Hakuwa na hali yoyote ambayo kwa kawaida ingechukuliwa kuwa ya kuua. Hata hivyo, nchini Kanada si lazima mtu awe na hali ya ugonjwa wa kuua ili kuomba msaada wa daktari wa kumsaidia kujiua. Kanada inaita utaratibu huu “Msaada wa Kimatibabu wa Kufa” (MAID). Jina hilo linadokeza kwamba unahusu huduma ya kumstarehesha mgonjwa, lakini kwa kweli si huduma ya kumstarehesha hata kidogo.

Daktari bingwa wa magonjwa ya wazee alisikiliza kisa chake na kukubali kumsaidia. Aliruhusiwa kuondoka hospitalini ili akae wiki iliyofuata na familia yake. Mwishoni mwa wakati huo, alidungwa sindano ya sumu ya kuua huku familia yake ikiwa hapo. Hili si tukio la pekee. Mwaka 2020, watu 7,595 walijiua kwa msaada wa daktari.

Ninapozitafakari takwimu hizi zenye kuhuzunisha, nahisi huzuni kubwa. Kwa namna fulani, familia nyingi huwaacha wazee au wagonjwa wa familia zao. COVID imeonekana tu kuzidisha tatizo hili. Jambo kubwa zaidi ni kwamba jamii yetu haithamini tena maisha ya watu wazee.

Jamii ambayo haithamini tena maisha yote ya wanadamu kuwa muhimu huanza kuruhusu mambo kama vile kujiua kwa msaada wa daktari, na hata kuwaua wagonjwa kwa huruma. Kumuua mgonjwa kwa huruma ni pale mtu anapompa mtu mwingine dawa kwa madhumuni ya kumuua, ilhali kujiua kwa msaada ni pale mtu mmoja anapompa mtu mwingine dawa ambazo mtu huyo hujitumia mwenyewe, na hivyo kujiua.

Ni vyema kutazama jinsi sisi kama Wakristo tunavyokabiliana na hali za mwisho wa maisha na kujaribu kuelewa ni wapi ulimwengu unaotuzunguka umekosea sana.

Tumeumbwa kwa Mfano wa Mungu

Basi Mungu akamwumba mtu kwa mfano wake mwenyewe, kwa mfano wa Mungu alimwumba, mwanamume na mwanamke aliwaumba –Mwanzo 1:27. Bwana Mungu akamfanya mtu kwa mavumbi ya ardhi, akampulizia puani pumzi ya uhai; mtu akawa nafsi hai –Mwanzo 2:7.

Mungu aliweka uhai ndani ya Adamu na Hawa wakati wa Uumbaji. Alimfinyanga Adamu kutoka mavumbi ya nchi na kumfanya Hawa kutokana na ubavu wa Adamu. Mungu Mwenyewe ndiye aliyewapulizia pumzi ya uhai. Zaidi ya hayo, aliweka ndani yao mfano wake mwenyewe.

Wanadamu hawana thamani kwa sababu ya huduma wanazowafanyia wengine. Hawana thamani kwa sababu ya akili au vipawa vyao. Badala yake, wanadamu wana thamani kwa sababu Mungu aliwaumba kwa kusudi. Anamthamini kila mmoja wao.

Kwa maana jinsi hii Mungu aliupenda ulimwengu, hata akamtoa Mwanawe wa pekee, ili kila mtu amwaminiye asipotee, bali awe na uzima wa milele –Yohana 3:16. Wengine wanaona huu kuwa mstari wa Maandiko unaojulikana zaidi, nao unaweka wazi kwamba kila mmoja wetu ana thamani kwa Mungu na anastahili ukombozi wake. “Kila mtu” maana yake ni “kila mmoja wetu”.

Kuna mistari mingine mingi kama Yeremia 1:4-5 na Zaburi 139:13-15 inayozungumzia kujua kwa Mungu tangu zamani kuhusu uumbaji wetu. Mungu hakupanga tu kuwaleta Adamu na Hawa ulimwenguni kisha kuyaacha mambo yaende yenyewe kuanzia hapo. Badala yake, anaongoza kutungwa mimba na kukua kwa kila mmoja anayezaliwa. Huenda tusielewe makusudi yote ya Mungu, lakini tunaweza kusema kwa hakika kwamba Mungu hafanyi makosa.

Ubora wa Maisha

Sehemu kubwa ya maadili yanayohusu masuala ya mwisho wa maisha inahusu dhana kama “ubora wa maisha” na “heshima”. Ubora wa maisha ni kiwango ambacho mtu anaweza kufurahia shughuli zake za kawaida za kila siku. Heshima inahusu watu kuhisi kwamba wanatendewa kwa heshima inayofaa.

Watu wengi huhisi kwamba mambo haya yote mawili—ubora wa maisha na heshima—hupungua mtu anapopata ugonjwa mkali unaomdhoofisha. Wale walio na magonjwa kama hayo na wasio na uhusiano binafsi na Yesu wanaweza kuhisi kwamba wamefika mahali ambapo hawataki kuendelea kuishi.

Ni hatari watu wanapoamini kwamba maisha yana thamani ya kuishi tu wakati mambo ni rahisi na ubora wa maisha uko juu.

Sisi, kama wafuasi wa Kristo, tunaelewa kwamba mateso yatatupata sote. Tunapoteseka kwa roho ya upole na utulivu, hilo humletea Mungu utukufu. Zaidi ya hayo, huwafundisha watu wengine nguvu ya maisha yaliyobadilishwa na Mungu. Hatuwezi kuvumilia majaribu haya peke yetu. Na hatuhitaji kufanya hivyo kwa sababu Roho wa Mungu yu pamoja nasi na hutupa nguvu ya kuvumilia kwa uaminifu hadi mwisho.

Kuyakabidhi Maisha Yetu Mikononi mwa Mungu

Wakristo hawapaswi kuwa na mtazamo wa kukubali kila jambo kana kwamba limeamuliwa mapema. Hatuamini kwamba hata tufanye nini, bila shaka tutakufa siku iliyopangwa kimbele.

Inaonekana kuna uwezekano kwamba, ingawa kila mmoja wetu ana muda wa juu zaidi wa kuishi, tunaweza kuufupisha sana kwa kufanya maamuzi mabaya.

Mtu anayeendesha gari akiwa amelewa, au anayetumia dawa za kulevya za mitaani, huenda asiishi maisha marefu isipokuwa abadili mwenendo wake. Kwa kiwango kidogo zaidi, mtu anayekula vibaya na kukataa kufanya mazoezi pia anaweza kufupisha maisha yake na kuwa na afya mbaya zaidi kuliko mtu anayechagua mtindo bora wa maisha.

Kwa kuwa siku zake zimeamriwa, hesabu ya miezi yake iko kwako; umemwekea mipaka yake asiyoweza kuivuka –Ayubu 14:5. Siku zetu ziko mikononi mwa Mungu. Si wajibu wetu kufanya jambo la kuzifupisha kimakusudi.

Moja ya Amri Kumi ni: Usiue – Kutoka 20:13. Bila shaka amri hii ingewakataza madaktari kuua wagonjwa wao kimakusudi. Pia ingekuwa amri inayomkataza mtu kujiua.

Ni afadhali zaidi tuyaache maisha yetu na saa zetu mikononi mwa Mungu. Tunachopaswa kufanya ni kumtumikia kadiri tuwezavyo kwa muda tulio nao. Hatuwezi kuchagua muda tuliopangiwa.

Wakati wa Mwisho wa Maisha

Ni vigumu kutoa kauli za jumla kuhusu kile ambacho mtu anaweza au anapaswa kupitia mwishoni mwa maisha yake. Baadhi ya magonjwa ya kuua, kama vile saratani iliyoenea hadi kwenye mifupa, yanaweza kusababisha maumivu makali sana. Kwa upande mwingine, baadhi ya magonjwa, kama vile figo kushindwa kufanya kazi au shida ya akili ya kupoteza kumbukumbu, husababisha maumivu machache sana, ikiwa yapo.

Baadhi ya watu hawapendi kufuata matibabu makali. Tiba ya kemikali, dayalisisi na matibabu mengine mengi ya kisasa yana madhara, ambayo baadhi yake yanaweza kuwa mabaya sana. Kuchagua kutopokea matibabu ya ugonjwa ni tofauti na kuchagua kuyakatisha maisha yetu kwa makusudi.

Pia ni muhimu kwamba uamuzi uwe wa mtu binafsi mwenyewe, wala usilazimishwe kwake. Nchini Uswidi wakati wa COVID, serikali iliamua kwamba wakazi wazee wa vituo vya kulea hawatatibiwa COVID. Wengi hawakupewa hata oksijeni, bali walianzishiwa tu morfini na dawa za kutuliza ili “kuwastarehesha” walipokuwa wakingojea mwisho.

Usitende kwa Hofu

Maamuzi mengi ambayo watu hufanya wanapokabiliwa na utambuzi wa ugonjwa wa kuua hufanywa kwa hofu. Huenda wakaogopa madhara ya dawa, wakaogopa kifo, au wakaogopa tu kuwa mzigo kwa familia zao.

Wakristo hawapaswi kutenda kwa sababu hizo. Maana Mungu hakutupa roho ya woga, bali ya nguvu na ya upendo na ya moyo wa kiasi –2 Timotheo 1:7.

Kwa kuwa sisi ni watoto wa Mungu, hatuogopi kifo. Lakini, ndugu, hatutaki msijue habari zao waliolala mauti, msije mkahuzunika kama na wengine wasio na matumaini. Maana, ikiwa twaamini ya kwamba Yesu alikufa akafufuka, vivyo hivyo na hao waliolala katika Yesu, Mungu atawaleta pamoja naye –1 Wathesalonike 4:13-14.

Tunaelewa kwamba Mwokozi wetu ameshinda kifo na ameondoa uchungu wake. Yesu alishinda kifo na kaburi, ili sisi pia tuweze kuishi bila hofu.

Tunaweza kuchagua matibabu makali, lakini hatutasukumwa na jaribio la kukata tamaa la kuzuia kifo kisitufikie.

Tegemea Nguvu za Mungu

Nayaweza mambo yote katika yeye anitiaye nguvu –Wafilipi 4:13. Mstari huu unafuata baada ya Mtume Paulo kuzungumzia jinsi anavyoweza kuridhika katika hali yoyote, wakati wa kuwa na vingi na wakati wa kuwa na uhitaji.

Tunaona wazi katika maisha yake kwamba alitenda jambo hili hasa. Alipigwa mawe, akapigwa na akavunjikiwa na meli. Mtu anaweza kuamini kwamba mwili wake ulilalamika kila jioni alipolala, ukimkumbusha kuhusu shida zote ulizovumilia.

Si ibuprofen wala Tylenol iliyomsaidia kuvumilia nyakati hizo (dawa hizo hazingevumbuliwa kwa karne nyingi). Badala yake, ilikuwa ni nguvu aliyopewa na uhusiano wake na Mungu. Nguvu hiyo hiyo inapatikana kwetu leo, haidhuru tunakabiliwa na nini, hata ugonjwa wa kuua.

Fahamu Kwamba Kuna Uwezekano wa Kuwa na Maumivu

Mojawapo ya maamuzi ambayo watu wanaweza kufanya mwishoni mwa maisha ni kukubali huduma ya kupunguza maumivu na dalili nyingine. Hii ni aina ya huduma iliyoundwa mahsusi kutibu maumivu na dalili nyingine, kwa kawaida kwa mgonjwa aliye mahututi (ili kumstarehesha, wala si kujaribu kumponya). Aina hii ya huduma hutolewa na programu za hospice.

Madaktari na wauguzi katika programu za hospice hulenga hasa kuondoa maumivu badala ya kutafuta tiba ya mgonjwa. Kwa hiyo, wanategemea sana wagonjwa kusema ukweli kuhusu kiwango cha maumivu yao, ili waweze kuwapa dozi ambazo wagonjwa huhisi wanahitaji ili kudhibiti maumivu yao.

Bila shaka, hili ni gumu. Mara nyingi, njia pekee ya kuondoa maumivu kabisa ni kumpa mtu dawa nyingi sana za maumivu kiasi cha kumfanya ashindwe kuwasiliana na watu wanaomzunguka. Kama kawaida, kuna haja ya kuwa na uwiano kati ya kudhibiti maumivu na kutopewa dawa nyingi kiasi cha kumfanya mtu asinzie na kulegea.

Mungu Hutukuzwa Katika Mateso Yetu

Maana dhiki yetu nyepesi, iliyo ya muda wa kitambo tu, yatufanyia utukufu wa milele uzidio kuwa mwingi sana; tusiviangalie vinavyoonekana, bali visivyoonekana. Kwa maana vinavyoonekana ni vya muda tu, bali visivyoonekana ni vya milele –2 Wakorintho 4:17-18.

Hakuna hata mmoja wetu anayefurahia kuteseka, na kwa hakika hatutafuti mateso. Tunapopitia mateso, ulimwengu unaotuzunguka huona jinsi tunavyokabiliana nayo, nao unaweza kutambua kama kuna jambo tofauti ndani yetu.

Tunajua kwamba Yesu aliteseka sana wakati wa kesi yake na kusulubiwa kwake. Mateso yoyote tunayopitia ni madogo sana yakilinganishwa na hayo.

Jambo muhimu zaidi ni kumtazama Mwokozi wetu. Yeye ndiye anayetupa nguvu za kuvumilia hadi mwisho. Yeye ni mwaminifu daima.

Hitimisho

Ulimwengu ni mahali penye giza siku hizi. Thamani ya maisha inaonekana kupungua kadiri muda unavyopita. Nchi nyingi zaidi na zaidi zinaruhusu madaktari kuandika dawa zinazowawezesha wagonjwa kuyakatisha maisha yao wenyewe, huku nyingine zikiruhusu hata madaktari kuwapa wagonjwa wao dawa zitakazowaua.

Ni muhimu tuendelee kuthamini uhai wa binadamu na kumtukuza Mungu katika kila jambo tunalokabili—hata tunapokuwa na ugonjwa wa kuua.

Ikiwa tunawajibika kumtunza mtu aliye katika hali hii, ni muhimu sana kumhakikishia kwamba ana thamani na kuhakikisha kwamba anaelewa kuwa yeye si mzigo. Mungu anathamini maisha yao, nasi tunapaswa kufanya vivyo hivyo. Msaada huu utawasaidia wanapopambana na vizuizi ambavyo afya yao imewawekea.

Hakuna hata mmoja wetu atakayeishi milele, lakini mambo tunayofanya hapa yana matokeo ya milele kwetu na kwa wale tunaowashawishi.

Pride is something that everyone must deal with. It is something that naturally tends to come into our lives and stay. Like many other things, it is very deceitful, because it is commonly accepted by the world in which we live. People today are proud of being proud. Americans are proud of their country, their jobs, their children, their lawns, their sports teams, their vehicles, their ambitions, their goals, their looks, their friends, their homes, and the list could go on. If we think about it, the carnal man is proud of just about anything. People stand and proclaim they are proud and boast of their great accomplishments. People look at something someone has done and proclaim to the doer, “You should be proud of yourself!”

There is one problem; God hates pride! God actually despises the proud. In Psalms, it says that God will cut off …the tongue that speaketh proud things –Psalm 12:3. And in Job it says He will …behold every one that is proud, and abase [put down or make low] him –Job 40:11. Psalms 40:4 says He will not respect the proud and in Psalm 119: Thou hast rebuked the proud that are cursed, which do err from thy commandments –Psalm 119:21. In Proverbs, we read that: The LORD will destroy the house of the proud… –Proverbs 15:25, and that Every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to the LORD… –Proverbs 16:5. In Malachi, it says that …behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud… –Malachi 4:1. Finally, James states that …God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble –James 4:6.

As we can see, the Bible is very clear on pride, and the people who are proud. There is no room for pride in our hearts or lives. So, what do we do with this? Are we proud? Do we boast as the world does?

I would like to call attention to a hidden form of pride that can slip into our lives, sometimes unnoticed. We will call it false humility. If we have a false humility, would it not actually be a form of pride?

Let us look first at Law and Grace. Someone that is under the law does not desire to do what he must do, but rather, he does it because of the law. For example, the law states that we should not kill, yet (according to the law) we are allowed to be angry. Someone can hate another and even desire to kill him, but if they resist the temptation to kill, they have indeed kept the law. Many people today who claim to be Christians, are actually under the law. They do all that they do because of a law, or an order from their authority. We can see this clearly when people push the law, doing the least that is required, but still technically keeping the law.

The head covering is a good example. A woman who desires to cover her head because of what the Bible teaches, will indeed cover her head. She does not need to be reminded to do it or be admonished for doing it half-heartedly. On the other hand, there are Christians that cover their heads; however, the actual covering continues to get smaller, and less noticeable. Some even put it all the way on the back of the head and color it the same as their hair, trying to keep it from being noticed by the uncovered public. This clearly reveals the heart; they are simply complying with the law.

This type of thinking can go for many things. One more would be adornment. The bible says that the adornment should not be outward. Many Christians will not adorn themselves with flashy eye-catching things, however there are no standards about adorning homes, vehicles, and such like. So, a plain, unadorned person gets out of their adorned vehicle and walks into their very adorned home. This shows where the heart is—under the law.

Now let us look at grace. It is the power of God in the life of a human being. It causes one to actually love their enemies, to do good to those who mistreat them. It causes one to love their God with all their heart and obey God’s commands because of a passionate love for Him. The law is no longer needed because the heart is new; it desires to live for God. When someone does evil to you, you do not think about getting even. In fact, you do not even get angry. You are a new creature and because of this power—grace from God—you love him that has done you wrong. Forgiving is not a problem; helping others is natural. You are not your own and you desire to be all you can be for your Savior who died for you.

What does this have to do with pride or humility?

The Bible says that …the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ –John 1:17. It does not take God’s Spirit in our lives for us to obey the law—we can do that on our own. Therefore, we can become proud by doing things for God because WE did them. When we did not allow our anger to spew out when disagreeing with a neighbor, we think well of ourselves, and we can become proud. However, when we actually love our neighbor that has a problem with us, we cannot become proud because it was grace; it was the power of God that caused this, not ourselves. Therefore, we marvel at God and his abundant grace.

It would be foolish for someone to be proud of something that God clearly did! If Lazarus walked around boasting of himself for being raised from the dead, people would question his sanity, saying, “You did nothing! It was Jesus that did everything.”

I’m not trying to say that the Christian does nothing. No, we must humbly obey the commandments of God and walk in His ways. However, I am saying that we cannot boast in ourselves because it is God that enables us to obey His commandments.

Let us look at the popular story of David and Goliath. David went to the army to take provisions to his brothers who were fighting there. As he approached, he marveled at what he saw, a large man challenging his people! David seemed a bit shocked, and aggrieved as he asked, …who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God? –1 Samuel 17:26.

What does David’s oldest brother Eliab say to him? “I know thy pride.”

Eliab thought the attitude of David was prideful, and we can see why. A ruddy youth walks up from tending sheep and wonders why someone is not taking care of this large man. It sounds a bit off. But what was David thinking? He was only thinking about what God could, and most likely, wanted to do! He did not think for a moment that he himself could do anything in this situation.

He is then brought before King Saul: And Saul said to David, Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth –1 Samuel 17:33.

David responded, … Thy servant kept his father’s sheep, and there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock: And I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth: and when he arose against me, I caught him by his beard, and smote him, and slew him. Thy servant slew both the lion and the bear: and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, seeing he hath defied the armies of the living God –1 Samuel 17:34-36.

David here is super confident, but why?! David said moreover, The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine… –1 Samuel 17:37.

Clearly his confidence is because the Lord is fighting for him. David was not concerned that he was “but a youth” and he did not understand why people questioned him. He was only thinking about what God was going to do! However, Eliab saw David’s confidence as pride. Possibly God had not worked in Eliab’s life. Maybe he did not know of the power of God; therefore, to him it looked like foolish pride.

And Saul armed David with his armour, and he put an helmet of brass upon his head; also he armed him with a coat of mail. And David girded his sword upon his armour, and he assayed to go; for he had not proved it. And David said unto Saul, I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them. And David put them off him –1 Samuel 17:38-39.

So, David chose to not wear the armor; it would only have been a hindrance. Rather, he chose some stones then he ran out to fight the giant. Of course, the giant also did not understand. When he …saw David, he disdained him: for he was but a youth … And the Philistine said unto David, Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods. And the Philistine said to David, Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field –1 Samuel 17:42-44.

Then David said …Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied. This day will the LORD deliver thee into mine hand; and I will smite thee … that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel –1 Samuel 17:45-46.

Notice then what David did. He killed the giant, cut off his head, and took his head back to Jerusalem. What do you think Eliab thought now? Here is the younger brother marching around the streets of Jerusalem with the head of the defeated giant! King Saul calls for David and he goes to see Saul, still holding the severed head.

Why was David not proud? Because he knew it was not he himself that did it. It was God who had done a marvelous work! He was simply testifying of the grace of God.

When we do a work on our own, we cannot boast of it because we did it. It would be pride, so we remain silent and call it humility, even if we desire others to see it. However, when it is a super-natural work of God, we now must boast of what God has done! We are called to this.

Is God working in your life? Are you confused as to whether it is you or God? Ask yourself a question, “Am I doing things that people who are not relying on God can still do?” If we are not doing anything differently than the world, then God is not working in our life. It is that simple. No one enjoys getting angry. I spent most of my childhood and teenage years going to anger management classes where counselors tried to teach us how to control our anger. The unregenerate heart can learn to hide anger, but only God can change the heart. I never heard a counselor teach us how to love people instead of getting angry with them, since it is impossible! It is only a work of the living God in one’s life, and in that work, we must boast! We testify of the outpouring of the grace of God in our lives. When someone believes it is pride, just like Eliab did, it’s because they only see the working of the Law, where all is done by man’s feeble attempts.

Let us look at an example to help us understand. If you decide to build a house, every day you put on your nail bag and get to work. It takes you time and energy, but finally the house is finished. You are standing in front of the newly constructed home with a friend. “Wow,” he states, “This house is beautiful! It looks perfectly built!”

Your cheeks blush a little and you begin to point out the flaws that you know, “No, it’s not perfect, you see that over there? I messed up on that gable…. And the siding over there… it’s not exactly straight.” We do this because we want to be humble! If we would say, “Yes, it is a beautiful house; I did a great job building it!” it would be prideful, right?

Now, what if you wanted to build a house and you realize you are not able to build it; you need God’s help. You pray for help then bam, the house is built! You never even put on your nail bag; the house miraculously appeared. God built it. Now how would the conversation go with your friend? Would you still point out all the flaws? NO! You would boast of its perfection, boldly proclaiming what the Lord had done.

When God does a work in our lives, it is not pride to tell people about it. It takes humility to say that we did not do it, but that God did! However, the devil wants us to quiet down and say it is humility like Eliab wanted David to do. We need men and women today that can boldly proclaim what God is doing in their lives!

Instead, it seems we have many defeated people that actually believe it is godly to talk down about ourselves, to act as if we are a defeated sinner trying to struggle through this earthly existence. “Rise up, Oh man of God! Be done with lesser things!”

I realize one could ask, “So, we should go around boasting about how righteous we are?” To this question, I will paint another picture. A poor criminal who has only known the city streets as home, steals and robs just to get by. He knows he is a bad person, yet he knows nothing else. One day God reveals himself to this man. In a dark alley he repents of his sin and gives his life to the Lord. God saves him, transforms him, converts him. He leaves that alley a new person! He has joy in his heart and peace in his soul!

What do you expect him to tell his friends? Um, the siding over there is not straight, the windows are too small….

NO, certainly not! Rather, he would say I’m perfect! God has done a great work, look at me! I’ve been saved by the power of God! By the blood of Jesus! All this as he skips down the road in the beauty of holiness.

El orgullo es algo con lo que todos deben lidiar. Es algo que naturalmente tiende a entrar en nuestra vida y quedarse. Como muchas otras cosas, es muy engañoso, porque el mundo en que vivimos lo acepta comúnmente. Hoy en día, la gente se enorgullece de estar orgullosa. Los estadounidenses se enorgullecen de su país, sus trabajos, sus hijos, sus jardines, sus equipos deportivos, sus vehículos, sus ambiciones, sus metas, su aspecto, sus amigos, sus hogares, y la lista podría continuar. Si lo pensamos, el hombre carnal se enorgullece de casi cualquier cosa. La gente se pone de pie y proclama que está orgullosa, y se jacta de sus grandes logros. La gente ve algo que alguien ha hecho y le dice a quien lo hizo: «¡Deberías estar orgulloso de ti mismo!»

Hay un problema: ¡Dios aborrece el orgullo! Dios realmente desprecia a los orgullosos. En Salmos dice que Dios cortará …la lengua que habla con arrogancia —Salmo 12:3. Y en Job dice que …mirará a todo soberbio y lo humillará [lo rebajará o lo hará descender] —Job 40:11. Salmo 40:4 dice que no tendrá en cuenta a los orgullosos, y en Salmo 119: Reprendiste a los soberbios, malditos, que se desvían de tus mandamientos —Salmo 119:21. En Proverbios leemos que El SEÑOR destruirá la casa de los soberbios… —Proverbios 15:25, y que Abominación es al SEÑOR todo altivo de corazón… —Proverbios 16:5. En Malaquías dice que …he aquí, viene el día que arderá como un horno; y todos los soberbios… —Malaquías 4:1. Finalmente, Santiago afirma que …Dios resiste a los soberbios, y da gracia a los humildes —Santiago 4:6.

Como podemos ver, la Biblia es muy clara con respecto al orgullo y a las personas orgullosas. No hay lugar para el orgullo en nuestro corazón ni en nuestra vida. Entonces, ¿qué hacemos con esto? ¿Somos orgullosos? ¿Nos jactamos como lo hace el mundo?

Quisiera llamar la atención sobre una forma oculta de orgullo que puede infiltrarse en nuestra vida, a veces sin que nos demos cuenta. La llamaremos falsa humildad. Si tenemos una falsa humildad, ¿no sería en realidad una forma de orgullo?

Veamos primero la Ley y la Gracia. Quien está bajo la ley no desea hacer lo que debe hacer, sino que lo hace por causa de la ley. Por ejemplo, la ley dice que no debemos matar, pero (según la ley) se nos permite enojarnos. Alguien puede odiar a otra persona e incluso desear matarla, pero si resiste la tentación de matarla, en efecto ha cumplido la ley. Muchas personas hoy que afirman ser cristianas en realidad están bajo la ley. Hacen todo lo que hacen por causa de una ley o de una orden de su autoridad. Podemos verlo claramente cuando la gente se aferra a la ley y hace lo mínimo requerido, pero aun así la cumple técnicamente.

El cubrimiento de la cabeza es un buen ejemplo. Una mujer que desea cubrirse la cabeza por lo que enseña la Biblia, ciertamente se cubrirá la cabeza. No hace falta recordárselo ni reprenderla por hacerlo sin entusiasmo. Por otro lado, hay cristianas que se cubren la cabeza; sin embargo, el cubrimiento se hace cada vez más pequeño y menos visible. Algunas incluso lo colocan hasta atrás de la cabeza y lo tiñen del mismo color que su cabello, intentando que no lo note el público que va sin cubrirse. Esto revela claramente el corazón: simplemente están cumpliendo la ley.

Este tipo de pensamiento puede aplicarse a muchas cosas. Otro ejemplo sería el adorno. La Biblia dice que el adorno no debe ser exterior. Muchos cristianos no se adornan con cosas llamativas que atraigan la mirada; sin embargo, no hay normas sobre adornar las casas, los vehículos y cosas semejantes. Así que una persona sencilla, sin adornos, se baja de su vehículo adornado y entra en su casa muy adornada. Esto muestra dónde está el corazón: bajo la ley.

Ahora veamos la gracia. Es el poder de Dios en la vida de un ser humano. Hace que uno ame de verdad a sus enemigos y haga el bien a quienes lo maltratan. Hace que uno ame a Dios con todo su corazón y obedezca sus mandamientos por un amor apasionado hacia Él. La ley ya no es necesaria porque el corazón es nuevo; desea vivir para Dios. Cuando alguien te hace mal, no piensas en desquitarte. De hecho, ni siquiera te enojas. Eres una nueva criatura y, por este poder —la gracia de Dios—, amas a quien te ha hecho mal. Perdonar no es un problema; ayudar a los demás es algo natural. Ya no eres tuyo y deseas ser todo lo que puedas para tu Salvador, que murió por ti.

¿Qué tiene que ver esto con el orgullo o la humildad?

La Biblia dice que …la ley fue dada por medio de Moisés, pero la gracia y la verdad vinieron por medio de Jesucristo —Juan 1:17. No necesitamos que el Espíritu de Dios actúe en nuestra vida para obedecer la ley: podemos hacerlo por nuestra cuenta. Por lo tanto, podemos enorgullecernos de hacer cosas para Dios porque NOSOTROS las hicimos. Cuando no dejamos que la ira se desborde al estar en desacuerdo con un vecino, pensamos bien de nosotros mismos y podemos enorgullecernos. Sin embargo, cuando de verdad amamos a nuestro vecino que tiene un problema con nosotros, no podemos enorgullecernos, porque fue la gracia; fue el poder de Dios lo que lo hizo posible, no nosotros. Por eso, nos maravillamos de Dios y de su abundante gracia.

Sería insensato que alguien se enorgulleciera de algo que claramente hizo Dios. Si Lázaro anduviera por ahí jactándose de que él mismo había resucitado de entre los muertos, la gente cuestionaría su cordura y diría: «¡Tú no hiciste nada! Jesús fue quien lo hizo todo».

No estoy tratando de decir que el cristiano no hace nada. No, debemos obedecer humildemente los mandamientos de Dios y andar en sus caminos. Sin embargo, digo que no podemos jactarnos de nosotros mismos, porque es Dios quien nos capacita para obedecer sus mandamientos.

Veamos la conocida historia de David y Goliat. David fue al campamento del ejército para llevar provisiones a sus hermanos, que estaban peleando allí. Al acercarse, se asombró de lo que vio: ¡un hombre enorme que desafiaba a su pueblo! David pareció algo sorprendido y afligido cuando preguntó: …¿quién es este filisteo incircunciso, para que provoque a los escuadrones del Dios viviente? —1 Samuel 17:26.

¿Qué le dice Eliab, el hermano mayor de David? «Yo conozco tu orgullo».

Eliab pensó que la actitud de David era orgullosa, y podemos ver por qué. Un joven rubicundo que viene de cuidar ovejas se acerca y se pregunta por qué nadie se ocupa de ese hombre enorme. Suena un poco extraño. Pero ¿qué pensaba David? ¡Solo pensaba en lo que Dios podía hacer y, muy probablemente, quería hacer! Ni por un momento pensó que él mismo pudiera hacer algo en esa situación.

Luego lo llevan ante el rey Saúl: Y Saúl dijo a David: No podrás tú ir contra aquel filisteo, para pelear con él; porque tú eres muchacho, y él un hombre de guerra desde su juventud —1 Samuel 17:33.

David respondió: …Tu siervo era pastor de las ovejas de su padre, y cuando venía un león, o un oso, y tomaba algún cordero de la manada, salía yo tras él, y lo hería, y lo libraba de su boca; y si se levantaba contra mí, lo agarré por la barba, y lo hería y lo mataba. Fuese león, fuese oso, tu siervo lo mataba; y este filisteo incircunciso será como uno de ellos, porque ha provocado a los escuadrones del Dios viviente —1 Samuel 17:34-36.

David está muy seguro de sí mismo aquí, pero ¿por qué? Además dijo David: El SEÑOR, que me ha librado de las garras del león y de las garras del oso, Él también me librará de la mano de este filisteo… —1 Samuel 17:37.

Está claro que su confianza se debe a que el Señor lucha por él. A David no le preocupaba ser «solo un muchacho» y no entendía por qué la gente lo cuestionaba. ¡Solo pensaba en lo que Dios iba a hacer! Sin embargo, Eliab vio la confianza de David como orgullo. Es posible que Dios no hubiera obrado en la vida de Eliab. Quizá no conocía el poder de Dios; por eso, a sus ojos, aquello parecía un orgullo insensato.

Y Saúl vistió a David con sus ropas, y puso sobre su cabeza un casco de bronce, y le armó de coraza. Y ciñó David su espada sobre sus ropas, y probó a andar, porque nunca había hecho la prueba. Y dijo David a Saúl: Yo no puedo andar con esto, porque nunca lo practiqué. Y David echó de sí aquellas cosas —1 Samuel 17:38-39.

Así que David decidió no ponerse la armadura; solo habría sido un estorbo. En cambio, escogió unas piedras y salió corriendo a luchar contra el gigante. Por supuesto, el gigante tampoco lo entendía. Cuando …vio a David, le tuvo en poco; porque era muchacho… Y dijo el filisteo a David: ¿Soy yo perro, para que vengas a mí con palos? Y maldijo a David por sus dioses. Dijo luego el filisteo a David: Ven a mí, y daré tu carne a las aves del cielo y a las bestias del campo —1 Samuel 17:42-44.

Entonces David dijo: …Tú vienes a mí con espada, lanza y escudo; mas yo vengo a ti en el nombre del SEÑOR de los ejércitos, el Dios de los escuadrones de Israel, a quien tú has provocado. El SEÑOR te entregará hoy en mi mano, y yo te venceré… y toda la tierra sabrá que hay Dios en Israel —1 Samuel 17:45-46.

Fíjense entonces en lo que hizo David. Mató al gigante, le cortó la cabeza y llevó su cabeza de vuelta a Jerusalén. ¿Qué creen que pensó Eliab entonces? ¡Allí está el hermano menor marchando por las calles de Jerusalén con la cabeza del gigante derrotado! El rey Saúl manda llamar a David, y él va a ver a Saúl, todavía con la cabeza cortada en la mano.

¿Por qué David no estaba orgulloso? Porque sabía que no lo había hecho él mismo. ¡Dios había realizado una obra maravillosa! Él simplemente daba testimonio de la gracia de Dios.

Cuando hacemos una obra por nuestra cuenta, no podemos jactarnos de ella porque la hicimos nosotros. Sería orgullo, así que guardamos silencio y lo llamamos humildad, incluso si deseamos que otros lo vean. Sin embargo, cuando se trata de una obra sobrenatural de Dios, ¡ahora debemos jactarnos de lo que Dios ha hecho! Estamos llamados a hacerlo.

¿Está obrando Dios en tu vida? ¿No sabes si eres tú o Dios? Hazte esta pregunta: «¿Estoy haciendo cosas que también pueden hacer quienes no dependen de Dios?». Si no hacemos nada distinto del mundo, entonces Dios no está obrando en nuestra vida. Es así de sencillo. A nadie le gusta enojarse. Pasé la mayor parte de mi niñez y adolescencia asistiendo a clases de control de la ira, donde los consejeros intentaban enseñarnos a controlar nuestro enojo. El corazón no regenerado puede aprender a ocultar la ira, pero solo Dios puede cambiar el corazón. Nunca oí a un consejero enseñarnos a amar a las personas en vez de enojarnos con ellas, ¡porque es imposible! Es una obra que solo el Dios viviente puede hacer en la vida de una persona, y de esa obra debemos jactarnos. Damos testimonio del derramamiento de la gracia de Dios en nuestra vida. Cuando alguien cree que eso es orgullo, tal como lo hizo Eliab, es porque solo ve la obra de la Ley, donde todo se hace mediante los débiles esfuerzos del hombre.

Veamos un ejemplo que nos ayude a entender. Si decides construir una casa, todos los días te pones el cinturón de clavos y te pones a trabajar. Te lleva tiempo y esfuerzo, pero por fin la casa está terminada. Estás de pie delante de la casa recién construida con un amigo. «¡Vaya!», dice él, «¡Esta casa es hermosa! ¡Parece perfectamente construida!»

Se te sonrojan un poco las mejillas y empiezas a señalar los defectos que conoces: «No, no es perfecta, ¿ves aquello de allí? Me equivoqué con ese hastial… Y el revestimiento de allí… no está del todo recto». Hacemos esto porque queremos ser humildes. Si dijéramos: «Sí, es una casa hermosa; ¡hice un gran trabajo al construirla!», sería orgullo, ¿verdad?

Ahora bien, ¿qué pasaría si quisieras construir una casa y te dieras cuenta de que no puedes hacerlo, que necesitas la ayuda de Dios? Oras por ayuda y, ¡zas!, ¡la casa está construida! Ni siquiera te pusiste el cinturón de clavos; la casa apareció milagrosamente. Dios la construyó. ¿Cómo sería entonces la conversación con tu amigo? ¿Seguirías señalando todos los defectos? ¡NO! Te jactarías de su perfección y proclamarías con valentía lo que el Señor había hecho.

Cuando Dios obra en nuestra vida, no es orgullo contárselo a la gente. Hace falta humildad para decir que no lo hicimos nosotros, ¡sino que lo hizo Dios! Sin embargo, el diablo quiere que nos callemos y digamos que eso es humildad, como Eliab quería que hiciera David. ¡Hoy necesitamos hombres y mujeres que puedan proclamar con valentía lo que Dios está haciendo en su vida!

En cambio, parece que tenemos a muchas personas derrotadas que realmente creen que es piadoso hablar mal de nosotros mismos, actuar como si fuéramos pecadores derrotados que intentan abrirse paso con dificultad por esta existencia terrenal. «¡Levántate, oh hombre de Dios! ¡Deja atrás las cosas inferiores!»

Me doy cuenta de que alguien podría preguntar: «Entonces, ¿deberíamos andar jactándonos de lo justos que somos?». A esta pregunta responderé con otra imagen. Un pobre delincuente que solo ha conocido las calles de la ciudad como hogar, roba y asalta para poder salir adelante. Sabe que es una mala persona, pero no conoce otra cosa. Un día, Dios se revela a este hombre. En un callejón oscuro se arrepiente de su pecado y entrega su vida al Señor. Dios lo salva, lo transforma, lo convierte. ¡Sale de aquel callejón convertido en una persona nueva! ¡Tiene alegría en el corazón y paz en el alma!

¿Qué esperan que les cuente a sus amigos? «Mmm, el revestimiento de allí no está recto, las ventanas son demasiado pequeñas…».

¡NO, por supuesto que no! Más bien diría: «¡Soy perfecto! ¡Dios ha hecho una gran obra, mírenme! ¡He sido salvado por el poder de Dios! ¡Por la sangre de Jesús!». Todo esto mientras avanza dando saltos por el camino, en la hermosura de la santidad.

The storm was dark and threatening,
Dark clouds billowed o’er head.
Lightning flashed around me,
Fears gripped and filled me with dread.

Thunder rolled out its forebodings.
My heart felt heavy and numb.
All around the storm was raging,
The turmoil inside struck me dumb.

Not only was the danger around me,
But just as real was the peril within.
I trembled as I looked at the future,
Not knowing how next to begin.

What lay behind the fog?
The wind whistled in my ears.
Suggesting questions, tripping my feet,
And ladening me down with fears.

This storm had removed all signs of the path,
That one time I had thought I could see.
Now, all the familiar was gone to my eyes,
Each step taken hesitatingly.

At the end of myself, I cried out in fear...
"Lord, come unto me! Tarry not, oh my King!"
Silence reigned heavy, I felt all alone,
Only to hope did I cling.

Then a still, but strong voice spoke in my ear,
"My precious child, look up."
Why such a request? When engulfed as I was,
In the fog that refused to break up.

Still in hope, I lifted my eyes,
Trembling at the dark clouds around.
Yet as I looked, I saw something more,
A treasure in the sky there was found.

Amidst all the dark and threatening clouds,
There it was! A cleft of light!
A rainbow shone through, of loveliest hue,
A beacon amidst this dark night.

"My child, fear not, you were never alone.
Not for a second could I leave your side.
Though the path is obscure, and there is much to endure,
Do not doubt that in Me you can hide."

"Yes, for now, you walk amidst trials,
Fears threaten both inside and out.
You wonder and question what is next to be done,
Dangers seem to laugh and flout."

"But here I have placed My rainbow,
That amidst all the darkness and fear,
You can see that My promise is certain.
I will never forsake, but always be near."

"If you keep your eyes on this promise,
My light will guide your way.
The fears and dangers surrounding,
Will then be held at bay."

"This promise can also open to you,
The secrets that are hid 'midst the storm.
For My strength and power are manifest,
When these to My will conform."

"So, My child, gaze long at the rainbow.
Ponder the message it brings.
Though all around you is angry and wild,
Remember the promise that it sings."

~by Adrianna Fanton

Η καταιγίδα ήταν σκοτεινή και απειλητική,
Σκούρα σύννεφα φούσκωναν από πάνω μου.
Αστραπές έλαμπαν γύρω μου,
Ο φόβος με άρπαξε και με γέμισε τρόμο.

Η βροντή αντήχησε προμηνύοντας συμφορές.
Η καρδιά μου ένιωθε βαριά και μουδιασμένη.
Ολόγυρα η καταιγίδα λυσσομανούσε,
Η αναταραχή μέσα μου με άφησε άφωνη.

Δεν ήταν μόνο ο κίνδυνος γύρω μου,
Μα εξίσου αληθινός ήταν ο κίνδυνος μέσα μου.
Έτρεμα καθώς κοίταζα το μέλλον,
Μη γνωρίζοντας πώς να κάνω το επόμενο βήμα.

Τι κρυβόταν πίσω από την ομίχλη;
Ο άνεμος σφύριζε στ’ αυτιά μου.
Γεννούσε ερωτήματα, μου έκοβε τα βήματα,
Και με φόρτωνε με φόβους.

Αυτή η καταιγίδα είχε σβήσει όλα τα σημάδια του μονοπατιού,
Που κάποτε νόμιζα πως μπορούσα να δω.
Τώρα, όλα τα γνώριμα είχαν χαθεί από τα μάτια μου,
Κάθε βήμα το έκανα διστακτικά.

Όταν έφτασα στα όριά μου, φώναξα τρομαγμένη...
«Κύριε, έλα κοντά μου! Μη χρονοτριβείς, Βασιλιά μου!»
Η σιωπή απλώθηκε βαριά, ένιωσα ολομόναχη,
Μόνο στην ελπίδα γαντζώθηκα.

Τότε μια ήρεμη, μα δυνατή φωνή μού μίλησε στ’ αυτί,
«Πολύτιμο παιδί μου, κοίτα ψηλά».
Γιατί τέτοιο αίτημα; Αφού με είχε καταπιεί
Η ομίχλη που αρνιόταν να διαλυθεί.

Κρατώντας ακόμη την ελπίδα, σήκωσα τα μάτια μου,
Τρέμοντας μπροστά στα σκοτεινά σύννεφα γύρω μου.
Κι όμως, καθώς κοίταξα, είδα κάτι περισσότερο,
Έναν θησαυρό στον ουρανό.

Ανάμεσα στα σκοτεινά και απειλητικά σύννεφα,
Να το! Ένα άνοιγμα φωτός!
Ένα ουράνιο τόξο έλαμπε, με το ομορφότερο χρώμα,
Ένας φάρος μέσα σ’ αυτή τη σκοτεινή νύχτα.

«Παιδί μου, μη φοβάσαι, ποτέ δεν ήσουν μόνο.
Ούτε για μια στιγμή δεν θα μπορούσα να φύγω από κοντά σου.
Αν και το μονοπάτι είναι ασαφές και υπάρχουν πολλά που πρέπει να υπομείνεις,
Μην αμφιβάλλεις πως μπορείς να βρεις καταφύγιο σε Μένα».

«Ναι, προς το παρόν περπατάς ανάμεσα σε δοκιμασίες,
Οι φόβοι απειλούν από μέσα κι απ’ έξω.
Αναρωτιέσαι και ρωτάς τι πρέπει να κάνεις στη συνέχεια,
Οι κίνδυνοι μοιάζουν να γελούν και να περιφρονούν».

«Μα εδώ έχω τοποθετήσει το ουράνιο τόξο Μου,
Για να μπορείς, μέσα σε όλο το σκοτάδι και τον φόβο,
Να βλέπεις πως η υπόσχεσή Μου είναι βέβαιη.
Δεν θα σε εγκαταλείψω ποτέ, μα θα είμαι πάντα κοντά».
